title.en: Rav Nachum of Chernobyl and his little bread

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rav Nachum of Chernobyl ate only a very small amount of bread each day, and yet he was a heavy man. The Ba'al Shem Tov said of him that he was heavy from the nourishment he received from answering 'Amen, yehei shmei rabba'. The Mashgiach brings this to show that a tzaddik extracts much life from little food.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and Moses Mendelssohn's Shavuos tree

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Moses Mendelssohn outwardly looked like a learned, observant Jew, but the great tzaddikim sensed who he was. The Chasam Sofer used to ask what was happening with him, and once after Shavuos asked whether he had put a tree in his house, as is the minhag. When told that this time he had not, the Chasam Sofer said that until now he still had some connection, but now he had c…

title.en: Rabbi Mendel of Vitebsk's Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch said of Rabbi Mendel of Vitebsk that he saw in him such love of Shabbos that he felt each Shabbos as if there had never been a Shabbos in the world before and never would be again.

title.en: The Lechovitcher's glass of mead for Rabbi Michel

retelling.en: One of the Lechovitcher's students was called Rabbi Michel. Every erev Shabbos at candle lighting the Lechovitcher would call him in and have him drink a glass of mead, honey wine. He understood that Rabbi Michel needed strength, because he became so fired up on Shabbos that without it he would faint.

title.en: The Ramban and his student Avner

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions the well-known story of the Ramban and his student Avner, who had gone astray. The Ramban told him that he is hinted in the passuk in Haazinu that speaks of erasing their memory: the third letters of its four words spell Avner.

title.en: Chizkiyahu sleeps while Sancheriv's camp falls

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that King Chizkiyahu said he would go to sleep and Hashem would fight his wars. When Sancheriv besieged Yerushalayim on the night of Pesach, the Jews made the Korban Pesach and told of the Exodus, and in the middle of the night Sancheriv's whole camp was destroyed by an angel.

title.en: The man who nursed his infant

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara in Shabbos about a poor man who could not afford a nursemaid for his infant. A miracle happened and he was able to nurse the child himself. The Gemara comments how lowly this man was that the order of creation was changed for him.

title.en: Moshe in the teiva on Shavuos

retelling.en: Miriam prophesied that her mother would give birth to the one who would redeem the Jews from Egypt. Moshe was hidden for three months, and when the Egyptians were expected to come searching, he was placed in a teiva and put into the water, on the day that would later be Shavuos. Chazal say Miriam was struck on the head and asked where her prophecy was; the day of hope seemed to become the greates…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's 'shalom aleichem' after davening

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once greeted a Jew with 'shalom aleichem' after davening, as one greets a person returning from a journey, because during the davening his mind had been in Danzig. The Mashgiach uses this to explain that a person who davens without his heart is thrown out of the teiva of tefillah.

title.en: The Arizal and R' Chaim Vital's soul

retelling.en: The Arizal told R' Chaim Vital that his soul was very high, greater than the Amoraim and the Tannaim. R' Chaim Vital asked how this could be, when looking into the words of Chazal and the Rishonim he did not reach their heel. The Arizal answered that it was not because of his soul's root or ability, but because in a generation of great kelipah a small light counts for much; had he lived in the ti…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's dream of Gan Eden

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe dreamed that an angel led him around Gan Eden. He asked to see a certain Tanna, and was shown the Tanna standing in a plain room at a shtender with a Gemara. Surprised that this was Gan Eden, he was told by the angel that he thought the Tanna is in Gan Eden, but Gan Eden is in the Tanna.

title.en: The jealous man at the shoemaker's wedding

retelling.en: In a town in Lita, a shoemaker became wealthy and made a rich wedding for his child. One man could not bear that a person from the lower classes now equaled him. When everyone stood at the chuppah, he ran up, took out a torn shoe and asked the father before the whole crowd how much it would cost to fix, shaming him publicly. The Mashgiach connects this to Rav Yisrael Salanter's saying that the ra…

title.en: Who opened the aron?

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Rosh Chodesh in a certain chassidish shul, where a man honored with opening the aron took out a Sefer Torah still rolled to Bereishis. The congregation had to wait while it was rolled to Pinchas, and grew impatient. Rather than having mercy, people began demanding to know who had opened the aron, as if launching an investigation. The Mashgiach asks whether this shows we h…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's dream

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe told his grandson, the Yitav Lev, who wrote it down, that he once dreamed he was led through Gan Eden by an angel. Coming to the chamber of a certain Tanna, he saw a fine room where the Tanna stood at a shtender learning. He asked whether this was that Tanna's Gan Eden, and the angel answered that the Tanna is not in Gan Eden; Gan Eden is in the Tanna.

title.en: The anatomy book

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he once stayed in an apartment whose owner was a student of anatomy, and having nothing else to read he found a beginners' anatomy book. Every page held twenty or thirty wonders. He learned from it, for example, why the human spine is S-shaped: so that it can absorb the shock when a person jumps.

title.en: Avraham and Nimrod

retelling.en: From the Midrashim the Mashgiach recounts that Nimrod declared himself a god, and Avraham defied him, saying there is one G-d who created heaven and earth, and preached His existence at the risk of his life. Nimrod threw him into the fire, and Hashem made a miracle so that he came out unharmed. Then Hashem revealed Himself to him as the Maker of the world he had given his life for, and this was t…

title.en: The Slonimer chassid who would not eat the meat

retelling.en: A Slonimer chassid came to a misnagdish town and was given meat, but he did not eat it. When asked why, he said he had learned from his Rebbe to sense things: the meat was kosher, but it gave off a bad smell from a shochet who had slaughtered while he needed the mikveh and had not immersed.

title.en: The Lechovitcher chassid in Moscow

retelling.en: A disciple of Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch, a big businessman, traveled to Moscow, where under the Czar Jews were not allowed to live, with a license for a few days. With no mikveh there, he went to a small river where people sat on benches on both sides, and with self-sacrifice he undressed and immersed. When he returned, Rabbi Mordechai went out to greet him and thanked him, saying he had remo…

title.en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan and a difficult question

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard through a chain of listeners, going back to the secretary of Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan, that when Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan had a difficulty in psak or in Gemara that he could not resolve, he would go to the mikveh, hoping that with a little more purity he would understand it.

title.en: Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's answer

retelling.en: Rabbi Isser Zalman Meltzer, the father-in-law of Rabbi Aharon Kotler, asked Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, who went to the mikveh very often, sometimes even in the middle of the day, why a great talmid chacham needs it. He answered that a convert becomes a Jew through the mikveh; if it can make a Jew out of a gentile, it can surely make a better Jew out of a Jew. When Rabbi Isser Zalman heard this…

title.en: Rebbe Elimelech's grave in Lizhensk

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew he knew who saw Rebbe Elimelech, though the Rebbe passed away nearly two hundred years earlier. When the Nazis entered Lizhensk they wanted to disgrace Jews and forced ten Jews to dig open Rebbe Elimelech's grave. One of them later lived in Skver, a respected talmid chacham among the people of the previous Skverer Rebbe. Some hundred and fifty years after his burial t…

title.en: A letter whose signature stayed black

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he has at home a letter from about sixty or seventy years earlier, written by a gabbai and signed by a Stoliner Rebbe. Ordinary ink turns light brown with age, as seen in old sefarim, and so did the gabbai's writing. The signature, however, stayed black as if written the day before, because a tzaddik is not something that spoils.

title.en: The 'people of the sukkah'

people: the Spinka Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Meir

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells what the Spinka Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Meir, related: there were chassidim who felt such holiness in the sukkah that when Sukkos ended they did not want to leave it. It grew cold and snowed, and they could not endure it. A year later they went into the sukkah again and swore not to leave; when the snow and frost came Hashem had mercy on them, and angels carried them with the sukka…

title.en: The rebbetzin's kvitel for Rabbi Shlomo Leib of Lentshno

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that during a great machlokes between Galician and Polish rebbes, chassidim persecuted Rabbi Shlomo Leib of Lentshno. His rebbetzin went to a tzaddik, perhaps the Rimanover (the Mashgiach says he does not remember exactly), with a kvitel that did not say who she was, asking that her husband merit yiras shamayim and teshuvah. The tzaddik looked into the kvitel and said: why ask…

title.en: Rebbi and Nebuchadnezzar

retelling.en: According to the Midrash the Mashgiach brings, Rebbi was darshening the Megillah and, reaching the passuk about Mordechai being exiled, cursed Nebuchadnezzar. Later, darshening Yirmiyahu, he mentioned Nebuchadnezzar plainly. His students asked why, and he answered that in Yirmiyahu Nebuchadnezzar is a king, whom one may not curse, while in the Megillah he was already dead.

title.en: The Yetev Lev in the cheder

retelling.en: The Yetev Lev once came to see how a melamed taught Gemara to beginners. They were learning Eizehu Neshech, and the melamed began by explaining what neshech and tarbis are. The Yetev Lev told him that this is not how to teach; one must start with the source, the passuk.

title.en: The man in the 42nd Street library

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that he once needed a sefer that was not available, so he went to the large Judaica department of the 42nd Street library in Manhattan. There he saw a man with a gray beard studying a Gemara. The Mashgiach says that learning brought the man nowhere: he was swallowing an empty capsule, plain words without the kedushah.

title.en: Avraham in the fire of Ur Kasdim

retelling.en: Avraham, searching for truth, could not accept that a stone, wood, the sun or the moon was a god, and concluded there must be one Creator. He preached this, and Nimrod, who had declared himself a god, warned him; when Avraham did not stop, Nimrod threw him into the fire of Ur Kasdim. Avraham came out alive without a burn on his clothing, and Hashem then revealed Himself to him.

title.en: Bar Daroma and the Roman king

retelling.en: At the time of the churban there was a great warrior called Bar Daroma who could strike down thousands of Romans. The Roman king, seeing he was being defeated, took off his crown and pleaded that his kingdom not be destroyed because of one man. Bar Daroma then said the passuk 'Have You not abandoned us, G-d, and do not go out with our armies', and he was killed by a snake. The Mashgiach explains…

title.en: The ship of exiles and the fire

retelling.en: A ship of Jews fleeing Yerushalayim after the churban reached a land whose king said he would accept them only if one of them entered a fire and was saved, as Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah were. They asked for thirty days, in which they fasted and davened. A simple Jew who could not learn dreamed of a passuk he could not remember, only that it had 'ki' twice and 'lo' three times, and a sage reco…

title.en: The Rebbe of Chernobyl and the maid

retelling.en: There was a quarrel between the Rebbetzin and the maid, and the maid said she was leaving, though the Rebbetzin needed her. The Rebbe of Chernobyl stood in a corner and asked Hashem to put it in the maid's heart not to leave. His students asked why the Rebbe would pray to Hashem over such a trivial matter. He answered that they were right that one should not trouble the great Ribono shel Olam wit…

title.en: Reb Dovid'l of Talne and the roll

retelling.en: On Rosh Hashanah the chassidim waited for Reb Dovid'l of Talne for the shofar blowing, but he stayed in his room. Peeking through the cracks, they saw him pacing back and forth, saying the words 'holy and awesome' and then asking: and what does one ask of You? A roll. Suddenly his face lit up: of whom else should one ask for the roll? There is no one else. He then went in to the shofar blowing wi…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov, the wind and the worm

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was sitting under a tree with his students, teaching avodas Hashem, when a strong wind suddenly blew. He told them it had been revealed from Heaven why: on a hot day a small worm on a leaf of a tree could not bear the sun, Hashem had mercy and sent a wind, and the wind blew the worm with its leaf down into the shade of the tree, where it revived. The Mashgiach adds that making…

title.en: The Beis Aharon and the poretz's sugar sled

retelling.en: A chassid came to the Beis Aharon of Karlin and told him of a poretz who had it so good that he went mad from it. On a hot day in Tammuz the poretz wanted a sleigh ride, so his peasants brought hundreds of sacks of sugar, spread them over a field, and he rode his sleigh over the sugar as over snow. The Beis Aharon answered: that is called having it good? How does his pleasure compare to the pleas…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's long davening as a bachur

retelling.en: When the Chasam Sofer was a young bachur he davened at length. A friend teased him that while he was still davening Shemoneh Esrei, the friend had already finished and learned a siman of Shulchan Aruch with the Magen Avraham. The Chasam Sofer answered with the Gemara that one who lengthens his prayer has his days lengthened, so Hashem would give him enough days to learn what the Magen Avraham wro…

title.en: The tzaddikim's dispute over Napoleon

retelling.en: When Napoleon entered Russia there was a great dispute among the tzaddikim over whether he should win. The Ba'al HaTanya worked hard for Napoleon's defeat. He said that if Napoleon won, things would be very good for Jews materially, but he feared the joining with the nations that the freedom and equal rights would bring.

title.en: The Shpoler Zeide's two thieves

retelling.en: The Shpoler Zeide disliked noisy davening, and when a man in his shul clapped his hands in excitement, he told him what real clapping is. In his youth he had taught two students who would not learn; he still taught them Shema Yisrael, and they grew up to be thieves. Caught stealing from a church, a crime punishable by death, they refused to convert, were smeared with tar, and when the priest set…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's blessing for a traveler

retelling.en: A man came to the Chofetz Chaim for a brachah before going to Eretz Yisrael. The Chofetz Chaim told him he would encounter the Yishmaelim, who are difficult to deal with because they are a 'pere adam': whether doctor, lawyer, engineer or diplomat, he remains a 'pere adam'.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael paved with diamonds

retelling.en: A talmid of R' Nachum of Chernobyl, while still in chutz laaretz, described Eretz Yisrael to someone as a land paved with diamonds. Later the man traveled to Eretz Yisrael, met that Jew, and said he did not see it. For about three months he did not show himself, and then announced that he was making a large seudah for his friends, because now he was certain he felt that the land is paved with dia…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya and Reb Baruch of Mezhibuzh

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a dispute between the Ba'al HaTanya and Reb Baruch of Mezhibuzh, the Ba'al Shem Tov's grandson. Reb Baruch asked him whether he too wanted to be considered a grandson of the Ba'al Shem Tov. The Ba'al HaTanya answered that he was indeed one, since he was a talmid of the Maggid, who was a talmid of the Ba'al Shem Tov, and one who teaches another's son Torah is considered as if…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's question to the Chazon Ish

retelling.en: The Satmar Rav asked the Chazon Ish where one can hide today, when even in the deserts one cannot be an upright Jew. The Chazon Ish answered that one can hide in the yeshiva, and the yeshiva is a good place. The Mashgiach adds that even in a yeshiva one must find the 'desert', choosing good friends.

title.en: Reb Mendel's deal with the yetzer hara

retelling.en: Reb Mendel, one of the great disciples of the Maggid, told that when he traveled to Eretz Yisrael he made a deal with the yetzer hara: he had money for only one ticket, so either he would go or the yetzer hara would. The yetzer hara agreed to stay behind. When he got off the ship in Eretz Yisrael he met a great yetzer hara and asked whether they had not agreed it would stay in chutz la'aretz. It…

title.en: The Ropshitzer bakes matzos during Napoleon's war

retelling.en: During Napoleon's war, the Ropshitzer on erev Pesach put matzos into the oven, and each time he put one in he declared that another five hundred soldiers should fall. In this way, the Mashgiach says, he laid them down on the battlefield through baking matzah, because matzah holds the power of all redemptions.

title.en: The Satan becomes a river

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Satan left all his other business and concentrated on Avraham Avinu on his way to the Akeidah. He turned himself into a river, and Avraham found himself in water reaching almost to his mouth. Avraham called out to Hashem, and Hashem helped him; the Satan then tried all kinds of other tricks to divert him from going to the Akeidah.

title.en: The Arizal on Rav Chaim Vital's greatness

retelling.en: The Arizal used to tell his disciple Rav Chaim Vital how great he was, greater than the Rishonim and even the Tannaim and Amoraim. Rav Chaim Vital asked how that could be. The Arizal answered that Hashem measures by the generation: in a later generation one cannot reach the level of the earlier ones, but had he lived in their time he would have been greater than them, since what counts is how muc…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the machine-made tzitzis

retelling.en: In the Divrei Chaim's time a large factory began producing tzitzis by machine and flooded the country with them, though tzitzis must be made by hand with intent for the mitzvah. When asked, the Divrei Chaim ruled the machine tzitzis invalid and wished that the machine be destroyed. A note in the sefer records that some time later the whole factory burned down at great loss, and this was seen as t…

title.en: The martyrs of France

retelling.en: In France, the Mashgiach relates, enemies came to Jewish towns and said that whoever would not convert would be thrown into the river, and thousands of Jews were thrown in rather than convert. Others were gathered into their shuls, which were set on fire when they refused to give up their emunah, and they let themselves be burned together with the shul.

title.en: Kamtza, Bar Kamtza and the Caesar's offering

retelling.en: Following the Gemara, the Mashgiach tells that Bar Kamtza went to the Roman Caesar and said that the Jews had rebelled and would not offer his sacrifice. The Caesar sent an offering, and Bar Kamtza made a small blemish on it, on the lip or the eye, which is a blemish for Jews but not for the gentiles. The Chachamim wanted to offer it, but Rabbi Zechariah ben Avkulas did not allow it, the Caesar m…

title.en: Avraham the zealot in Ur Kasdim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that in Ur Kasdim Avraham fought openly against idol worship, broke his father's idols and entered into a conflict with Nimrod. Nimrod wanted to kill him and threw him into the fire, and from there came the miracle of his emerging alive.

title.en: Rebbi and Nebuchadnezzar's name

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash: when Rebbi read the Megillah and reached Nebuchadnezzar's name, he cursed him. Later, when learning the book of Yirmiyahu, he came to Nebuchadnezzar's name and did not curse him. Asked why, he answered that one does not curse a king; in the time of the Megillah, Nebuchadnezzar was long dead, but in Yirmiyahu's time he was alive and reigning.

title.en: The calf that led Avraham into the Me'aras HaMachpelah

retelling.en: Avraham went to the barn for a fine calf for his guests, but the calf was the angel Refael, who had come to heal his milah. It ran, Avraham chased it into a cave, and the cave was the Me'aras HaMachpelah, where he saw Adam and Chava buried and the light shining there. He had no time to stay, the calf turned back into an angel, and since it was late Avraham created a calf with Sefer Yetzirah.

title.en: Adam and Chava protest Sarah's burial

retelling.en: When Avraham came to bury Sarah, Adam and Chava stood up and walked out of the cave, saying Sarah was a perfect tzaddekes who put them to shame since they had eaten from the Eitz HaDa'as. Avraham promised to daven for them and Adam went back in, but Chava refused. Avraham pleaded with her, took her by the hand, brought her back and buried her again, and only afterwards buried Sarah.

title.en: Avraham in the fire of Ur Kasdim

retelling.en: As the Midrashim relate, Avraham sought the truth and tried all the idols, seeing that none could be true. With his own understanding he grasped that there must be one Master of the world who created the sun and moon, summer and winter, day and night. He was ready to give his life for this, and was thrown into the fire after telling them that their idol was not G-d. A miracle happened and he was…

title.en: Haran and the fire

retelling.en: Haran, Avraham's brother, waited to see what would happen to Avraham in Ur Kasdim. When he saw that Avraham was saved, he declared that he sided with Avraham, was thrown into the fire as well, and was burned. The Mashgiach says it was not entirely for the sake of Heaven, yet Haran did sanctify Hashem's name, and his son was Lot.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rav and the request for a heavenly answer

retelling.en: During a time of killings of Jews, a Jew named Reb Yitzchak, whose children had all been killed in one night, traveled to the Bluzhever Rav. Late at night he came in with two Belzer chassidim and asked the Bluzhever Rav to undertake forty fasts with holy names and ask in a dream from heaven how to save the Jews. The Bluzhever Rav, smoking a long pipe, was silent for a while, then asked whether th…

title.en: Three tzaddikim at the kever of the Ohr HaChaim

retelling.en: When Rommel's army had reached the borders of Eretz Yisroel and there was great fear there, three great tzaddikim took a Sefer Torah and went up to Har HaZeisim to the kever of the Ohr HaChaim to daven. When they returned, one of them said with a smile that he had seen Hashem's name in letters of light, meaning the Jews would be saved, and another told the people that it had been revealed to him…

title.en: The girl of Sedom who fed a poor man

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from Chazal that a girl in Sedom secretly gave food to a poor man whom the townspeople had decreed should starve. Each day when she went to draw water she took along a piece of bread for him. She was caught, taken up to a roof, smeared with honey and bound, and the bees came and stung her to death. The Mashgiach explains that this was Sedom's outlook: whoever wants to feed t…

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the frozen river

retelling.en: Lumber merchants who floated logs down the river to the mills came to the Belzer Rav in the spring: the river was still frozen and they would lose their fortune if the logs missed the contract's deadline. The Rebbe asked what the children in their town's cheder were learning, and they said Parshas Mikeitz. He told them that is why it is cold, since Mikeitz is a winter sedra read around Chanukah;…

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the frozen river

retelling.en: Jewish timber merchants floated logs down a river to a sawmill and had contracts to deliver them by a certain time. In Nissan a hard frost froze the river and the logs did not move, and as the contract neared expiry they feared losing everything, so they came to Rabbi Shalom of Belz. He asked what their children had learned that week and heard it was Parshas Mikeitz, since in their area children…

title.en: The widow's curse fulfilled literally

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Gittin: a widow was unhappy with a ruling of Rav Huna and cursed that his seat should be overturned, which in those days meant that a person would die. When he heard this he went and overturned his seat and afterwards set it straight, so that the curse would be fulfilled literally.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer leaves his city after a dream

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer once dreamed that he would have to leave his city. He went and left the city for a short time and lived elsewhere, so that the dream would be fulfilled that way and nothing worse would come, and he brought the Gemara in Gittin as a proof.

title.en: The girl in Sodom who fed a poor man

retelling.en: In Sodom there was a girl, according to the Mashgiach the daughter of Lot, who gave bread to a poor man. The people found out, smeared her with honey and set her up on the roof so that the insects would come and bite her. Their system was that one may not give to the poor, who should go to work.

title.en: The Mashgiach's impressions of Eretz Yisrael over the years

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that on his first trip to Eretz Yisrael, about twenty-five years earlier, he would look out at the land from the car and see how empty and barren it was, stony and with nothing else. Now, he says, every year he sees it growing more beautiful, with all kinds of produce and fruit getting better and bigger from year to year.

title.en: Ramadan on the Mashgiach's trips

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when he used to travel to Eretz Yisrael some years earlier, the month of Ramadan, when the Arabs fast by day and feast at night, would cause difficulties for visitors in Yerushalayim. Each year it came eleven or twelve days earlier, and now it falls in the middle of winter, because they do not reckon with the sun.

title.en: The wolf and the sour grapes

retelling.en: A wolf saw delicious grapes in a vineyard and tried for three days and three nights to climb the fence, but it was too high. In the end he turned around, declared the grapes sour, and left. The Mashgiach explains that the wolf would not admit his own inability, so he blamed the grapes.

title.en: The two newcomers and the watch

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that about forty years earlier, when he taught fifth grade, pupils told him what they had been taught about evolution, and he told them a story. Two intelligent men newly arrived from Africa saw a watch for the first time and theorized that inside it bugs in tubes chase cheese on splinters and pull the hands with strings; the second proved it by hearing the bugs stamping. T…

title.en: Bar Daroma's boast

retelling.en: In the war of the Churban there was a great Jewish warrior who could kill a thousand Romans with one blow and won great victories, until the Roman ruler despaired. In one moment he said words lacking emunah, that Hashem need not help since they were strong, and he was killed. Afterwards the Romans killed tens of thousands of Jews. The Mashgiach explains that the Jews had relied on his might and f…

title.en: Raphael as a calf leads Avraham to the Machpela

retelling.en: On the third day after Avraham's milah, the angel Raphael came disguised as a calf. Avraham chased it to prepare it for his guests, and it ran into the Machpela. Following it, Avraham suddenly saw the greatness and holiness of the cave, and from then on he longed for it.

title.en: Lavan runs to Eliezer

retelling.en: When Eliezer put the bracelets and nose ring on Rivka, Lavan, who understood such things, concluded that Eliezer must have looked at her improperly and was now in his power. He ran to Eliezer at the spring hoping to draw his holiness to himself. He found Eliezer standing firm, having guarded himself completely, and so Lavan said 'come, blessed of Hashem'.

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech's daughter on the island

retelling.en: Shlomo HaMelech saw that his daughter was destined to marry a poor man, and wanting her to marry someone of her own standing, he built a palace on an island and placed her there with servants and food. Her destined husband, wandering in a cold forest in a torn shirt, crawled into a carcass to keep warm and fell asleep. A great bird carried the carcass to the island and dropped it on the palace ro…

title.en: Cleopatra pairs a thousand slaves

retelling.en: Cleopatra used to call Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya to discuss matters, and once asked what Hashem does since He created the world. He answered that He makes matches, and she said she could do that too. She lined up a thousand men and a thousand women slaves facing each other and had each marry the one opposite. The next morning one had a black eye, another a bloody nose, another needed first aid,…

title.en: Paying the shadchan restores shalom bayis

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he knows of many cases, some personally, where a couple had no shalom bayis and came to a tzaddik. The tzaddik asked whether they had paid the shadchan; they had not, thinking they could have managed without him. They paid the shadchan and the shalom bayis returned.

title.en: Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky's shidduch meeting

retelling.en: Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky told how his shidduch was made: the girl was the daughter of a great Rav, and his mother went to see her and came back with a good report. They arranged to meet in the house of a Rav in a town between the two towns. He sat learning with the host, she came in with a tray of coffee and cake, he glanced and said 'a dank', she answered 'bitte' and walked out, and that was all he…

title.en: Besuel's poison

retelling.en: Besuel wanted to kill Eliezer and take his money, and put poison into his food. A malach exchanged the dishes and Besuel died overnight from his own poison, as Rashi brings. Eliezer had given gifts to Rivka, her brother and her mother but not to Besuel, so that no one could accuse him of the death.

title.en: Eliyahu late to Rebbi's yeshiva

retelling.en: Eliyahu used to come to Rebbi, and once he came late on Rosh Chodesh. He explained that he had to wake the avos in the Me'aras HaMachpelah, wash their hands and let each one daven separately, one after the other. Had all three davened together, Moshiach would have come, but the time had not yet arrived.

title.en: A request to the chassidim in Yerushalayim

retelling.en: At a time of disputes in Yerushalayim over the rabbanus, when Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld was the rav there, someone arrived in Yerushalayim and said a few words to the chassidim. He asked that their place be used for nothing but avodas Hashem: only learning, davening and ahavas chaverim, with no talk of anything else. The elders of Yerushalayim relate that these words lit a fire: fervent davening…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the worm

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov sat learning with his students under a tree on a hot day, when a strong wind suddenly passed and then it was hot again. He said that on a leaf at the top of the tree a worm was suffering from the sun's heat, and Hashem had pity on it and sent a wind that blew it down into the shade. The Mashgiach adds that a change in the weather over miles around was made for one worm.

title.en: Who appreciated Reb Shraga Feivel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that today everyone speaks of Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, founder of the yeshivah, as the great man who saved America for Yiddishkeit. In those days, however, it was the finer bochurim who were drawn to him, going to his talks and to his home on Shabbos to see how a Jew conducts himself. Others did not appreciate him, called him names and made jokes about him.

title.en: The melamed who wanted to study psychology

retelling.en: A very successful melamed asked whether he should study educational psychology to understand children better and become a better teacher. He was answered: why not learn Chumash and Rashi? Whoever learns Chumash and Rashi, and Gemara and the other parts of the Torah, already knows all these things.

title.en: The Kedushas Levi in the kitchen at Mezritch

retelling.en: When the Kedushas Levi came to the Maggid of Mezritch, where the students were very strict about prayer, he put on tallis and tefillin, went into the kitchen and began talking with the Rebbetzin about cooking. The students were upset at this. At the meal they told the Maggid, who said the Kedushas Levi understood his own conduct: tzaddikim can speak what seems like ordinary talk while speaking to…

title.en: A tzaddik's complaint about milk

retelling.en: A tzaddik once went into the kitchen and complained angrily that he was not given a little milk, and the next day that the milk was weak and not nourishing. His disciple, who was present, wondered at such talk. A few minutes later a woman came home who had a baby and no milk, and said she had obtained milk but it was weak. Then the disciple understood that the tzaddik's words had been a prayer fo…

title.en: Cleopatra tries her hand at matchmaking

retelling.en: Queen Cleopatra asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya what Hashem does now that He has made the world, since she did not believe He still guides it. He answered that Hashem makes shidduchim, and she said she could do that too. That evening she lined up five hundred of her male slaves opposite five hundred maidservants and told each to marry the one facing him. The next morning they came with a black…

title.en: The man who invented a proposal for the shadchanus

retelling.en: A tzaddik used to give a small token of shadchanus to anyone who proposed a shidduch, even one that did not go through, since every proposal is a step toward the real one. One man who wanted money picked someone at random and proposed him for the tzaddik's daughter. The tzaddik said no, and when the man asked for payment he answered that this had not even been a real possibility.

title.en: Shmuel HaNavi in the house of Yishai

retelling.en: Hashem sent Shmuel HaNavi to the house of Yishai to anoint one of his sons as king. Shmuel saw a tall, handsome son and thought he was the one, but Hashem said no, and so with each of the six sons. The youngest was out tending the sheep; when he was called, Hashem said this is the one, and David was anointed. The Mashgiach notes that even a navi did not know.

title.en: Miriam bas Bilgah kicks the mizbe'ach

retelling.en: Miriam, from the priestly family of Bilgah, abandoned her faith and married one of the generals of the Greek kings. When the Greeks entered the Beis HaMikdash, she went up to the mizbe'ach and kicked it with her feet. She cried 'lukos, lukos', 'wolf, wolf', accusing it of consuming the wealth of Klal Yisrael without standing by them in their distress.

title.en: The broken promise in Sefer Chassidim

retelling.en: Reuven agreed with Shimon that Shimon would marry his daughter, and Shimon promised, but then married another woman and shamed Reuven's daughter. The Sefer Chassidim says Shimon was not punished for this, because since he married the other woman it had been decreed that she was his. Had he married Reuven's daughter instead, he would have had to die so that he could return to the one decreed for h…

title.en: The daughters of Tzelafchad wait until forty

retelling.en: The daughters of Tzelafchad were orphans whose father had been executed in the desert as the mekoshesh, with no family standing to recommend them. When they reached their twenties and neighbors urged them to lower their demands, they insisted on waiting for a tzaddik like themselves, trusting that Hashem would not give their zivug to another. They waited until forty, and the Gemara tells this in…

title.en: The matron who tried to make matches

retelling.en: A matron asked one of the sages what Hashem does all day, and he answered that He makes shidduchim. She said she could do that too, took a thousand of her servants, and paired them all in one night, telling each one whom to marry. In the morning they were all beaten up, with black eyes and bloody noses. She admitted that only Hashem can make shidduchim.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva wakes his sleeping audience

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Rabbi Akiva was giving a drashah and saw the audience dozing off. To wake them he said something surprising: why did Esther merit to rule over 127 provinces? Because she was a descendant of Sarah, who lived 127 years. Following the Chasam Sofer, the Mashgiach explains that this was not said merely to wake them but carried a message for them.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe and the pot on the stove

retelling.en: Once the Yismach Moshe's wife had to go away, and she told him to take his food himself from the stove where she had prepared it. On the stove there was also a pot of dirty dishwater that had been warmed for washing the dishes. Absorbed in his thoughts, he took that pot and ate from it. When she came back she understood what had happened, while he had noticed nothing.

title.en: The tzaddik in Tzfas and the bottle of brandy

retelling.en: A tzaddik in Tzfas used to learn in depth every motzaei Shabbos at the home of a certain householder, who would bring out a bottle of brandy for a lechayim. One hot night, deep in the sugya and very thirsty, he noticed a bottle and a glass, poured himself a big glass thinking it was water, drank it and went on learning. The householder found the bottle empty and, puzzled, set out another and hid…

title.en: The Slonimer's disciple who could not taste the meat

retelling.en: One of the great disciples of the Slonimer, a rav in a certain town and a very refined Jew, was once served meat and pushed it away, saying he could not taste it. Inquiry showed that the town had a chassidishe and a misnagdishe kehillah, and since the chassidishe shochet was away, the misnagdishe shochet had slaughtered. Asked why, since that shochet was an ehrlicher Jew, a talmid chacham and God…

title.en: The Belzer Rav and his dentist

retelling.en: That week someone from Eretz Yisrael told in the beis medrash that his father, a dentist, treated the Belzer Rav once a week. Understanding that one comes to a holy Jew only after the mikveh, he always went to the mikveh first. Once he could not go and still had to keep the appointment. After the treatment the Belzer Rav asked him why he had not been to the mikveh.

title.en: Reb Shmuel of Karov, the hidden thief

retelling.en: Reb Shmuel of Karov, one of the great disciples of the Lubliner, said about himself that he was born to be a thief, and a thief he is: he can say Tikkun Chatzos in the middle of a fair without anyone knowing. The Mashgiach explains that this is the art of hiding one's good deeds, and that this is what Yitzchak thought Esav was.

title.en: The simple Jew's luminous beard

retelling.en: By the Lechovitcher there was a simple Jew who had not merited to learn great things, and the Lechovitcher said that a great light rests in his beard. The followers investigated and asked the man what this meant. He answered that he cannot learn and knows nothing, so when he wants to remember that he is a Jew he takes hold of his beard and says to Hashem that he does not shave it, and from that h…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's supper of soapy water

retelling.en: The wife of the Yismach Moshe had to go out one evening and asked him to serve himself supper from the pot on the stove. On the same stove stood a dirty pot soaking in soapy water. He warmed the wrong pot and ate the soapy water for supper. When his wife returned and discovered it, it was clear he had not known the difference.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe and the unimmersed plates

retelling.en: On a visit to Yerushalayim the Slonimer Rebbe ate each night at a different chassid's house, and once chose a poor, G-d-fearing man without a beard. When the fish was served the Rebbe did not eat, and asked for a big plate; the host looked at a man with a long beard from whom he had borrowed the plates. The Rebbe asked that man whether the plates were immersed in a mikveh, and he said no, relying…

title.en: The tzaddik's secret chulent ingredient

retelling.en: A great rav spent a Shabbos with a tzaddik about 150 years ago and found the chulent more delicious than any he had eaten. He asked the Rebbetzin for the recipe, but when his wife followed it the chulent was ordinary. The next time he came, the Rebbetzin explained what was missing: every Friday her husband the tzaddik came into the kitchen and threw a handful of beans into the pot himself.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from someone who was there that many years earlier the Mississippi flooded, thousands of miles away. In Radin, a small town, the Chofetz Chaim gave a drashah about it, saying that when people are killed in such a disaster it is a sign that teshuvah is needed. The Mashgiach notes that the Chofetz Chaim was perhaps the only one in Radin who had even heard of the Mississippi.

title.en: Doubts dissolved by words of truth

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls a story he had told before. A man troubled by doubts in emunah came while the davening was in the middle of Mizmor l'Sodah. Hearing the words said there, all his questions were answered and the stones fell from his heart, and he became a complete believer, because they were words of truth.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's supper

retelling.en: When the Yismach Moshe's wife had to go away, she left his supper in a pot on the stove. On returning she found the pot still full, yet he insisted he had eaten. It turned out he had eaten the soapy water left in another pot to soak it clean, without noticing the difference.

title.en: The brandy left on the table in Tzfas

retelling.en: A man in Tzfas used to give a tzaddik a glass of brandy after his long Motzaei Shabbos learning. One hot night the tzaddik was absorbed in a difficult sugya, so the man left the bottle on the table; the thirsty tzaddik took it for water and drank a large glass. This happened again with a second and third bottle, until the man waited and learned what had happened.

title.en: The Berditchever and the pepper

retelling.en: On a cold night the Berditchever Rav came to an inn where the only room was taken by Reb Boruch'l of Mezhibuzh, a calm and orderly tzaddik. Reb Boruch'l agreed to share it only after the Berditchever promised to behave quietly and not jump. All went well until the innkeeper asked the Berditchever whether he loves pepper in his soup; he leapt up crying that he loves the Creator, and the soup spill…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim senses a doubtful dish

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim would not eat a dish over which a halachic question had been asked, even if it was ruled kosher. Once by mistake such a dish was served to him; stirring it with his spoon, he said he sensed it was kosher but that there had been a question about it.

title.en: Meat from a shochet who skipped the mikveh

retelling.en: A chassid, a simple but great disciple, was served meat while visiting another town; he raised it to his mouth and put it back, saying he could not eat it. An inquiry found everything kosher, but the meat came from a different shochet than he was used to. He explained that he knew it was kosher, but meat slaughtered by a shochet who should have gone to the mikveh and did not gives off a bad smell…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's soup

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe, great-grandfather of the Satmar Rav, usually ate his one meal late at night, prepared by the rebbetzin. Once she went to a relative's chasuna and left him a pot of soup and a pot of meat on the oven. When she returned the soup was untouched, yet he said he had eaten it: he had taken from the pot of soapy water she had prepared for washing dishes, and did not know the difference.

title.en: The Levushei Serad and the whiskey

retelling.en: The Levushei Serad, a great posek who lived in Tzfas, learned for hours every motzaei Shabbos, and a Yid who revered him would bring him a flask of whiskey and a small glass to warm him. Once, finding him absorbed in the Gemara, the Yid left the flask on the table. The Levushei Serad, his mouth dry, took it for water, filled a large glass, made a shehakol and drank it, then did so again. The Yid,…

title.en: The cholent made 'lekavod Shabbos kodesh'

retelling.en: A rav who spent a Shabbos with a great rebbe tasted a cholent like none he had eaten before, and asked the rebbetzin for the recipe. At home his wife followed it, but it came out plain. The next time he asked for the secret ingredient, and the rebbetzin told him that every erev Shabbos the rebbe came into the kitchen, dropped a handful of beans into the pot and said 'lekavod Shabbos kodesh'. The…

title.en: His rebbe's chumash class on Yishmael's greatness

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that his rebbe, Reb Mendlowitz, used to learn chumash with the students. When they reached the verse that Yishmael would become great, someone asked when this would happen, since Yishmael had never been great. The Mashgiach says it came about much faster than had been imagined.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya's passing

retelling.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya used to debate the heretics. When he was about to pass away his students asked who would now stand up to them. He answered that if he goes away, they go away too: the heretics were as great as he was, and when he departs they must diminish as well.

title.en: The Konigsberg Rav's letter to Rabbi Yonasan

people: Rabbi Aryeh Leib, the Konigsberg Rav

retelling.en: The Konigsberg Rav, Rabbi Aryeh Leib, wrote to Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz that he lengthened Shacharis on Rosh Hashanah almost until the Torah reading because of the kavanos, and people mocked him; he asked what he should do. Rabbi Yonasan answered that he too prolongs his davening, finishing Shemoneh Esrei when the tzibbur is already at Kedushah or Aleinu, and that even if people mock him, standin…

title.en: Learning all day for a good tefillah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in Yerushalayim he was told, from R' Refael the son of the Brisker Rav, that the Brisker Rav reported his father saying the same words: he learns the whole day so that through it he will merit a good tefillah.

title.en: The man in the public library

retelling.en: Once, needing a rare sefer, the Mashgiach went to the 42nd Street library, which has a large collection of seforim. There he saw a Jew sitting bareheaded at a table studying Maseches Sanhedrin, who had evidently not davened that morning; by the Mashgiach's account, such study is academic, not learning in the true sense.

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim's last erev Shabbos

retelling.en: The story is printed in a sefer of stories bearing the approbation of the Gerrer Rebbe R' Avraham Mordechai. The Chiddushei HaRim used to occupy himself on erev Shabbos with the tikkun of souls that came to him. On his last erev Shabbos he sat alone at the table, and he was heard saying, evidently to a soul, that he could do nothing for it, since the Rebbetzin had already lit candles and it was t…

title.en: The Rebbe who removed the chazzan

retelling.en: In Karlin-Stolin it is told that the previous Rebbe, R' Yochanan, once went up in the middle of davening to the baal tefillah, removed him from the amud and put another in his place, later explaining that a baal tefillah must lift the congregation and this one davened sleepily. The Mashgiach says he saw in a sefer that the same happened with the Sanzer Rav.

title.en: The Levushei Srad and the brandy

retelling.en: The Levushei Srad, who lived in Tzfas, would sit and learn for many hours on motzaei Shabbos, and a householder used to bring him a small glass of brandy. Once, finding him deep in a sugya, the man left the bottle on the table. The Levushei Srad, thirsty and not realizing it was brandy, poured a large glass and drank it, then went on learning; this repeated with a second and third bottle, while t…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's supper

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe's rebbetzin once had to go to a simcha and could not serve him supper, so she told him his supper was in the pot on the stove. There was also a pot of dirty water with soap on it. He took that pot and ate it as his supper. When she returned and asked why he had not eaten, he said he had eaten from the pot, and she realized what he had eaten; he had not noticed at all.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's bed

retelling.en: The Chozeh of Lublin insisted that his furniture be made by upright Jews, since he felt the maker's power in it. Once, when he was to spend Shabbos with a disciple, the disciples had a bed made for him by a pious carpenter, yet he could not sleep all night. When told that a great upright Jew had made it, he said that the man had made it during the Nine Days, and the bed was full of thoughts of sa…

title.en: Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir's cholent

retelling.en: A rav who spent Shabbos with Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir found the cholent delicious and asked the rebbetzin for the recipe for his own wife, but at home it was not the same. The next time he asked what ingredient she had left out. She said she had told him everything, except that every Erev Shabbos her husband the Rebbe comes in, throws in a handful of beans and says 'lekavod Shabbos kodesh'; that i…

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya's last words to his talmidim

retelling.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya used to debate the philosophers of the nations and always came out the victor. When he was about to pass away his talmidim asked who would debate for them now. He answered from the passuk of Esav's words to Yaakov that the opponents exist only opposite him, so when he leaves the scene they too will leave it, and they need not be afraid.

title.en: Esav at the burial of Yaakov

retelling.en: At the burial of Yaakov, Esav came to protest Yaakov's burial in the Me'aras Hamachpelah, claiming that only one place was left and that as the elder it belonged to him. He was killed and his head fell into the cave. The Mashgiach notes that Yaakov had died seventy days earlier, but Esav left the scene only once Yaakov was buried.

title.en: The Apter Rav remembers being Yaakov's sheep

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Apter Rav, the Ohev Yisrael, remembered what happened to him in earlier gilgulim and used to relate them: once a king of Israel, once a nasi, once a wealthy householder in Yerushalayim. He also said he remembered being one of Yaakov Avinu's sheep, and showed a mark on his forehead from a blow of Yaakov's staff. He sang for his chassidim a niggun that Yaakov Avinu had…

title.en: The Arizal at the Alshich's derashah

retelling.en: The Arizal once came to hear a derashah of the Alshich, a great darshan, and sat smiling and delighting in it, with his talmidim beside him. Afterwards they asked why he was so moved, since his own Torah was far higher. He answered that the Alshich had explained Rashi that Lavan deceived Yaakov a hundred times, showing from the pesukim exactly how, and that Lavan had come to hear the derashah; ea…

title.en: Recognizing Torah written with yiras shamayim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a gadol who, as a young man, used to test himself: he would read a piece of Torah in a journal without looking at the author's name and judge whether it was real Torah and whether a yarei shamayim had written it, and only then look at the name. He was never mistaken. When asked about a candidate for a rabbinical post he knew only from such a piece, he could vouch for him as…

title.en: The Baal Shem Tov's parable of the simple worker

retelling.en: From the Toldos Yaakov Yosef in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, the Mashgiach tells of a very simple man who hired himself out to a householder for a year's work for room and board and wages. At the end of each year he asked how much was owed him, and the count came out wrong each time, such as ten and ten making nineteen, yet he kept working in his simplicity.

title.en: The Bnei Yissaschar's account of his youth

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Bnei Yissaschar wrote about himself and his levels. He says that by about the age of nine he no longer saw ordinary things but only holy names. The Mashgiach uses this to show how much greater Yaakov's holiness must have been.

title.en: The Ropshitzer and the Satan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that tzaddikim said that until the last day of the Ropshitzer's life the Satan thought he was an ordinary man. All his life the Ropshitzer led him by the nose, and only on his last day did it become clear that he had been fooled the whole time. The Mashgiach compares this to Lavan, who after fourteen years still did not understand who Yaakov was.

title.en: A chassid's last words: a great yetzer hara

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of one of the great chassidim who was visited by a great tzaddik when he was near his passing, and was asked what he had heard from his Rebbe. Weak, he first kept silent and asked to rest, and then said that his Rebbe had taught that there is a great yetzer hara. The Mashgiach says this is a teaching one must know.

title.en: The tzaddik who remembered Yaakov's niggun

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a tzaddik used to sing a certain niggun and say that he remembered it from when Yaakov Avinu played it on his flute while shepherding his sheep. He said he remembered that he had been a lamb in Yaakov's flock. The Mashgiach brings this to show that Yaakov's sheep were Jewish souls.

title.en: The hole in the pocket

retelling.en: Someone asked a tzaddik why, although Chazal say that one who makes Havdalah on wine will have sons, he made Havdalah on wine every Motzaei Shabbos and had no sons. The tzaddik answered that he does receive the bracha, but there is a hole in his pocket. An aveirah makes a hole, so he cannot hold on to the bracha.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's hesped for his rebbe

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer's rebbe muvhak was Rabbi Nosson Adler. When the news came that he had passed away, the Chasam Sofer delivered a hesped, which is printed among his writings. In it he laments that he was not present at his rebbe's petirah, for one who is present receives a double portion.

title.en: Esav at the Me'aras HaMachpelah

retelling.en: When the shevatim brought Yaakov from Mitzrayim to be buried, Esav came and claimed that the last place in the Me'aras HaMachpelah belonged to him. Chushim ben Dan cut off his head, which rolled into the Me'arah, and the place remained for Yaakov. So Yaakov and Esav were buried on the same day, as Rivka had prophetically feared.

title.en: Two deathbeds on one day

retelling.en: On the day Avraham Avinu passed away, the Shechinah and great tzaddikim came, and all his mitzvos and nisyonos, the milah and the akeidah, gathered to escort him to Gan Eden; Yaakov was there and received a double portion of his kedushah. On the same day, in the forest, Esav met Nimrod as he was dying, and all of Nimrod's sins, from the dor haflagah to throwing Avraham into the furnace, gathered…

title.en: The Baal HaTanya and Napoleon

retelling.en: During Napoleon's war, many hoped he would win, since he promised freedom and Jews suffered under the Russian yoke. The Baal HaTanya, however, prayed and worked with great effort for Russia to win, with mesiras nefesh. He said that if Napoleon won it would be good for Jews materially but bring a great spiritual decline, and he preferred that Jews suffer under the Czar while their spiritual level…

title.en: R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld and the Sanzer Rav

retelling.en: R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld waged a great battle against the new Chief Rabbinate in Jerusalem and did not recognize it, although the world considered its head a fine Jew. As a bochur in Sanz, the Sanzer Rav said of him that he would be king of Jerusalem, and later he became the Rav of Jerusalem. The Mashgiach says that had his way been followed, Jerusalem would have stayed holy as it should be.

title.en: The Skverer Rebbe and Mesechta Mikvaos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he heard, the day before, about the Skverer Rebbe, who was at one time in a certain place and learned through Mesechta Mikvaos with great pleasure. Walking in the street, he said, as one who never spoke idly, that we have such a Ribono shel Olam who gives us such sweet Torah, and on top of that one is rewarded for learning it. To him it was a wonder: what greater pleasure…

title.en: The father who complained about his son

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that someone once called him with a great complaint: why does he not see to it that the man's son, who goes through the yeshivah, has yiras shamayim. The Mashgiach answered that he must indeed try, but the father should make the same claim against himself, since the yeshivah is not the only influence on his son. Other influences, he explains, reach everyone, whether in the sub…

title.en: David, Naval and Avigail

retelling.en: While fleeing from Shaul, David stayed near Naval's fields and guarded his sheep so that nothing happened to them. At shearing time, when everyone made feasts, David asked Naval for food for his men, and Naval refused. David set out to kill Naval, but Avigail, Naval's wife, came out to meet him with food and talked him out of it. Soon after, Naval died, and David thanked Hashem that he had not ki…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembers being Yaakov's lamb

retelling.en: The Mashgiach calls it a well-known story that the Yismach Moshe said he remembered being a lamb with Yaakov Avinu. He showed a mark on his shoulder that he had received from a blow of Yaakov's staff.

title.en: The Ohev Yisrael's niggun

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions a niggun of the Ohev Yisrael. The Ohev Yisrael said he remembered that Yaakov Avinu played it on his flute among the sheep when he himself was a lamb there.

title.en: The tzaddik who saw an ox on the stairs

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he does not remember exactly which great tzaddik it was. The head of the community came up to see him, and the tzaddik asked who the ox was that was climbing the stairs. He looked with inner sight and saw no tzelem Elokim, only an animal.

title.en: The Lechovitcher's silence on Vayeitzei

retelling.en: The Lechovitcher, Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch, did not say any Torah to his students on Parshas Vayeitzei. He said he found it unnecessary: the parsha itself shows Yaakov in Lavan's impure surroundings, raising twelve children and amassing wealth, and growing as a tzaddik there. One need only learn the parsha and try to emulate Yaakov.

title.en: The Shechinah at the Kosel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that tzaddikim, not so long ago, saw on the night of Tisha B'Av at the Kosel HaMaaravi a beautiful woman clad in black, and that was the Shechinah. Such an appearance, he says, does not arouse earthly temptation but stirs heavenly emotions.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembers his past lives

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe remembered his earlier times in this world, and told his grandson, the Yitav Lev, that he had been present at the dispute of Korach and had stayed neutral. When the grandson wondered that he had not sided with Moshe, he answered that had the grandson been there, he would have sided with Korach. He also remembered being a little sheep of Yaakov Avinu, and showed a mark on his bac…

title.en: The Apter Rav and Yaakov's tune

retelling.en: The Apter Rav, the Ohev Yisrael, who lived a little before the Yismach Moshe, also told what he remembered from earlier lives, among them being a Kohen Gadol. He remembered being a sheep of Yaakov Avinu, and even the tune Yaakov played on his flute to gather the sheep; he sang it for his talmidim. The Mashgiach says he knows that tune and it is sung to 'Amar Hashem l'Yaakov'.

title.en: The ox coming up the stairs

retelling.en: A great tzaddik who was a Rav was visited by the president of the shul. As the man came up the stairs, the tzaddik called out to his wife in the kitchen that an ox was coming up the stairs, because he saw him in the image of an ox, which, the Mashgiach says, he really was.

title.en: The soul that came to the Kozhnitzer Maggid

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions, among the stories of souls that came to tzaddikim for a tikkun, the soul of the one who threw the first stone at the prophet Zecharyah. It had wandered for a very long time without a tikkun until it came to Rabbi Yisrael of Kozhnitz.

title.en: The Chernobyler and the coin

retelling.en: The Chernobyler was once traveling when the horses stopped and could not go on. He took a coin and threw it back onto the road, and the horses went on. He explained that a great rasha had once given him a coin, and so had attached himself to him; but seeing he could not repair him, he gave the coin back, so that he received nothing from him and was not bound to help him.

title.en: Asnas and the amulet

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a Midrash brought by Rabbeinu Bachya: a daughter was born to Dinah from Shechem, and Yaakov took her to the desert, hid her in a bush, and hung on her neck an amulet whose writing said she was of Yaakov's family, the daughter of Dinah. The angel Michael carried her to Egypt, where Potiphar's wife, who had no children, raised her as her own daughter. When Yosef rode out, the gi…

title.en: The villager on Rosh Hashanah

retelling.en: A simple villager came to shul on Rosh Hashanah, and at the Shemoneh Esrei of Shacharis everyone began to cry. He wondered why, and decided they must be hungry because it was late, so he cried along with them. Then he remembered that at home his wife had put a piece of dried meat into the tzimmes, which gets better the longer it cooks, and he consoled himself that it was worth waiting. When the p…

title.en: The animals' trial during a plague

retelling.en: During a plague in the jungle, the animals gathered to find which sinner had caused it, with the lion, the bear and the tiger as judges. One witness told of a leopard that ate a child, and another of a wolf that snatched a chicken; the judges excused both, since that is their nature. A third told of a sheep that ate the straw a poor shepherd had stuffed into a hole in his shoe, and the judges dec…

title.en: Lavan's soul at the Alshich's drasha

retelling.en: The Alshich used to give a drasha every Shabbos for the townspeople of Tzfas, and once the Arizal came to his drasha on Parshas Vayeitzei and smiled throughout. His talmidim wondered why, since the Arizal was far greater than the Alshich. The Arizal explained that Lavan's soul had come to the drasha, and each time the Alshich showed from the pesukim another of Lavan's hundred tricks against Yaako…

title.en: Dama ben Nesina and the precious stone

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara's story of Dama ben Nesina, a gentile of Ashkelon, who could have sold a stone and earned six hundred thousand, but his father was sleeping. Tosafos brings from the Yerushalmi that the father's foot was on the box, so he could not open it, and he did not wake his father. Later a red heifer was born in his herd, the Jews needed it, and he regained the money by sellin…

title.en: Avimi waits over his sleeping father

retelling.en: Avimi was very careful in kibud av and would rise as soon as he heard his father's voice. Once his father asked for water, and when Avimi brought it his father had fallen asleep. Avimi stood bent over him with the water in his hand the whole time, not leaving in case his father woke and needed him. While standing so, the meaning of 'Mizmor l'Asaf' was revealed to him.

title.en: The child who would not go to cheder

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Rebbe who as a small child wanted to sleep in the morning and not go to cheder. His father, distressed, pointed out the window at the gentile children already going to school and asked whether he was not ashamed before them. The child answered that the same Satan who pushes them to go to school tells him to stay in bed.

title.en: The Mashgiach's childhood question on Dama ben Nesina

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls learning Kiddushin as a child and coming to the story of Dama ben Nesina. He felt something was not in order: had he done the same, his father would have woken, found out, and grieved all week that his child could have earned six hundred thousand. Now, with a white beard, he says he understands better that something was indeed wrong with Dama ben Nesina's kibud av.

title.en: Elifaz and his father's command

retelling.en: When Yaakov fled, Elifaz came after him, sent by Esav. Elifaz had been raised near Yitzchak and was reluctant, so he asked Yaakov what he should do with his father's command, since he was obligated in kibud av. The Mashgiach contrasts this with a Jew, who knows that when a father commands a sin, one does not obey.

title.en: The Maggid touches the Ba'al Shem Tov's kittel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, as received from the Ruzhiner, that once the Ba'al Shem Tov left his kittel for a few minutes. The Maggid of Mezritch saw it was not lying properly and went to straighten it. When he touched it, he was seized with such trembling from fear of Heaven that he grabbed a shtender, which shook with him, and he had to be put to bed. The Mashgiach uses it to show how much greater t…

title.en: Potiphar hears Yosef's whispered prayer

retelling.en: Following the Midrash, the Mashgiach tells that whatever Potiphar asked of Yosef succeeded in his hands: if he wanted hot water it was hot, and if cold, it was cold. Potiphar suspected Yosef of witchcraft because he was always murmuring to himself, and asked what he was saying. Listening closely, he heard that Yosef was constantly praying to Hashem and declaring his trust in Him.

title.en: A tzaddik's Nittel-night custom

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of an earlier tzaddik: on Nittel night he did not learn, but instead tore the paper he would need for the whole year, although others could easily have done it for him. The Mashgiach says he wanted to do it himself precisely at that time, and hints that there is inner meaning in it which he does not explain.

title.en: The mezuzah checker in Yerushalayim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story he heard in Yerushalayim from his mechutan: a man there checks mezuzos once a week, and people from all over Eretz Yisrael bring theirs, because from a mezuzah he can tell what is happening with the person. A son once brought his father's mezuzos, and the checker asked if he was a melamed. The son said no, but his father was, a top melamed in the Etz Chaim yeshiva who…

title.en: Osnas, Dinah's daughter, and the amulet

retelling.en: According to the Midrash the Mashgiach relates, Dinah had a daughter from Shechem, and the brothers wanted to kill her for the family's shame. Yaakov named her Osnas, placed her in a thornbush in the desert and hung on her an amulet saying she was of Yaakov's family. The angel Michael brought her to Egypt, where Potiphar, who could have no children, adopted her. When Yosef rode through Egypt the…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's mark from Yaakov's stick

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Yismach Moshe, whom he identifies as an ancestor of the Satmar Rav, showed a mark on his shoulder. He said he remembered when he was a sheep with Yaakov Avinu, and Yaakov once gave him a small tap on the shoulder with a stick, and the mark remained.

title.en: The niggun Yaakov played for his sheep

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that a Rebbe sang a niggun for his chassidim and said that Yaakov Avinu had played this niggun on his flute for them when they were sheep with him. He remembered it, the Mashgiach explains, because tzaddikim remember what happened to them before. The Mashgiach adds that this niggun is known today and that he knows it.

title.en: The menorah that burned a year without oil

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Midrash Tanchuma that Rabbi Chanina Segan HaKohanim told of a time when there was no oil for the menorah in the Beis HaMikdash. The kohanim wept that they would not be able to light it. A miracle happened and the menorah burned and did not go out, for about a year, and the kohanim rejoiced. Rabbi Chanina said he saw it with his own eyes.

title.en: The wise man and Alexander

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that when Alexander came back from war, a wise man told him that the greatest war he had not yet won, the war against the yetzer hara.

title.en: Asenath and the amulet

retelling.en: According to Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer as the Mashgiach tells it, Dinah had a daughter from Shechem, and the brothers wanted to harm her. Yaakov wrote on an amulet that she was of his children, placed her in a thornbush, and she was carried to Egypt and given to Potiphar's wife, who had no children and adopted her. When Yosef rode through Egypt and the girls threw ornaments to make him look, Asenath…

title.en: The Lubliner and the informer

retelling.en: In a certain town an informer caused many troubles, informing on Jews to the government. Disciples of the Rebbe of Lublin wrote a kvittel with his name and gave it to the Rebbe, who looked at it and spoke of a light; they wondered how this could be said of such a wicked man. When they asked, the Lubliner explained that at the moment they handed him the kvittel the man was lighting Chanukah candle…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the hunter's birds

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai hid in a cave for thirteen years from the Roman king. When he came out he saw a hunter catching birds and heard a heavenly voice announce for each bird whether it would be caught. He concluded that if a bird is not caught without a decree from Hashem, he would certainly not be caught by the king of Rome without one, and he went out.

title.en: The donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair

retelling.en: At an inn, the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair refused to eat the oats it was served. When the innkeeper complained, Rabbi Pinchas asked whether the tithe had been taken; once it was, the donkey ate. The Mashgiach notes that a donkey may eat untithed food, especially where the obligation was only a doubt, but this donkey held sparks of its master's soul and would not transgress.

title.en: Eliyahu's two oxen

retelling.en: At Eliyahu's contest with the worshippers of the Baal, two oxen were prepared, one for Hashem and one for the Baal. The ox chosen for the Baal refused to move, arguing that it and its companion had eaten from the same trough. Eliyahu told it that by being offered to the Baal, with no fire descending, it too would sanctify Hashem's name by proving the negative, and the ox agreed to go.

title.en: Rabbi Hoshaya and the unlearned man

retelling.en: An unlearned man asked Rabbi Hoshaya whether he would repeat a chiddush of his in his name, and Rabbi Hoshaya said he would if it was fitting for the congregation. The man explained that the verse in Tehillim says the kings will 'return' a gift to Moshiach because Esav still holds Yaakov's gift and will have to give it back. Rabbi Hoshaya praised it and repeated it in his name, and it entered the…

title.en: Osnas and Yosef in Shechem

retelling.en: Dina bore a daughter to Shechem, and the brothers wanted to kill her. According to the Midrash, Yaakov carried her to the desert and placed her on a thorn bush, which is where her name came from, and the angel Gavriel carried her to Mitzrayim. She became Osnas, who married Yosef; Yosef was given Shechem and is buried there with his two sons at his sides.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the passing of the Or HaChaim

retelling.en: Something happened to the Ba'al Shem Tov at shalosh seudos, and those around him thought he had passed away. Later it was learned that at that very time the Or HaChaim HaKadosh had passed away in Eretz Yisroel. The Mashgiach explains that a certain level is given to only one tzaddik in a generation, and once the Or HaChaim passed away it was handed over to the Ba'al Shem Tov.

title.en: Chassidim before the Chozeh of Lublin

retelling.en: The Imrei Emes brings a story he heard from his father about the Chozeh of Lublin. Chassidim came to the Chozeh about a certain town and brought a kvittel, and the Chozeh looked into it and responded.

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the frozen river

retelling.en: Timber merchants in the days of Rabbi Sholom of Belz cut logs in the forests, bound them and floated them down the river to the lumber mills when the river opened at Nissan time. One year it was already spring time but the river was still frozen, and they had a contract to deliver the logs by a set day, so they feared a great loss. They came to the Belzer Rav, who asked which parsha the children…

title.en: The angel turns Yehuda from his way

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Midrash that as Yehuda walked on, the angel appointed over desire came to him and asked where he was going, saying that kings and redeemers, and Moshiach, must come from somewhere. Yehuda was turned aside against his will, not knowing the woman was Tamar. The Mashgiach explains that Yehuda's desire was a holy one for Moshiach, and his yetzer was a holy angel that compell…

title.en: Pinchas and Kozbi

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes how the tribes at Shittim, believing they could bring Moshiach through Bnos Moav, were met by Midianite women in disguise. Pinchas came and killed Kozbi, and although ten miracles happened to him, the tribes mocked him as a descendant of one who fattened calves for idolatry, holding that he lacked their lofty understanding and their readiness for mesirus nefesh.

title.en: Shammai and Hillel with the would-be converts

retelling.en: A non-Jew came to Shammai asking to be converted on condition that he be taught the whole Torah while standing on one leg, and Shammai pushed him out with his builder's ruler. Hillel accepted him, was warm to him, and taught him how to come close to Hashem. Another came wanting to convert on condition that he become kohen gadol; Shammai again drove him out, while Hillel drew him close and little…

title.en: The Yesod HaAvodah and the chassid with a good friend

retelling.en: A chassid came to the Yesod HaAvodah after a long time away, and the Rebbe asked whether he had a good friend in his town to strengthen himself with; he said he had a chassidishe friend with whom he spoke words of chizuk. Another chassid who had just been there said he had no such friend. The Rebbe explained that the first still carried the freshness of avodas Hashem in his soul, while the second…

title.en: The Lentshner's wife and her kvittel

retelling.en: During the bitter dispute in which Reb Naftali of Ropshitz pursued Reb Shlomo Leib of Lentshna, the Lentshner's wife traveled to a great tzaddik with a kvittel and a pidyon, asking that her husband have yiras shamayim. The tzaddik, reading the kvittel, said her husband lights up the world with his Torah and avodah, and she asked why then the Ropshitzer attacks him. He answered that the Ropshitzer…

title.en: The bris that did not wait for the Lentshner

retelling.en: In the time of the dispute, a family honored the Lentshner with a bris, and he came late as was his way. A great talmid of the Ropshitzer, of whom it was said he had ruach hakodesh, wanted to stand with his Rebbe's dispute, took the knife and did the milah himself, saying one should not wait. He then hurried to Ropshitz so that the Rebbe would protect him; the Rebbe gave him an instruction to sta…

title.en: Reb Baruch'l and the Kedushas Levi

retelling.en: Reb Baruch'l used to speak harshly against the Kedushas Levi, yet when the Kedushas Levi passed away he wept and lamented that the glory of Israel was gone. Asked why he had always knocked him, he answered that the Kedushas Levi was so great that the Satan argued before the Heavenly Throne that there was no need for a Beis HaMikdash and Moshiach, since his avodah was enough; so he lowered his sta…

title.en: The talmid of Lechovitch who would not eat the meat

retelling.en: A talmid of the Lechovitcher, a man of great madreigah, came to a town and was served meat, but would not eat it. When asked why, since the shochet was an erliche Yid and a talmid chacham, he said the meat was kosher by halachah, but he sensed that the shochet should have gone to the mikveh and had not. The Mashgiach explains that this was the takanah of Ezra, which halachah no longer requires, y…

title.en: The Vaitzener Rav bangs on the table

retelling.en: The Vaitzener Rav, Reb Yeshaya Silberstein, a great and holy man, knew nothing of secular learning, not even the ABC. At a gathering of rabbanim, after something was said, he stood up and banged on the table, declaring he valued a Jew who does not know the ABC. The Mashgiach says people laugh at this because they do not feel the pegam, but he felt it with a fine sensitivity that we lack.

title.en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe and the chocolates

retelling.en: When a Lubavitcher Rebbe arrived in Germany, he was offered chocolates and said that he had not seen this by his fathers and did not eat this food. People made fun of him, but the Mashgiach says they did not grasp his point: a Jew must not only dress, speak and be named in a Jewish way, he must also eat Jewish food.

title.en: The Yesod HaAvodah brings good news at night

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story handed down among the chassidim of Yerushalayim. In the middle of the night the Yesod HaAvodah, whose legs were ailing, climbed up to his grandson, the Divrei Shmuel, and knocked to tell him that a certain Jew's cow, on which his livelihood depended, had been sick and now felt better. The grandson asked why he had climbed up with his sick legs instead of waiting until…

title.en: Asnas and the charm

retelling.en: Dinah had a baby girl fathered by Shechem, and the brothers were angry and wanted to harm her. Yaakov took the baby, hung a charm around her neck on which he wrote that she was from the family of Yaakov and signed his name, and set her down on a thorn bush. The angel Gavriel brought her to Mitzrayim to the childless house of Potiphar, who adopted her. Years later, when girls on the rooftops threw…

title.en: A woman asks the Mashgiach about world events

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a woman who had asked him two years earlier for his explanation of the Twin Towers, and had printed it in a book that became a bestseller, called again that week.
