She wanted his explanation of why the Arabs were being roused to such terror now. He told her his explanation and left it to her whether to print it.

title.en: Yehudis and the decree

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Midrashim that the Greeks decreed against Jewish brides before their weddings. Yehudis, daughter of Yochanan Kohen Gadol, fed the king dairy, put him to sleep, and cut off his head, and the decree was annulled.

title.en: Reb Mendel of Vitebsk and the souls of chutz la'aretz

retelling.en: After the Maggid passed away there was a call to travel to Eretz Yisrael. Reb Mendel of Vitebsk traveled with Reb Avraham of Kalisk, and wrote a letter explaining that some souls are connected to Eretz Yisrael and some to chutz la'aretz. The Mashgiach adds that the Baal HaTanya also wanted to go, and it was revealed to him from heaven that he must stay in chutz la'aretz and reveal Hashem's kingsh…

title.en: Learning mishnayos for his own soul

retelling.en: Someone was found learning mishnayos and was asked for which deceased person he was learning. He answered that he was learning for his own soul: why wait until others learn mishnayos for him, when he can repair his soul now.

title.en: The Slonimer chassid's seven jokes

retelling.en: One of the great Slonimer chassidim, an old and sick man, once had to walk a long, hard, uphill journey for a mitzvah, a matter of many hours. When he arrived he was asked how he managed it, and he said he did it with seven jokes. He divided the way into seven parts between towns: an hour and a half to the next town is nothing, a joke; two hours to the one after, also a joke; and so he arrived wi…

title.en: The Baal Shem Tov and the poritz

retelling.en: The Baal Shem Tov once had to visit a poritz and took along his grandson, Reb Baruch'l. The poritz complained of an illness, and the Baal Shem Tov told him it came from desires; the poritz asked whether the Rebbe had no desires himself. Afterwards Reb Baruch'l asked why he had not simply answered that a Jew fears the Ribono shel Olam and keeps the Torah. The Baal Shem Tov answered: go explain to…

title.en: Reb Elimelech's body found whole

retelling.en: The Mashgiach knew a Jew who lived in Skver and was one of ten Jews the Germans forced to dig up the grave of Reb Elimelech at the Lizhensk cemetery. They dug while the Germans watched. Though Reb Elimelech had been buried well over a hundred years, perhaps a hundred and fifty, they found his body completely whole. When the Germans saw it they ran off, and the grave was covered again.

title.en: The Kotzker and Reb Meir of Apta on the ushpizin

retelling.en: The Kotzker had a great dispute with other tzaddikim over his new path. One of them, Reb Meir of Apta, sent a messenger asking whether he dared dispute with someone who sees the seven ushpizin come into his sukkah. The Kotzker answered that he dared, because he believes the ushpizin come into his sukkah, and believing is greater than seeing.

title.en: The Chafetz Chaim and the man going to Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he may have told this before. A man came to take leave of the Chafetz Chaim before going to Eretz Yisrael and worried about the Arabs who make pogroms there. The Chafetz Chaim agreed it was a great problem and said they cannot help it: the Torah calls Yishmael a 'pere adam', and whatever such a person becomes, doctor, lawyer, banker or professor, he remains a pere adam.

title.en: Serach tells Yaakov that Yosef is alive

retelling.en: Following the Medrash, the Mashgiach tells that the Shevatim were afraid to tell the aged Yaakov that Yosef was alive, lest the shock harm him. Serach, Asher's young daughter whom Yaakov loved and who was known to be bright, offered to do it. She came playing an instrument and singing 'Od Yosef chai' until Yaakov brightened, and then the Shevatim came in and told him, and he believed. Yaakov bles…

title.en: Rav Savitsky's report from Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rav Savitsky had just returned from Eretz Yisrael, where he spent Chanukah. Asked what was new there, he answered that the situation is beyond nature: by natural means there is no other way out, and Moshiach must come now.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what he heard from people who were present many years earlier. When the Mississippi River overflowed, thousands of miles away, the Chofetz Chaim spoke about it in his yeshiva and cried out over the middas hadin coming onto the world. Most of his listeners did not even know there was such a river, yet he saw in it a sign.

title.en: The tzaddik who leapt from the mikveh

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who kept a piece of wood by his bed to tie Moshiach's donkey, and told his gabbai to wake him if Moshiach came in the middle of the night. Once, on a Shabbos, while he was in the mikveh, the gabbai ran in and said 'he is here', meaning his beloved son who had come to visit. The tzaddik leapt out of the mikveh, threw on his clothes and ran to the house, for he thou…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim sitting outside

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that in his last years the Chofetz Chaim used to sit outside on a chair. When asked why he sat there, the answer was that he was waiting for Moshiach.

title.en: The brandy seller who took Hashem as a partner

retelling.en: A simple Jew who sold brandy to gentiles became known because all his blessings were fulfilled. The Apter Rav visited him and asked where the power of his blessings came from. The man told that when his business failed, his wife pressed him to find a partner with capital; instead he took Ribono shel Olam as his partner, made two boxes, and put half of every sale in Hashem's box for tzedakah. Sinc…

title.en: Forced secular study does not harm

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from a grandson of the Chofetz Chaim that the Chofetz Chaim strongly opposed secular studies. When a government decree forced Jewish children to learn secular subjects a couple of hours a day, he was asked what would become of them, and he answered that what is done under compulsion does not harm, because the one who is forced has special protection.

title.en: Bread in the garbage can

retelling.en: Decades earlier in America it was very hard to find work without desecrating Shabbos. One Jew went from shop to shop and was told everywhere that without coming on Saturday he would not get the job. He considered whether to give in, but resolved that as long as he could find bread in a garbage can he would not work on Shabbos.

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim on naming a child

retelling.en: A chassid who had a child asked the Chiddushei HaRim what name to give. The Chiddushei HaRim answered: when else does a person have a chance at ruach hakodesh, if not when he gives a name? Why should he give away that opportunity?

title.en: The Tiferes Shlomo and the forgotten name

people: the Tiferes Shlomo (Rabbi Shlomo of Radomsk)

retelling.en: A chassid going to the Tiferes Shlomo, Rabbi Shlomo of Radomsk, for Shabbos was asked by a friend to mention a sick relative with his mother's name, but he forgot the names. The Tiferes Shlomo asked whether the sick man was called Yaakov and his mother Chana, and the chassid remembered that it was so. When the chassid spoke of ruach hakodesh, the Tiferes Shlomo said he had none, but he has a sefe…

title.en: The tzaddik on the train going the wrong way

retelling.en: A great tzaddik and illui, whom Rav Chaim Ozer called a true illui, had to travel with a friend on a three-day train journey in Russia. At the last stop they realized they had taken the train going east instead of west, far in the opposite direction. The friend was beside himself, but the tzaddik was calm and explained that everything is by hashgacha pratis: perhaps he needed to make a brachah on…

title.en: The Rebbe Reb Elimelech found intact

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he personally knew a Jew who lived in Skver and who saw the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. The Nazis ordered the graves of Lizhensk removed, but whenever they came to the Rebbe's grave something happened and they could not move it, so they had ten Jews do it, and this Jew was one of them. When they opened the grave of the Rebbe Reb Elimelech, who had passed away close to two hundred year…

title.en: The Stoliner signature that stayed black

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he has at home a letter written some sixty years earlier by the gabbai of Rabbi Yisroel of Stolin, the Yenuka, and signed by the Rebbe himself. Writing ink turns brown after about thirty years, and indeed the whole letter has turned brown, but the tzaddik's signature is black and fresh as if written today.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe at the Rebbe Reb Elimelech's kever

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe once came to daven at the kever of the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. He announced at the cemetery that he would give a perutah to tzedakah for the merit of any neshama that would go tell the Rebbe Reb Elimelech that he had come, in case the Rebbe was not at his kever. The Mashgiach adds that whether or not the neshama was there, a trace of life always remains at the kever.

title.en: The lion, the donkey and the fox

retelling.en: The Midrash tells that the lion, king of the animals, was walking with his attendants and came to a bridge where the donkey collected the toll. The donkey demanded that the king pay, and the lion, insisting that all the tolls belong to him, tore the donkey to pieces and continued on his walk, leaving the fox to prepare it as a meal. When the lion returned he found the heart missing, because the f…

title.en: Rebbi and Nevuchadnetzar

retelling.en: Rebbi was asked about Nevuchadnetzar and would not curse him, since one may not curse a king. When he read the sefer and reached Nevuchadnetzar king of Bavel, he cursed him, and when asked he answered that in the sefer one may curse him. The Mashgiach explains that one who reads Yirmiyahu lives in that time.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the student on the sechach

retelling.en: Two students came to the Chasam Sofer after Sukkos to be accepted to his yeshivah and were told to return the next day. Meanwhile they helped take down the Rebbe's sukkah while he watched from the window. He accepted one and not the other, and later explained that one had been careful not to step on the sechach while the other stepped on it, and a bochur who treads on sechach on which the Shechin…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's prayer on the road

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe once davened mincha at a place on a journey and felt a fire of hislahavus he had never felt before, and said a great tzaddik must have davened there. It was found that Rebbe Reb Elimelech had passed through and davened at that spot.

title.en: The Mashgiach's visit to the chatzar hamatarah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that about ten years earlier he was in the chatzar hamatarah, a place hewn in stone and very cool even in the heat outside, where the Arabs stored their bananas so they would not spoil. From the pasuk he shows that it was part of the king's house that Shlomo built.

title.en: The frog and David HaMelech

retelling.en: When David HaMelech finished Sefer Tehillim he said before Hashem: is there any creature in Your world that sings more than I do? A frog came toward him and told him not to be proud, for it sings more than he does.

title.en: Rabbi Yeshaya's 85 fasts

retelling.en: Rabbi Yeshaya, a disciple of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, fasted 85 fasts so that it would be revealed to him from heaven why dogs, of whom it is said that they are brazen and never satisfied, merit to say song. He was answered from heaven that it is because in Egypt no dog moved its tongue.

title.en: Rabbi Chatzkel of Kuzmir on fasting

retelling.en: Someone came to Rabbi Chatzkel of Kuzmir and asked how many fasts he should take. He answered that it was not enough that the aveiros had already cut away at his body; he wanted to cut away more? One must be healthy and strong and serve Hashem.

title.en: The survivor in Detroit called 'crazy frum'

retelling.en: A Jew the Mashgiach knows came from Europe after the war to a relative in Detroit, who found him a job. When Shabbos morning came he stayed home and said Tehillim. His uncle asked why he was not going to work, and when he answered that it was Shabbos, the uncle called him 'meshugah frum'.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's body after sixteen months

retelling.en: The Stoliner Rebbe, Rabbi Yochanan, at whose shul the Mashgiach davened in Williamsburg, died of diabetes and was buried near New York. After a long dispute a beis din ruled that he had wished to be buried in Eretz Yisrael. When he was disinterred after sixteen months, his body was intact with pink skin and his shrouds pure white, as many people saw. The standard sealed casket would not fit into…

title.en: The Nazis open the Rebbe Reb Elimelech's grave

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: A refugee from Lizhensk, later one of the men the Skverer Rebbe supported to learn all day, told the Mashgiach what he saw. The Nazis came to the cemetery to unearth the Rebbe Reb Elimelech but could not, so they forced ten Jews, among them this man, to dig. When the coffin was opened, after some 150 years, the Rebbe lay intact as he had been buried; the Nazis fled and the Jews covered the grave…

title.en: The Rebbe's signature that did not fade

retelling.en: The Mashgiach has a letter, some seventy or eighty years old, written by a gabbai and signed by the Stoliner Rebbe's father. The gabbai's writing has turned brown with age, while the Rebbe's signature remained black as if just written, and the Mashgiach offers to show it.

title.en: Erev Shabbos in Rebbe Reb Elimelech's town

retelling.en: Elderly tzaddikim who had served Rebbe Reb Elimelech in their youth were asked what they remembered of him. They told that during the week the people of the town quarreled and fought with one another. But when erev Shabbos came at midday, a great yiras shamayim suddenly came down on the whole town, and those who had fought all week began asking each other forgiveness as a preparation for Shabbos.

title.en: Reb Chaim Ozer's advice to a sick man

retelling.en: A man was ill in his lungs and the doctors had given up on him. He came to Reb Chaim Ozer, who advised him to settle in Eretz Yisrael. The Mashgiach explains the reasoning: his illness was a treifah according to the Rema but not according to the Beis Yosef, and in Eretz Yisrael, where the ruling follows the Beis Yosef, nature would follow that ruling.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's fruit

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what is said of the Ohr HaChaim, that he had no children because he put all his power of bearing children into his holy sefer on the Chumash. The Mashgiach calls this a fine spiritual kind of fruit.

title.en: The general who must not lose courage

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a story from a letter of the Yesod HaAvodah to his chassidim. A general received a dispatch that a great fortress had fallen to the enemy, and he was deeply distressed. When asked what happened, he told of the bad news, and was answered that there was worse news: that he had lost his courage. The Mashgiach concludes that a Jew must never lose his courage.

title.en: Yosef and the women on the rooftops

retelling.en: Following the Midrash, the Mashgiach tells that when Yosef went out as the king's viceroy, the girls climbed onto the rooftops and threw down trinkets and jewelry so that he would look up at them. Yosef did not look; he looked at the wall. This, the Mashgiach says, is how the Alshich explains 'ben poras Yosef'.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and his son's question

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer's son asked him a strong question in learning, and his father did not answer. Later the father gave him an answer and told him that he had had it all along, but he wanted him to become used to living for a while with a question unanswered.

title.en: The Maggid sends a man to Reb Zusha

retelling.en: A man came to the Maggid complaining that things were bad for him and asked how one can strengthen oneself. The Maggid sent him to the beis medrash to ask Reb Zusha. Reb Zusha answered that he did not know why the Rebbe had sent him, since nothing was lacking to him.

title.en: A wealthy man boasts before the Kotzker

retelling.en: A man who had become wealthy and left avodas Hashem boasted before the Kotzker Rebbe of his comfortable life and his possessions. The Kotzker answered him that such a this-world is not what counts, pointing him to the World to Come.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov knocks and walks on

retelling.en: Before he was revealed, the Ba'al Shem Tov was once hungry, knocked on a door and walked on. When the owner opened and saw him far away, he called after him and asked why he had not waited. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that his teacher had told him one must do something for parnassah, so he knocked, but he did not need to wait for the man, since it is not he who provides.

title.en: Rabbi Yisrael Salanter's watch

retelling.en: In a discussion in Vilna about how strong one's bitachon must be, Rabbi Yisrael Salanter gave the example that he had lost his watch and needed one. While they were speaking a Jewish soldier came in from the war: a fatally wounded comrade had given him a gold watch, asking that it be brought to the Rav of Vilna to give to a Jewish talmid chacham, and the watch reached Rabbi Yisrael.

title.en: Running for the bus

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the day before he had run after a bus, fearing he would be late as had happened the previous day, slipped and fell hard. He applied to himself Koheles' words that the race is not to the swift.

title.en: The man who kept his load on his shoulder

retelling.en: A man was walking with a heavy box of scrap, and a wagon owner offered him a ride. He climbed onto the wagon but kept holding the box on his shoulder, saying he did not want to make it heavy for the horses. The owner told him the horses carry it anyway, so he may as well put it down on the wagon.

title.en: Yosef flees his test

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes Yosef as a seventeen-year-old torn from home, the only Jew in an immoral city, pressed every day for a whole year. A person is not made of iron, and there is a point beyond which he cannot hold out. When Yosef reached that point, Hashem held him back, and he fled outside, leaving his garment, accepting the shame that followed rather than lose his free choice.

title.en: The tzaddik who could not sleep

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Rav who had a rule never to leave anything over in his house overnight. Once he could not fall asleep and understood that something had been left. The household searched until they found a coin, which was taken to a poor man, and then he could sleep.

title.en: The gematria of 'radish'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, as he had told before, of a chassid from Poland who visited a Rebbe in Galicia and heard him give a gematria for 'radish', the Galician name for the round Rosh Hashanah challah. He laughed, since in Poland it is not called that. When he returned, his own Rebbe asked him about the tefillin he had put on that day, and pointed to the Gemara that explains the word for tefillin fr…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer waits three days to answer

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer's son came to him with a deep question touching on matters of emunah, and his father gave no answer. Three days later he called him and gave a wonderful answer. He told his son that he could have answered three days earlier, but he wanted him to learn that one can go around for three days with a kashya and still believe in the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin declines to choose a name

retelling.en: A chassid asked the Chozeh of Lublin what name to give his child. The Chozeh answered that a father names his child with heavenly inspiration, giving the name the soul received on coming down. If he chose the name himself, he said, he would deprive the father of that ruach hakodesh.

title.en: The Radomsker finds the names in Sefer Shemos

retelling.en: A sick townsman asked someone going to Rabbi Shlomo of Radomsk to mention his name. The messenger could not recall the man's name or his mother's, and the Rebbe suggested Yaakov and Chanah, which proved correct. Asked how he knew, the Rebbe said it was not ruach hakodesh: in Sefer Shemos, the book of names, are the names of all Jews, and he glanced through it and found them. The Mashgiach adds th…

title.en: Calling a patient by name in the hospital

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he saw in a hospital an unconscious patient whose doctors wanted to know whether the coma was full or partial. They did not shake him or ask how he felt; they shouted his name, because a person responds to his name, since he responds through his neshama.

title.en: Rabbi Meir and the man named Kidor

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites the Gemara's story that Rabbi Meir, hearing a man's name, Kidor, knew he was wicked, since it was not a holy name, and that one must beware of him. Rabbi Meir was proven right.

title.en: The boys who went to the movies

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a boy his father never let him go to the movies, though all the boys in his class went, and he is very thankful for it. The boys would tell what they saw, with good guys and bad guys shooting at each other, and he uses this to ask whether a Shimon belongs with the good guys or the bad.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's second plate of cholent

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what R' Nosson Wachtfogel told: the Stoliner Rebbe in Williamsburg never said Torah at the table, only plain talk in which those who understood heard hints. Once at the Shabbos kiddush, where cholent was served, he spoke at length about cholent, citing Rishonim and the Beis Yosef, to everyone's surprise. He gave R' Nosson a plate of cholent and then asked the gabbai for anot…

title.en: The chassid and the roots of the hair

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from a Midrash a chassid who heard it expounded that every hair on a person's head has its own root, and no two hairs grow from one root. He concluded that Hashem provides each person his own source. When his wife asked why he did not go out to seek a livelihood, he relied on Hashem, and Hashem indeed helped him and he had parnassa while sitting at home.

title.en: What an old man remembered of R' Avraham Kalisker

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a tradition from the time R' Avraham Kalisker lived in Tzfas: later tzaddikim asked an old man what he remembered of him. He said he did not know what R' Avraham had said and did not understand his words, but when he began to speak it was like someone hammering nails into the heart.

title.en: 'I don't like fish'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, told of a drasha given to students in America about the reward of tzaddikim, who will be served the Livyasan in Gan Eden. As the students sat listening intently, one of them raised his hand and said, 'Rebbi, I don't like fish.' He did not refute anything; he simply made a joke, and with that the whole talk was destroyed.

title.en: The lion, the donkey and the fox

retelling.en: In the Midrash's mashal, the lion walks with his retinue and comes to a log bridge where a donkey collects the toll. The lion says a king need not pay, the donkey insists, and the furious lion kills him and tells the fox to prepare a meal from the donkey. The fox eats the heart himself, and when the lion asks where the heart is, the fox answers that a donkey who spoke with such chutzpah to the ki…

title.en: Dancing at Az Yashir before the Vizhnitzer Rebbe

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a young man, when Rebbe Chaim Meir of Vizhnitz was in America, he saw a great Jew there, a grandson of the Chortkover Rebbe. At Az Yashir this man began to dance and clap his hands, without any shame. The Vizhnitzer Rebbe turned to look at him and took great delight in it.

title.en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe and the revolver

retelling.en: In Soviet Russia it was forbidden to learn Torah, run a yeshivah or keep Shabbos, and the Lubavitcher Rebbe ran yeshivos and underground chadarim with mesiras nefesh. He was imprisoned and sentenced to death, and American Chassidim asked the American government to intervene, so the Russians released him. During an interrogation, when he refused to name those who ran the yeshivah with him, the int…

title.en: The roped mountain climbers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that while at a camp he once went walking and passed a mountain with a sheer, smooth face, where twenty or thirty climbers were going up with spikes and nails. Because the rock was slippery, one of them would often slip and fall. But they were all tied to one rope, and since the others did not slip, the rope caught him and he did not fall down.

title.en: Reb Elchonon at a seudah in Baranovich

retelling.en: A Jew who was present told the Mashgiach that at a seudah in Baranovich, Reb Elchonon Wasserman sat with a prominent rav of the Mizrachi and they argued. Reb Elchonon said that either he was right or the other was. When they come to the next world, if he was wrong he could say that great rabbanim, Reb Chaim Brisker and Reb Chaim Ozer, told him so. But if the other was wrong, he would have nothing…

title.en: A Pesachdik vessel

retelling.en: A great chassid of Reb Avraham of Slonim, who could rarely travel to the Rebbe, wrote him before Pesach asking him to send 'a dish for Pesach', meaning a thought to work with through the Yom Tov. The Rebbe answered that he wanted to give him a dish for Pesach, but the chassid should send him a Pesachdik vessel. With that word the chassid lived the whole Pesach.

title.en: The Karliner chassid and the Ba'al HaTanya

retelling.en: A chassid of great stature, a talmid of Reb Shlomo of Karlin, once passed through the Ba'al HaTanya's town and spent Shabbos there. Seeing what an elevated Jew he was, the Ba'al HaTanya asked where he was from, and he answered that he was with Reb Shlomo of Karlin. The Ba'al HaTanya told him to stay, and he would make him into a vessel. The chassid answered that his Rebbe had already worked on hi…

title.en: David HaMelech and the frog

retelling.en: According to the braisa in the introduction to Perek Shira, when David HaMelech finished Sefer Tehillim he wondered whether any creature says more shira than he does. A frog met him and told him not to be so proud, because it sings more shira than he does. The Mashgiach notes how surprising this is, given the frog's croak.

title.en: The fox and the fish

retelling.en: In the time of the Roman decree against learning Torah, Rabbi Akiva was asked why he still taught, and he answered with a parable. A fox stood by a river and told the fish to come up onto dry land and live with him in friendship, safe from the bigger fish that swallow them. The fish answered that if they are afraid in the water, which is their life, how much more will they die if they leave it. T…

title.en: The thief who set the house on fire

retelling.en: A lowly man, a robber, came to a place on a cold night and asked to be let in; the family gave him food and a bed. In the middle of the night he took their things and, so no one would know, set the house on fire, then ran through the rooms shouting while the people ran out. Afterwards people praised him for saving them, until someone who knew him said that he was the one who had started the fire.…

title.en: The Bnei Yissaschar's calculation

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, as brought in the sefarim, that the Bnei Yissaschar sat with people and made a very exact calculation of their income and their expenses. He showed them that their expenses were greater than their income, and told them that their parnassah is above calculation.

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah and the porters

retelling.en: Porters carrying a barrel of wine for Rabbah bar bar Chanah broke it and the wine was lost. The matter came to judgment, and he was told not only to forgo the loss but even to pay them for their work, since they were poor laborers who had nothing to bring home to their families. Rabbah bar bar Chanah asked whether this was the law, and was answered that for him, yes, this is the law.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov tears a debt document

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov visited a wealthy man who showed him his very strong horse that did a great deal of work. When the host offered him a gift, the Ba'al Shem Tov asked for one particular debt document, which the host said was worthless since the debtor had died leaving nothing. The Ba'al Shem Tov tore it up, and at once the stable keeper came in to say the horse had fallen dead. The Ba'al Shem To…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim's two kvitlach

retelling.en: A man came to the Chiddushei HaRim with a kvitel for a woman in very difficult labor. The Rebbe told him that being a Rebbe is no simple matter: he held two kvitlach, one for this woman and one for a dying man for whom a full recovery was requested. He knew that the dying man's soul was to enter this child, which is why the birth was delayed, and he asked for whom he should now daven.

title.en: The Maggid asks who is the tzaddik of the generation

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch once asked his great students, among them Reb Elimelech, Reb Zusha and Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, who is the tzaddik of the generation, and they were silent, even when he asked three times. He then told them that had they declared him the tzaddik of the generation, it would have been accepted in Heaven and brought the geulah. The Mashgiach explains that the Satan caus…

title.en: Rebbe Reb Bunim and the maskil

retelling.en: A young man in Rebbe Reb Bunim's circle was a fine scholar but carried Haskalah ideas, which were then spreading in Poland. Rebbe Reb Bunim was glad that he had managed to draw him away from his chassidim. The young man later wrote a mocking piece on the Zohar's statement about walking four amos without washing the hands, and became a heretic.

title.en: Rebbe Reb Elimelech's tashlich

retelling.en: Rebbe Reb Elimelech did not let people accompany him to tashlich, but the Lubliner went along secretly to see how he did it. Rebbe Reb Elimelech said that he was casting off his aveiros, and that what would be a mitzvah for a smaller man is an aveirah for a great one.

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the fruit

retelling.en: When the Belzer Rav, R' Aharon, was served an apple and a pear, he would not eat them. Asked why, he said perhaps they had lain on a dairy plate; he had eaten meat less than six hours before. By halacha there was no problem, but he sensed one.

title.en: The Maggid at the spring

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov sent the Maggid to sit hidden in a crevice by a spring until midday. A rich man rode up, rested, drank, put down his wallet and rode off without it; a second man drank and took the wallet; then a poor, exhausted man sat down to eat dry bread dipped in the water. The rich man returned, accused the poor man and beat him badly. The Ba'al Shem Tov explained that in an earlier life…

title.en: The Kotzker on the father of the Avnei Nezer

retelling.en: A great gaon in Poland some generations ago merited a son who lit up the world with Torah, the Avnei Nezer. The Kotzker said he merited it because on Purim, when no one was learning, he sat and learned Gemara. The Mashgiach adds that he does not recommend this, since each time has its own avodah.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's Purim seudah

retelling.en: Years ago in America, at a Purim seudah of the Stoliner Rebbe, R' Yochanan, something was done concerning Stalin, who was then persecuting Jews. Soon after, the newspapers reported Stalin's death, and it was said that this had been brought about at the Purim seudah.

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair came to a place and his donkey was given food, but it would not eat. When they told him, he said that perhaps maaser had not been separated, even though the doubt was a weak one. They separated maaser and the donkey ate.

title.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's goats

retelling.en: People came to tell Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa that his goats were doing damage. He answered that it could not be, his goats do not damage. It turned out that the report was not true.

title.en: Rebbi and Rabbi Meir's staff

retelling.en: According to the Yerushalmi, Rebbi attributed his greatness in Torah to having had the staff of Rabbi Meir. The Mashgiach explains that Rabbi Meir's soul had spread into his staff, and an impression of it remained there even after his passing.

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah's broken barrel

retelling.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah hired porters to carry barrels of wine, and one of them broke a barrel. They came to Rav for judgment, and Rav ruled that the porter was exempt; when Rabbah bar bar Chanah asked whether that was the law, Rav answered with a passuk about walking in the way of the good. The porter then said he had worked all day and needed his wages, and Rav ruled that he be paid.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the lost wallet

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov told his talmidim to hide on a hill, watch what happens, and say nothing. A man lay down in a field, his wallet fell out as he slept, and another man came, found it and took it. Then a third man came and lay down there; the owner returned, accused him and beat him, while the talmidim wanted to cry out that he was innocent. The Ba'al Shem Tov then explained that in an earlier gi…

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah and the porters

retelling.en: Porters carrying a barrel of wine for Rabbah bar bar Chanah stumbled and broke it, and all the wine spilled. He brought them to Rav to make them pay, but Rav told him to forgo, citing 'lema'an telech bederech tovim'. The workers then said they were poor, had worked all day and needed bread for their families, and Rav told him to pay them too. When he asked whether that is the din, Rav answered th…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the mohel's mishap

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story he heard from the Chasam Sofer's students. In a small town near Pressburg, an inexperienced mohel's bris led to a dangerous infection, and the town's rav, fearing a terrible danger to the Jews of the whole region, travelled to the Chasam Sofer, who rebuked the mohel for taking on such a case. He told them to take the patient in a wagon as though to a doctor in the city…

title.en: The Lubliner's plate of soup

retelling.en: Rabbi Mendel of Rimanov sat at the Shabbos table of the Chozeh of Lublin when the Lubliner poured out a plate of soup. Rabbi Mendel cried out that they could be arrested and taken to prison, and the Lubliner answered that there was nothing to fear, since they were sitting here at the table. Later the Lubliner told what had happened: an official was writing an evil decree against the Jews; the Lub…

title.en: The neighbor's plastic-roofed sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a neighbor in his previous apartment, whose porch adjoined his, who built a sukkah with a plastic roof and hardly left it for all seven days. He later learned the man was one of those who do not accept the oral law. When he told him the sukkah was not kosher without schach, the neighbor argued that the Torah says to live in the sukkah seven days, which is impossible if rain…

title.en: The third wall of Yerushalayim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that, staying near the edge of East Yerushalayim, he wondered at the many new churches along one street and inquired. He was told that archaeologists had found, hundreds of yards beyond the Old City walls, an ancient wall of the same stones as the Kosel, showing that Yerushalayim once reached there. This would place the site the Christians believe is their founder's grave in…

title.en: The Ruzhiner tzaddik's couch

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's uncle in Yerushalayim, who had been in the upholstery trade in Vienna, opened an upholstery shop there after the war. A great tzaddik of the Ruzhin line in Yerushalayim ordered an expensive couch from him. When it was delivered, the tzaddik asked why the back was canvas, since he had chosen the best material. The uncle explained that the back stands against the wall and no one put…

title.en: The Ropshitzer on the Ruzhiner's carriage

retelling.en: In Ruzhin the court conducted itself with royal splendor, and the Ruzhiner rode in a gilded carriage drawn by four white horses. The Ropshitzer once saw him riding like a king with his hand held to his heart. He said that the Ruzhiner held his heart so that it would not burst from the pain of the galus of the Shechinah.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the rich visitor

retelling.en: A rich man from America visited the Chofetz Chaim and saw that there was almost no furniture in his house; to sit on a bench one had to prop it up with a milk crate. The Chofetz Chaim asked him how he sat on the train, and he answered on a simple bench, because at home he has an upholstered couch. The Chofetz Chaim answered that he too is on a journey in this world, and at home, there, he has.

title.en: The chassid who copied the coffee

retelling.en: A chassid once came to his Rebbe just when the Rebbe felt weak and, before davening, drank a cup of coffee while wearing his tefillin. The chassid went home with a new practice: from then on he drank coffee in tefillin. The Mashgiach tells it to show that one must know what to learn from tzaddikim and what not.

title.en: R' Chaim Vital's dream

retelling.en: R' Chaim Vital writes that in a dream at night he was shown that he fought with the Samael and with his female counterpart. He quickly overcame the Samael, but against the female he strengthened himself many times with great effort, until he went down several levels and still could not overcome her. The Mashgiach explains that in the sitra achra the female is stronger than the male.

title.en: R' Yechiel of Gostynin at the Kotzker's door

retelling.en: A young man came on Purim to the door of the Kotzker Rebbe. The Kotzker asked what he wanted, and he answered that today is Purim, when whoever stretches out his hand is given, so he was knocking and asking. The Kotzker told him to come in, and he stayed a while. When he came out he was an entirely different person, and he became the great R' Yechiel of Gostynin.

title.en: The rosh yeshivah and the cook

retelling.en: A rosh yeshivah of a great yeshivah did not have Yiddishe nachas from his children; one son grew up a professor wearing a yarmulke. The yeshivah's cook was a Chassidishe Yid whose sons were the best bochurim in the yeshivah. The rosh yeshivah asked what made him different from the cook, and the answer was that the cook sang zemiros on Shabbos.

title.en: The poor chassid's challah and fish

retelling.en: One of the great chassidim was very poor and could scrape together only a few groschen to buy a piece of challah and fish for Shabbos. Taking a piece of challah he said: Ribono shel Olam, You gave me challah for Shabbos, give me Shabbos for the challah. He said the same over the fish.

title.en: The cholent in the Bronx shul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's mechutan, who lived in the Bronx, used to make a kiddush with cholent every Shabbos in the small shul where he davened. A boy who used to come eat the cholent later drifted away, was taken into the army during the war, and fell into the worst aveiros. Once on Shabbos he suddenly remembered the cholent in the little shul in the Bronx, and that memory lifted him so that he remained…

title.en: The poritz who sledded on sugar

retelling.en: A wild poritz once wanted to go sledding in the middle of summer. He had his servants pour thousands of sacks of sugar over a field until it looked like snow, harnessed two white horses and rode his sled over the sugar, at a time when sugar was very expensive in Russia. Jews ran to the tzaddik to describe this great pleasure, and he answered: what is that compared to the pleasure of saying Nishma…

title.en: The counselor of his youth group

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that about fifty years earlier, at a class reunion, it emerged that of some forty classmates only three had remained Shabbos observant. His friends drew him into a youth group whose counselor, Rabbi Elimelech, spoke to them every Shabbos. He taught them that Yiddishkeit is not just a tradition but the dearest thing a Jew owns, that one must fight and pay a price for it, and…

title.en: A tzaddik guards the holiness of his mouth

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a well-known tzaddik who had trouble with his gums, and the pain disturbed his learning. A specialist used to come and massage his gums. The tzaddik said that if his mouth would not be holy, he could not merit Torah. The Mashgiach brings this to show that the great ones guarded their kedushah.

title.en: The Rebbe Reb Elimelech could not sleep

retelling.en: Tzaddikim like the Rebbe Reb Elimelech would not go to sleep while they still had something put away for tomorrow. Once he could not fall asleep and understood that something must be left in the house. He searched, found some money, rushed it off to a poor person, and was then able to sleep.

title.en: Reb Elya Lopian and the bochur who wanted to leave yeshiva

retelling.en: A talented bochur in the yeshiva where Reb Elya Lopian was mashgiach told him he was leaving to earn a living. To each reason he gave, that he needed to live, to marry, to support children and to pay medical bills, Reb Elya answered: maybe you won't live, maybe you won't marry, maybe you won't have children, and the bochur protested that he was cursing him. Reb Elya explained that he was not curs…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's son and his kasha

retelling.en: A son of the Chasam Sofer, the Mashgiach is not sure which one, asked his father as a boy a philosophical question that seemed to contradict the Chumash, and his father did not answer. Three days later he called the boy and gave him a splendid answer. He told him that he had known the answer all along, but wanted to teach him that one can go around three days with a kasha and still be a Jew who b…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from someone who was present that news once reached Radin that the Mississippi River had flooded. The Chofetz Chaim gathered the people and told them that the forces of nature are Hashem's messengers, and that if the Mississippi overflowed it was a sign that they needed to do teshuvah, even thousands of miles away in Radin.

title.en: The stranger who asked for twenty rubles

retelling.en: A stranger with a fine beard and rabbinic clothing came to a town, and nobody knew who he was. He asked his host to lend him twenty rubles, and the host refused, saying he had never seen him and could not trust a stranger. The man then asked how the host had relied on him as a shochet, and admitted he was not really a shochet; he had wanted to show the host how he was fooling himself, refusing a…

title.en: The children of the Lower East Side

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he was a boy there was a beautiful Jewish community on the Lower East Side of New York, with many upright Jews and tzaddikim, yet almost nothing became of their children. When someone called him about a reunion of his graduating class and he asked after one classmate and another, the answer was the same. He attributes it to the laxity in kashrus in those days, when…

title.en: The Beis HaLevi and the chicken for the road

retelling.en: The Beis HaLevi of Brisk visited Rabbi Yehoshua Leib Diskin while both still lived in Lita, and for the long trip home he was given a piece of chicken. After he left, the rebbetzin ran in alarmed: a shailah had been found on the other part of that chicken. Rabbi Yehoshua Leib smiled and told her not to worry, the Brisker Rav would not stumble. When the Beis HaLevi later passed through again, he t…

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the cold pancake

retelling.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov, Rav of Lemberg, stopped on a journey at the Rav of a town, and the rebbetzin served two plates of pancakes made of eggs. When the host invited him to eat, he took the fork and began to cut, then said he now had an answer to a difficult Rambam, and his pilpul lasted half an hour until the pancake was cold. The rebbetzin then ran in, thankful he had not eaten: by mistake it had…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the torn paroches

retelling.en: The Divrei Chaim once sat at his tish and said that the Beis HaMikdash in heaven was complete except for the paroches. One of the rabbanim at the table asked why the Rebbe, surely the tzaddik of the generation, did not make it. The Divrei Chaim answered that he had made the paroches, but a certain great rasha of the generation came and tore it.

title.en: Rabbah bar Avuha meets Eliyahu in a cemetery

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara that Rabbah bar Avuha found Eliyahu in a cemetery of non-Jews and asked him questions of halacha, which Eliyahu answered. Rabbah bar Avuha then asked how Eliyahu, a kohen, could stand in a cemetery, and Eliyahu answered that the graves of non-Jews do not convey impurity by being under one roof.

title.en: Gechazi tells the king of Elisha's wonders

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash on the verse where the king of Israel asked Gechazi to tell him the great deeds of Elisha. As Gechazi began to tell of the boy Elisha revived, the woman whose son it was arrived to plead for her field after seven years away, and she told the king the miracle herself. The Midrash says she was brought from far away so that the story would not be told by Gechazi.

title.en: The Skverer's son looks for Eliyahu

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, as heard from a Slonimer tzaddik who had stories of tzaddikim from mouth to mouth, that Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver once told his son that Eliyahu was now in the street. The son went out and did not find him, but saw a market of oxen tied to posts at feeding time: some strained and tore at their ropes, while others stood quietly. He thought: why do they tear, when the food will b…

title.en: Yonasan ben Uziel and the bas kol

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, from the Gemara in Megillah, that when Yonasan ben Uziel wrote the Targum on Nevi'im, a bas kol came out and asked who revealed its secrets to people. Yonasan ben Uziel stood up and said that he had done it, not for his own honor or his father's, but so there should be no disputes about the Nevi'im and there should be peace in Yisrael. The bas kol did not know who it was unti…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the Or HaChaim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that the Ba'al Shem Tov traveled toward Eretz Yisrael to meet the Or HaChaim HaKadosh, and Heaven did not allow it, because had they met, Moshiach would have come.

title.en: A posek moved by tears

retelling.en: A woman came with a question to a posek, apparently the Noda BiYehudah, and began to weep. He excused himself from ruling, saying tears are a kind of bribe: his feeling had been stirred, and a ruling must come from the intellect.

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim on naming a child

retelling.en: Someone asked the Chiddushei HaRim what name to give his child. He would not answer, saying that every father who names his child does so with a measure of ruach hakodesh and hits upon the name of the child's root, so why give away that chance.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's son and the tochachah

retelling.en: The son of the Ba'al HaTanya once heard the tochachah of Bechukosai read by someone other than his father, and fainted. When revived and asked why, he said that when his father read it he heard only blessings, since his father transformed the curses.

title.en: Reb Hershele Zidichoiver at the tochachah

retelling.en: Reb Hershele of Zidichov once read the tochachah in Bechukosai and could not restrain himself; at one of the verses he cried out to the Ribono shel Olam. The Mashgiach says he saw the blessing within it.

title.en: The wealthy guest and the order of the Shabbos meal

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a wealthy guest who came for Shabbos, from whom a large donation for the yeshiva was hoped. Among the finer people in Lita the custom was to serve one dish before another, while the Jewish Shabbos custom was the reverse. The question arose whether to change the order for the guest, and the answer was no: one serves as Jews conduct themselves, without being impressed by the…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon leaves the cave

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai spent twelve years in the cave. When he came out and saw people busy plowing and harvesting, he said they were leaving eternal life to occupy themselves with temporary life. The Mashgiach brings this to show that for Rabbi Shimon every day was Shabbos.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya answers with a niggun

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a tradition of the Chabad chassidim that the Ba'al HaTanya once came to Shklov, where there were great scholars. They asked him to come because they had many questions in Torah for him to answer. They gathered and he told each one to ask his question; when they had all finished, instead of answering he sang a niggun.

title.en: Bombs in Meah She'arim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach reports that shortly before the shiur he heard news that was both bad and good. About two hours earlier two pipe bombs set by Arabs had exploded in a street of Meah She'arim, and only one person was slightly wounded. He calls it open miracles, like in the Gulf War, and says Klal Yisrael needs much mercy.

title.en: The Satmar Rav singing in Meron in the Three Weeks

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites a sefer which records that its author was in Meron with the Satmar Rav during the Three Weeks, and they sang at Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's resting place. When asked how one sings during bein hametzarim, the Satmar Rav answered that by Rabbi Shimon there is only strength and joy; the churban does not exist there.

title.en: The Rebbe who seats everyone

retelling.en: When asked what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai being 'for everyone' means, someone answered with a mashal of Rebbes and chassidim. Some Rebbes admit to their tish only those with a shtreimel, so the gabbai keeps spare shtreimlach to hand out; others want a long kapote, others a beard, others at least a hat. Rabbi Shimon is a Rebbe who seats everyone, shtreimel or not, beard or not.

title.en: The chassid saved by the thought of his friends

retelling.en: A chassidic merchant travelling through a forest was rescued from danger and brought to a settlement, where his yetzer hara burned strongly to sin. He reckoned that he could not sin, because he would soon be back with his friends the chassidim, who would drag him to the Rebbe; this thought saved him. When he came to the Rebbe, the Rebbe told him that what geonim cannot do and a Rebbe cannot do, g…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav's son and the lightning in Belz

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that a son of the Sanzer Rav traveled to Belz for Shavuos and saw there, as it were, the lightning of Matan Torah. The next Shavuos he again wanted to travel, and explained that in Belz he saw the lightning. He was told that here too one can see it. The Mashgiach adds that it is a gift given to some, and better still is to believe that the lightning is present.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim: why am I a kohen?

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim once asked a man for some mesiras nefesh in Yiddishkeit, and the man answered that it was too hard for him. The Chofetz Chaim asked whether he was a kohen or a Levi, and he said no. The Chofetz Chaim explained why he himself was a kohen: over three thousand years ago, when Moshe called 'whoever is for Hashem, to me' after the Golden Calf, his ancestor gathered around Moshe with…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's face on each Yom Tov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that he lived in Williamsburg on the same block as the Satmar Rav. One could see on his face that Pesach looked different from Sukkos and Sukkos from Shavuos, beyond the difference between Shabbos and weekday that can be seen on other Jews too.

title.en: The Imrei Emes changes the Shavuos schedule

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in Peshischa, Kotzk and Ger the custom was to learn all night and daven late. The Imrei Emes, the Gerrer Rebbe, changed it so that Shacharis would be at half past seven, and said at his tish that since there would be no time to rest before davening, people should rather sleep at night so as to be fresh for davening and the reading of the Torah, because that is the main…

title.en: Dasan and Aviram's private splitting of the sea

retelling.en: According to the Targum Yonasan the Mashgiach cites, Dasan and Aviram were the only Jews who stayed behind in Mitzrayim. When the Egyptians who remained were shown the drowning of their army at the sea, Dasan and Aviram decided they too wanted to go and ran to join the Jewish camp. It was already after Kriyas Yam Suf, so Hashem parted the sea again, a private splitting just for these two latecome…

title.en: Yisro asks Moshe to come out to him

retelling.en: Yisro sent word to Moshe that he, his father-in-law, was arriving with Moshe's wife and two sons, and asked Moshe to come out from under the Clouds of Glory to greet him. Rashi adds that he said: if not for my sake, come out for your wife and your children. The Mashgiach explains that Yisro, who had tried every idol, was not seeking honor; he feared he would lose his courage before entering and w…

title.en: Yosef and Potiphar's wife

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells from the Midrash how Potiphar's wife pressed Yosef every day for close to a year, changing her clothes morning and evening. Yosef lowered his eyes so as not to look at her, and she put a sharp iron under his chin to force his head up. She threatened him with hunger, blindness and prison, and to each threat he answered that Hashem helps. On the day all of Mitzrayim went to a…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's wagon driver

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was traveling with a wagon driver who suddenly turned to him on the way and demanded that he hand himself over to be killed. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered calmly and asked him to drive a little further, past that place. Once past it the driver apologized, saying he did not know what madness had entered him. The Ba'al Shem Tov later explained to his students that they had passed a…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's student and the melon seller

retelling.en: The story is brought in a sefer by a student of the Chasam Sofer, printed by his son. As a young bochur in the Chasam Sofer's yeshiva he went one erev Shabbos to buy fruit, and passed a stand where a girl was selling melons. He asked the price, found it too dear and walked away; she called him back with a clever play on words from the Gemara. Struck by her wit, he glanced at her, and then went to…

title.en: Yosef and the wife of Potiphar

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells from the Midrash that the wife of Potiphar tormented Yosef and that he would not even look at her, keeping his head bent down. She put a sharp knife under his chin so that he would have to look up, and threatened him with prison and with blinding him, and to each threat he answered with a passuk about Hashem. She changed her clothes morning and evening to tempt him, day afte…

title.en: The Belzer Rav declines to come to America

retelling.en: About a hundred years earlier, when Jewish life in America was very weak, some Jews who wanted to bring order there went to Rabbi Yehoshua of Belz and asked him to come and save the situation. He asked for three days to consider, and then told them that it is very hard to be a Jew in America. In Europe, he said, there are a thousand years of Jewish history, with crusades and decrees in which hund…

title.en: The Bnei Yissaschar's accounting

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Bnei Yissaschar used to sit with people and have them reckon how much they spent in a year and how much they earned. He showed them that they had spent more than they earned. The Mashgiach uses this to show that a Jew's parnassah does not follow calculation.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's sheep

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, as written in holy seforim, that the Ba'al Shem Tov used to go say Tehillim and daven in the forest where sheep came to graze. When he stood up for Shemoneh Esrei, all the sheep stood up on their hind legs and davened with him the whole time. The Mashgiach adds that this is the praise of Hashem: when a Jew praises Him, he brings all creation to praise Him.

title.en: Diamonds or tallow candles

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Chofetz Chaim's parable of a poor man whose wife heard that in the far-off dark mountains, cold and dark all year, diamonds and pearls lie on the ground. He travelled for months, but there candles were scarce and costly, so he spent all his money on them and finally emptied his bags of diamonds to fill them with candles. Sailing home into the summer heat, the tallow candle…

title.en: The Gerrer Rebbe and the peyos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the earlier Gerrer Rebbe was a calm person who did not go around stirring things up. In Poland it was customary to tuck the peyos away, a practice going back to an old decree from the Russian period. When Poland was independent, the Rebbe remarked to a bochur that it would be fitting for the peyos to be worn openly and long. The bochur went out and told the others, and wi…

title.en: Two Jews on the wrong train

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from a great man of two Jews in Russia who set out on a three-day train journey. When they got off at the end, they discovered they had taken the train in the wrong direction, west instead of east, and were now six days from their destination. One of them was a refined Jew who remained calm, understanding that it was not by chance; the other was distraught and asked his friend…

title.en: The Mashgiach counts the pesukim of Yisro

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that, being curious by nature, he counted the pesukim of Parshas Yisro to check the Masorah's figure of 72. He found 75. He counted again, backwards, and on his fingers, and again found 75. This led him to the idea he then develops.

title.en: The budget that never balances

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of someone who would sit with young men learning Torah and draw up a full account of their yearly income and expenses. Each time he showed them that the expenses were more than the income, and told them that their parnassah defies numbers.

title.en: A child's answer in the Mashgiach's chumash class

retelling.en: Many years earlier, the Mashgiach was teaching chumash to young children and they learned the curses of Ki Savo, where Rashi brings the Gemara that blessings were said first. A question came up in class: why did the Torah write the curses and leave the blessings for Rashi to add, rather than the reverse? A child gave a wonderful answer whose depth he himself did not understand: Hashem wanted to g…

title.en: The call from the minaret at the Kosel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says that those who have been at the Kosel have heard the Arab caller who goes up five times a day and sings a prayer in Arabic. He was told that each time the caller mentions that the Jews sinned and made the golden calf, and that they must be kept far from the place. The Mashgiach compares this to Bilam, who turned to the sin of the egel.

title.en: Reb Zusha and the fallen bundle of hay

retelling.en: A non-Jew with a wagon of hay lost a bundle off the wagon and called to Reb Zusha to help him lift it. Reb Zusha answered that he could not, it was too heavy. The man told him that he could lift it but did not want to. Reb Zusha wept, hearing in it a message from Heaven about lifting the fallen letter hei of Hashem's Name, which is the whole task in the world.

title.en: Rav Ketina and the necromancer

retelling.en: Rav Ketina passed by a necromancer when the earth shook with a loud noise, and asked him the reason. The necromancer said that when Hashem remembers the destroyed Beis HaMikdash He lets two tears fall into the sea, and that is the noise. Rav Ketina called him a liar. The Gemara concludes that the necromancer was right, and Rav Ketina said it so that people would not be drawn after him.

title.en: Rabbi Yaakov Emden's stand on the Zohar

retelling.en: In Rabbi Yaakov Emden's time there was a great war against the sect of Shabsai Tzvi, which built itself on Kabbalah, and the leaders feared people would again be drawn after it through mystical matters. Rabbi Yaakov Emden wrote that he was not sure the whole Zohar was authentic. The Mashgiach notes that he himself cites the Zohar, and explains that he did so to cut Klal Yisrael off from the sect.

title.en: The Baal Shem Tov and the horse

retelling.en: The Baal Shem Tov visited a wealthy man who showed him a horse that worked as much as ten horses, and asked for it as a gift; the man refused. He then asked to see the man's loan documents and asked for one IOU whose debtor had died; the man gave it, and the Baal Shem Tov tore it up. Moments later the horse dropped dead. The Baal Shem Tov explained that the debtor could not enter Gan Eden owing m…

title.en: The talmid who watched from the mountain

retelling.en: A talmid asked the Baal Shem Tov about the Zohar on Mishpatim, and was told to hide on a mountain and watch without reacting. He saw a rider nap under a tree and lose his wallet, a second man find it and take it, and a pauper sit down to eat his dry bread; the rider returned and beat the pauper until he fell unconscious, but found nothing. The Baal Shem Tov explained that some sixty or seventy ye…

title.en: Reb Chaim Ozer's advice to the sick man

retelling.en: A man whose doctor found a lung condition and gave him no hope came to Reb Chaim Ozer in Vilna for a brachah. Reb Chaim Ozer asked for the exact details of the condition, and then told him to move to Eretz Yisrael. He explained that in an animal this condition is disputed between the Beis Yosef and the Rema; in Europe the Rema is followed and it is treif, while in Eretz Yisrael the Beis Yosef is…

title.en: The Mashgiach at a modern wedding

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that he recently attended a modern wedding. The chassan asked him to dance with him and he did, while the band played in the style called rock. The music shrieked and crashed, and all the dancers shouted and jumped; the Mashgiach, who says he is no connoisseur of such music, wondered at them, while they did not consider themselves mad at all.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer fasts before a masechta

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Chasam Sofer used to fast when he had to begin learning with his yeshiva a masechta such as Chullin, because it deals with slaughter, or Bava Kamma, because it deals with damages. The Mashgiach draws from this that the perek being learned is a sign from Heaven.

title.en: R' Aharon of Karlin in the cheder

retelling.en: R' Aharon of Karlin, the Beis Aharon, once entered a cheder where the melamed was learning with the children in the parsha of Eliezer's mission. The melamed asked the children what Rashi says, and taught them with feeling that Lavan was a rasha who spoke up before his father. The Mashgiach says this is how one must teach children, so that they feel the rebbe means it.

title.en: The heavenly minister of Hungary in red

retelling.en: In connection with the Bnei Yissaschar, who was then in Munkatch in Hungary, the Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who said he knew the heavenly minister of Hungary, though he did not live there. He gave a sign: that minister wears red trousers. The Mashgiach uses this to show that a nation's dress follows the dress of its angel above.

title.en: Avraham's discovery of the Creator and the fire

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells how Avraham searched until he understood that one Creator made all of nature, the trees, the seas and the animals. He went out into the world calling on people to break their idols, and Nimrod had him thrown into the fire, from which he was saved by a miracle. Only after this did Hashem speak to him for the first time, with 'Lech lecha'.

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair came to an inn with his donkey, and the innkeeper put out food, but the donkey would not eat. Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair suggested that the food had not been tithed, since his animal does not eat untithed food. The tithes were taken, and then the donkey ate.

title.en: The Bluzhever and the Stoliner on one Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Bluzhever Rebbe and the Stoliner Rebbe were once together for a Shabbos. The Bluzhever read from the Sefer Torah, and afterwards, as he went up to daven Musaf, the Stoliner gave him a pat on the shoulder and urged him on. The Mashgiach brings it to show how one praises someone who sang well, as Hashem, so to speak, praises the Kinneres for its song.

title.en: Rebbe Moshe Leib of Sassov and Nishmas

retelling.en: Rebbe Moshe Leib of Sassov went to a poritz on a mission of redeeming captives. There was a lavish feast with many dishes, and he was so hungry he feared he would faint. He began to think that Shabbos would soon come and he would say Nishmas, and the sweetness of that thought made him forget his appetite, as if he already smelled a better food.

title.en: The lost chassid's blessings

retelling.en: A chassid of the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk got lost far away with nothing to eat or drink and was close to dying of thirst when he found a small stream. Remembering that he was a disciple of the Rebbe, he held himself back and made a shehakol with great kavanah before drinking, and afterwards a borei nefashos. The Rebbe Reb Elimelech later said that souls had been trapped in that place for…

title.en: The melamed and his 'uncle'

retelling.en: A simple melamed, hired for a season by a farmer, saw something wrong in the farmer's household and decided he must go to the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. At the end of winter, through deep mud and with torn shoes, he ran with all his strength, and there was great joy in heaven at his self-sacrifice. The Satan, disguised as his uncle, met him on the way, shouted at him that he was a fool who had a job an…

title.en: R' Naftali Amsterdam's sefer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what is told among the Lithuanian ba'alei mussar about R' Naftali Amsterdam: he always went about holding a sefer. When he came into the shul he took a sefer with him, so that if people rose for him he would not feel they rose for him, since one rises for a sefer anyway.

title.en: King Yannai and the Sanhedrin

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara's story that a servant of King Yannai killed someone and Yannai had to be brought to judgment. Shimon ben Shetach called on Yannai to come and stand before the court, but he would not. From then on, the Mashgiach says, it was established that kings of Yisrael neither judge nor are judged, while the kings of Dovid's house must stand before the Sanhedrin.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the faithless wagon driver

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was traveling with a wagon driver when the town's priest came toward them. It was the custom for a gentile to cross himself at such a sight, and the driver did not. The Ba'al Shem Tov jumped off the wagon: he would not travel with someone who had no faith at all, not even a gentile's faith.

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the tailor

retelling.en: Someone asked the Chazon Ish why Hashem destroyed so much of Klal Yisroel. He answered with a parable: one who sees a tailor cut up an expensive piece of silk would think him mad, but only because he does not know how a silk garment is made. The Mashgiach adds that when Moshiach comes and the finished product is seen, everyone will understand.

title.en: Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's mikveh

retelling.en: Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, the Rav of Yerushalayim, went to the mikveh every day to daven and learn in purity. Rabbi Isser Zalman Meltzer, the rosh yeshiva and father-in-law of Rabbi Aharon Kotler, asked him why he spent those minutes on the mikveh instead of learning. He answered that a convert becomes a Jew through immersion in a mikveh; if a mikveh can turn a gentile into a Jew, it can sure…

title.en: Shlomo at the gates of the Mikdash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when Shlomo said 'lift up your heads, O gates, and the King of glory will enter', the gates wanted to swallow him, asking whether he was the King of glory. He answered that Hashem Tzevakos is the King of glory. The Mashgiach explains that the purpose of a Jewish king is to reveal who the King of glory is.

title.en: Yanai's servant and the beis din

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that King Yanai's servant killed a man, and Shimon ben Shetach summoned Yanai to beis din. Told to stand, Yanai would not stand. After that it was enacted that a king is neither judged nor judges, but kings of the house of David may be judged, since they will stand when the beis din tells them to.

title.en: Avraham's dust against the four kings

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts from Chazal that Avraham went to war against the four kings, who correspond to the four exiles, and threw dust at them, and the dust became weapons. He asks why dust was needed, and explains that Avraham, who saw himself as dust and ashes, declared them nothing, and they were indeed nullified.

title.en: Dovid, Naval and Avigail

retelling.en: Fleeing Shaul, Dovid was in the area of Naval the Carmelite and protected his shepherds. When Dovid asked Naval to provide a meal for his men and Naval, a coarse man, refused, Dovid set out to kill him as a rebel against the kingship, having already been anointed by Shmuel. Avigail came out to meet him and talked him out of it, telling him not to take matters into his own hands. Dovid thanked her…

title.en: A tzaddik's last words to the Satan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who, in his last minutes before his passing, snapped his finger and said that all his life the Satan had thought he was his. Now the Satan found out he was not. The Mashgiach compares this to Dovid, whom the Satan thought was his until the secret was revealed.

title.en: Napoleon would not sleep

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a saying of Slonimer Chassidim that Napoleon never wanted to go to sleep, asking how one can sleep away a kingdom. They applied this to Shabbos: how can one sleep away the kingdom of Shabbos? So too, the Mashgiach says, one with a soul of Eretz Yisrael, near Yerushalayim, is in the King's city, and every moment is precious.

title.en: The Baal Shem Tov on Reb Yitzchak of Drohobitch

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Baal Shem Tov said of Reb Yitzchak of Drohobitch that he was born with the smallest soul a Jew can have. Yet he raised himself to become one of the greatest souls there can be. The Mashgiach brings this to show that no Jew is beyond hope.

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair came to an inn and his donkey would not eat. When asked why, he suggested the grain had not been tithed. They separated the tithe and the donkey ate. The Mashgiach explains that the donkey was part of the tzaddik's property, and his nefesh extended into it.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav's pot of knedlach

retelling.en: Chassidim keep the old custom of eating on Pesach only what is prepared in one's own home, and avoid gebrokts. Yet on Acharon shel Pesach, the people of the town would bring knedlach to the Sanzer Rav and put them into one big pot. The Sanzer Rav mixed them together, ate, and gave out shirayim, although during the year he would not have eaten from such homes, despite the concern of chametz.

title.en: The imprisoned minister who danced on the coronation day

retelling.en: In the Chasam Sofer's parable, one of the king's ministers sat in prison awaiting judgment, and the king used to judge prisoners on the anniversary of his coronation. On that day the minister sang and danced, and the jailer thought he had gone mad, since he might be hanged that day. The minister answered that whatever happens to him, today is the king's joy, and his joy in it overshadows his own…

title.en: The chassid who wanted fresh years

retelling.en: The Baal HaTanya once blessed one of his chassidim with long life. The chassid answered that he does not want old years but fresh years: not to grow old and worn out, unable to serve Hashem with freshness and desire.

title.en: The young man who danced every Shabbos

retelling.en: A young man would come home on Shabbos and dance for an hour before the meal, and his wife, who had prepared everything, complained that he was acting strangely. An elder chassid was sent to her and asked whether, if her husband won a million dollars in a raffle and danced for an hour, she would understand it. When a young man feels the joy of Shabbos, the Mashgiach explains, it is worth a millio…

title.en: Counting the kohanim in the beis medrash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in the beis medrash they went around the poskim and maggidei shiur one by one, noting who is a kohen and who is a levi. They found that eight of them were kohanim or levi'im. He brings it as a sign of the special gift of teaching given to the tribe of Levi.

title.en: The maiden who took the angel's wings

retelling.en: In the generation of the Flood, the fallen angels took human women for themselves. One of them wanted a certain maiden, and she asked him first to give her his wings. When he gave them to her, she flew up to the Throne of Glory and told Hashem she was under His protection. Hashem sheltered her and set her among the constellations as the mazal of Elul, the maiden who escaped from sin.

title.en: The tzaddik and the dybbuk

retelling.en: A dybbuk was brought to a tzaddik, who ordered it to leave. The dybbuk laughed and reminded him that in an earlier lifetime the two of them had committed the same sins together. The tzaddik thought for a few minutes and admitted it was true, but said that he had done teshuvah and the dybbuk had not; therefore he could command it, and the dybbuk left.

title.en: The prisoner who danced at the king's jubilee

retelling.en: A man who had sinned against the king sat in prison awaiting his trial, which fell on the day the king celebrated the jubilee of his coronation. On that day the prisoner danced and sang, and the others thought he had gone mad. When the king asked him why he was dancing on the day of his judgement, he answered that the day had a small personal meaning, his own trial, and a far greater one, the joy…

title.en: A tzaddik prays through the gates of parnasah

retelling.en: A tzaddik saw that a sick man's judgement was already sealed and the gates of life were closed, so he could not pray for his life. Following the Gemara's guidance, he went instead to the gates of parnasah and prayed that the man should have a livelihood. Once parnasah had been decreed for him, he had to live, and he recovered.

title.en: Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver's son looks for Eliyahu

retelling.en: Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver once told his son that Eliyahu HaNavi was in the street. The son went out and did not find him, but he saw animals tied to posts: some were wild and tried to tear themselves loose because they were hungry, while another stood quietly. He thought that when the grain is given out they will all get it at the same time, so the jumping gains nothing. When he told his father he…

title.en: The Lechovitcher chassid who heard 'HaMelech'

retelling.en: A chassid of Lechovitch named Reb Meirel once had to daven Rosh Hashana in a strange town, away from his Rebbe, with a simple minyan he was not used to. It became dark for him as he remembered Rosh Hashana in Lechovitch. Suddenly the Rebbe appeared before his eyes and he heard him cry out 'HaMelech', and he was revived. When he came to the Rebbe on Purim, the Lechovitcher told him that when a Jew…

title.en: Rabbeinu Yonah's teshuvah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbeinu Yonah had a dispute with the Rambam, and afterwards saw holy books being burned and harsh decrees from the government. He did great teshuvah and wrote Shaarei Teshuvah, and also the Yesod HaTeshuvah with its short vidui.

title.en: Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's one refused shidduch

retelling.en: Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld always accepted the shidduchim proposed for his children, but once in his life he declined one. Asked why, he explained that each Rosh Hashana he davened for the child who would need a shidduch that year, so when one came he accepted it and saw Hashem's help. That year he had not davened for this child to find a shidduch, so he was afraid to accept it.

title.en: The Ramban and his student Avner

retelling.en: The Ramban told his students that everything is contained in Haazinu. A student named Avner, who had left the path, asked where he himself was hinted, not expecting his teacher to know. The Ramban showed him his name in a verse of Haazinu, and the student was shaken by it. The account ends with a ship that sank.

title.en: R' Nosson Wachtfogel's mashal of the wedding

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that R' Nosson Wachtfogel, who always speaks of the redemption being near, had promised him the redemption, and when it had not come he asked him about it. R' Nosson answered with a mashal of a bachur who waited very long for his match; his friends kept pushing him, but once the wedding had begun, the guests were seated and the kallah was waiting, there was no more need to pus…

title.en: The Lechovitcher chassid lost in the forest

retelling.en: A Lechovitcher chassid travelling to his Rebbe for Rosh Hashanah got lost in a forest and had to daven alone there. At Shacharis, the word 'HaMelech' as his Rebbe says it suddenly came into his mind, and this gave him great strength to daven. When he later came to the Rebbe, R' Mordechai of Lechovitch told him that when a Jew says 'HaMelech' it is heard across the whole world.

title.en: Rebbi and the calf

retelling.en: A calf being led to slaughter fled to Rebbi for protection, and he sent it back, saying it was created for this. Because he showed no mercy, he suffered great pain for thirteen years, until he again showed mercy.

title.en: The Ramban and his student Avner

retelling.en: A student of the Ramban went off the path, rose to a high position near the government and did much evil. One Yom Kippur he sent for the Ramban, slaughtered a pig, cooked and ate it, and asked how many kareis he had incurred; the Ramban said four, the student insisted five, and the Ramban's sharp look silenced him. Asked why he had left the way, he said he could not believe the Ramban's teaching…

title.en: The chassan waiting for the mechutan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach repeats a story from Rabbi Nosson Wachtfogel. A bochur could not find a shidduch until he was well past thirty, and his friends teased him that their children were already bar mitzvah.
