Finally he became a chassan, invitations were sent, and at the kabbalas panim the kesubah was already written, but all waited for the mechutan who had called that he was delayed. When a friend again a…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the man on the horse

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was walking with his students and passed a man in a fine costume on a white horse with red ribbons, holding a sword, doing tricks while the crowd around him watched and clapped. The Ba'al Shem Tov told his students that this man was born under a mazal to become king that day, but a decree in Heaven prevented it. So the mazal was fulfilled in this way: he sat on a horse with eve…

title.en: Rabbi Avraham Kalisker and the candle tax

retelling.en: When Rabbi Avraham Kalisker's community was in great distress, a Sephardi chacham came with a plan to raise revenue by taxing the candles sold for Yom Kippur and so cover the deficit. Rabbi Avraham answered that in the Ten Days of Teshuvah, which Hashem gave for teshuvah, such matters are foolishness to him. He told him to look at the hunger and poverty in his town, and said that if he walked in…

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the pancake

retelling.en: On a journey, the Yeshuos Yaakov stopped to rest at the home of a rav in a small town, who asked his rebbetzin to prepare something good. She served pancakes, and the hungry guest, as he cut into his, began asking and answering a question on the Rambam, then another, for some twenty minutes while the food grew cold. The rebbetzin then rushed in to say she had mistakenly made it with butter in a f…

title.en: The Rebbe, the fish and the borrowed plates

retelling.en: A great Rebbe from Russia visited Yerushalayim, and each night a different chassid hosted him with many others. He chose to eat at a poor, simple, G-d-fearing man without a beard, who borrowed money to prepare a meal. The Rebbe would not touch the fish and suggested all eat from one big plate; the host glanced at a bearded neighbor and admitted he had borrowed the plates from him. Asked, the neig…

title.en: The Shpoler Zeide and the melamed

retelling.en: At the Seder, the Shpoler Zeide had his son recite the Yiddish explanation of Kadesh, which says the father hurries to make kiddush so the children should not fall asleep. The child left out that part and said his melamed had not taught it. The next morning the Shpoler Zeide invited the melamed for kiddush, served him wine and matzah, and then pointed out that his child had left out the words abo…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov greets a man after davening

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once came over to a man after davening and greeted him with 'shalom aleichem'. The man asked why, since he had been there all along. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that during davening the man had been in Danzig, where his thoughts about his merchandise were.

title.en: The child who did not like fish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a story he was told about a teacher of young students who spoke to them about the good prepared for tzaddikim, including the great fish, the Leviasan, made ready for them. A child raised his hand and said that he does not like fish. That was the end of the derashah, the Mashgiach says, since one cannot answer such a remark.

title.en: The torn shoe at the chuppah

retelling.en: A shoemaker became wealthy and made a lavish wedding, and another man resented it. When everyone stood under the chuppah, that man ran up, called out loudly and handed the father a torn shoe, asking how much it would cost to fix. People laughed and the father was badly shamed. When Rabbi Yisrael Salanter heard of it, he said the rabbanim of Vilna must make an accounting for such a thing happening…

title.en: The Malbim in the Chasam Sofer's place

retelling.en: As a young bachur of about seventeen, already famous as a genius, the Malbim came to Pressburg, where the Chasam Sofer hosted him and gave him permission to say a drashah on Shabbos before Minchah, though the Chasam Sofer did not attend. When the minyan then stood up to daven, the Malbim stood in the Chasam Sofer's place, and the Chasam Sofer came in and saw it and was distressed. The results wer…

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's sealed notebook

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar relates that each Rosh Chodesh Nisan the Chozeh of Lublin took a notebook, and on each of the first twelve days of Nisan wrote what would happen in one month of the coming year. At the end he put it aside and told his talmidim not to look into it until the year's end, when they found that everything had come true. One year he wrote the first four months but refused to write th…

title.en: The prisoner who danced on coronation day

retelling.en: In the Chasam Sofer's parable, one of the king's ministers sat in prison awaiting judgment on the day the king celebrated his coronation, when prisoners were judged. Instead of worrying, he sang and danced, and when asked why, he said that his own fate was overshadowed by his joy in the king's celebration. When the king heard this, he said such a servant would go free and be raised up.

title.en: The Beis Avraham's dancing and the million dollars

retelling.en: When the Beis Avraham of Slonim married as a young man, his wife was unhappy that he came home from davening on Friday night, tired as she was from preparing Shabbos, and danced for an hour. His father-in-law sent an elder chassid, a talmid chacham, to answer her. The chassid asked what she would do if her husband came home having won a million dollars in a raffle and danced; she would gladly dan…

title.en: The Baal HaTanya's blessing of long years

retelling.en: The Baal HaTanya once blessed one of his chassidim with long years. The chassid answered that he did not want old years, growing old and broken and unable to serve Hashem with freshness and desire, but fresh years.

title.en: The Ropshitzer and the mitzvah of sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what tzaddikim said of Reb Naftali of Ropshitz, that he had a special bond with the mitzvah of sukkah. Every day he would hammer a nail into the sukkah, or learn Maseches Sukkah, or speak about the sukkah. The Mashgiach brings this to show that a person can be rooted in one particular mitzvah.

title.en: Naming a child with ruach hakodesh

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that someone came to the Chiddushei HaRim after a child was born and asked what name to give. The Rebbe answered that he now had a chance to have ruach hakodesh himself, and he should give the name on his own. The Mashgiach brings it after explaining that a parent naming a child is guided to the name that holds the child's mission.

title.en: The Jew who rejoiced to be let into Stolin

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he lived in Williamsburg he davened in the Stolin shtibel. There was a precious, refined Jew there who used to say, 'Baruch Hashem, they let me into Stolin!' He took such pleasure in being let in. The Mashgiach applies this to how a Jew should feel entering a shul: 'berov chasdecha avo veisecha'.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya and his rejected student

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara's account, missing from censored editions, of a student of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya who remarked at an inn on the eyes of the woman who kept it. His rebbe, angry that he was looking at women, sent him away and refused him again and again. When the rebbe finally decided to accept him, the student came while he was in the middle of Krias Shema and could not answer;…

title.en: The shofar that terrified the captors

retelling.en: A woman's husband disappeared for a long time, and she had nearly given up hope. Advised to go to Rebbe Reb Elimelech, she received a letter to take into the forest and deliver at a certain house, where she found a band of forces of impurity; after a dispute among them they brought her husband out. He remembered nothing of his captivity except that when Jews blew the shofar in Elul, his captors w…

title.en: Dovid and Shmuel search for the Mikdash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Dovid HaMelech, together with Shmuel HaNavi, searched for the place of the Beis HaMikdash. They thought it belonged at Eitam, a very high place, until they found through the Torah that it was Har HaMoriah, a little lower than Eitam. Dovid wandered and erred until he found the place.

title.en: Shmuel chooses among Yishai's sons

retelling.en: When Hashem sent Shmuel HaNavi to anoint a king from Yishai's sons, he first took the eldest, a tall and handsome son, and thought he was the anointed one, and Hashem told him he was mistaken. He went on to the second, the third, up to the sixth son and kept erring, until the one nobody expected, the hidden Dovid who was out in the field with the sheep, was the one Hashem chose.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua's mother and the beis medrash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Yerushalmi that when Rabbi Yehoshua was a small infant his mother brought him to the beis medrash so that his ears would absorb the sound of Torah. Although he did not know what he heard, it left an impression on him for his whole life.

title.en: Rabban Gamliel's decree on Rabbi Yehoshua

retelling.en: Rabban Gamliel accepted witnesses for the new month in a way Rabbi Yehoshua knew could not be right, and sanctified the month. As nasi he ordered Rabbi Yehoshua to come to him with his staff and his money on the day that by Rabbi Yehoshua's reckoning was Yom Kippur. Rabbi Yehoshua was told that one cannot question the court of Rabban Gamliel, and he came; Rabban Gamliel kissed him on the head and…

title.en: The white beard of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya

retelling.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was young, and by the ways of this world he would not have been chosen as nasi. But Heaven showed that he was to be nasi: at eighteen years old a miracle happened and his beard grew white.

title.en: The prisoner who rejoiced on the king's coronation day

retelling.en: In a parable, a servant who sinned against the king sat in prison, waiting for judgment on the king's coronation day, when the king judged his subjects. On that day he sang and danced, and when asked whether he would go free or be hanged, he answered that today is his king's celebration and he rejoices in it, whatever happens to him. When the king heard this, he said that a man who forgets his ow…

title.en: Avner and the Ramban on Yom Kippur

retelling.en: Avner, a student of the Ramban, became an apikores and rose to be a high officer of the king. On Yom Kippur he summoned the Ramban, ate a forbidden creature in front of him and asked how many lashes he had earned, arguing with his rebbi over the count. When the Ramban asked why he had left the derech, Avner said it was the Ramban's teaching that every Jew is hinted in Ha'azinu, which he could not…

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz and the shtender

retelling.en: When Rosh Hashanah came, Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz took hold of a shtender and said that even this shtender is judged on Rosh Hashanah: whether it will last the year, or be burned or broken.

title.en: Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld and the shidduch

retelling.en: Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld used to agree quickly when a shidduch was suggested for one of his children, but once he did not agree. Asked why, he answered that on the last Rosh Hashanah he had not davened for that child to find a shidduch, so the child was not yet ready for one.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the rich man who wanted a child

retelling.en: A man came to the Ba'al Shem Tov asking for a child. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that he could help him have a child, but the man, who was very wealthy, would have to become poor if he took it upon himself. The Mashgiach explains that on Rosh Hashanah great blessing had been decided for him in sustenance but not in children, and the Ba'al Shem Tov could redirect that surplus from sustenance to ch…

title.en: The chassid who gave a hundred coins for a child

retelling.en: A chassid of Reb Aharon'le asked his Rebbe repeatedly for a child. Once, when the Rebbe needed a large sum for hachnasas kallah, the chassid gave a hundred coins, hoping it would bring him a child. Three days later the Rebbe called him in, said he had searched the heavens and found no child for him, and returned the money. The chassid went to another tzaddik, who blessed him, and a child was born…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the man who read the haftarah

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer was in a house where a woman was having a difficult labor. He said to bring in the man who had been called up for the haftarah on Rosh Hashanah, and when that man came into the house she was helped at once. The Mashgiach explains that the one who reads the haftarah of Chana's remembrance carries something of its power of remembrance with him.

title.en: The village boy's whistle

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls the Ba'al Shem Tov's story in which a decree that the Ba'al Shem Tov and all his companions could not annul was annulled by a village boy who could not daven and whistled before Hashem with all his heart.

title.en: Reb Zusha and the wagon of hay

retelling.en: Reb Zusha was walking on the road when a wagon of hay driven by a gentile passed and a bundle of hay fell off. The gentile called out, 'Zusha, lift the hay!', and when Reb Zusha said he could not, the gentile answered that he could but did not want to. Reb Zusha was deeply moved, taking it as a call to teshuvah, since tzaddikim hear a message in everything, even from a gentile.

title.en: The chassid who asked for Shabbos on his fish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great chassid, a poor man who went hungry all week and scraped together a little money for Shabbos. At the Shabbos table he made the blessing on the challah and said to the Ribono shel Olam that He had given him challah for Shabbos, and now he asked Him for Shabbos on the challah. When he ate a piece of fish he said the same: You gave me fish for Shabbos, give me Shabbos…

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua's cradle in the beis medrash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Yerushalmi that when Rabbi Yehoshua was a small infant, his mother brought him into the beis medrash so his ears would absorb the sound of Torah. Though he understood nothing, it left an impression on his whole life. The opposite, he adds, happened with Elisha ben Avuyah, who heard non-Jewish songs as a child, and this later contributed to his downfall.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua comes on 'his' Yom Kippur

retelling.en: Rabban Gamliel accepted witnesses for the new month in a way Rabbi Yehoshua knew could not be right. As nasi, he decreed that Rabbi Yehoshua come to him with his staff and money on the day that was Yom Kippur by Rabbi Yehoshua's reckoning. After being told that the beis din's decision stands, Rabbi Yehoshua came, and Rabban Gamliel kissed him on the head and called him 'my teacher and my student'.

title.en: The white beard of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts from the Gemara in Berachos that Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah was young and circumstances did not call for him to be chosen as nasi. A miracle happened: at eighteen years old he grew a white beard, to show that Heaven had appointed him.

title.en: The prisoner who danced on the coronation day

retelling.en: In the Chasam Sofer's mashal, a servant who sinned against the king sat in prison awaiting judgment, which was given on the day the king celebrated his coronation. On that day he sang and danced, and when asked whether he knew he was to be judged, he answered that today is the king's joy. Hearing this, the king said that a man who forgot his own judgment out of joy for the king must go free.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva weeps on Shabbos

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva was seen weeping on Shabbos while saying Shir Hashirim. Asked why he weeps on Shabbos, he answered that he does not weep from sorrow but from joy, because Shir Hashirim is full of verses of devekus.

title.en: Moshiach greets every Jew

retelling.en: The Mashgiach quotes a tzaddik that when Moshiach comes he will stand as each Jew passes before him and look at him from head to foot. He will sigh over what the exile did to him, pat him on the cheek and tell him 'your sin is removed'. The Mashgiach adds that this happens every Rosh Hashanah, when all pass before Hashem.

title.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin on a Shabbos without longing

retelling.en: It is told of Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin that he heard from Heaven about one who keeps Shabbos as written, does no melachah, learns and davens, but has no longing to reach the pleasure of Shabbos. When such a person comes to Gan Eden he will sit there like a log, without any pleasure, though he is in Gan Eden.

title.en: R' Mordechai of Lechovitch and the simple chassid

retelling.en: R' Mordechai of Lechovitch once saw one of his chassidim, a simple Jew who knew nothing, saying Shir Hashirim with great fervor. He asked him whether he knew the meaning of the words. The chassid answered that he did not need the meaning, and R' Mordechai was very pleased with his answer. The Mashgiach adds that this is no longer possible today, when hearts are not pure, so one must learn the mea…

title.en: The poor Karliner chassid's Shabbos meal

retelling.en: A Karliner chassid, a poor man, scraped together a few pennies for Shabbos and could afford only a little challah and a small piece of fish. Over the challah he said to the Ribono shel Olam that what he had been given was challah for the honor of Shabbos, and over the fish the same. The Mashgiach brings it to show that the point of the Shabbos meal is that each bite be for the honor of Shabbos.

title.en: Rav Shraga Feivel's talk in the yeshivah

retelling.en: When the Mashgiach was a talmid in the yeshivah, Rav Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, who usually did not speak before the whole assembly, once came into the beis medrash in the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah, banged on the table and spoke for a few minutes. He explained the five levels of the soul and said that every Jew has a moment in these days when he is in contact with Hashem, the level of yechidah, and on…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's place in Haazinu

retelling.en: The Satmar Rav was once asked where he is alluded to in Haazinu. Those who did not understand his zealous opposition to Zionism and the state accused him of hating Eretz Yisrael, though he loved it so much he could not bear any impurity falling on it. He answered with a smile with the last words of the parshah, 'and He will atone for His land, His people'.

title.en: The tailor who bought the fish on Erev Yom Kippur

retelling.en: According to the Midrash, a Jewish tailor went to the market on Erev Yom Kippur to buy fish for the meal, and only one large fish was left. The governor's servant also wanted it, and they bid against each other until the Jew paid twelve zuz. When the governor asked why he paid so much, the Jew explained that on this day Hashem forgives all their sins and they rejoice with a meal of fish, and the…

title.en: The Warsaw company that bought Maftir Yonah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that in Warsaw there was a large financial company whose president heard that buying Maftir Yonah brings success and wealth. Before Yom Kippur he sent agents to every large shul in Warsaw to buy Maftir Yonah for the company, hoping to become rich.

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chana and the heavenly oath

retelling.en: The Gemara tells that Rabbah bar bar Chana heard a heavenly voice saying 'woe is Me that I swore', and he stayed silent. When he told the sages, they criticized him sharply for not annulling the vow. He had thought it meant the oath not to bring another Mabul, but the sages knew it meant the oath of galus, and had he annulled it the geulah would have come.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon purifies Tiveria

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from the Gemara that Tiveria was considered impure because graves there had been lost and no one knew where they were, so kohanim could not go there. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, with his holy spirit, pointed out every place where a dead body was buried, and the bodies came up and were carried away, so he purified Tiveria. The Mashgiach adds that the Gemara calls the people of T…

title.en: Rashbi's passing on the word 'chaim'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai passed away on Lag Baomer while saying the pasuk 'ki sham tzivah Hashem es haberachah chaim'. As he uttered the word 'chaim', with the breath of that word, his neshamah went up.

title.en: Rabbi Hirsh of Rimanov's shidduch

retelling.en: Rabbi Hirsh of Rimanov was, as a young man, the attendant of Rabbi Mendel of Rimanov, and later became his successor. In one home, at twelve o'clock on Friday it was already Shabbos: the challos were on the table, the candles were ready, and everyone sat waiting for Shabbos while saying shiurim or learning mishnayos. When the time came for his shidduch, he asked Hashem for a match from a home whe…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's derashah on Moshiach's shame

retelling.en: The Satmar Rav related a family tradition that the Yismach Moshe, known to hear heavenly proclamations, once described in a derashah on a Yom Tov what happens in Heaven: the books of judgment are set out and the princes of the nations each demand food, water and money for his land. Then David, king of Israel, comes in and asks for a year of geulah for the Jews, and in earlier years he was answere…

title.en: The Tzeduki Kohen Gadol

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites the Gemara about a Tzeduki Kohen Gadol who prepared the ketores outside and only then brought it into the Kodesh HaKodashim. Within a short time he died, and worms came out of his nose. Later in the shiur the Mashgiach connects this punishment to the sense of smell.

title.en: The Kozhnitzer Maggid's joy on Rosh Hashanah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites a sefer of Reb Moshe of Kozhnitz, who as a child saw his father, the Kozhnitzer Maggid, rejoicing greatly on Rosh Hashanah. He did not understand how his father could rejoice so on the Day of Judgment. Later he understood that the joy came together with fear: his father was rejoicing with the Ribono shel Olam, our Father in Heaven.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's dry sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from reliable seforim of tzaddikim, that when the Ba'al Shem Tov sat in his sukkah and it rained, it did not rain in his sukkah. Reb Yitzchak of Drohobitch had a dispute with him; once, when it rained hard on Sukkos, a man told him that by the Ba'al Shem Tov it was not raining. He took his challah and his plate, went over to the Ba'al Shem Tov's sukkah, made a blessing on t…

title.en: A house from the Second Beis Hamikdash era

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he was in Yerushalayim that summer, and digging near where he stayed uncovered a dwelling from the time of the Second Beis Hamikdash. He wonders who lived there, perhaps even a navi, and says he does not know. He uses it to say that one must picture who walked in those places.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's drasha about the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: A young bochur heard a drasha from Rav Avraham Kalmanowitz, who told that when a hurricane struck America and the Mississippi overflowed, causing great loss of life and property, someone reported it to the Chofetz Chaim. The Chofetz Chaim called the people together for a drasha and cried out that Hashem makes the winds His messengers. The Mashgiach notes that in Radin hardly anyone had heard of t…

title.en: Sitting where the sukkah stood during a plague

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from tzaddikim, that there was once a plague. A tzaddik told people to stand and sit in the place where the sukkah had stood on Sukkos. The sukkah itself was no longer there, but by sitting on its place they would be protected from the plague.

title.en: The wheat of Komemiyus in Shemitah 5712

retelling.en: In the Shemitah year 5712 the farmers of Komemiyus, led by Rav Binyamin Mendelson, did not work their fields, while neighbors who relied on the heter planted at the usual time and mocked them. The rain did not come, and the neighbors' seeds dried up and rotted. After Sukkos Komemiyus had only old, broken and wormy wheat from the sixth year, which experts said would not grow, but Rav Mendelson tol…

title.en: The locusts that turned back at Komemiyus

retelling.en: In the Shemitah year 5719 the surrounding farmers did not keep Shemitah while Komemiyus did. When the crops began to grow, clouds of locusts swept from field to field and ate everything, but when they reached Komemiyus they turned around, and its crops grew. The Brisker Rav told Rav Mendelson to publicize it, and it was written up in the papers.

title.en: The orchards of Komemiyus

retelling.en: The Jewish Agency planted fruit trees across Eretz Yisrael but at first refused Komemiyus, fearing that untended saplings would be ruined in Shemitah. Rav Mendelson persuaded the official in charge, telling him openly that in Shemitah they would not tend the trees, and the official warned that the investment was at risk. When the inspectors came at the end of Av, they found the orchards of Komemi…

title.en: No rain in the Ba'al Shem Tov's sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the tradition, accepted among Jews, that it did not rain in the Ba'al Shem Tov's sukkah even in a heavy rain. He tells that once, during a strong rain, word came that no rain was falling in the Ba'al Shem Tov's sukkah, and someone took his wine and challah and went there to fulfill the mitzvah. The Mashgiach notes a halachic question discussed by tzaddikim, among them Rabbi Y…

title.en: Standing where the sukkah stood during a plague

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that at a time of a plague, people were instructed that each one should stand in the place where his sukkah had stood on Sukkos. There, in that place, he would be saved from the plague.

title.en: Chizkiyahu sleeps during Sanheriv's siege

retelling.en: Sanheriv surrounded Yerushalayim with an army so vast that he boasted each soldier could throw one stone and bury the city. Yeshayahu told Chizkiyahu not to worry. It was the night of Pesach, and after midnight Chizkiyahu went to sleep; that night the army was destroyed. The Mashgiach says Chazal apply 'ani shachavti va'ishana' to this, and that Chizkiyahu's strength was that he could sleep, unli…

title.en: Yaakov's vision of Shimshon

retelling.en: As Yaakov Avinu blessed his sons, he looked through the future generations. Reaching the tribe of Dan, he saw Shimshon's strength protecting the Jews and thought he was Moshiach. Then he saw Shimshon killed by the Pelishtim, realized he was not yet Moshiach, and said 'I hope for Your salvation'.

title.en: Shimshon and the gates of the city

retelling.en: The Pelishtim surrounded Shimshon and locked the heavy city gates on him, afraid to face him at night and planning to deal with him in the morning. Shimshon walked over to the gates, ripped them out with their foundations, put them on his shoulder and carried them up the mountain.

title.en: Moshiach weeps for Klal Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Midrash of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who went up to Heaven and was seen by Moshiach. Moshiach asked him about the Jews in the world, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi answered that they are waiting for him every day. When Moshiach heard this he burst into great weeping, out of his longing to come and redeem the Jews.

title.en: The torn shoes of Simchas Torah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a tradition that once there was a heavenly accusation against the Jews, and the accuser brought their sins and laid them on the scale. Then the malach Michael came and brought torn shoes, and laid them on the other side of the scale. The torn shoes belonged to Jews who had danced on Simchas Torah, and they tipped the judgment toward merit.

title.en: The yoshev of the Rebbe Reb Elimelech and the two brachos

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: A yoshev who learned and davened all week by the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk received six rubles every Friday, then four, then two, then an empty envelope, and each week did teshuvah thinking he had sinned. His friends gathered about two hundred rubles and sent him overseas to trade; at an island stop he went off to say Tehillim and the ship left without him. After days without water he rolle…

title.en: Rabbi Zeira crosses the river

retelling.en: When Rabbi Zeira came from Bavel to Eretz Yisrael, he crossed a river on a rope rather than wait for the ferry. Asked why he could not wait an hour or two, he answered that Moshe and Aharon yearned to enter the land and were not granted it, so how could he know he would be; he wanted to seize the opportunity while it was there.

title.en: The diamonds and the candles (the Chofetz Chaim's mashal)

retelling.en: A poor man who could not make a living was urged by his wife to travel to the far-off dark mountains, where diamonds lay in the streets like pebbles. There it was always dark, candles made of animal fat were precious, and everyone sought candles, until he forgot why he had come, emptied his cases of diamonds and filled them with candles. On the way home, in the warmth, the candles rotted and stan…

title.en: The merchant who went to Australia for kangaroo furs (the Ba'al Shem Tov's mashal)

retelling.en: A merchant travels to Australia to buy kangaroo furs and bring them back to America for profit. The Mashgiach explains, following the Ba'al Shem Tov, that this is only the merchant's reason: Hashem sends him there so that he will make a shehakol over the water of a certain brook, where sparks belonging to his neshamah are found.

title.en: The child's translation in Lublin

retelling.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Lentshna once took his young son, Yeshayah, to Lublin. The Lubliner tested the child on the Gemara he was learning. When they reached 'Rabban Gamliel haZaken', the child translated it as Rabban Gamliel thinking into his beard. The Lubliner was very taken with the child's translation.

title.en: The tzaddik who did not answer amen

retelling.en: On Shemini Atzeres one of the great tzaddikim, whom the Mashgiach does not name, was wished long life by a chassid over a l'chaim, and did not answer. The chassidim were frightened that he had not answered amen. After Simchas Torah the chassid asked why, and the tzaddik answered that on Shemini Atzeres one has no connection to this world, and the chassid had confused him with long life when he wa…

title.en: The angel Michael and the torn shoes

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw in Chabad sefarim, he does not remember whether from the Ba'al HaTanya or the Tzemach Tzedek, that one Shemini Atzeres the accuser came against the Jews and their mitzvos and sins were being weighed. The angel Michael brought torn shoes and put them on the scale, and they tipped it. They were the shoes of Jews who had torn them dancing at the Simchas Torah hakafos.

title.en: Napoleon in the shul on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, from history books, that Napoleon once passed a shul, went in and saw fathers and children sitting on the ground and weeping. He was told it was Tisha B'Av and they were mourning the destruction of the Beis Hamikdash some 1700 years earlier. Napoleon said that a people that can still weep over its Beis Hamikdash after so long will surely get it back.

title.en: The wise men of Chelm and the missing pazer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts a joke told in the old towns of Poland and Lita to keep spirits up. The leaders of Chelm called an emergency meeting because for five weeks the Torah reading had not had a single 'pazer', a cantillation note that cheers people up, and the people needed one. The Mashgiach tells the bochurim the good news that this week's sedra has seven.

title.en: Rebbi raises his ten fingers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara that when Rebbi was passing away he raised his ten fingers and said before Hashem that he had not benefited from this world even with one finger. Rebbi, of the house of David, was a wealthy nasi with honor and power, yet he was totally batel to Hashem.

title.en: Shlomo, Pharaoh's daughter and the late tamid

retelling.en: Shlomo succeeded in drawing other nations' princesses to Hashem, but failed with Pharaoh's daughter. He married her on the night of the eighth of Tishrei, the eve of the Mikdash's dedication; she occupied him with her instruments and follies, he rose late, and the morning tamid was not offered on time. Hashem was angered and the decree of destruction was sealed.

title.en: The Berditchever Rav waits for the esrog

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that the Berditchever Rav, before he could bentch esrog, stayed awake the whole night, going to the esrog every few minutes, kissing it and looking out the window to see whether it was time to make the brachah. He contrasts this with Shlomo marrying on the night before the dedication.

title.en: Shlomo's judgment of the two women

retelling.en: Two women each had a baby; one lay on her child in her sleep and killed it, then took the living child of the other. Each claimed the living child, and they came to Shlomo for judgment. He ordered a sword brought to cut the living child, the true mother cried out to give it to the other rather than kill it, and Shlomo ruled that she was its mother. All Israel marveled at his wisdom.

title.en: A Jew with a cane at the Chiddushei HaRim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Chiddushei HaRim sitting with his gabbai when a Jew came running to him, helping himself along with a cane because he could not run on his own. The Mashgiach draws from it that the Chiddushei HaRim understood one must reach higher levels by giving something away, and that holding on to one's cane while giving nothing up is not yet readiness.

title.en: Two kvitlach at once

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a woman in prolonged, difficult labor whose family came to a Rebbe with a kvitel. The Rebbe said he was holding two kvitlach: one for this woman, and one for a man who was dying and asking for a full recovery. He explained that the soul of the dying man must enter this child, and since he had not yet died, she was in difficult labor. The Mashgiach asks: now whom should the…

title.en: The Maggid asks who is the tzaddik of the generation

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Maggid once asked his great talmidim, among them the Ba'al HaTanya and Rebbe Levi Yitzchak, who is the tzaddik of the generation. They were silent; he asked three times and they were silent. He then explained that had they answered, it would have been accepted in Heaven and the redemption would have come, but they lacked the courage to answer.

title.en: The bochur with doubts and the tzaddik's sefer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions a sefer by a wondrous tzaddik, the grandfather of the Bluzhever Rebbe who lived in Boro Park. A bochur once complained to the Mashgiach about doubts he had, and the Mashgiach told him to learn that sefer. The tzaddik's greatest Torah for Sukkos was prepared during the Nine Days, one day for each day of Sukkos, up to Tisha B'Av itself.

title.en: Kiddush for Tisha B'Av on Shabbos Chazon

retelling.en: A very great tzaddik used, on Shabbos Chazon, to give a small presentation of what will happen when Moshiach comes. He took a cup of wine in his hand and made kiddush for Tisha B'Av. As he said it, two streams of tears flowed from his eyes.

title.en: The Bnei Yissaschar asks the Chozeh of Lublin about his soul

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar felt a great awakening when Chanukah came, and nearly a quarter of his sefer is about Chanukah. He thought his soul came from the Chashmona'im and went to ask his rebbe, the Chozeh of Lublin. The Chozeh told him no: his soul came from the Sanhedrin of the tribe of Yissaschar in the time of Chanukah, and for this reason he named his sefer Bnei Yissaschar.

title.en: The Chernobyler sees joy in Heaven

retelling.en: The Chernobyler often used to go up to Heaven to see what was happening there. Once he saw a great joy there and asked what the celebration was that day. The Mashgiach uses the story to ask what is special about Rosh Chodesh Kislev that other Rosh Chodesh days do not have, and at the end of the shiur he speaks of the great joy in Heaven on Rosh Chodesh Kislev, when Jews are given the power to do…

title.en: The Lubliner Rebbe and the informer's kvitel

retelling.en: In the days of the Rebbe of Lublin, a town suffered from an informer who slandered the Jews to the authorities. The townspeople came to the Rebbe with a kvitel bearing the informer's name and asked that he be removed. At night the Rebbe looked at the kvitel and said the man was shining in all the worlds, and he could do nothing. The next morning they brought the kvitel again; the Rebbe looked at…

title.en: Two job offers and the Satmar Rav's letter

retelling.en: Someone asked the Mashgiach that week which of two job offers to take, and he answered briefly that he has no hotline to Heaven and the man should take whichever he wants. The Mashgiach says that had he elaborated, he would have cited a published letter of the Satmar Rav to a man who was offered two matches. The Satmar Rav answered that in this generation no one is qualified to decide, but Hashem…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the dentist's hands

retelling.en: The Chazon Ish suffered pain in his gums, and a dentist living nearby would come and massage them. Once, early in the morning, the pain was so great that he could not learn, and he sent for the dentist. Afterwards he told him that he wants to merit Torah, which comes only through purity, and asked that next time he first wash negel vasser. Once the dentist came in a hurry without washing; the Cha…

title.en: 'Kein Jude' in Germany

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Toras Chaim that during a decree against Jews in Germany, soldiers stopped a Jew, a talmid chacham, and asked him whether he was a Jew. He answered 'kein Jude', which in German means 'not a Jew', while he intended it in loshon hakodesh as 'kein Yehudah', 'yes, a Jew'.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's question: where can one flee today?

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that when the Satmar Rav visited Eretz Yisroel he paid a visit and asked a question. The Rambam writes that one whose neighbors are bad must move away, and if the whole city or country is bad he must leave for another place; where, asked the Satmar Rav, can one flee today? The answer given was that there is a refuge: one flees into the yeshiva.

title.en: Kamtza and Bar Kamtza

retelling.en: A man had an enemy named Bar Kamtza, who was invited to his party by mistake. The host had him thrown out. Bar Kamtza went to the Roman king and spoke lashon hara, and the king sent his armies, who destroyed Yerushalayim. The Mashgiach brings it as the event that symbolizes the destruction through sinas chinam.

title.en: Onkelos consults the souls of the wicked

retelling.en: When Onkelos wanted to convert, he spoke with the souls of the wicked, among them Titus, and asked whether to become a Jew. They told him no and to make trouble for the Jews. The founder of Christianity told him to become a Jew and to do good for the Jews. The Mashgiach brings the Maharal that he could say this because, as a Jew, he has a connection to Olam Haba.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram as Eliyahu's oxen

retelling.en: In the days of Achav and Izevel, when the people served avodah zarah, Eliyahu HaNavi brought two oxen on Har HaKarmel to show who is the true G-d: one for the avodah zarah and one for the mizbeach of Hashem he built there. Fire came down on his offering and everyone proclaimed that Hashem is G-d. According to the Rema MiPano, those two oxen were Dasan and Aviram, and this was their tikkun.

title.en: Yiftach driven out

retelling.en: Yiftach was a man of valor, son of Gilad and of a woman of lower standing. His father's sons from another wife grew up and drove him away, telling him he had no share with them. He went to Eretz Tov, which the Yerushalmi says was outside Eretz Yisrael, and empty men gathered around him and became his army, with which he later fought the king of Ammon.

title.en: The informer's kvittel and the Chozeh of Lublin

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim told of a town of Lubliner chassidim where an informer caused many Jews terrible troubles. They wrote his name and his mother's name on a kvittel asking for his downfall and gave it to the Rebbe of Lublin, who looked at it and asked what they want from this Jew, he is shining in all the worlds. Some time later they gave the kvittel again, and this time the man fell. When they…

title.en: Chizkiyahu and Yeshayahu

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells from the Gemara that there was a dispute between King Chizkiyahu and the prophet Yeshayahu. Chizkiyahu said Yeshayahu should come to him, since he is the king; Yeshayahu said Chizkiyahu should come to him, since he is the prophet. Hashem made Chizkiyahu fall ill, and then Yeshayahu went to visit him, because when someone is sick one does not weigh whose honor it is.

title.en: Vinegar that burned

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that once the lights had to burn but there was no oil to light them, only vinegar. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa said that He who told oil to burn can tell vinegar to burn, and it burned. The Mashgiach adds that for Rabbi Chanina this was not a special act, because his whole life was a life of miracles.

title.en: Avraham discovers the Me'aras haMachpelah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Avraham Avinu ran after a calf and came to the Me'aras haMachpelah. There he saw a great light and saw that all tefillos go up from that place. Only many years later did the cave come into his possession.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva and the fox on the Har HaBayis

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva and his companions went up to Yerushalayim, saw the Har HaBayis and tore kriah. They saw a fox coming out of the Kodesh HaKodashim, and the Tannaim wept while Rabbi Akiva laughed. Asked why, he answered that since the prophecy of destruction was fulfilled, he awaits the prophecies of comfort. They answered him, 'Akiva, you have comforted us.'

title.en: Rabbi Akiva and the wife of Turnus Rufus

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva once saw the wife of Turnus Rufus, who came around a corner unexpectedly. He spat, because of her impure origin; he laughed, because he foresaw with ruach hakodesh that she would convert and become his wife; and he cried, because such beauty would one day be buried in the ground.

title.en: The Maggid tests his ba'al korei

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch once needed a ba'al korei, and he was told that the young Shneur Zalman could read. The Maggid called him in alone and asked whether he knew the connection of each parsha to its week, of each aliyah to its day, and the connection according to the root of his soul. Each time he answered yes, and the Maggid told him that if so he could be his ba'al korei.

title.en: Money hidden in the thief's sack

retelling.en: A rich man came to a wedding with money that he had to keep hidden over Shabbos, and he found out that a thief was among the guests. He hid his money in the thief's own sack, reasoning that the thief would not search there. Right after Shabbos he took his money back from the thief's sack; his own sack had already been turned over and searched, and nothing was found.

title.en: The Alter Rebbe's interrogation

retelling.en: When the Alter Rebbe stood for interrogation in his trial in Russia, he was asked whether he was a talmid of the Ba'al Shem Tov. Answering no would have meant his release, and he could truthfully have said he was a talmid of the Maggid, yet he declared that he was a talmid of the holy Ba'al Shem Tov. One accusation was that he sent money to Eretz Yisroel, then near the Turks with whom Russia was…

title.en: The Tzemach Tzedek refuses to sign

retelling.en: Three of the greatest gedolim of Russia and Lita were summoned to Moscow for questioning, one of them the Tzemach Tzedek. They were asked to sign the bottom of a long letter to the Czar, with the text to be filled in later and a promise that it would be favorable. The other two signed; the Tzemach Tzedek refused. The officials then said that since this small rav wanted to give his life they would…

title.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz asks for strong milk

retelling.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz went into his kitchen and asked why he was not given a glass of milk for his toil in avodas Hashem. He was given one, but complained that it was thin, green milk without strength, and asked for strong milk, which was brought. His chassidim wondered at such strange words. Soon a woman came who had just had a child and had no milk; he told her she would have milk, and when s…

title.en: Dovid HaMelech and Shimi ben Gera

retelling.en: When Dovid HaMelech fled from his son Avshalom, Shimi ben Gera came out and cursed him, and Yoav wanted to kill him. Dovid said to leave him alone, since Hashem had told him to curse, and it was from Heaven. If they killed him, others would come and curse in his place.

title.en: The parable of the king's relative

retelling.en: A man broke the law, and officers took him to prison and began to beat him. He told them to stop because he was a relative of the king, so they brought him to the king to confirm it. The king asked him why he had said so, and he answered that he knew that if he said he was the king's relative they would not beat him. The king said that since he had relied on him, they should let him go free.

title.en: Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah in the fire

retelling.en: Nevuchadnetzar had Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah thrown into the fire because they would not bow to his image, and they went with bitachon. As they were led to the fire each said a passuk, and when Mishael mentioned Yaakov, the wicked there laughed and mocked Yaakov. It was said that the three tzaddikim would be saved in the merit of Yaakov, whom they had mocked; the mockers were burned, and the…

title.en: A segulah for a spreading illness

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of someone who was publicized as a great master of ruach hakodesh. He said that against a certain illness that had recently spread, there is one counsel: to say Ketores together with the tzibbur. The Mashgiach says this was given as a segulah for it, and then adds a segulah of his own, to say Hodu together with the minyan.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembers his gilgulim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Yismach Moshe told his grandson, the Yetev Lev, that he remembered his earlier gilgulim, including the dispute of Korach in the Midbar. The grandson assumed he had sided with Moshe Rabbeinu, but the Yismach Moshe said he had been neutral, and that had the grandson been there he would have sided with Korach, since Korach was very great. He also said he remembered bei…

title.en: Locked in for eight hours

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who was locked into a place where one may not think words of Torah and could not get out. To keep Torah thoughts out of his head he knocked and drummed on the walls, and he sat there eight hours. The Mashgiach asks how one serves Hashem in such a situation, and answers that being placed there is itself the avodah.

title.en: The chassid sustained three years by one teaching

retelling.en: A chassid came to the Beis Aharon after three years away, and the Rebbe asked why he had not come until now. He answered that three years earlier he had heard a short teaching from the Rebbe, and it had served him until now; only now did he feel he needed something new. The teaching was that no creature can raise itself to serve G-d except as He wills. The Rebbe said he had not said it quite so,…

title.en: The boy who did not know what playing meant

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from the Skverer Rebbe about a child, a great reckoner, who was called in by his father when he was found playing. The child recounted that from the age of six, when he grew tired of learning, he rested by learning a complicated Mishnah of measurements with the Tosfos Yom Tov, and at eleven by going through the Rambam's Hilchos Kiddush HaChodesh. He said he did not know what p…

title.en: Seeing the ushpizin or believing

retelling.en: A tzaddik who had a dispute with the Kotzker Rebbe sent him a message asking how he could dispute with him, when the seven ushpizin came to his sukkah and he saw them with his own eyes. The Kotzker answered through the same messenger that when Sukkos comes he believes the ushpizin come. The Mashgiach says believing is a greater level.

title.en: Rabbi Chanina's daughter and the vinegar

retelling.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's daughter lit the Shabbos lamp and then realized she had poured in vinegar instead of oil, and she was distressed that it would not burn on Shabbos. Her father told her that the One who said oil should burn can say vinegar should burn. The lamp burned all Shabbos, and they took from it for havdalah.

title.en: The rebbe, the knife and the bread

retelling.en: A rebbe laughed at the scientists, asking why a knife cuts bread and not bread the knife. The scientist answers that the knife is hard and the bread soft. The rebbe said he understood more than that: why it is that a hard thing cuts a soft one, when it could just as well be the reverse.

title.en: Reb Hersh sweeps the beis medrash

retelling.en: Reb Mendel of Rimanov told his devoted attendant Reb Hersh not to come to sweep the beis medrash on the morning after his wedding. Reb Hersh came early anyway and swept it before davening. Reb Mendel said that when Reb Hersh sweeps the beis medrash he sweeps out the foreign thoughts, and he had not known how he would be able to daven without it.

title.en: The Midrash Shmuel and the Arizal

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital relates that the Midrash Shmuel once came in to the Arizal, and the Arizal stood up for him, to everyone's surprise. The Arizal asked which mitzvah he had just been busy with, and he answered pidyon shevuyim, redeeming captives. The Arizal said he had not stood for him, but for the soul of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, who was devoted to that mitzvah and whose soul was now in him to h…

title.en: The informer's kvittel and the Chozeh of Lublin

retelling.en: In a town an informer caused the Jews unbearable troubles, so they brought the Chozeh of Lublin a kvittel asking that he be removed from the world. The Chozeh said that the man named in the kvittel had a soul shining in all the worlds. Some time later they brought the kvittel again, and this time it took effect right away. Asked about the difference, the Chozeh answered that the first time the ma…

title.en: The chassid who came just to see his Rebbe

retelling.en: A chassid felt a strong need to see his Rebbe, not to speak with him but only to look at him, and traveled for days by horse and wagon. When he arrived the Rebbe came out to him and asked whether he loved him, and the chassid said he did. The Rebbe told him that his own love for his chassidim is nothing compared to Hashem's love for a notorious moser in a certain town.

title.en: The father who asked what name to give

retelling.en: A man who had a baby asked a Rebbe to tell him what name to give the child. The Rebbe answered that he would not take away the father's own opportunity for ruach hakodesh, and told him to choose the name himself.

title.en: Young men who became chassidish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he was at a place of baalei teshuvah and young men came to him. They had once worn rings and piercings on the nose and tongue, and had become chassidish young men. He says he would be ashamed of himself seeing how they daven and sing to Hashem with fire.

title.en: The Imrei Emes and 'kol hakelim'

retelling.en: The Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, returned exhausted from a long journey and stopped at his sister's home in a certain town, asking for a room to rest. Those in the house listened at the door and heard him learning Maseches Shabbos, the chapter 'Kol HaKelim'. He grew excited at the words 'kol hakelim', as if to say one must learn with all one's faculties, and learned on with great enthusiasm.

title.en: The Arizal rises before Rav Chaim Vital

retelling.en: Rav Chaim Vital relates that he once came in to the Arizal, who stood up for him. Asked which mitzvah he had done that day, he answered that he had been involved in redeeming captives. The Arizal explained that when a Jew does a mitzvah properly, the soul of a tzaddik who excelled in that mitzvah joins him; he had not stood for Rav Chaim Vital himself but for Rav Pinchas ben Yair, who excelled in…

title.en: A ba'al teshuvah descended from Rav Meir of Premishlan

retelling.en: A young man from a non-religious background became a true, observant Jew. His mother, seeing that he was doing well and was respectful, wanted to know where she came from, perhaps from a Jew with a beard. Through a bureau on 16th Avenue that researches lineage for a fee, she found that she is a descendant of Rav Meir of Premishlan. The Mashgiach says that this brings great nachas ruach in heaven,…

title.en: Yaakov wakes at the place of the Beis HaMikdash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Yaakov Avinu, not knowing it, went to sleep at the place of the Beis HaMikdash, and Hashem told him in a dream what place it was. When he awoke he called it the gate of heaven and was sorry, and Rashi explains that had he known, he would not have slept there.

title.en: A listener counts the pesukim of Ki Savo

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that when he once said this derashah before an audience, someone remarked that Ki Savo, the parsha before these, also has 122 pesukim. The Mashgiach calls it very fitting, since Ki Savo ushers in the season of teshuvah.

title.en: Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky and the non-religious father

retelling.en: On an airplane from Eretz Yisroel, a non-religious man saw how Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky's children treated him with respect, and asked why: his own children want nothing to do with him. Rav Yaakov answered that in the man's world every generation counts itself more advanced than the one before, with better computers and the like, so the children look down on their parents. With us, the generations g…

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the plain Jews

retelling.en: The Ruzhiner came to a town to visit his chassidim, and the head of the community asked him to come with his followers to the big town shul. The Ruzhiner said there would not be room for everyone, and the head of the community answered that they would not let in the plain Jews. The Ruzhiner replied that he himself was a plain Jew, as were his father, his grandfather the Malach and his great-grand…

title.en: Yosef and Potiphar's wife

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from Chazal that Potiphar's wife pressed Yosef not once but for an entire year, changing her clothing several times a day. She threatened to starve him, and he refused. She threatened to blind him, to chain him bent over, and to throw him into prison, which she later did; to each threat he answered with a pasuk that Hashem gives sight to the blind, straightens the bent, and…

title.en: Why do we shout in davening?

retelling.en: Someone once asked the Mashgiach why they shout during davening. The Mashgiach notes it was the custom in places like Karlin, Stolin and Slonim in earlier times. He asked the questioner in return whether he does not shout at Neilah, explaining that one does not decide to shout; it shouts by itself.

title.en: The tzaddik learning on a Teves night

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that the Bnei Yissaschar brings, about one of the great tzaddikim, that he learned Torah at night during tekufas Teves, at the time of nittel. A dog came into his house. The Mashgiach tells it in connection with the sefarim's statement that this period is under the rule of the 'dogs'.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva and Bar Koziva

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbi Akiva thought Bar Koziva was Moshiach and supported him. When Bar Koziva was killed, Rabbi Akiva knew he was not Moshiach. The Mashgiach notes that the Rambam, who does not usually bring stories, brings this one to show that even Rabbi Akiva did not know who Moshiach is.

title.en: The kvitel about the informer

retelling.en: Chassidim gave the Lubliner a kvitel about an informer from whom they were suffering. He took it and said that the man shines in all the worlds, and that he does not understand what is happening. Later they gave the kvitel again; the next morning he saw it, cursed the man, and the informer was removed from the world. When they asked, the Rebbe explained that the first time they had handed him the…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's Shovavim talk in Williamsburg

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that over sixty years earlier, when he lived in Williamsburg, people went to the Satmar Rav during the six weeks of Shovavim. When the Satmar Rav spoke then, the beis medrash was packed with perhaps thousands of people standing, and there was not a dry eye. He aroused the crowd to teshuvah, since it is a time of teshuvah.

title.en: The Arizal and Rav Chaim Vital on the last generation

retelling.en: Rav Chaim Vital relates that the Arizal told him how great he was, even more than earlier great ones. Rav Chaim Vital protested that compared with the level of the Tannaim and Amoraim he was nothing at all. The Arizal answered that it is because he lives in such a late generation, and the Mashgiach adds that today this is all the more so.

title.en: Rabbah bar Shila meets Eliyahu

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara: Rabbah bar Shila met Eliyahu and asked what Hashem was doing. Eliyahu said Hashem was saying Torah in the name of all the Rabbis but not Rabbi Meir, because he learned from Acher. Rabbah bar Shila answered that Rabbi Meir found a pomegranate, ate the inside and threw away the peel. Eliyahu then said that Hashem now quotes Rabbi Meir.

title.en: Rav Hamnuna and Rav Chisda at the meal

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara in Berachos: Rav Hamnuna and Rav Chisda were at a meal and were served dates and pomegranates. Rav Hamnuna made the blessing on the dates, and Rav Chisda asked why, since the pomegranate comes first in the passuk. Rav Hamnuna answered that the date is second to Eretz and the pomegranate fifth. Rav Chisda was greatly moved by the answer.

title.en: The Scud attacks on Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: When Scud missiles were fired at Eretz Yisroel and people feared that Saddam would send gas bombs, those without adequate emunah built sealed rooms to run to. The Gedolei Yisroel said not to run to the sealed rooms and not to buy the masks, but to sit and learn, and they would be helped. The Mashgiach says that is what happened.

title.en: The Mashgiach opens Graetz's history

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a young man he once came upon Graetz's famous multi-volume history of the Jews. He opened it exactly at the account of the splitting of the sea. Graetz wrote that the event cannot be denied, since it is a historical fact, but that it happened to coincide with an exceptionally strong wind, stronger than any in history, which split the sea.

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the maskil

retelling.en: A maskil came to the Ruzhiner and claimed that the splitting of the sea was no miracle, only a strong wind that came at that moment. The Ruzhiner answered that he believes with complete emunah that it was a miracle. But by the maskil's own account it was an even greater miracle: that just when the Jews fled Egypt and the Egyptians pursued them, the sea split by a wind.

title.en: The doctor who taught evolution

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions a visit to a prominent doctor who began explaining to him about monkeys as the ancestors of man. The Mashgiach answered that he had come for medical advice, not to learn evolution.

title.en: The old Jew who had to wait six hours

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of an old Jew who had eaten meat and then wanted to drink a coffee. When he was told he must wait six hours, he grew angry. The Mashgiach explains that the anger came from his desire: the very existence of the Jew demands that a person set aside his desires, and that is what he could not bear.

title.en: Naftali runs for the deed

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal's account that when a dispute arose with Esav over the burial place, a deed was needed from Egypt, and Naftali, the swift one, was sent to bring it.

title.en: Rabbi Avraham of Ciechanow drinks wine

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions Rabbi Avraham of Ciechanow, a tzaddik and a great baal halachah. He did not want to drink wine, as it would disturb his avodah, yet he drank in order to fulfil the mitzvah of making the days ones of mishteh v'simcha.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's struggle with the Satan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Ohr HaChaim, in Parshas Vayechi, tells of a struggle he had with the Satan, who came to him in two forms, a masculine and a feminine one. The masculine one he overcame at once, but against the feminine one he had a very hard struggle and did not fully win. The Mashgiach uses it to show that in the side of tumah the feminine is the stronger.

title.en: Gedolim learning during the missile attacks

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that some years earlier, during the war with Iraq, every apartment had a sealed room against a gas attack, and building one is now required by law. When the missiles were being fired, gedolei Yisrael sat in the beis medrash and learned and did not run to the sealed rooms. He mentions Rav Chaim Kanievsky and others sitting near the window, unconcerned, because the Torah was t…

title.en: Chizkiyahu sleeps on Pesach night

retelling.en: On Pesach night, when Sancheriv's army surrounded Yerushalayim and planned to attack the next day, the Jews brought the korban Pesach and King Chizkiyahu went to sleep. The Mashgiach stresses that a nervous, frightened person cannot sleep, but Chizkiyahu slept without any fear because he had emunah and bitachon.

title.en: Mordechai and the children's pesukim

retelling.en: When Haman's decree came, Mordechai met a child and asked him to tell the passuk he had learned in cheder. The child said 'al tira mipachad pisom', and Mordechai rejoiced, along with the other two pesukim the children told him. The Mashgiach adds that 'pachad pisom' equals in gematria Haman ben Hamedasa ha'Agagi, so Mordechai knew at once that the passuk was about Haman and that there was no need…

title.en: Avigail stops David from killing Naval

retelling.en: While fleeing from Shaul, David came to the place of Naval of Carmel and asked him for food for his men, and Naval refused. David set out to kill him, and Avigail, Naval's wife, came out to meet him. She argued that he was not yet king in the eyes of all Israel, since Shaul still reigned, and he agreed and thanked her. Soon after, Naval died, and David married Avigail.

title.en: Purim Krakow

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that many towns in Europe, and especially Sephardic communities, had their own Purim for a miracle that happened to them. In Krakow there was a great miracle when the Jews were saved from a priest who was an enemy of the Jews. The day of his downfall was called Purim Krakow, and they used to rejoice and make a seudah on it.

title.en: Rabbi Avraham of Tshechanov's revi'is

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbi Avraham of Tshechanov was careful on Purim to pour a revi'is of wine and drink it, and with that he fulfilled the obligation. The Mashgiach adds that the Polish revi'is cups were very small.

title.en: Yehoash, saved in the Kodesh HaKodashim

retelling.en: Atalyah set out to kill the whole royal line of Beis David. The infant Yehoash was rescued by Yehoyada the Kohen Gadol and hidden for six years in the Kodesh HaKodashim. At seven he was brought out and crowned, and he did what was right as long as Yehoyada lived. After Yehoyada's death his servants told him he must be a god for having survived six years in the Kodesh HaKodashim, and he accepted i…

title.en: Why the Yaaros Devash davened long

retelling.en: The Mashgiach reads a letter from the Yaaros Devash written by Rabbi Yonasan Eibeschutz to the Rav of Königsberg, who had heard that he davened at length. Rabbi Yonasan answers that he has shiurim to give his students, yet he needs time to collect his thoughts and attach his soul in tefillah. While the congregation was already saying kedushah he was still in the middle of Shemoneh Esrei, and his…

title.en: The servant, the gems and the princess

retelling.en: A king loved a faithful servant and, after the servant died, extended his kindness to his children. One son was sent to a distant land to mine gems for the king but neglected the work; at each year's day of inventory the finance minister, his friend at court, pleaded for him. One year the minister was absent and the princess, a relative whom the son had abused and thrown down the stairs, took ove…

title.en: The poritz's sled ride on sugar

retelling.en: A powerful poritz in Russia, always seeking new pleasures, wanted to go sled riding on an August afternoon. He had hundreds of his vassals carry heavy bags of sugar to a meadow and spread it like snow, and rode over it in a horse-drawn sled. A chassid told his Rebbe of the poritz's enjoyment, and the Rebbe answered that it could in no way compare to the pleasure he had on Shabbos morning saying N…

title.en: Reb Moshe Leib Sassover remembers Nishmas

retelling.en: Reb Moshe Leib Sassover was active in redeeming Jews whom the paritzim threw into dungeons for failing to pay their rent. Once he came to a poritz on the day of a feast, which was a fast day for him, and the waiters carried a very costly hot dish whose aroma was so tempting that he felt himself in danger. He later recounted that he saved himself by recalling how he says Nishmas on Shabbos, a plea…

title.en: The ten-year-old who leapt from the window

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that when the tzaddik who had just passed away was ten years old, on Purim his sister came into his room in disguise. He did not realize it was his sister, and rather than remain with her he jumped out of the window, two floors down. The Mashgiach brings it as an example of his extreme care in kedushah.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer answers a hard question quickly

retelling.en: The Ksav Sofer once saw his father, the Chasam Sofer, answer a difficult halachic question in a few minutes, and asked how he could write so quickly on so hard a question. The Chasam Sofer answered that in every generation there is one Jew who decides the questions of Klal Yisrael, and in this generation that is he. Even if someone refutes his proof, the halacha will not change.

title.en: The bochur who said all of Tehillim before davening

retelling.en: A Rebbe was told of a bochur who rose early on Shabbos and said all of Tehillim sweetly before davening. The Rebbe asked whether he had been at the Friday night tisch, and when he heard that he had not, he waved it off with his hand. Coming to the tisch and singing zemiros with joy and fervor, he said, is more important than rising early to say all of Tehillim.

title.en: Rav and the butcher on Erev Yom Kippur

retelling.en: A butcher was disrespectful to Rav and, out of arrogance, did not come to ask his forgiveness. On Erev Yom Kippur, when he still did not come, Rav went himself and stood in front of the butcher shop. The butcher ignored him and kept chopping meat; a bone flew into his throat and he died. The Mashgiach calls it a punishment for not using the opportunity when Rav made himself available.

title.en: The Arvei Nachal's mashal of the king's servant

retelling.en: A king had a servant who stayed faithful when all his subjects abandoned him, so the king brought him into the palace and set him over all the ministers. In time the servant forgot his privilege, disobeyed, and was expelled. The king's two children always argued in his favor at his judgment, until he quarreled with them and they refused. A wise man told him to fall at their feet and ask forgivene…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mother

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mother liked to talk a lot, also on Shabbos. He told her that today is Shabbos. The words were said with such kedushah that she was overcome by the kedushah of Shabbos and never again spoke an extra word on Shabbos.

title.en: The lovesick man in the Gemara

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara about a man whose heart was taken with a certain woman until he fell ill. The doctors said he could not live unless his desire was satisfied, and then suggested that he at least speak with her from behind a fence. The Sages answered that he should rather die, because even these are offshoots of giluy arayos.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's dream

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Ohr HaChaim told of a dream in which he fought the male of the sitra achra and threw him down easily. When the female of the sitra achra came, he had to strain with all his strength, and he threw her down many levels, but not as far as the male. The Ohr HaChaim connects this to the passuk about the two redemptions.

title.en: The Ruzhiner asks the Sanzer Rav about moving

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Ruzhiner asked the Sanzer Rav whether he may move to another, nicer dwelling, and the Sanzer answered, why not. Then the Sanzer realized that the Ruzhiner meant he wished to leave this world for the upper world, and wanted to take back his answer, but the Ruzhiner said it was too late, he had already ruled. The Mashgiach brings it to show that the court below decides.

title.en: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon on Rome

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara: Rabbi Yehuda praised the Roman kingdom for its roads and works, Rabbi Yose kept silent, and Rabbi Shimon said they did everything only for themselves. When the words reached the government, it decreed that Rabbi Yehuda be raised, Rabbi Yose be exiled to Tzippori, and Rabbi Shimon be killed. Rabbi Shimon fled and hid in a cave for thirteen years.

title.en: The Gostininer knocks on the Kotzker's door

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Gostininer was once not so great. In the Kotzker's last years he had locked himself in, and people were afraid to approach him. One Purim the Gostininer took courage and knocked hard until the Kotzker opened and asked what he wanted; he answered that he was poor and wanted 'matanos la'evyonim'. The Kotzker let him in for several hours, and he came out a different pe…

title.en: The boy whose covered head guarded him

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's account of a child whose mother kept his head covered, because the stargazers had said he would be a thief. She told him to cover his head so that he would have fear of Heaven. Once his head became uncovered, and at that moment he took from a fig tree. The Mashgiach explains that covering the head guards the place of holiness so that the outside forces have no ho…

title.en: The stained suit and the expert cleaner

retelling.en: In the Yismach Moshe's parable, a man invited to the king buys a fine suit. While he handles it, tar from a roof repair gets on it; turpentine removes most of it but leaves a small smudge. He could wear it in the street or the office, but not before the king, so he goes to an expert chemist with an expensive cleaning agent who removes every trace.

title.en: Chaim and Yankel on Yom Kippur

retelling.en: Chaim enjoys Yom Kippur, while his neighbor Yankel keeps looking at his watch, waiting to eat. After Ma'ariv both come home and eat at the same time. Chaim lost nothing, and Yankel only spoiled his Yom Kippur, which could have been far greater had he kept it with joy.

title.en: A tzaddik reads 'Napoleon' in the Megillah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a certain great tzaddik, on a Purim when he was waiting for Napoleon to suffer a defeat, read the verse 'ki nafol tipol lefanav' during the Megillah reading as 'Napoleon tipol lefanav'. From then on, the Mashgiach says, it was decreed that Napoleon would fall. He brings it to show that all great salvations lie in Purim.

title.en: Oranges for a sick child

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he was a small boy, orange juice was very expensive and a family could not afford it. Once, when he was sick with a high fever, he was given some oranges, because a sick child needs something special. He compares this to Purim: after the Jews lost the Beis HaMikdash, Hashem gave them Purim as a special treat.

title.en: Mordechai HaTzaddik at Reb Pinchas of Koretz's seudah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that one Purim, for some reason, only one person remained with Reb Pinchas of Koretz while everyone else went elsewhere. A Jew came in, there was great joy and dancing, and it was later found out that the guest was Mordechai HaTzaddik. The Mashgiach draws from it that Mordechai comes to every Jewish seudah together with Esther.

title.en: R' Elazar of Amsterdam and the queen

retelling.en: When the dikes broke, the queen asked R' Elazar of Amsterdam to bring salvation for the city, as he would bring miracles for the country. She found him on Purim sitting with his students, drinking and singing. She said she knew that salvation came from him, but asked why he did not say Tehillim. He answered that on Purim one achieves it through drinking, dancing and rejoicing with Hashem.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe's second Purim seudah

retelling.en: The Slonimer Rebbe in Yerushalayim, R' Shmuel, would make a Purim seudah at the end of Shushan Purim, as his father had done. One year he announced that he would also make a seudah on the night of Purim, so that there would be two Purim seudos and the people would gather twice. His reason was that the Jews need great salvation, and for that more merits are needed.

title.en: The Avnei Nezer's father learned all Purim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells how the father of the Avnei Nezer merited such a son. On Purim, when the whole country was busy with mishloach manos, matanos la'evyonim and feasting and rejoicing, he sat and learned. This was something that stood out in the whole country, and for this he merited a son like the Avnei Nezer.

title.en: The Chabadnik who davened until four

retelling.en: The Mashgiach knew Jews who davened with great sweetness, among them a Chabadnik who davened in their shtiebel. He davened with great taste, weeping, with two streams of tears flowing from his eyes. He would stop in the middle of davening to hear the Torah reading and then continue, and on a winter day he came to Minchah at four o'clock.

title.en: The soul that found its tikkun on Pesach

retelling.en: The Imrei Yosef of Spinka told his Chassidim of a young man, and they knew he meant himself, who on the second night of Pesach, after the Haggadah, wished to keep praising Hashem and remembered that Haman was hanged that night, so he read the Megillah. In the middle a soul came to him for a tikkun: on Purim souls without a tikkun come to a heichal in Gan Eden and receive one even without merit, b…

title.en: Mordechai rejoices with a lonely tzaddik

retelling.en: Two tzaddikim lived in one town, and on Purim the whole crowd went to one of them, R' Pinchas'l, to sing and dance, while the other sat alone. A Jew came in to him and began rejoicing with him, singing and dancing so beautifully that all those sitting with R' Pinchas'l ran over to hear. That Jew was Mordechai.

title.en: Rav Yisroel of Vizhnitz and the window-shade string

retelling.en: A great tzaddik two generations ago, Rav Yisroel of Vizhnitz, stood near the window in his shul on Rosh Hashanah and played with the string of the window shade in the middle of Shemoneh Esrei. A chassid wondered how he could do such a thing. When he finished Shemoneh Esrei, the Rebbe turned to the chassid and told him he had held the string so that a time should come when even that string would k…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's Purim tish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that the Satmar Rav used to drink cup after cup on Purim until he became drunk and had to be carried out. His whole Purim tish took about twenty minutes: he washed, ate a little challah and fish, and began drinking. In those minutes he spoke lofty words and secrets of the Torah that he never revealed the rest of the year, though his sefarim are full of halachah and sweet de…

title.en: The Shomer Emunim and the silver ke'arah

retelling.en: On Purim, the Shomer Emunim, a man with ruach hakodesh, suddenly announced that whoever needed a yeshuah with children could come to him, but he wanted a ke'arah for Pesach. One man, in the poverty of Yerushalayim then, bought a copper ke'arah plated with silver; the Rebbe threw it to the other end of the beis medrash, calling it falsehood because it fooled people into thinking it was silver. Ano…

title.en: The tzaddik who skipped mayim emtza'im

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, in the name of the Satmar Rav, that a great tzaddik who was a rav had the custom of washing his hands between fish and meat. Once he did not do it, and his rebbetzin asked him why he had not washed. He took this to heart and searched until he found the root: he had spoken with one of the followers of Shabsai Tzvi and it had left some confusion in his mind. The Mashgiach exp…

title.en: The chassan who left the Stoliner Rebbe's minyan

retelling.en: At the Stoliner Rebbe's court, a chassan during his Shabbos of sheva brachos had to go daven in another beis medrash, and came to take leave of the Rebbe. The Rebbe asked him how a young man could permit himself to leave 'our souls' on the first Shabbos after his wedding. It did not help, and he went; the Mashgiach adds that he davened there until the Torah reading and then went to the shtibel.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam and the broken dam

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, from the seforim, that Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam was respected at the royal court, and the queen would ask him to daven when help was needed. Once on Purim a dam burst and the whole country was in danger, so the queen sent messengers to ask him to pray. He was sitting at the Purim seudah, had barrels of wine brought, and everyone drank, danced and rejoiced. Through some natur…

title.en: The man whose blessings were all fulfilled

retelling.en: In the stretch on the Chiddushei HaRim, the Mashgiach tells of a certain Jew who, in the merit of a great kindness he did for a tzaddik, received the blessing that all his blessings would be fulfilled. Heaven did not want him to hand out blessings freely, so he was made into a drunkard, and after that he could not give blessings except in isolated cases.

title.en: A Rebbe teaches the five parts of the soul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he was a bochur, a Rebbe, who usually spoke only in his own room to whoever came to him, once came into the beis medrash. He interrupted the learning and spoke about the five parts of the Jewish soul: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah and yechidah, the yechidah being where a Jew is connected with Hashem.

title.en: The tailor who bought the fish

retelling.en: On Erev Yom Kippur a Jewish tailor went to buy fish, and the governor's servant came to buy fish too, but there was only one large fish.
