They bid against each other until the tailor bought it for twelve dinarim. The servant told the governor the fish had gone for twelve dinarim, and the governor summoned the Jew. The Jew explained that since Jews cannot eat on Yom Kippur, they rejoice with choice…

title.en: The Beis Aharon and the simple Jew's Shir HaShirim

people: the Beis Aharon (Rabbi Aharon of Karlin)

retelling.en: The Beis Aharon once entered the beis medrash on Erev Shabbos and found a very simple Jew, a chassid who was no talmid chacham, saying Shir HaShirim with great feeling. He asked him, Yankel, whether he knew the meaning of Shir HaShirim. The man answered that he did not, but the words themselves are so sweet. The Beis Aharon valued him greatly: he had a pure soul and felt that holiness comes out o…

title.en: The Satmar Rav on Purim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that he saw the Satmar Rav become truly drunk on Purim. At the Purim tish he drank again and again and began saying Torah of a kind he did not say all year, secrets of the Torah, while all year he would speak on the plain meaning. When it seemed he would soon collapse he was carried to his room to sleep, and five or six hours later, around two or three in the morning, he ca…

title.en: The Rashash's broken watch

retelling.en: Rabbi Yisrael Salanter once came to Vilna and visited the Rashash. The Rashash's watch had broken, and he said he needed a watch to keep the times of his shiurim and his tefillos, and believed with complete faith that Hashem would bring him one. There was a knock at the door, and a Jewish soldier came in, back from the war. A comrade of his had been shot and, knowing he would die, gave him his go…

title.en: The child whom nobody looked for

retelling.en: A small child came crying to Reb Baruch'l, who asked him why he was crying. The child answered that he had hidden himself and nobody came to look for him. Reb Baruch'l burst into tears and said that Ribono shel Olam says the same: He hides, and nobody looks for Him.

title.en: Rav Shraga Feivel speaks in the beis medrash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that close to seventy years earlier, as a teenager in Williamsburg, he saw Rav Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz do something he never did before or after: he walked into the beis medrash in the middle of the learning, clapped on the shtender and announced he would speak. He normally spoke only in his room to those who came. During the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah he spoke for about three m…

title.en: Tzaddikim held back from Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says great Jews wanted to go to Eretz Yisroel and Heaven did not let them. The Ba'al Shem Tov set out and was shown from Above that he must turn back. The Vilna Gaon wanted to go and had to return, and the Chofetz Chaim was already packed with his bags and had to unpack.

title.en: Shluchim who came to 770 for Yom Tov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that shluchim came to 770 for Yom Tov and the Lubavitcher Rebbe was displeased with them. He showed them their shlichus again and asked what they were doing there.

title.en: Deveikus of the Sanzer Rav and Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes the Sanzer Rav's deveikus: he would throw back his head, not know what was happening with him and not hear when spoken to. Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz said that between Yom Kippur and Sukkos, speaking to him was like speaking to a wall, because Yom Kippur had brought him to a state where he did not know in which world he was.

title.en: Havdalah on wine and the hole in the pocket

retelling.en: On the Gemara that one who makes havdalah over wine on Motzei Shabbos will have sons, someone told a rav that he made havdalah on wine every week but had no sons. The rav answered that he is given sons, but there is a hole in the pocket and they fall out: his other deeds undo the segulah. The Mashgiach applies this to the earlier years of Shabbos Erev Pesach in which Moshiach did not come.

title.en: How Hillel became Nasi

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara that one year Erev Pesach fell on Shabbos and the leaders did not know whether the korban Pesach overrides Shabbos. Hillel resolved the question, and because of this he was made Nasi. From him descends the line of nesi'im, Rabban Gamliel and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, all from Beis Dovid.

title.en: The Kotzker chassid who borrowed a Father

retelling.en: A chassid of Kotzk, visiting another tzaddik, came into his beis medrash and cried out 'Oy, Tatte!' The tzaddik questioned him on how he could call Hashem his father. When the chassid returned to Kotzk and told the Rebbe what happened, the Kotzker answered that one borrows a father: since he will be good, he may already now call Hashem 'Father'.

title.en: The Tzeduki Kohen Gadol

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara about a Tzeduki who managed, at great cost, to be appointed Kohen Gadol. He prepared the ketores outside and brought it in already burning. Afterwards he was found dead outside, with worms coming out of his nose.

title.en: Throwing off the wheels

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a mashal from the sefarim of a group of Jews in a hurry, traveling in a weak old wagon pulled by a weak old horse. Going up a hill, the horses could not pull, so everyone threw off whatever he could do without to lighten the wagon. One not-so-clever passenger suggested throwing off the heaviest thing, the wheels, but without the wheels the wagon cannot move at all.

title.en: The Jews' complaint to Mordechai on the night of the king's sleeplessness

retelling.en: As the Mashgiach reads it from the Targum, on the night the king could not sleep the Jews gathered around Mordechai and complained that his refusal to bow to Haman had brought the whole trouble upon them. Mordechai answered that Haman wore a garment with images painted on its front and back, so bowing to him would be bowing to an idol. Hearing this, the Jews fell silent and complained no more.

title.en: The Arizal and the Beis Yosef

retelling.en: The Beis Yosef used to fall asleep at the Arizal's derashos. When he asked the Arizal to learn the secrets of the Torah with him, the Arizal refused, telling him that he had come into the world to teach halachos to Jews, and that this was the root of his soul; he should not enter what was not his root.

title.en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe's 'hurrah' and Stalin's fall

retelling.en: Fifty years earlier, Stalin had made a libel against the Jewish doctors of Moscow and prepared trains to take Jews to Siberia, and Jews were very worried. At a Purim seudah the Lubavitcher Rebbe told a story from the time of the Rebbe Rashab: an old chassid who knew nothing of politics went to the mikvah, put on his gartel, voted as the Rebbe wished, and when the crowd shouted 'hurrah' for their…

title.en: Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam and the queen of Holland

retelling.en: In the days of Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam, the queen knew that in times of trouble one should go to the Jews to pray to the Jewish G-d. When a dike broke and the sea threatened the city, which lies below sea level, she sent to him to pray, and the danger passed and the dike was repaired. She came herself to thank him, expecting to find him saying Tehillim with his students, and found them sitting,…

title.en: The bachurim from Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he saw what an organization for drawing distant Jews close does in Eretz Yisrael. Bachurim came to him and he spoke to them: fine Jewish young men who not long before had been deep in the klipah. Torah and emunah, he says, rescued them.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's last drasha in Yerushalayim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from a man who was present at the last drasha the Satmar Rav gave in Yerushalayim, when he sensed he would not return. The Satmar Rav wept greatly and said it was very hard for him to leave Yerushalayim. Yet he would remain in Yerushalayim, because the Chesed L'Avraham writes that one who gives money for the upkeep of Yerushalayim is as if he were there.

title.en: The Maggid's illness and the jewel for the prince

retelling.en: The Maggid saw writings in which his teachings had been copied lying around on the ground, and it displeased him as a disgrace to holiness; at that time he became ill. The Baal HaTanya told a parable: a king's son fell ill, and the doctors said only a precious stone at the top of the king's crown could cure him. The king refused to scrape off even a piece until all other cures failed, and by then…

title.en: Mordechai steps on Haman

retelling.en: When Mordechai went up onto the horse, Haman bent down so that Mordechai could step up on him, and Mordechai gave him a kick. Haman quoted to him the verse that one should not rejoice when one's enemy falls. Mordechai answered that this applies among Jews, but for Haman the opposite is written: 'v'atah al bamoseimo tidroch'.

title.en: The wise man and the queen's wine

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara's story of a great chacham who was always called to the king's court for debates and always won, but was not handsome. The queen remarked on such wisdom in such an ugly vessel, and he kept quiet. The next day he asked her how the royal wine was stored, and she said in clay containers; he suggested gold containers for royal wine, and when it was served the wine had s…

title.en: Adam HaRishon and the shortening days

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that after the sin of the Eitz HaDaas, Adam HaRishon saw each day grow shorter and each night longer. He thought that because of his sin Hashem was darkening the world and it was doomed to eternal night, and he grieved. At the tekufah, the longest night, he saw the next morning that the sun rose earlier and the days began to grow, and he made that day a festival, w…

title.en: Thirty boys receive a bris in Russia

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he spoke with someone who had just returned from Russia, where a collective bris was made for thirty boys aged sixteen to eighteen. Under the Communists there had been no milah, and now, returning to Yiddishkeit, they underwent the painful bris as grown boys with mesiras nefesh.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's mezuzos

retelling.en: The Ba'al HaTanya asked a Jew traveling to a certain town to order mezuzos for him from a sofer there, and the man ordered mezuzos for himself too. When he came to collect them, the sofer showed him which were for the Rebbe and which for him; thinking the sofer wrote differently for the Ba'al HaTanya, the man swapped them. The Ba'al HaTanya looked at the mezuzos and asked whether these were writt…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov on Rosh Chodesh Nissan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Ba'al Shem Tov used to seclude himself on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, locked in his room. He would then appoint the angels who are the ministers of the nations, and if one did not please him he would lower him and set up another, since Nissan is the Rosh Hashanah for kings.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's pinkas

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Bnei Yissaschar that the Chozeh of Lublin would take a new pinkas each Rosh Chodesh Nissan. On the first day he wrote all that would happen in Nissan, on the second all that would happen in Iyar, and so on, then sealed it and let no one look until the end of the year, when everything was found written. One year he wrote only the first four days and would write no mor…

title.en: The Lechovitcher Rebbe's messenger

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that on the night of bedikas chametz the Lechovitcher Rebbe sent a messenger to announce in a certain beis medrash that one must search the 'holes and cracks'. The messenger obeyed, went in, banged on the table and announced it. A great liveliness came over the people there, because a living tzaddik can put life into others, and that evening they all searched the holes and cra…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe and the korban Pesach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells that the Yismach Moshe asked to be shown what the Midrashim say, that even nowadays Eliyahu HaNavi offers korbanos, and he was shown Eliyahu in the garments of a kohen offering them. The tzaddik who retold this said that tonight, too, a korban Pesach is brought, and Eliyahu brings a piece to each tzaddik. When he finished saying this he ate his afikoman with such desire that…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim after the seder

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Divrei Chaim once sat down after the seder and stroked his stomach, with tears flowing from his eyes. He said that his innards were full of holy names: of the matzah, the four cups, the maror, korech and the afikoman. The Mashgiach explains that the seder had become part of him, absorbed into his physical being.

title.en: Baron Rothschild's Pesach house

retelling.en: Baron Rothschild, a wealthy Jew who did much for Klal Yisrael, once visited the Divrei Chaim of Sanz, who received him warmly. When talk turned to Pesach, the Baron boasted that he had a special Pesach house that no one entered all year and that chametz never touched, so he knew his Pesach was kosher. The Divrei Chaim answered that his holy Rebbes gave their lives for every mitzvah, yet had no Pe…

title.en: The wheat kernel in the tzaddik's soup

retelling.en: A tzaddik worked hard to make a truly kosher Pesach and cleaned his whole house, certain there was no chametz. At the seder, after the matzah, a soup was served and a wheat kernel was floating in it. Distraught, he asked a question in Heaven, as great tzaddikim could, why this happened to him and how. He was answered that the pot stood under the chimney and a bird dropped the kernel into it, and…

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's Nissan notebook

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar, a disciple of the Chozeh of Lublin, testifies that every Rosh Chodesh Nissan the Chozeh had a notebook brought to him. On each of the first twelve days of Nissan he wrote down everything that would happen in the corresponding month, then sealed the book; at the end of the year he let his disciples look, and everything had come true. One year he wrote only for the first four d…

title.en: Osnas and Yosef

retelling.en: A child was born to Dina from Shechem, and the brothers wanted to harm her. Yaakov placed the child in the desert in a thornbush with a charm around her neck saying she was from his family, and angels carried her to Egypt, where the childless Potiphar adopted her and named her Osnas. When Yosef rode out as ruler, the girls of Egypt threw their jewelry at him to make him look up, but he did not lo…

title.en: The Chafetz Chaim on three wars

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from a new sefer of Reb Nosson Wachtfogel on Chanukah, that the Chafetz Chaim was asked during the First World War whether it was the war of Moshiach. He answered no: there would be a pause, then another war that would also not be final, and with the third war Moshiach would come.

title.en: The Avnei Nezer teaches his talmid

retelling.en: The Avnei Nezer, the Sochatchover Rebbe, told a talmid to accept kvitlach and help people. When the talmid said he was not a rebbe, the Avnei Nezer showed him that in this Tosafos and in this piece of Gemara lies a yeshuah for a particular need, such as a childless woman.

title.en: King David and the frog

retelling.en: When King David finished Sefer Tehillim he felt uplifted and said that no creature sings as he does. A frog came to him and said that its song was greater than his. It added that at the seashore there is a creature that eats it when hungry, and it offers itself to be eaten.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Arach and the ten tribes

retelling.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Arach went to a place of the ten tribes known for its pleasures, fruits and baths, to bring them back. He was drawn after them and forgot his learning, and when called up to read 'hachodesh hazeh lachem' he read 'hacharesh haya libam'. The Sages davened for him and his learning returned. The Mashgiach explains that he grasped the passuk of his own root and was lamenting that thei…

title.en: The Chazon Ish's story of the light on Shabbos

retelling.en: The Chazon Ish told of a respectable Jew in Eretz Yisroel who came to shul, bought aliyos and kept Shabbos. An important official agreed to visit him on Friday night, and he prepared fruit and waited, imagining the newspaper reports. A child passed by and switched off the electricity, leaving the house dark. He could not restrain himself and turned the light back on. The Mashgiach explains that h…

title.en: Rav Gifter takes out the garbage

retelling.en: A young couple came to Rav Gifter with an argument: the wife, busy with the children, wanted her husband to take out the garbage, and he said that as a ben Torah it was beneath the honor of the Torah. Rav Gifter ruled that the husband was right. Ten minutes after they went home there was a knock at the door, and it was Rav Gifter. He said that the wife is busy with the babies and cannot take out…

title.en: Reb Arele lights the Chanukah lights

retelling.en: Reb Arele was always very weak; his daily food was a glass of borsht, which he would bring back up, living on the little that remained. Once he grew so weak that he could not move a finger, and the doctor said that this was the end. It was a night of Chanukah, and he signaled that the menorah be brought to his bed. With the greatest mesirus nefesh he said the brachah word by word, sat up, stood,…

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's Nissan pinkas

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar relates that the Chozeh of Lublin would write in a pinkas on Rosh Chodesh Nissan what would happen in Nissan, on the second day what would happen in Iyar, and so on. Afterwards his followers looked in the pinkas and saw that it was fulfilled. One year he wrote only for the first four days and stopped, and that year he passed away on Tisha B'Av. The Mashgiach explains that he d…

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech planting peppers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Shlomo HaMelech knew how to plant peppers in any land, because he knew that everything draws from Eretz Yisrael. He knew which channel from Eretz Yisrael fed each country, and planted the peppers along that channel.

title.en: The Ohev Yisrael and the souls that would be lost

retelling.en: The Ohev Yisrael sat at his table and said he was able to bring Moshiach but did not want to, because if Moshiach came now some souls not yet ready would be lost. One of the rabbanim at the table asked why all of Klal Yisrael should suffer for the sake of a few souls. The Ohev Yisrael answered him: and if you are one of those souls that would be lost if Moshiach came now?

title.en: The Chasam Sofer during Napoleon's war

retelling.en: When Napoleon came to conquer the land where the Chasam Sofer lived, there was a great battle at Pressburg lasting some months, and many gentiles were killed by cannon fire from both sides, while the Jews were saved. During the war the Chasam Sofer instituted saying the long Vehu Rachum, Avinu Malkeinu and chapters of Tehillim daily. When the war ended he gathered the people to thank Hashem with…

title.en: The Lithuanian Jew who thanked for everything

retelling.en: The Chozeh of Lublin said of a great, upright Lithuanian Jew that his avodah was precious in heaven because he thanked Hashem for every small thing. When a glass fell and did not break, he thanked Hashem; when he was handed coffee that had not gone cold, he thanked Hashem.

title.en: Rav Yonasan Steif and the breeze

retelling.en: Rav Yonasan Steif spent a summer at a camp, before there was air conditioning. On a very hot day he sat outside speaking to talmidim, and when a small breeze came he stopped in the middle and thanked the Ribono shel Olam for the breeze.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's tears when thanking the Kaiser

retelling.en: When the Kaiser in Austria granted the Jews freedom from their special restrictions and taxes, the community leaders asked the Chasam Sofer to gather the people to thank him, and he agreed and gave a derashah. He thanked Hashem and the kind king, and then wept and told a mashal of a king who banished his son and sent him money now and then; when the king sent engineers to build the son a fine hou…

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the heretic on kriyas Yam Suf

retelling.en: A heretic argued with the Ruzhiner that the splitting of the sea, a historical fact, came from natural causes: winds, the moon and tides. The Ruzhiner answered that this would be an even greater nes, since exactly then the winds blew, the moon shone and the sand dried, exactly when the Jews left Mitzrayim and Pharaoh chased them, and the phenomena stopped exactly when the last Jew came out. He co…

title.en: The poritz who spread sugar to sled in summer

people: the Beis Aharon (Rabbi Aharon of Karlin)

retelling.en: A chassid who worked for a poritz came to his Rebbe, apparently the Beis Aharon, and told him the poritz had gone mad: in the middle of August he wanted to ride his sled. The Mashgiach adds what his father told him, that in Poland and Russia sugar was so precious that people drank tea holding a small piece of sugar under the tongue, and imagined the king drinking tea poured into a hole dug in a l…

title.en: A chassid's Pesach preparation

retelling.en: In the poor shtetlach of earlier generations, people would greet each other before Pesach by asking how they stood with Pesach, meaning matzos and expenses. A Rebbe met one of his great chassidim a week before Pesach and asked him the same. The chassid answered that he had already gone through the Shulchan Aruch and Gevuras Hashem, since that was his Pesach.

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai and Nakdimon's daughter

retelling.en: After the churban, Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai saw a Jewish girl picking barley grains out of the dung of donkeys belonging to Arabs, to have something to eat in the great hunger. When she saw him she stood up and covered herself with her hair. He asked who she was, and she said she was the daughter of Nakdimon ben Gurion. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai then said 'ashreichem Yisrael'.

title.en: The man who was 'dead' during his shiur

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, in the name of the Chofetz Chaim, of a man whose practice was to learn his fixed shiur right after davening, before going to business. Once a big merchant came to do business with him, and he made him wait. His wife came shouting, and he told her that while he learns his shiur he is dead and nothing else exists for him. The Mashgiach connects this to Chazal's words that the T…

title.en: Reb Shimon of Yaroslav and his two cows

retelling.en: When Reb Shimon of Yaroslav was a young man, before he was known as a tzaddik, he was very poor. A man from his town who saw him sitting in the beis medrash day and night realized he was a great tzaddik, and would leave the rebbetzin some money, fish and potatoes. Once he asked Reb Shimon what he lived from, and he answered that he had two cows. When the man asked the rebbetzin why she then neede…

title.en: Dancing on the way to the gas chambers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what survivors told about the last generation in Germany. When Jews were gathered like cattle and sent into the gas chambers, some began to dance and said that they would outlive their murderers. They saw where they were going, but they knew that the Jewish people would survive; what spoke from them was not their personal life but the life of Klal Yisroel.

title.en: The Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe and the revolver

retelling.en: When the Russians arrested the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe for his work for Yiddishkeit and for not letting the Jews of Russia bow to communism, an interrogator pointed a revolver at him and demanded that he obey. The Rebbe answered that he was not afraid of the revolver: only one who has one world and many gods must fear it, not one who has two worlds and one G-d. The Mashgiach explains that this…

title.en: The Rebbe who knew the shortcut

retelling.en: A wealthy man from America visited a Rebbe and complained of his long walk each day from his fine home to his office. The Rebbe told him of a small alley near his house that would bring him there in five minutes. The man followed the directions and it worked. On his next trip he asked how the Rebbe knew his city, and the Rebbe answered that when he says a brachah, 'King of the world', he looks at…

title.en: Asnas, daughter of Dinah

retelling.en: Asnas was born from Dinah's abduction by Shechem. Yaakov, fearing the brothers would harm her, placed her in the desert, and a malach carried her to Potiphar in Mitzrayim, with a charm around her neck bearing her father's name. When Yosef ruled and the girls threw trinkets to him, Asnas threw her charm; Yosef saw the name, asked Pharaoh to marry her, and from what seemed a tragedy came Moshiach b…

title.en: The Apter Rav remembers his earlier lives

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Apter Rav used to tell that he remembered his earlier lives. In one generation he had been a king and in another a kohen gadol, and when he said the Yom Kippur avodah he would say the words describing the kohen gadol as one who remembered. Once he sat and complained to his people that he had always been someone, and now he was nothing.

title.en: The child whose mother kept his head covered

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls the Gemara about Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: astrologers said he would be a thief, so his mother kept his head covered. The Mashgiach adds that every Jew covers his head, and she covered it even more so that he would not steal.

title.en: The Maggid chooses a ba'al korei

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch needed a new ba'al korei, and was told that Zalman, later the Ba'al HaTanya, was a good one. The Maggid asked him whether he knew how the sedra relates to the events of each week, why each of the seven aliyos belongs to its day, and why the person the gabbai calls up belongs to his aliyah. He answered that he knew each time, and the Maggid made him his ba'al korei.

title.en: The general who was turned back

retelling.en: In the war a German general was already in Alexandria, conquering one country after another, and said he would drink coffee in Tel Aviv the next morning. That night was the turning point of the entire war; he could not enter Eretz Yisrael, and through miracles the British army pushed them back.

title.en: The relative who wanted to move to America

retelling.en: About five years earlier, a relative of the Rav in Eretz Yisrael told him during his summer visit that she could not sleep for fear of the intifada and wanted to move to America. He answered that he was more afraid to be in America. Two days after he arrived back in America the Twin Towers fell, with about three thousand victims.

title.en: The tzaddik's kneidlach on the last day of Pesach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a certain tzaddik, on the last day of Pesach, would have kneidlach, including meat kneidlach, brought to the table in a large pot. He would mix them and give everyone a portion, and he himself ate kneidlach then, though he would not eat such food the whole year. The Mashgiach brings it as an example of a minhag.

title.en: R' Yechezkel of Kuzmir's wheat on the ceiling

retelling.en: R' Yechezkel of Kuzmir kept great chumros for Pesach. He hung the wheat for his matzos in a sack from the ceiling on a rope, so that nothing could reach it. Before Pesach, when it was time to bake, the rope had to be cut, and his chumra was that it be cut with a knife kept for Pesach.

title.en: R' Yechezkel of Kuzmir and the penitent

retelling.en: A great ba'al aveiros came to R' Yechezkel of Kuzmir and asked how many fasts he should take on. The Rebbe answered that he must kill the sin, not his body. The Mashgiach concludes from this that one must be healthy and strong to serve Hashem.

title.en: 'Meshuga frum' in Detroit

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew he knows who came from Europe after the war to a relative in Detroit, who found him a job. On Shabbos morning he stayed home saying Tehillim, and his uncle asked why he was not going to work. When he answered that it was Shabbos, the uncle called him 'meshuga frum'. The Mashgiach says that today anyone with a bit of yiras Shamayim is called that.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's notes for the year

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar writes that he saw his Rebbe, the Chozeh of Lublin, write down at the start of Nissan, day by day, all that would happen in the year, and keep it sealed. At the end of the year the students looked and saw that everything had happened exactly. In the year he passed away he wrote only the first days and stopped; when he passed away in Av, the students understood why he had not w…

title.en: The Lechovitcher's message on the night of bedikah

retelling.en: The Lechovitcher Rebbe once sent a messenger to a town where he had a shtiebel, telling him to go in and say that one must search in the holes and cracks. The messenger arrived on the night of bedikas chametz and delivered the words. The chassidim then davened Maariv with great strength and shouting for several hours, until the town said they had gone mad. The Mashgiach explains that the Lechovit…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and his son's question

retelling.en: The son of the Chasam Sofer once asked his father a question touching on the principles of emunah, and the Chasam Sofer gave no answer. The son went around with the question while his father did not respond. Later the Chasam Sofer told him a wonderful explanation, and said that he had waited so that his son would know that one can go around for days with a question and still believe in Hashem.

title.en: The Ropshitzer's matzos and Napoleon's war

retelling.en: During the war between Napoleon and the Russians, the tzaddikim disagreed about who should win: the Rimanover held that Napoleon should win, and his talmid the Ropshitzer held that the Russians should. On Erev Pesach the Ropshitzer stood by the oven as matzos were baked, throwing them in and saying with each one a number of soldiers. The Mashgiach brings this to show that what Jews do on Pesach i…

title.en: The oven worker at the bakery

retelling.en: The Mashgiach once went with a fine group of bnei Torah to bake matzos in a bakery on erev Pesach. The man who put the matzos into the oven was the company's regular worker, employed there all season before Pesach. Something about him did not please the Mashgiach, so he asked the owner whether he was a Jew, and the owner said yes. When the Mashgiach asked further, the owner said he did not know.

title.en: The talmid of the Lechovitcher and the meat

retelling.en: A great talmid of the Lechovitcher, an elevated Jew, once came to a town and was served meat on Shabbos, but he would not eat it. He did not say the meat was treif; he felt that the shochet had needed to go to mikvah and had not gone, and that this entered the meat.

title.en: Rav Avraham of Slonim and the plates

retelling.en: In Yerushalayim, when all the Yidden had beards, there was one man without a beard whom Rav Avraham of Slonim held to be an ehrlicher Yid, and he told him he wished to eat a seudah at his home. In the middle of the meal, while talking, the Rav of Slonim suddenly asked the host whether the plates had been toveled. It turned out that one plate had come from another Jew, a chassid with a long beard,…

title.en: The tzaddik who found wheat in his soup

retelling.en: The Mashgiach repeats a story he heard in the name of the Satmar Rav about a great tzaddik who resolved to have a fully chametz-free Pesach. He cleaned, kashered, scrubbed and took on the greatest chumros, and ate his matzah on the Seder night with contentment. Then a wheat kernel was found floating in his soup, and he was shaken. He asked a sh'eilas chalom why this had come to him after all his…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the dentist

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from a biography of the Chazon Ish that he once suffered excruciating toothaches and needed a dentist in Bnei Brak, a neighbor, to massage his gums. One night, while the Chazon Ish was learning, he had such an attack, and the dentist was woken and gladly came to help. Afterwards the Chazon Ish made a request of him for the next time, since the dentist, woken in the night, ha…

title.en: The souls' protest in heaven

retelling.en: A great disciple of the Ba'al Shem Tov, who used to tell what happens in heaven, told his students that souls gathered to protest before the angel in charge of souls. They had come down to fulfill the Torah, failed, and were sent down again and again in further gilgulim without end. Each angel sent them higher, until they came before Hashem Himself, who advised them that on their next descent the…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the last dybbuk

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions the story of the dybbuk at the Chofetz Chaim, recently written down by someone who was present, when wondrous things from heaven were seen. The Chofetz Chaim said that there would be no more dybbuks until Moshiach, because now the test is emunah, to believe even without seeing.

title.en: The grain of wheat in the tzaddik's soup

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from the Klausenburger Rav about a great tzaddik who worked hard for a kosher Pesach, scrubbing and cleaning and keeping every stringency. At the Seder he rejoiced, but when the soup was served he saw a grain of wheat in it. He asked a question in a dream: why had this happened to him after so much effort, and how could it happen. He was answered that he had forgotten to pray…

title.en: The Ropshitzer's matzos against the Russians

retelling.en: During the war of the Russians with Napoleon, the Ropshitzer, who was against the Russians, put matzos into the oven on Erev Pesach, saying with each one 'another ten thousand Russians'. The Mashgiach says that as many matzos as he put into the oven, so many Russians fell.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav's joy after the Seder

retelling.en: After the Seder the Sanzer Rav shed tears and stroked his stomach, rejoicing that so many holy names were now within him: the holy names of the matzah, of the four cups, of the korech, karpas and charoses.

title.en: Hillel and the Bnei Beseira

retelling.en: Once Erev Pesach fell on Shabbos and the Bnei Beseira, the leaders in Eretz Yisroel, did not know whether the Pesach offering overrides Shabbos. They were told that Hillel from Bavel had come, asked him, and he answered that it does, from 'bemoado'. They stepped down and appointed him Nasi at once, and he rebuked them for not having served Shemaya and Avtalyon. When the question arose how to brin…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's warning

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from a biography of the Chofetz Chaim that someone took leave of him before travelling to Eretz Yisroel. The Chofetz Chaim told him that, since there he would have to deal with Yishmaelim, he should know that a Yishmaeli is a 'pere adam': if he becomes a doctor, a lawyer or a professor, he is a doctor, lawyer or professor who is a 'pere adam'.

title.en: Chushim ben Dan and Esav at the Me'aras HaMachpelah

retelling.en: When Yaakov Avinu was brought back to Eretz Yisrael for burial, Esav came and claimed a share in the Me'aras HaMachpelah as a fellow son of Yitzchak. Yaakov had bought Esav's share and had a deed of sale, but it had been left in Mitzrayim, so Naftali, a swift runner, ran to fetch it while everyone waited. Chushim ben Dan, who was deaf and mute, asked why the burial was held up; when he was told,…

title.en: The Seer of Lublin lifts his tallis

retelling.en: A tzaddik was once at the Seder of the Seer of Lublin, who sat with his tallis over his head while saying the Haggadah. When he reached the words 'u-ve-mora gadol, zeh gilui Shechinah', he lifted the tallis and his face was seen. The guest fainted, for he had seen a revelation of the Shechinah.

title.en: Retelling the Kuzmirer's miracle

retelling.en: A man with an illness that no cure could help came to Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir, who blessed him and worked a wonder, and he was healed. Later another man with the same illness came to Reb Yechezkel's son, who told him the story of his father's miracle. Through the retelling that man was helped as well.

title.en: The simple Jew's broken bracha

retelling.en: There was a great decree against the Jews, and the tzaddikim could not annul it. The Ropshitzer and the Rimanover sat together trying to annul it when suddenly they smiled. They explained that a simple Jew who did not know Hebrew, knowing of the decree, had davened with great intent and, in the bracha of the years, said the words wrongly. His sincere bracha annulled the decree that the tzaddikim…

title.en: The Imrei Emes and the bachurim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, drew close bachurim. During davening he would turn to the bachurim at the passuk asking Hashem to guard the thoughts of His people's hearts and direct their hearts to Him, and cry out. He was praying that the hearts of the bachurim be turned to Hashem.

title.en: Adam Harishon and the lengthening days

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara that Adam Harishon, created on Rosh Hashanah, saw the days grow shorter and the nights longer and thought that because of his sin the world would sink into an eternal night. He fasted and did teshuvah. When the tekufah of Teves came and he saw the next day grow longer, he made a festival for Hashem; the idolaters after him kept the day for their avodah zarah.

title.en: Onkelos consults the dead

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara in Gittin that Onkelos, when he considered becoming a ger, raised the dead through kishuf to consult them. Titus and Bilaam told him not to become a Jew, while Yeshu told him to. When asked his punishment, Yeshu answered that he is punished with excrement, and the Mashgiach explains that it is something rejected from the body, as he was rejected from Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Rabbi Yonasan Eybeshutz answers the priests

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbi Yonasan Eybeshutz used to debate with the priests. They asked him how the world exists on Nittel, when Jews say the world stands on Torah and yet they do not learn. He answered that since not learning is a minhag Yisrael, the minhag itself is Torah, and through it the world exists.

title.en: The Slonim tradition about the war before Moshiach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Reb Mottele of Slonim told only stories received from tzaddikim, and his stories were written down by one of his great Chassidim on the day he told them. One such tradition, handed down from tzaddik to tzaddik, says that before Moshiach the nations will not want to go to war, but they will be grabbed by the forelock and dragged into it, and that will bring the end. The…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe and Russia

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says that about thirty years earlier Shlomo, the gabbai of the Stoliner Rebbe, told him that when the Rebbe was asked what would become of Jews in communist Russia, he said Russia would last seventy years. It happened so, and Russia fell apart, which the Mashgiach calls one of the great miracles for the Jews. The Rebbe also said there would be troubles for Jews and that someone in A…

title.en: The Bluzhever Rav and the joke about Moshiach

retelling.en: Someone once made a Chassidic joke to the Bluzhever Rav, a wondrous tzaddik, and said that Moshiach was in the street. The Mashgiach, who heard this from Rabbi Steinberg, relates that the Bluzhever turned white and was frightened until it became clear it was only a joke. Asked why, he answered that he had thought Moshiach was already coming and he was not yet ready.

title.en: The kneader and the newspaper

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he once saw, in a matzah bakery, the man kneading the dough with a Yiddish newspaper open in front of him, showing immodest pictures, and he kept looking at it as he kneaded. Such 'kavanos', the Mashgiach says, go into the matzos.

title.en: The chaplain's phone call

retelling.en: The Mashgiach received a call from someone who had once studied with him years earlier and now serves as a spiritual advisor to Jewish soldiers in the army. Calling from North Carolina before flying to Iraq, he told the Mashgiach that over a thousand Jewish soldiers are in Iraq. The Mashgiach also mentions a newspaper picture of a Jewish soldier davening beside a tank, and that the chaplain told…

title.en: The boy who whistled on Yom Kippur

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was seen to be very troubled on Yom Kippur. Suddenly a simple village boy, who had been brought to davening and could not even read, took out a whistle and whistled, and the people grew angry. But the Ba'al Shem Tov became joyful and began a happy niggun. After Yom Kippur he related that there had been a great decree against the Jews which he could not annul; the boy, unable to…

title.en: Rebbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Pri Tzaddik that the donkey of Rebbi Pinchas ben Yair would not eat food from which ma'aser had not been separated. He explains that the donkey was part of its master's possessions, into which his soul extended, so the tzaddik's care in ma'aser reached even his donkey.

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the simple Jews

retelling.en: The Ruzhiner once came to a town and planned to daven with his Chassidim in their shtibel. The head of the community asked him to daven in the big town shul as an honor for the town, and when the Rebbe noted there would be no room for everyone, offered to keep the simple Jews out. The Ruzhiner answered that his great-grandfather the Maggid of Mezritch, his grandfather the Malach and his father Re…

title.en: The Baal HaTanya answers with a niggun in Shklov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a tradition among Chabad chassidim: when the Baal HaTanya came to Shklov, the scholars there asked to speak and learn with him, and gathered so that each could put his questions to him. He let each one ask his questions. When his turn came, he sang a niggun, and as he sang, all their questions were answered.

title.en: The Divrei Chaim paid every shadchan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that it is known that the Divrei Chaim used to give a small sum of shadchanus money to every shadchan who proposed a match for him, even when it did not go through. He explained that the bas kol announces one match after another until it reaches the right one, and a couple must pass through all these announcements before reaching their true match; each shadchan brought them…

title.en: Rabbi Meir and the two who quarreled every erev Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Gittin about two men among whom a quarrel broke out every erev Shabbos, because the Satan stirred them up at twilight. Rabbi Meir came and watched over them for three erev Shabbos, and the quarrel ended. The Mashgiach notes that the Satan then lamented that Rabbi Meir had driven him out.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim and the two dogs

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what the Ohr HaChaim writes in Parshas Vayechi: he had a dream in which the power of tumah appeared to him as two dogs, a male and a female. The male he overpowered immediately. With the female he had a very hard time, and even when he overpowered it, it was not completely.

title.en: Rachel gives Leah the simanim

retelling.en: Yaakov, afraid that Lavan would trick him, gave Rachel signs. When Rachel saw that her father was giving Leah to Yaakov, she feared her sister would be shamed, so she passed the signs to Leah, telling her only that they were a message from Yaakov. Leah never knew the signs had been Rachel's, which is why she later said to Rachel, 'Is it a small thing that you took my husband?'

title.en: Tamar would not shame Yehuda

retelling.en: Tamar was taken out to be burned and the fire had already caught her clothes. She could have said openly that Yehuda had given her the seal and cord, but she only sent them with the words 'recognize, please', leaving it to him to admit. Yehuda admitted, and from them came the kingship of the house of David and prophets such as Yeshayahu.

title.en: Yosef reveals himself alone

retelling.en: Before revealing himself, Yosef sent out all the Egyptian officers so that no one stood with him. Chazal say this was a great danger: the brothers, who had judged him a rodef, could have killed him. Yosef chose the danger rather than shame his brothers before the Egyptians.

title.en: The chol bird in the Teivah

retelling.en: Noach worked day and night feeding every creature in the Teivah at its time. Once he found the chol bird sitting silently in a corner and asked why it did not call for food like the others. It answered that it saw how worn out Noach was and did not want to trouble him. Noach blessed it never to die, and it renews itself every thousand years.

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the man who shamed

retelling.en: Someone once shamed another person, and the Divrei Chaim of Sanz asked him how he could shame a fellow Jew. He answered that the man was a rasha and it was a mitzvah to 'bury' him. The Divrei Chaim answered that during the plague of darkness the Jews buried the wicked who died, yet Hashem still had to give them Pesach and milah because they had no mitzvos; so burying a rasha is no mitzvah.

title.en: Shaul and his servant

retelling.en: Shaul went with his father's servant to search for the lost donkeys and could not find them. He said they should turn back, lest his father worry about 'us', placing the servant together with himself. For treating the servant as his equal he was told that he would become king.

title.en: Finishing Masechta Yoma after Yom Kippur

retelling.en: After Yom Kippur, at the house of an earlier Gerer Rebbe, the family made Havdalah and ate, but one member of the family arrived about two hours later. Asked what had kept him, he said he had been learning Masechta Yoma and had not managed to finish it before Yom Kippur, so he finished it first. He explained that in their family a Yom Tov does not pass without completing its masechta.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the driver who did not cross himself

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was once riding in a wagon with a gentile driver when a priest wearing a cross came toward them. A gentile who saw a priest would usually cross himself, but this driver ignored him. The Ba'al Shem Tov jumped down from the wagon and said he would not ride with someone who does not cross himself before a priest, since such a man believes in nothing and could be a murderer.

title.en: The coin of fire heard in Germany

retelling.en: A talmid of Rebbe Reb Bunim traveled to Germany on business, at a time when assimilation was already widespread there. When he returned, Rebbe Reb Bunim asked whether he had heard any words of Torah, and he said he had heard a German preacher explain that Hashem showed Moshe a coin of fire because one must give with fire and devotion. Rebbe Reb Bunim wondered how such a fine vort reached Germany,…

title.en: The tzaddik whose soul came from sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great tzaddik of several generations ago whose neshama, the tzaddikim said, came from the mitzvah of sukkah. Every day of the year he was busy with his sukkah: fixing something in it, talking about it or buying something for it.

title.en: Yehoash, Yehoyada and Zechariah

retelling.en: When Asalyah killed the royal seed of David, the Kohen Gadol Yehoyada saved the infant Yehoash and hid him in the Kodesh HaKadashim for six years, where he was fed and cared for. Crowned at seven, Yehoash was righteous while Yehoyada lived, but later his servants told him he must be a deity and he let them worship him. When Yehoyada's son Zechariah, the Kohen Gadol, rebuked the people on Yom Kipp…

title.en: Kamtza and bar Kamtza

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls the incident that brought the destruction of Yerushalayim. A man was not allowed to come to a party, and because of this he went and spoke lashon hara to the Roman ruler. The Mashgiach explains that the episode is a symbol: Yerushalayim was destroyed because of sins between man and his fellow, hatred and lashon hara.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's pupils and Sinai

retelling.en: Before he was revealed, the Ba'al Shem Tov was a melamed who taught young children Chumash with the Yiddish translation, and no one knew who he was. Before Shavuos he asked the children whether they remembered standing at Mount Sinai. He had instilled such holiness in them that they answered they remembered, and saw themselves standing there. One child said he did not remember, and that child lat…

title.en: A boy's kvitel at the Kosel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that at the Kosel people from all over the world, gentiles too, put in kvitlach, and he mentions that he had suggested collecting the kvitlach that fall out into a book. He once found a kvitel that had fallen out, written in Hebrew by an Israeli boy, asking Hashem for a dog and a bicycle. The Mashgiach notes that one can tell what sort of boy wants a dog, but he asked it of…

title.en: Boaz who did not invite Manoach

retelling.en: Boaz, identified by the Gemara with Ivtzan, had sixty children and made weddings for them, but never invited the childless Manoach, reasoning that Manoach would never be able to reciprocate. In the end all of Boaz's children died, while Manoach had a son, Shimshon. The Mashgiach adds a reading of Naomi's words to Ruth, that Ruth feared Boaz's children had all died.

title.en: The chol bird in Noach's ark

retelling.en: In the ark Noach fed all the creatures and found the chol bird hiding in a corner without coming to eat. When asked why, it answered that it saw Noach was busy day and night feeding everyone and did not want to burden him. Noach blessed it to live forever.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rebbe and the king's doctor

retelling.en: When the Bluzhever Rebbe was old and weak, the king's personal doctor passed through Bluzhov, and the chassidim arranged for him to examine the Rebbe. The doctor, once a Jewish yeshivah boy, found all in order except that the heart was not beating regularly. The Rebbe asked him whether he remembered what day it was, six days before Matan Torah, and asked how he could expect a Jewish heart to beat…

title.en: The responsum that saved the Bluzhever Rebbe

retelling.en: As a boy, the Bluzhever Rebbe was called in by his grandfather, the author of Tzvi LaTzaddik, who never showed his responsa to anyone, and shown one responsum: that the prohibition of taking one's own life applies even to passively not saving oneself. Years later, starving in the camps at about seventy pounds, he decided to stop eating his daily bread to end his suffering, then remembered that re…

title.en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan's secretary

retelling.en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan fought the Zionists and maskilim of his time, and his secretary was a fierce anti-Zionist who enjoyed attacking them. Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan said the difference between them was like that between a housewife and a cat: both want no mice in the house, but the housewife is glad when there are none, while the cat is glad when there is one to catch.

title.en: The chassid and the carcass

retelling.en: In the story the Mashgiach brings from Chovos HaLevavos, a chassid walked with others through a forest and passed a carcass with a terrible smell. The others complained about the smell, but the chassid pointed out its beautiful white teeth. The Mashgiach explains that each person sees in another according to his own goodness or badness.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the gebrokts

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim was very stringent and did not eat gebrokts on Pesach, but when a relative who did eat it came as a guest, he told his rebbetzin to make knaidlach so as not to offend him.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's valley of gold

retelling.en: A student of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai left to trade overseas and came back rich, and the other students wanted to do the same. Rabbi Shimon took them out to a valley and said, 'Valley, valley, fill up with gold dinars,' and it did. As the students began to gather it, he told them that whoever takes now loses his share in Olam Haba.

title.en: Yehoash, Yehoyada and Zechariah

retelling.en: When the king died, the wicked Asalyah killed the royal family to take the kingdom. Yehoyada hid a newborn prince, Yehoash, in the Holy of Holies, where no one would search, fed and cared for him there, and at seven years old crowned him king in a revolt that killed Asalyah. Yehoash was a tzaddik while Yehoyada lived, but later, when Yehoyada's son Zechariah, a navi, warned the people that the Be…

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah's broken barrel

retelling.en: Workers carrying a barrel of wine for Rabbah bar bar Chanah dropped and broke it. When he asked them to pay, Rav ruled they did not have to, and when they asked for their day's wages, Rav told him to pay them, since they were poor and needed it. Each time Rabbah bar bar Chanah asked, 'Is that the din?', and Rav answered yes.

title.en: The brilliant student who mocked a Zohar

retelling.en: A very bright student, an ilui, studied with Rebbe Reb Bunim of Peshischa. Someone told him the Rebbe was not genuine and everything was for show, and the student left. That student wrote a note mocking a Zohar that says one who walks four amos after rising without washing is liable to death. The Kotzker later took pride in having driven out someone harmful, having seen it from the beginning.

title.en: The Bas Ayin and the name Hadas

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, from a Yerushalmi Jew whose grandfather was a chassid of the Bas Ayin, that the Bas Ayin's shul in Tzfas still bears a plaque recalling how half of it stood in an earthquake when he gathered the people around him. When a girl was named at the Torah in his presence, the gabbai called her Hadassah; the Bas Ayin stopped him and insisted on Hadas. Seventeen years later she became…

title.en: R' Yosef tested by a hungry guest

retelling.en: R' Yosef was a tzaddik who always took the poor guests nobody else would take. When it was decreed in Heaven to give him a son with a great soul, the Satan asked permission to test him, and came as a smelly poor man in the middle of his long davening, saying he was hungry. R' Yosef cut his davening short and took him home, fed him again and again, and when the guest demanded fish and challah he w…

title.en: R' Mordechai Banet's six months

retelling.en: R' Mordechai Banet, rav of Nikolsburg, passed away in a small town and was buried there, and Nikolsburg asked the Chasam Sofer whether he could be reburied in their city. The Chasam Sofer wrote a teshuvah but held it back; that night R' Mordechai Banet appeared to him in a dream. As a young rav in that town he had not done enough to stop a chassan from breaking a shidduch with a girl, who was bad…

title.en: The bochur who shamed a visiting rav

retelling.en: R' Shlomo Bloch, a talmid of the Chofetz Chaim, told of a great, sharp rosh yeshiva whose children died. As a seventeen-year-old bochur with a fiery temperament, he had challenged a visiting rav's pilpul with kushyos, refused to accept the answers, and in the heated exchange shamed him in front of everyone. R' Shlomo Bloch said this was the cause.

title.en: The soul that shamed a chassan

retelling.en: A soul came to R' Moshe of Savran seeking a tikkun. It had been a true tzaddik and had done teshuvah for its sins, except one: at a wedding where the father-in-law boasted of his chassan's learning, the chassan made a mistake saying Tehillim, and this man pointed it out so that the chassan turned red with shame before his father-in-law. For that he was not let in.

title.en: R' Akiva Eiger at sheva brachos, at the Seder and in Nikolsburg

retelling.en: At sheva brachos shared with another chassan, R' Akiva Eiger said nothing while the other chassan said Torah, and only after he left did R' Akiva Eiger say a wondrous pilpul, explaining that he did not want to shame him. At his Seder, when a poor guest spilled wine over the beautiful tablecloth, R' Akiva Eiger at once spilled his own cup with his elbow so the guest would not feel hurt. In Nikolsb…

title.en: R' Yisrael Salanter steps aside

retelling.en: R' Yisrael Salanter received a position as rosh yeshiva in a yeshiva where another great rosh yeshiva already gave shiurim. When he noticed the students were more drawn to him, he left the yeshiva, giving up his position rather than compete with and pain the other rosh yeshiva.

title.en: The shoemaker at his daughter's chuppah

retelling.en: A shoemaker who had worked his way up made his daughter's wedding in the hall where only the very rich held weddings. At the chuppah a wealthy man, displeased that a plain shoemaker was mixing with the rich, took off his shoe and asked the father how much it would cost to fix it, and the man was deeply hurt. R' Yisrael Salanter said the rabbanim of Vilna would give a din v'cheshbon for it, since…

title.en: The Imrei Emes at the Knessia Gedolah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw the Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, give a drashah at the Knessia Gedolah on 'Vayischazeik Dovid': when Dovid's wives and children were taken captive, he strengthened himself in Hashem. The Imrei Emes said Klal Yisrael must strengthen itself, that more would be returned than was taken, and that the main thing is that there be no sinas chinam. Nobody understood the drashah…

title.en: Petty meetings in Vienna

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's father-in-law was a prominent member of the board of the kehillah in Vienna. He told that while Hitler was strong and wanted to swallow all of Europe, the board met and argued about petty things: positions, seats, honor and who would be president or vice president. In the end those who could fled to America or Eretz Yisrael, and what happened to the rest is known.

title.en: R' Yisrael Salanter and the widow who served

retelling.en: A wealthy, G-d-fearing host invited R' Yisrael Salanter for Shabbos and boasted of his long meal with zemiros and divrei Torah. R' Yisrael agreed on condition the meal take no more than an hour and a half, and it was done quickly. Asked why, he called in the maid, a poor widow, and apologized to her for the rushing; she said that every Shabbos she worked from early Friday and could hardly stand b…

title.en: R' Yisrael Salanter's last night

retelling.en: At the end of his life R' Yisrael Salanter was in a place where he was not known, sharing a room with another Jew. When he fell ill and understood that his last hour had come, at night, he spent it explaining to his roommate that there is no reason to fear a dead body, that it harms nobody. Then he passed away, and the roommate remained with him the whole night until morning, when the chevra kadi…

title.en: R' Yitzchak Elchanan keeps a secret

retelling.en: R' Yitzchak Elchanan went collecting for a wealthy man who had lost his fortune. One rich man asked who it was for and offered twenty-five, then fifty, then a hundred rubles to know, but R' Yitzchak Elchanan refused to reveal it. Then the man asked to speak to him privately and told him that he too had lost everything, and had been afraid to tell him lest his secret come out; now he saw it would…

title.en: The kerosene cholent

retelling.en: R' Avigdor Halberstam, brother of the Divrei Chaim, was a guest at a Shabbos table where, as was the custom in Hungary and Galicia, the eldest was honored with the pot of cholent to serve. He put cholent on his plate, then took more and more, until the pot was empty and nobody else got any. Later the hostess noticed that the cholent smelled of kerosene, which she had put in by mistake; he ate it…

title.en: R' Shmuel Salant and the old woman's question

retelling.en: An old, simple woman came to R' Shmuel Salant, rav of Yerushalayim, while he sat with his students: as she salted meat, a cat had jumped up and taken a large piece of unsalted meat. The students laughed. R' Shmuel Salant did not laugh; he looked into a sefer, answered her seriously, and afterwards rebuked the students, saying that if they laughed at her she would not come again to ask.

title.en: R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld and the Lubliner Rav

retelling.en: Every Yom Tov nearly every Jew in Yerushalayim came to wish R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld a good Yom Tov. Once the Lubliner Rav, R' Eliyahu Klatzkin, was sitting with him, and R' Yosef Chaim asked each visitor whether he had been at the Kosel. His son asked why; he answered that so the Lubliner Rav would not be pained that people came to him and not to the guest, he made it appear that they came on t…

title.en: R' Nachum of Chernobyl and the silver spoon

retelling.en: A poor man received a generous donation from R' Nachum of Chernobyl and on his way out took a silver spoon from the table. The gabbai caught him and brought him back, and the man claimed the Rebbe had given it to him. R' Nachum confirmed that he had given him the spoon, and then gave him another large coin because he had been shamed.

title.en: R' Levi Yitzchak's matzah takanah

retelling.en: When R' Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev became rav, the leaders asked him for new takanos to make the matzah baking stricter and faster. He wrote a takanah that one may not put blood into the matzos. He explained that the bakers are poor widows working for a few rubles for Yom Tov, and driving them faster and faster is Jewish blood.

title.en: R' Mordechai Benet's burial

retelling.en: R' Mordechai Benet, rav of Nikolsburg, died in another city and was buried there, and the people of Nikolsburg asked the Chasam Sofer whether he could be brought back. The Chasam Sofer's answer came only six months later; his son R' Shimon Sofer revealed that R' Mordechai had come to him in a dream. He had once ruled that a broken shidduch was permitted, yet the kallah was shamed, and his punishm…

title.en: R' Akiva Eiger's crooked table

retelling.en: At R' Akiva Eiger's Seder a poor guest knocked over his wine onto the fine tablecloth and was deeply embarrassed. R' Akiva Eiger then nudged his own cup so that it spilled too, and said the table was crooked, so that the guest would not be ashamed.

title.en: R' Akiva Eiger's drasha in Nikolsburg

retelling.en: Visiting Nikolsburg, R' Akiva Eiger gave a drasha with a pilpul on the Rambam, and R' Mordechai Benet asked a kushya that seemed to topple it; R' Akiva Eiger stepped down without answering. When R' Mordechai went to apologize, R' Akiva Eiger told him a good answer, explaining he had not wanted to shame the rav of the city in public. The next day R' Mordechai Benet gathered the town, repeated the…

title.en: The shoemaker's shoe in Vilna

retelling.en: In Vilna, a former shoemaker who had become rich rented the fancy hall where the wealthy made their weddings. As he walked his son to the chuppah, a brazen man who begrudged him ran up, took off his own shoe, and asked how much it would cost to fix, shaming him badly. Hearing of it, R' Yisrael Salanter said that now in Heaven the earlier rabbanim of Vilna were being judged for not teaching mussar…

title.en: R' Yisrael Salanter and the cook

retelling.en: A wealthy man invited R' Yisrael Salanter for a Friday night meal, describing its kashrus and its long courses of zemiros and divrei Torah. R' Yisrael agreed on condition that the meal take only two hours, and the host hurried each course. Afterwards R' Yisrael asked for the cook, a widow, who thanked him: every week she stood on her feet all Friday and then had to wait through a four-hour meal,…

title.en: Calming a roommate on the last night

retelling.en: A tzaddik who was away from home, in Koenigsberg, shared a room with another man. On the last night of his life he spoke with him at length, convincing him that there is no reason to fear a dead person. When he passed away that night, the man was not frightened; even his last moment was used for chesed.

title.en: R' Yitzchak Elchanan's secret collection

retelling.en: A wealthy man lost his fortune, and R' Yitzchak Elchanan went personally with another man to the rich of the town to collect for him without revealing the name. One donor gave twenty-five rubles and offered fifty and then a hundred if told who it was for, but R' Yitzchak Elchanan refused. In private the donor revealed that he himself had become poor and had wanted to test whether his secret would…

title.en: The Dukla Rav and the kerosene cholent

retelling.en: The Dukla Rav, brother of the Divrei Chaim, was a guest in the Oberland, where the custom was that the most honored guest serves the cholent to everyone. He kept taking cholent for himself until he had eaten the whole pot and gave no one any. Asked why, he explained that the maid had mistakenly poured kerosene instead of oil into it, and he ate it so that the woman of the house would not shout at…

title.en: R' Yisrael Salanter and the cat

retelling.en: A simple woman asked R' Yisrael Salanter a question: a cat had eaten the meat that was not yet salted. He went to the bookcase and looked in a sefer while his students could barely keep from laughing. He told her gravely to be careful it should not happen again, and afterwards rebuked the students: had they laughed she would have been ashamed to come and ask again.

title.en: R' Yosef Chaim and the widow

retelling.en: A fine baal mussaf for the Yamim Noraim in R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's shul passed away before Elul, and the shul asked for a replacement. R' Yosef Chaim gave the amud to the late chazzan's son, who had a good voice, though he was an avel. Asked about the halachah, he explained that the widow in the women's section would break down hearing a stranger in her husband's place, but hearing her son wo…

title.en: R' Yosef Chaim returns to the Old City

retelling.en: When R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld was old and ill, the doctor had him moved out of the cramped Old City of Yerushalayim to an open area with better air. As he grew weaker he asked to return, against medical advice. He explained that his burial would be on Har HaZeisim, a few minutes from the Old City, and he did not want people to have to carry him a long distance.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim at the train window

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim travelled by train to a gathering of rabbanim together with R' Meir Dan Plotzki. At one town a crowd gathered and asked that he come to the window so they could see him. R' Meir Dan asked what harm a little honor would do to his Olam Haba if it gave Jews pleasure, and the Chofetz Chaim went to the window and showed himself.

title.en: R' Chaim Ozer's apartment

retelling.en: R' Chaim Ozer Grodzenski of Vilna needed a larger apartment, and of two available the rebbetzin preferred the nicer one. He asked to take the plainer one for the same price. He explained that in the nicer one the kitchen was far from the dining room, and the maid serving the Shabbos table would have to toil walking back and forth.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's envelope

retelling.en: A man came to the Satmar Rav needing help for a wedding that would cost ten thousand dollars. The Rebbe told him to return the next day and had his gabbai, R' Yosef Ashkenazi, prepare an envelope with nine thousand five hundred dollars. Asked why not the full amount, the Rebbe explained that had he given the full sum, the man would regret not having asked for twelve thousand.

title.en: Mordechai warns against Achashverosh's feast

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Achashverosh's feast celebrated seventy years without the Beis HaMikdash being rebuilt, and that kosher food was provided. Mordechai went around warning the Jews not to attend, calling it a chillul Hashem, but eighteen thousand Jews of Shushan went, saying it was unpatriotic to stay away. Four years later Mordechai refused to bow to Haman, and he was again blamed as a tro…

title.en: The Arizal and Rav Chaim Vital at the Kinneret

retelling.en: The Arizal took his disciple Rav Chaim Vital out on a boat on the Kinneret. When they reached a certain spot, he told him to drink the water there, because Miriam's well was there. After drinking from it, Rav Chaim Vital merited to understand the Arizal's deep Torah.

title.en: The Satmar Rav and the singing in Meron

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Satmar Rav once came to Meron and sang there, and when he was asked about it he answered that by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai there is "oz vechedvah bimkomo". The Mashgiach notes that the Satmar Rav was a strict ba'al halacha who did not accept new things, and that this concerned singing at Rashbi's place during the Nine Days.

title.en: The Arizal's student who said Nachem in Meron

retelling.en: A student of the Arizal, Rabbi Avraham, mourned the churban constantly and added the Nachem prayer of Tisha B'Av in his bentching every day. When he came to Meron with the Arizal he said it there too. The Arizal sent to tell him in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai that Rashbi was displeased that he said it on his day of joy, and he was punished.

title.en: The Belzer Rav and his son on Lag Ba'omer

retelling.en: Rabbi Sholom of Belz told his son that Lag Ba'omer is a great day. The son answered that it is probably like Yom Kippur, and his father told him that he had now hit upon the truth.

title.en: Meron this Lag Ba'omer

retelling.en: The government in Eretz Yisrael announced that Jews should not go to Meron for Lag Ba'omer, out of fear that terrorists could strike a large gathering. The Jews went anyway, and from the telephone calls the Mashgiach heard, there had never been so many Jews in Meron for Lag Ba'omer.

title.en: The letter to the editor about the miracles

retelling.en: After the Six Day War, the secular papers printed stories of miracles every day. A woman wrote a letter to one of them, and they printed it, asking them to stop writing about the miracles, because it spoiled her pleasure in driving to the beach every Shabbos.

title.en: The Arizal and the tzaddik who said Nachem in Meron

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital tells of a great tzaddik who mourned the Churban all year and always added 'Nachem' in the after-blessing on a meal. Once he was at Rashbi's place in Meron, bentched there and said Nachem. The Arizal told him that there one does not say Nachem. A short time later a relative of his passed away, and the Arizal said this was a punishment, because at Rashbi's place there is no mourn…

title.en: The Satmar Rav sings 'Bar Yochai' in the Nine Days

retelling.en: The Satmar Rav's biography relates that he came to Tzfas for the Arizal's yahrzeit and then went to Meron, to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. There he had 'Bar Yochai' sung with dancing, in the middle of the Nine Days. He said that at Rashbi's place mourning does not apply, for there is strength and joy in His place.

title.en: The gunpowder that came to mind

retelling.en: In a place where Jews were barred from ordinary business, some made a living trading goods without paying customs, among them gunpowder, which the law forbade. One morning the Rav of the town sent word that everyone with gunpowder at home should clear it out. Afterwards inspectors came and raided the houses but found nothing. Asked whether this was ruach hakodesh, he said no: his head is always f…

title.en: The Scud missiles on Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that the Iraqis fired 39 Scud missiles at Eretz Yisroel, which brought down many buildings, yet only one person was killed. That man had hung a sign on his door saying he eats pig and had ridden his motorcycle into a beis medrash on Shabbos, and the Steipler had cursed him. When the Iraqis fired a single Scud at the American army, some thirty soldiers were killed.

title.en: The Baal HaTanya's cup at the Maggid's seder

retelling.en: At the Maggid's seder each student had to bring his own cup, and the Baal HaTanya, who was poor, had none. Rather than ask for charity to buy a glass cup, he relied on the Mechaber that a glass cup soaked in water three days in a row is kashered, since it was a time of need. The Maggid came in and said it smelled of chametz; Reb Mendel of Vitebsk went among the students and smelled nothing. The B…

title.en: The ravens over the fat-seller's wagon

retelling.en: Fat sellers came through the town, and the new rav, the Rema, had one of them summoned and asked him where he had taken the fat. When the rav cried out at him, the seller broke down and admitted that what he sold was not kosher. The townspeople were amazed and took it for ruach hakodesh, but the rav said it was not: passing the market he had seen ravens circling only over that man's wagon, and si…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon's dove from the cave

retelling.en: While Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was in the cave, his students were troubled by the harsh things in the tochacha. They sent him a dove with a note asking their question, and he tied a note back onto the dove saying that everything written in the tochacha is blessing. They were greatly gladdened, for the dove brings good tidings.

title.en: Reb Moshe of Rozvadov at nightfall on Lag BaOmer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Reb Moshe of Rozvadov used to say, as evening came on Lag BaOmer, that he could not part from the day. He brings this as an example of how tzaddikim honored Lag BaOmer above other days.

title.en: The Kotzker: believing is greater than seeing

retelling.en: The Kotzker Rebbe, Reb Mendel, had a dispute with Galician tzaddikim over his way. One of them sent him a message that he sees the ushpizin when they come into his sukkah. The Kotzker sent back that he believes they come into his sukkah, and believing is greater than seeing. The Mashgiach applies this to Rabbi Shimon: even without understanding, believing in him is greater.

title.en: Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir and the laughter of the geulah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir said on the passuk of the return to Zion that 'then our mouths will be filled with laughter'. He said: the Ba'al Shem Tov did not bring the geulah, nor Rabbi Ber, nor Rabbi Elimelech, nor the Rebbe of Lublin; and Chatzkele who sits in Kuzmir will bring it? One would have to laugh. And in such a way, he said, Moshiach comes.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya becomes the Maggid's ba'al koreh

retelling.en: When the post of ba'al koreh in the Maggid's shul became vacant, he was told that his youngest talmid, the Ba'al HaTanya, would be good for it. The Maggid asked him whether he knew how each sedra relates to its week, how each of the seven aliyos relates to its day, and why the soul of each person called up belongs to his aliyah. To each question he answered yes, and the Maggid made him his ba'al…

title.en: The Belzer Rav at the window

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what people told him: on this day, the year before the Second World War broke out, the Belzer Rav went to the window in the morning and stood there the whole day waiting for Moshiach. At night, when the day passed and Moshiach did not come, he was very distressed. Nobody else knew why, but he knew what that year held and that when it ended the war would begin.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe receives the Chasam Sofer's teshuvah

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer wrote his objection to the Lag Baomer celebration in a teshuvah addressed to the Yismach Moshe. When the Yismach Moshe received it, he said that out of respect for the Chasam Sofer he would not speak against it, though he held that every line in it could be questioned.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon's thirteenth year in the cave

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was to stay in the cave twelve years. At the end of the twelfth year Eliyahu Hanavi came to tell him that the decree was annulled and he could come out. When he came out he looked at the world with an unfavorable eye and could not bear that there were sins in the world. A heavenly voice told him to return to his cave, and so his twelve years became thirteen.

title.en: The Mashgiach's father-in-law rebukes the Vienna community

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's father-in-law, a respected member of the Jewish community leadership in Vienna, told him how the community members would meet and talk about politics, positions, honor and other foolishness. Once he stood up and gave them a drashah: did they not see that Hitler in Germany was growing strong? Why were they busy with seeking honor and seats instead of doing something to save the Jew…

title.en: Menashe teaches Rav Ashi in a dream

retelling.en: Rav Ashi, about to expound on the kings who have no share in the World to Come, called Menashe 'our colleague'. That night Menashe came to him in a dream and asked from where one breaks the bread for hamotzi, and Rav Ashi did not know. Menashe told him: from the place where it is baked first, the hard crust. The next day Rav Ashi began his lecture calling Menashe 'our teacher'.

title.en: The father's soul in the glass of brandy

retelling.en: A simple Jew came into a place where people were drinking and was poured a glass of brandy, and he drank it without a brachah. A tzaddik who saw this asked him when his father had died, and it turned out to be close to the yahrzeit. The tzaddik told him that his father's soul had entered that drink, waiting for its tikkun through the son's brachah, and now it had been lost. The man fainted.

title.en: Reb Sholom of Belz and the fallen kugel

retelling.en: At Reb Sholom of Belz's Shabbos tish, a piece of kugel fell to the floor while it was being served, and he had it picked up and eaten. He explained that the wheat in it had prayed at every stage of its growth, harvest, grinding and baking to reach its tikkun, had become challah and then kugel for the tzaddik's tish; if it were left on the floor, all its prayers would have been in vain.

title.en: Menashe's teshuvah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara that Menashe was captured and placed in a heated vessel to be burned. He prayed to all the idols, and when they did not help, he turned to Hashem. The angels protested, but Hashem made an opening beneath the Throne of Glory, accepted his teshuvah, and miraculously brought him back to Yerushalayim.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's double appeal

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when the Satmar Rav came to America and was building up a Chassidish community among refugees fresh from the camps, an appeal was made in his small shul on Bedford Avenue. The Satmar Rav told the people to give beyond their strength, and the gabbai went around announcing each pledge. When everyone had pledged, the Satmar Rav told the gabbai to start over so they would p…

title.en: The treasure under the bridge in Hamburg

retelling.en: A poor Jew dreamed that a treasure lay on a bridge in Hamburg, and traveled for weeks to get there. On the bridge he could not find it, and a policeman who saw him searching asked what he was doing. When he told his dream, the policeman laughed at dreams and said he himself had dreamed of a treasure under the oven of a Jew named Chaim Yankel. That was the Jew's own name; he went home and found th…

title.en: The soldier who went swimming

retelling.en: A soldier was posted to guard a certain point. On a hot day he left his post and his uniform and went into the water to swim.
