Suddenly the king himself came to inspect, and the soldier ran back and stood at his post as he was. Asked about it, he answered that dressed or not dressed, he is a soldier on duty. The Mashgiach says a Jew too is a soldier who must always be ready to serve Hashem.

title.en: The Rozvadover's Shabbos table on parshas Kedoshim

retelling.en: Reb Moshe'le of Rozvadov, a grandson of the Ropshitzer, came as a guest to a town for Shabbos parshas Kedoshim. Chassidim crowded his table, simple people came out of curiosity, and a group of maskilim came to watch and laugh. He noted that 'Ani Hashem Elokeichem' appears three times at the start of the parsha. To the chassidim he said they must be holy and go beyond the letter of the law because…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe and the taxi driver at the Seder

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes the Stoliner Rebbe in Williamsburg as a man of extraordinary chesed, who would have twenty, thirty or more simple and far-off people at his table and make them a full seudah, even when they came on Shabbos with money jingling in their pockets. Once on Pesach night a taxi driver parked in front and came in, expecting to eat right away, and grew impatient when Hallel began.…

title.en: Reb Nachum of Chernobyl grows stout from Torah

retelling.en: Reb Nachum of Chernobyl was a heavy man although he hardly ate. His friends said that he grew stout from the Torah he learned.

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the grain of wheat

retelling.en: At the tisch of Rebbe Shalom of Belz a piece of kugel fell to the floor, and he told them to pick it up and eat it. He then told of a grain of wheat that prayed for rain, then not to fall when it was cut, then not to be blown away, then to be bought by a Jewish home. The Belzer Rebbetzin bought the flour, it was baked into challah, and the leftover challah was made into kugel for the next Shabbos…

title.en: Menashe appears to Rav Ashi

retelling.en: Rav Ashi announced that the next day they would expound about Menashe, calling him 'our colleague'. That night Menashe came to him in a dream and asked from where one breaks bread for hamotzi, and Rav Ashi did not know. Menashe told him: from the place that is baked first. Rav Ashi asked why one so wise served idols, and Menashe answered that had he lived then, he would have lifted his garments t…

title.en: The tzaddik who shared his bread in the camp

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls davening in the beis medrash of a rav who was a wondrous tzaddik and a great gaon in Torah, of whom wonderful things were told. In the concentration camp, from the small piece of bread he received to survive, he broke off a piece and gave it to another. The Mashgiach says that from the way this tzaddik drank coffee before davening, without settling down to it, one could lear…

title.en: The guest who finished davening during Ahavah Rabbah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the well-known story of a stranger who arrived one Shabbos morning in a town where the chazan had begun the davening. Not hearing the chazan, he assumed the chazan was saying it quietly, davened by himself and finished. Only then did the chazan, who had been taking that long, continue aloud. The Mashgiach says this is how Jews once davened, and that we have no grasp of it.

title.en: The Shinever Rav stays home in Sanz

retelling.en: The Shinever Rav, although his father was the Sanzer Rav, was a Belzer chassid and travelled to Belz for Shavuos. When he again wanted to go, his father asked why. He answered that by the Belzer Rav, when the parshah of Matan Torah is read, one sees and feels the sounds and the lightning and hears Hashem saying 'Anochi', and one lives through Matan Torah. His father told him to stay, since he wou…

title.en: The Ahavas Yisroel sends the bochurim to sleep

retelling.en: A group of students from a yeshiva came to the Ahavas Yisroel of Vizhnitz for Shavuos. They were used to davening Shacharis right after dawn, making Kiddush, eating something dairy and going to sleep. When the Rebbe came into the beis medrash at dawn and saw them about to form their own minyan because they were tired, he told them that one eats and sleeps in order to daven, not davens in order to…

title.en: The neshamah at the Spinka Rebbe's Megillah reading

retelling.en: The Spinka Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Meir, told of a young man, understood to be himself, who after the Seder on the second night of Pesach, the day Haman was hanged, sat down to learn the Megillah. A neshamah appeared and explained that a chamber in heaven, open only on Purim, cleanses whoever enters and admits him to Gan Eden, but it had never managed to get in. When the light of Purim was felt above…

title.en: Rabbi Lazar of Amsterdam and the leaking dike

retelling.en: Rabbi Lazar of Amsterdam was favored by the Queen, who would turn to him whenever the country needed a yeshuah, and he would say Tehillim. Once on Purim a dike leaked and the city was in grave danger, and she sent a messenger asking him to daven. Told the leak was controlled, she went to see how he davened and through the window saw him with his talmidim, feasting with barrels of wine. When she a…

title.en: The Rebbe who asked: do you believe?

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that a man once came to a Rebbe and complained that he was troubled by doubts. The Rebbe answered him with a question: does he believe or does he not believe? The Mashgiach tells this to the people who come to him with similar complaints.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer at the family Shabbos table

retelling.en: Rabbi Aharon Pollak, a Satmar chassid, used to visit an elderly rebbetzin, the widow of his father's rebbe, who lived to ninety-eight; her mother was a granddaughter of the Chasam Sofer. She told that the Chasam Sofer did not eat Friday night with his family because talmidim came, but on Shabbos day he ate with the whole family, even the maid, and spoke mussar to them rather than chiddushim. Once…

title.en: The bungalow colony

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that as a young man needing parnassah he took a job as ba'al tefillah in a bungalow colony, and saw how chassidish yungeleit behaved there: men and women gathered at night around a table playing Monopoly and similar games. He says that what goes on in the bungalows today is beyond recognition, and calls it a great test.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the Mishneh LaMelech

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that when the Ba'al Shem Tov was in the Sephardic lands, he visited the Mishneh LaMelech. The Mishneh LaMelech asked what was happening with the Jews of Europe, and he told him of harsh decrees in Russia. The Mishneh LaMelech shook his head, and the Ba'al Shem Tov said that with that shake the minister of Russia was cast down in heaven. The Mishneh LaMelech himself did not kno…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's wagon on the breaking ice

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story he heard told in the name of a man who recently passed away in America, who had been a wagon driver for the Stoliner Rebbe. At the end of one winter the Rebbe told him to drive across a frozen river; the driver warned that the ice was thin, but they went. In the middle the ice began to crack, and the Rebbe put his head out of the windows on all four sides and called ou…

title.en: The Shinever Rav sees the giving of the Torah in Belz

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Shinever Rav was once in Belz for Shavuos, against his father's wish. When the Belzer Rav read the Ten Commandments, the Shinever Rav truly saw the giving of the Torah. The next Shavuos he wanted to go to Belz again; his father, the Sanzer, told him to stay, saying that it happens here too, and that one need not see it but must believe it.

title.en: The frozen river and Parshas Miketz

retelling.en: Lumber merchants floated rafts of timber down a river to distant mills. One very cold winter the river stayed frozen past the date they had contracted to deliver, and they faced a great loss, so they came to the Rebbe of Belz to ask that warm weather come. He asked what the children in their towns were learning in cheder, and they said Parshas Miketz. He told them that is why the river is frozen:…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya becomes the Maggid's ba'al korei

retelling.en: When the Ba'al HaTanya was a young talmid of the Maggid of Mezritch, the Maggid's ba'al korei was no longer there, and they told him the newly arrived young man reads very well. The Maggid called him in and asked whether he knew what bond the sedra has with the week, what each day's portion has to do with that day, and why the gabbai calls up a particular person to a particular portion. Each time…

title.en: The Belzer Rav's heart before Shavuos

retelling.en: The king's personal physician, the greatest doctor in the land, was a Jew who had learned in cheder as a boy and later studied medicine at university. The chassidim asked him to examine the Belzer Rav, who was very weak. Listening to the Rebbe's heart, he said that it was not beating properly. The Rebbe answered that in six days it would be Shavuos, and asked how the doctor could expect his heart…

title.en: The Satmar Rav reading the Aseres Hadibros

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that on many Shavuos he merited to hear the Satmar Rav read the Aseres Hadibros. When he said 'Anochi', the walls trembled, and those present felt the day they stood before Hashem at Chorev.

title.en: The tzaddik's Pesach and the grain of wheat

retelling.en: A tzaddik resolved to have a truly kosher Pesach, koshered all his utensils and was present at the cutting of the wheat and the baking, with every stringency. At the seder, after the fish, he found a grain of wheat floating in his soup, real chametz. He asked a dream-question in Heaven why this happened to him after such care, and how it could have happened. He was answered that he had done every…

title.en: The bochur who threw off his yarmulke

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he watched from his window as bochurim played ball. One bochur felt that the yarmulke on his head kept him from running fast, so he pulled it off to run faster. The Mashgiach says that he thereby threw off the yoke of Heaven, since covering the head brings yiras shamayim.

title.en: The Slavita printer who would not run bareheaded

retelling.en: The Slavita printers, descendants of R' Pinchas of Koretz, were imprisoned by the Russian Czar over a libel and sentenced to run between two rows of soldiers with whips tipped with iron balls. The faster they ran, the sooner they were free of the blows. In the middle of running, the yarmulke fell off the head of one of them, and he stopped and would not go on without it.

title.en: The Chazon Ish on a troubled bochur

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in a letter the Chazon Ish wrote about a bochur who did not want to learn and caused problems. The Chazon Ish said this bochur had a bright future: if he turned his way to Torah he would rise far above the other bochurim. The Mashgiach explains that such a strong yetzer is a sign of great inner holiness.

title.en: The Plantcher Rebbe's kiddush on Tisha b'Av

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Plantcher Rebbe, a great Rebbe in Galicia and father-in-law of the Satmar Rebbe. Chassidim relate that on Tisha b'Av he took an empty glass and acted as one does at kiddush, saying that when Moshiach comes Tisha b'Av will be a Yom Tov on which kiddush is made. Tears ran from his eyes, and he told his talmidim that this is how it will be when Moshiach comes.

title.en: The chassid's weakened chassidus and the dream

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of someone who explained why a chassid's chassidus had weakened: because the emunah of simple Jews had weakened, and since all souls are one rope, this pulled the chassid down from above. That night he dreamt the reverse: perhaps the simple people faltered because the chassid weakened above. The Mashgiach says both views are true, and each person must know that this is his own…

title.en: The father and the third garment

retelling.en: Bringing the teaching attributed to the Kedushas Levi, the Mashgiach tells a parable. A father bought his son a garment, and the wild child tore it; he bought a second, and the child tore that too. He then bought a third, beautiful garment and said he would not give it until the son showed he could take care of it, but from time to time he showed it to him so he would improve himself and earn it.…

title.en: The Beis Aharon and the chassid's Shir HaShirim

retelling.en: The Beis Aharon once saw a precious chassidish Jew who could not learn, sitting in the beis medrash on Shabbos and saying Shir HaShirim with great sweetness. He asked him whether he perhaps knew its meaning. The man answered that one need not know the meaning, since the words themselves are so sweet. The Mashgiach compares this to the Shabbos meal of Atika Kadisha, which one tastes without unders…

title.en: Eliyahu in the non-Jewish cemetery

retelling.en: Rabbah bar Avuha found Eliyahu HaNavi in a non-Jewish cemetery and asked him questions in halacha, which Eliyahu answered. Then he asked: is the master not a kohen, so what is he doing in a cemetery? Eliyahu answered that he had forgotten what they learned, that according to Rabbi Shimon graves of non-Jews do not make tumah in a tent. The Mashgiach asks why Eliyahu did not simply say he was not a…

title.en: Mordechai's fast over Pesach

retelling.en: In the days of Esther, the three days of fasting fell over Pesach and the Jews did not eat matzah. The Mashgiach brings a sefer that Mordechai had a great plan: he knew that on Pesach night there is great joy in heaven from the Jews' seder and Hallel. When heaven saw a Pesach night without a seder, the decree against the Jews was turned away.

title.en: The Toldos Aharon Rebbe's Tisha B'Av davening

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Toldos Aharon Rebbe trained his students in tefillah and spoke even on Tisha B'Av about davening with taste and liveliness. Although the Shulchan Aruch says that on Tisha B'Av one davens quietly, he held that lively davening was more important. The Mashgiach adds that the Rebbe had broad shoulders, while we must follow the Shulchan Aruch.

title.en: Singing at the Arizal's tziyun in Tzfas

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls being at the tziyun of the Arizal in Tzfas. At the grave of a Tanna one usually says over a mishnah or a saying of his, but he asked himself what he could say over at the Arizal's tziyun. He thought of singing Bnei Heichala, and then of the Arizal's zemiros with the words about the soul's longing: he has a longing to know the secrets but does not know them, yet sing he can.

title.en: One hand for Shir HaShirim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach was invited to speak to a class in a certain yeshiva where all the parallel classes were gathered, close to a hundred boys. Wanting to quote a passuk from Shir HaShirim, he asked who says Shir HaShirim, and only one hand was raised. He calls it a sign of today's watered-down Yiddishkeit.

title.en: Graetz's history and the splitting of the sea

retelling.en: As a boy, the Mashgiach came across a set of history volumes by the historian Graetz, whom he calls a heretic. He innocently opened an early volume and found it discussing the splitting of the sea, admitting it was a historical fact experienced by a multitude. But Graetz explained it as natural changes in the tides and the atmosphere that opened a path just as the Jews passed.

title.en: The Rambam under the step of the Karaite synagogue

retelling.en: In the Old City of Yerushalayim, opposite the Ruzhiner shul of R' Nissan Bak, the Karaites had a synagogue where a gathering was once held, and the Ohr HaChaim went there. Going down one of the steps he trembled and asked what was under it. When it was opened they found a Rambam, which the Karaites had put there so people would step on it, since the Rambam writes that they are heretics. The Ohr H…

title.en: The lion that guarded the Ohr HaChaim on Shabbos

retelling.en: The Ohr HaChaim was traveling through the desert with a caravan when Shabbos came. He stopped and would not go on, though the place was full of murderers and wild animals, and the caravan left him behind. A lion came and stood by him, guarding him from all robbers and wild beasts for the whole Shabbos. On Motzaei Shabbos he rode the lion and caught up with the caravan.

title.en: Eliyahu HaNavi in the Ohr HaChaim's room

retelling.en: The Chida, a student of the Ohr HaChaim, writes that he was once with him when the Ohr HaChaim sent him outside, even though it was raining. Later he called him back in, and the Chida understood that Eliyahu HaNavi had been there. The Ohr HaChaim then told him that Eliyahu had said one should stand, not sit, when saying Mizmor Shir L'yom HaShabbos on Friday night.

title.en: R' Yitzchak Nafcha and his two students

retelling.en: R' Ami and R' Assi sat before R' Yitzchak Nafcha. When he began a halachah, one did not let him; when he began an agadah, the other did not let him, since each wanted to hear something different. He said he would tell them something fitting for both, and taught the halachah of one who lights a fire together with the agadah that Hashem lit a fire in Zion and will rebuild it with fire.

title.en: Rebbe Reb Elimelech's disciple on the island

retelling.en: One of the yoshvim in Rebbe Reb Elimelech's beis medrash found his weekly money shrinking and then gone, and after teshuvah and fasting his friends sent him overseas to trade. On the way back the ship stopped at an island; saying Tehillim alone under a tree, he missed the ship's whistle and was left behind. Days of thirst brought him close to death until he crawled to a little water, and there, a…

title.en: The brandy and the father's yahrzeit

retelling.en: A tzaddik, as a young man, kept a tavern where people came in to drink brandy. Once a man took a glass and drank it without a bracha. The tzaddik asked him whether there might be something in that brandy that he needed to elevate for his father, and the man then remembered that it was his father's yahrzeit that day. The Mashgiach notes that the story continues further.

title.en: The kohen and the sotah who was his mother

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a heartrending Midrash about a kohen who served in the Beis Hamikdash. A sotah was brought before him, and he had to uncover her hair. The woman turned out to be his own mother, and he cried out that he should have honored her, and now he sees her in such a state. The Mashgiach says this is what Yirmiyahu says about Tziyon, the mother of Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Kiddush with tears on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: A great tzaddik in Galicia once took a cup on Tisha B'Av as if to make kiddush, while tears ran from his eyes. He showed his chassidim that this is how kiddush will be made on Tisha B'Av when it becomes a yom tov.

title.en: The hole in the pocket

retelling.en: A woman asked a tzaddik why, although she made havdalah over a full cup every motzei Shabbos, which is said to bring sons, she had not been blessed with sons. He answered that she had a hole in her pocket: whatever is put in falls out. Had it not been for other deeds, her pocket would have been whole.

title.en: Rabbi Meir Auerbach and the takanah against music

retelling.en: During a great epidemic in Jerusalem, when teshuvah and tefillos did not help, Rabbi Meir Auerbach asked his teacher in Kabbalah at the Beis El yeshivah what Heaven wanted. He was told to perform the yichudim of she'elas chalom; he fasted a day, did so, and was shown the passuk 'behold he stands behind our wall'. He thought it meant to go daven at the Kosel, but his teacher explained that since t…

title.en: The ger tzedek's question to the Vilna Gaon

retelling.en: The ger tzedek Avraham ben Avraham, once Count Potocki, asked the Vilna Gaon that he did not understand the Gemara about one walking in the desert who does not know when it is Shabbos. How could one not know, he asked, when the very sand of the desert looks different on Shabbos? The Mashgiach says that to see Shabbos in the sand one needs a torch of havdalah.

title.en: The Malbim and the maskilim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Malbim used to debate the maskilim and always won. He once described to them how much he must wait: he wakes hungry but must first daven at length, then wash, make a brachah and dip the bread in salt three times before he may eat. They, he said, can eat breakfast in bed and need not wait.

title.en: Osnas, daughter of Dinah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, from the Midrash, Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer and Targum Yonasan, that from Shechem's taking of Dinah a daughter was born. The brothers were displeased with her, so Yaakov protected her and placed her in a bush, and the angel Gavriel carried her to Egypt, where Potiphar raised her; she was Osnas, Yosef's wife. She wore an amulet Yaakov had hung on her showing she was of his family…

title.en: The deaths in the desert and Tu B'Av

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that in the desert, every Tisha B'Av the people would lie down in graves, and some died each year of the forty. In the last year they all rose alive, and thinking they had erred in the date, they lay down again the next days. On the fifteenth of Av they saw the full moon and understood that the decree was over, and the day became a Yom Tov.

title.en: The poritz who sledded on sugar

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a poritz who, on a hot summer day, wanted to ride a sleigh. At a time when sugar was very expensive, he had thousands of sacks of sugar spread over the field so that it looked like snow, and rode over it in his sleigh. People came to a tzaddik and spoke of the great pleasure a poritz can allow himself. The tzaddik answered: what connection does his pleasure have with the pl…

title.en: Rebbe Reb Elimelech's circle as one family

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites the letter printed at the end of Noam Elimelech, written by Reb Mendel, describing the love among Rebbe Reb Elimelech's circle. It was so great that one could not tell whose children were whose; they were like one large family. Each one accepted the other's children like his own, and felt his friend to be a brother.

title.en: The slain of Beitar did not decay

retelling.en: After the destruction, Jews did not give up and gathered around Bar Koziva, thinking he was Moshiach; even Rabbi Akiva thought so, until it became clear he was not. The wicked enemies wanted those who had fought for him to lie unburied and rot, to show that the hope of the Jewish people had rotted away. Instead the slain did not decay, which the Mashgiach ties to the blessing 'Hatov' that they di…

title.en: A rav and the Shabbos farfel

retelling.en: A rav used to eat farfel every Shabbos, as is the Jewish custom. Over it he would say: Ribono shel Olam, what was until now is 'farfallen', lost; from now on it will be good.

title.en: The Kotzker on borrowing a father

retelling.en: A chassid of Kotzk visited a Galician tzaddik who would cry out 'Oy Tatte' in his prayer. When he returned to Kotzk and told of it, the Kotzker said that one could answer: I am borrowing a father.

title.en: The news about Vashti in the beis medrash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Chiddushei HaRim once mused about the days of the Megillah: young men were learning Gemara in the beis medrash when a man came in with news from the palace that Vashti had refused the king's order and was going to be executed. Someone got up and told him to sit down and learn and stop bringing such filth into the beis medrash. Little did he know that this would beco…

title.en: A tzaddik's three times of 'drunkenness'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who used to say that he becomes 'drunk' three times a year: once on Shemini Atzeres, from the great kedushah that comes down then, and a second time when he hears the Megillah. The Mashgiach says he does not remember the third time.

title.en: The generation of the desert and the full moon

retelling.en: As Tosafos brings, every Tisha B'Av in the desert the people lay down in graves and some of them died, for forty years. In the fortieth year they lay down and in the morning everyone rose. Thinking they had erred in the calendar, they lay down again night after night, until on the fifteenth they saw the full, shining moon and knew none would die; that became a Yom Tov.

title.en: No sword in Shlomo's camp

retelling.en: When two women came before Shlomo HaMelech for judgment, he stood surrounded by all his servants and soldiers and said, bring me a sword. Among all those soldiers no one had a sword, and one had to be fetched in a hurry from a museum. The Mashgiach explains that Shlomo had not conquered the world with a sword.

title.en: The man from Biala who chose right after Yom Kippur

retelling.en: Someone told about his father in Biala, whose custom was to go into the shop on his way home on motza'ei Yom Kippur and pick out a sealed box. He took it home and did not open it until the morning, and he always had the finest one in town. Asked how this happened, he said it was no wonder but a simple reckoning: what a Jew needs is set aside for him in heaven, but he must merit to receive it; rig…

title.en: The last Tisha b'Av in the desert

retelling.en: Because of the decree on the dor hamidbar, every Tisha b'Av they dug graves and lay down in them at night, and each year a certain part of them died while the rest got up and waited for the next Tisha b'Av. In the fortieth year all of them got up, and they thought they might have miscounted, so they lay down again on the tenth, eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth and fourteenth. When the fifteenth came…

title.en: The Radziner's techeiles and the Sfas Emes

retelling.en: The Radziner Rebbe, a great genius who also knew the sciences and chemistry, set out to find techeiles. He went to places near the Kinneret where the chilazon can be found, found it and made techeiles, and went around to rabbanim and gaonim claiming it was the original techeiles, but almost nobody would accept it, and he argued with proofs from Shas and poskim and from the sciences. He came to th…

title.en: Chushim kills Esav at Yaakov's burial

retelling.en: At the burial of Yaakov Avinu, Esav came running and claimed the Me'aras HaMachpelah belonged to him, and he tried to stop the burial. Chushim, the son of Dan, who could not hear or speak, asked what was happening, and was told by signs that Esav was not letting his grandfather be buried. Chushim took a rod and struck Esav, killing him.

title.en: The shoemaker chassid

retelling.en: A simple chassid, a shoemaker who knew little learning, would hammer shoes the whole day. As he worked he kept repeating his Rebbe's name together with the wish that the Rebbe be well. The Mashgiach relates that this was likened to one who learns the whole day.

title.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz and the milk

retelling.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz came into his kitchen and asked why no milk had come. The Mashgiach tells of a woman with a child who had no milk to give the child and who asked for help.

title.en: The messenger and the salvation

retelling.en: A man was gravely ill and the doctors could not help him, so a messenger was sent to a Rebbe. Later it was found that the change came at exactly the time the messenger was there. Afterwards they went to visit the Rebbe to thank him.

title.en: Yehoshua prepares the beis medrash

retelling.en: According to the Midrash the Mashgiach brings, Yehoshua's fellows called him a fool who could not learn. Wanting a share in Torah, he served Moshe: he spread a mat where Moshe sat and arranged the benches and seforim in the beis medrash so that the students would not lose time. Because of this service he was the one chosen to carry the Torah after Moshe.

title.en: When the Chofetz Chaim passed away

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that he was a small child when the Chofetz Chaim passed away, and that in his father's chassidish shtiebel too everyone knew who the leaders of Klal Yisroel were: the Chofetz Chaim, the Gerrer Rebbe, and later others. All of Klal Yisroel accepted them, and even Ben Gurion, when he wanted the Torah world's agreement on drafting women, knew whom to approach.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's quick teshuvah

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer once received a very difficult question and wrote the teshuvah quickly, during his meal. His son, the Ksav Sofer, asked how he could answer such a complicated matter without thinking it through. He answered that in every generation there is one through whom Hashem's halachah is decided, and even if someone later refutes his proofs, the halachah stays true.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva Eiger and the related witnesses

retelling.en: In a case involving certain witnesses, the Chasam Sofer, without being asked, wrote that one must also check that the witnesses are not relatives. Rabbi Akiva Eiger wrote in his teshuvah that his son-in-law Reb Moshe had answered something they had not asked, and when they investigated they found the witnesses were indeed relatives. The Mashgiach brings this as the siyata diShmaya earlier generat…

title.en: Reb Shimon of Yaroslav and the brandy

retelling.en: In his younger years Reb Shimon of Yaroslav ran a store selling brandy. A Jew came in, bought a glass and drank it without a brachah. Reb Shimon asked him when his father's yahrzeit was, and the man realized it was that very day. Reb Shimon told him his father's soul had been in the brandy and he had been sent to drink it with a brachah, and by drinking without one he had made his father's situat…

title.en: Reb Eizikel of Ziditchov's Hakol Yoducha in Sighet

retelling.en: Reb Eizikel of Ziditchov once came to Sighet, and the Yetev Lev, the grandfather of the Satmar Rav, received him with great honor. Some baalei batim in Sighet did not conduct themselves properly, and the Yetev Lev asked him to say words of mussar. The Ziditchover answered that he never says mussar, but whoever hears his 'Hakol yoducha' on Shabbos and does not do teshuvah, nothing will help him. T…

title.en: Ten years of learning for a cat

retelling.en: Rabbi Feivel Mendlowitz told of a man who took a young man from the yeshiva as a son-in-law and gave him ten years of kest with a room in his home. The first night the young man heard noise from the attic and assumed his father-in-law was checking whether he got up at night to learn, so tired as he was he got up and learned. This went on night after night for ten years. When the kest ended and he…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov on Rosh Chodesh Nisan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, when rulers are appointed in Heaven, the Ba'al Shem Tov was very active. If he did not want a certain ruler, or the malach over a nation, he would say so and that one would be deposed.

title.en: Dovid HaMelech waits for the sound in the treetops

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that when Dovid HaMelech went to war against the Pelishtim, the navi told him not to attack until he heard the footsteps of the malachim on the treetops. The Pelishtim charged so close that he saw the pupils of their eyes, yet he kept his sword at his side. Only when he heard the footsteps did he charge, and because he waited, Moshiach comes from him.

title.en: The drink without a brachah on the yahrzeit

retelling.en: A tzaddik, the Mashgiach recounts from old sefarim, sold liquor for a living. A simple Jew came in, poured himself a glass and drank at once without a brachah. The tzaddik asked him when his father's yahrzeit was, and the man realized it was that very day and he had forgotten. The tzaddik told him that his father's soul had been in that glass, waiting for him to make a brachah on it.

title.en: Leaving Spain with music

retelling.en: When King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella decreed the expulsion of the Jews from Spain, they had to leave with nothing but their clothes or convert. The rabbanim then instructed that they go out to music, with bands playing. The Mashgiach connects this to the masa'os being read with the tune of the Shirah.

title.en: The Chelm meeting about the missing pazer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a joke from Poland and Lithuania about the wise men of Chelm, who were always holding meetings. Once they met because for ten weeks of sidros there had not been a single pazer, and they had nothing to eat, a leaking roof and cold. When the chazzan finally sang a pazer, a Jew was revived by it.

title.en: Reb Feivel looking out the window

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's rebbe, Reb Feivel, stayed in a bungalow colony for his health when he had tuberculosis, before antibiotics. He davened with great strength and sweetness, sitting by the shul window and looking out. A man tapped him on the shoulder and asked why he was looking outside during davening. After davening Reb Feivel told him that he had been looking at Hashem's creations, saying along th…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the missing paroches

retelling.en: The Sanzer Rav said that the Beis Hamikdash built above through the Torah, tefillah and good deeds of the generations was already complete, and only the paroches was missing. One of the rabbanim at his table asked why the Rebbe, a great tzaddik, did not weave the paroches himself. He answered that he had made it, but some rasha came and ruined it.

title.en: Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: On Tisha B'Av a chassid was saying kinos with a broken heart and pouring tears. Reb Yechezkel'e of Kuzmir came over and asked him to go on an errand to do a favor for a Jew. The chassid was reluctant, since one is supposed to mourn the Beis Hamikdash. The Rebbe told him that the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed through sinas chinam, so the main kinah today is ahavas chinam, doing a favor for a Jew.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe as ba'al tefillah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Stoliner Rebbe had a powerful voice and would always serve as the ba'al tefillah himself. His davening carried far, and he did it so that his chassidim would learn from him to daven with warmth.

title.en: How the beis medrash began

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that bochurim in camp lacked a good davening, so they davened in Stolin, where davening was very warm and ran an hour and a half longer. After they left camp they missed it and asked him for a beis medrash of their own where they could keep davening as in camp, and so it was founded, which is why he always speaks about davening.

title.en: Davening aloud in Boyan

retelling.en: Coming to the Boyaner beis medrash for a weekday davening, it was seen that they davened aloud with hislahavus, and someone asked whether this was right. The answer given was that the Boyaner Rebbe said nowadays one cannot daven as in earlier times; one must daven louder with hislahavus, otherwise the yetzer hara takes the driver's seat.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's long davening

retelling.en: As a bochur in yeshiva the Chasam Sofer davened long. A friend told him that in the time he spent on Shemoneh Esrei he could have learned a siman of Shulchan Aruch. He answered that one who lengthens his tefilah has his days lengthened, so he would be given back the time.

title.en: Rabbi Aharon of Karlin before the beis din

retelling.en: When Chassidus began, misnagdim who had complaints against Rabbi Aharon of Karlin set up a beis din and summoned him because he davened aloud and shouted. The head of the beis din was a Rabbi Avraham. When Rabbi Aharon came in he cried out to him loudly, and when asked why he shouts, he asked what one does when one's house is burning; one shouts. In his davening, he said, our house is burning, so…

title.en: Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz's long Shemoneh Esrei

retelling.en: In a letter in the introduction to Yaaros Devash, Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz writes that the community had already gone on past Aleinu while he was still in the middle of Shemoneh Esrei, and the young men laughed at him. The Mashgiach notes they never laughed at his learning and his great pilpul, only at his davening, and that he wrote that his portion from all his toil was the time he stood before…

title.en: The neshamah that came too late

retelling.en: The Imrei Emes, son of the Sfas Emes, confirmed when asked that everything written in Meir Einei HaGolah is true. One thing written there is that every Erev Shabbos the Chidushei HaRim was occupied with tikkun of neshamos, until the Rebbetzin lit candles. Once a neshamah came after the candles were lit and he told it he could no longer do anything; that was his last Friday. The Mashgiach explains…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the chazzan

retelling.en: The Divrei Chaim once went over to a shliach tzibbur in the middle of davening, sent him away and had him replaced, telling him that a shliach tzibbur must lift the people.

title.en: The Satmar Rav: today one flees into the yeshiva

retelling.en: When the Satmar Rav came to visit Eretz Yisrael he spoke about the Rambam who says that if a person's surroundings are bad he should move to another city, another country, and if there is none, to the desert. He asked where one can flee today, and answered that today one can flee into the yeshiva; it is the only place left to run to.

title.en: The author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah thanks for small things

retelling.en: In his will, the author of Yesod V'Shoresh HaAvodah tells his children how he thanked Hashem aloud and with joy. He thanked many times a day for a private room for his avodah, and every time he put on his warm winter coat. When his snuffbox fell and did not spill, when a bottle was caught before it hit the ground, and when his glasses fell and did not break, he said a thanks to Hashem in set word…

title.en: The snuff during davening

retelling.en: A member of the Ba'al Shem Tov's circle saw a fellow take out a snuffbox and take snuff in the middle of davening. He held this against him and became so disturbed that he could not daven. Turning it over in his mind, he realized that taking snuff can give a person strength, and that there are holy sparks in tobacco that are elevated when a Jew uses it to strengthen himself, so his friend had don…

title.en: The Arizal stands up for Rabbi Chaim Vital

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital writes that he once came in to the Arizal, and the Arizal stood up for him. When he asked why, the Arizal said he did not know, but that he saw in him at that moment the soul of Benayahu ben Yehoyada. Some time later, walking on a road near Tzfas, the Arizal pointed to the cave of Benayahu ben Yehoyada, and Rabbi Chaim Vital recalled that he had once sat there and practiced a ka…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya and his jailer

retelling.en: While the Ba'al HaTanya was imprisoned, his gentile jailer asked him about the verse 'ayeka', where are you. The Ba'al HaTanya answered by telling him his exact age, in years, months, weeks, days and hours, and asked why in all that time he had never thought about what he is doing in the world. The jailer was deeply moved, because the age was exactly right.

title.en: The Mashgiach's first telephone

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that after his wedding he did not want a telephone at all. Then one night someone broke into their home, they were frightened and could not sleep, and only then did he get a phone so that they could call for help.

title.en: The man who wanted his cell phone in the beis medrash

retelling.en: When a sign was put up in the beis medrash asking that cell phones not be brought in, a man came to the Mashgiach to protest. He said he wants to sit and learn, but as a real estate owner he must have his phone in case of an emergency such as a fire. The Mashgiach says the man simply did not understand that a ringing phone takes away the seriousness of the beis medrash.

title.en: The Skverer Rebbe and the young man's mikveh

retelling.en: A young man eating at his father-in-law's table began going to the mikveh ten or fifteen times a day, and the father-in-law was unhappy and brought him to Reb Duvid'l of Skver. Asked why he did this, the young man answered that the Rebbe himself goes very often to the mikveh. The Mashgiach brings the story to ask whether every practice of the Rebbes must be imitated.

title.en: A Yerushalmi's will for Rosh Chodesh meals

retelling.en: Rabbi Moshe Halberstam of Yerushalayim, a grandson of the Tshakava Rav, owned a house with several apartments. He left a will that all the income from the apartments be used for seudos of Rosh Chodesh. The Mashgiach says he understood what a seudah of Rosh Chodesh is.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's supper of soap water

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe's rebbetzin once had to go to a wedding and told him his supper, a piece of meat and soup, was in a pot on the stove to warm up. When she came back in the morning the pot was untouched. Next to it had stood a pot of soapy water for washing dishes, and he had eaten that by mistake as his supper without noticing.

title.en: The poritz who sledded on sugar

retelling.en: A chassid came to Rabbi Aharon of Karlin and told him of a poritz who, on a hot summer day in Tammuz, wanted to ride a sleigh. Sugar was very expensive in Russia, yet he had his servants spread hundreds of sacks of sugar over the field and rode over it as over snow. Rabbi Aharon answered that this poritz is to be pitied, and asked how it compares to the pleasure of saying Nishmas kol chai.

title.en: Rabbi Aharon does not trust a bochur

retelling.en: Rabbi Eliyahu Steinberg told the Mashgiach that Rabbi Ahrele, the Shomer Emunim Rebbe, used to say that he does not believe a bochur who davens and learns; he wants to see how he is as a yungerman. The Mashgiach uses this to urge the young men to continue.

title.en: Rabbi Elchonon and the torn envelopes

retelling.en: A man asked Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman about the Gemara's promise of reward to one who makes Kiddush on wine: he made Kiddush on wine every Shabbos and had not merited it. Rabbi Elchonon answered that when one puts money into envelopes, the envelopes hold the money, but when the envelopes have holes, nothing remains. The Mashgiach applies this: the reward is there, but aveiros whose punishment is p…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov smiles at a fallen building

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once smiled, and his students asked why. He said that there had been a building on which twenty thousand workers labored for twenty years. A tzaddik passed by in a heavy rain and went in to shelter from it; when he left after the rain, the whole building collapsed. Its entire purpose had been to give a tzaddik a little comfort from the rain.

title.en: Reb Zusha: nothing bad ever happened to me

retelling.en: A man came to the Maggid of Mezritch and asked how one can accept suffering and bless on the bad as on the good. The Maggid sent him to ask Reb Zusha. Reb Zusha said he did not know why the Rebbe had sent him, for nothing bad had ever happened to him, so he did not know the meaning. The man then understood: for a tzaddik with emunah everything is good.

title.en: Two friends in Rome

retelling.en: A commentator brings a story, whether or not it happened: in Rome there were two dear friends, and when one of the king's buildings burned, one of them was accused and sentenced to hang. As he was led out, his friend ran up and said that he had burned the palace and should be hanged instead, and each refused to let the other be hanged. They were brought to the king, who said that seeing such love…

title.en: The chaplain going to Iraq

retelling.en: A former talmid of the yeshiva, now an army chaplain stationed in North Carolina, called the Mashgiach for a brachah before leaving for Iraq. The Mashgiach had thought Jewish soldiers there were rare exceptions, since the American army is all volunteers. The chaplain told him there are over a thousand Jewish soldiers in Iraq, and that he was taking along loads of matzos for them; the Mashgiach ga…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov on Rosh Chodesh Nissan

retelling.en: Every Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the new year for kings, the Ba'al Shem Tov would go into a private room for the whole day and let no one speak to him. In Heaven the ministering angels over the kings are appointed then, and he would have his say about which king should rule and which should be removed.

title.en: Reb Levi Yitzchak and the women kashering for Pesach

retelling.en: Before Pesach, Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev walked through the streets and saw the women outside scrubbing, polishing and kashering their dishes. He said the yehi ratzon that is said after the shofar blasts. Asked why, since no one was blowing shofar, he answered that this too is the 'tashrak', and asked that the angels created from it be advocates for Klal Yisrael. The women do not know what…

title.en: From fear of a decree to simcha at Selichos

retelling.en: A tzaddik was davening Selichos with great kavanah and saw that there was a harsh decree that could not be annulled. Then he became joyous, called someone over and asked him the meaning of the words that end 'anu banecha'. He explained it simply: whatever we have done, we are Your children.

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair came as a guest to a certain place, and his donkey would not eat. When they asked what was wrong with it, he said that perhaps the food had not been tithed, and so it was. The Mashgiach notes that a tzaddik avoiding forbidden food is understandable, but a donkey doing so is a great level.

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the cake

retelling.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov came to a certain rav, and the rebbetzin brought in a fine cake. Each time he was asked to make a brachah he began a pilpul instead, until someone ran in to say the cake had been baked in a fleishig pan. The host said he had not known the Yeshuos Yaakov had ruach hakodesh; he answered that it was not ruach hakodesh, but when he cut into the cake it sprayed into his face, and he…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya and the minister: 'Where are you?'

retelling.en: One of the ministers spoke with him and asked why Hashem asked Adam 'Where are you?', as though He did not know. The Ba'al HaTanya answered that Hashem asks every person, so many years old, who goes around doing nothing: where are you, what are you doing in your world, don't you know you were sent on a mission?

title.en: The cheder boy's answer about 'arur'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a melamed of eight- and nine-year-old children he learned Parshas Ki Savo with them, with Rashi that 'baruch' was also said. He asked them why a Torah of chesed writes only 'arur'. One child answered that Hashem wanted to honor the Oral Torah with the blessing, and the Mashgiach says the child did not realize how good his answer was.

title.en: Learning at three in the morning

retelling.en: The Mashgiach, who lived on the same block as the Satmar Rav for about twenty years, once came there at three in the morning. People would climb up and look through the cracks of the blinds to see what he was doing, and he sat and learned. He dozed for a few minutes in the middle of speaking and on waking knew exactly at which word he had stopped.

title.en: The Shovavim drashos

retelling.en: In the Shovavim weeks the Satmar Rav would arouse the people to teshuvah about kedushas habris, and thousands stood in his large shul like a pyramid. The Mashgiach once had to leave on a Motzaei Shabbos to give a shiur. He says the whole crowd wept, and there was not one dry cheek among the thousands.

title.en: Rabbi Yonasan Steif pushing to hear the Aseres HaDibros

retelling.en: The Mashgiach remembers Rabbi Yonasan Steif, an eighty-year-old who was rav of his own shul and had already davened and eaten, pushing his way through the packed crowd to hear the Satmar Rav lain the Aseres HaDibros. Nobody made way for him, and he waited, whether five minutes or two hours, to hear it.

title.en: Rabbi Shalom of Belz reads the Megillah in Lublin

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rabbi Shalom of Belz was once in Lublin, and the Chozeh of Lublin honored him with reading the Megillah. Afterwards the Chozeh said he had heard the story many times, but never told as beautifully as this young man told it.

title.en: Eating cherries on Motzaei Shabbos

retelling.en: One Motzaei Shabbos at three in the morning the Mashgiach and others looked through the gap in the blinds and saw the Satmar Rav eating cherries. He held each cherry in his hand and moved his hands for several minutes before eating it, not knowing anyone was watching; the Mashgiach says these were the kavanos with which he ate.

title.en: Holy names in the Shabbos fish

retelling.en: Rabbi Yonasan Steif, who knew Kabbalah, once sat at the Satmar Rav's tish and saw that as he cut the fish he arranged a piece of fish according to certain holy names. The Mashgiach says he does not know what it meant, but the Satmar Rav was clearly doing something there.

title.en: The beard in the concentration camp

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of an article by a writer who had been with the Satmar Rav in a concentration camp, describing his wondrous cleanliness. All the others had to cut their beards under a decree threatening death, but he did not. When an inspector came to check for cleanliness, he touched his beard and declared him clean.

title.en: A speech at a Mizrachi convention

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that eleven years earlier, when the Satmar Rav fell ill, Rabbi Yosef Soloveitchik spoke at a Mizrachi convention and told them to pray for the Satmar Rav's health. The reason he gave was that what little they held on to Yiddishkeit was only out of fear of how the Satmar Rav would react.

title.en: Shabbos in the challah and the fish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great chassid who was very poor and with effort prepared a little fish and a little challah for Shabbos. He spoke to the Ribono shel Olam: we have given challah for Shabbos, give me Shabbos in the challah; we have given fish for Shabbos, give me Shabbos in the fish.

title.en: The chassid who sang Nishmas while salting the fish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a story he attributes to Reb Mordechai of Slonim's stories. A chassid's task was to prepare the fish for Shabbos, and on Friday, while salting the fish, he would sing Nishmas. When the fish was served to the tzaddik on Friday night, the Lechovitcher said that a piece of Nishmas lies in the fish.

title.en: The Belzer Rav at the Shabbos candles

retelling.en: During the Sinai war, the Belzer Rav stood at the Shabbos candles for sixteen hours without a break, weak as he was. He kept repeating 'ufros aleinu sukkas shelomecha' and did not let up, and there were great salvations for the Jews. He said that the enemy had wanted to do even worse than the leader of Germany.

title.en: The Maggid's test of a ba'al korei

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch needed a new ba'al korei, and a young talmid was suggested. The Maggid asked him whether he knew how each of the seven portions of the week's parsha relates to its day of the week, and how each man called up is connected to his aliyah by hashgachah pratis. When he said he knew, the Maggid said he could be his ba'al korei.

title.en: Afraid to go to America

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that when he was in Eretz Yisrael some years earlier, someone told him she could not sleep because of the intifada and was thinking of going to America. He answered that he was afraid to go to America, and she laughed. Shortly after he arrived in America came the attack on the Twin Towers; he says he had based this on a Gemara.

title.en: The kernel of wheat in the tzaddik's soup

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story he heard from the Klausenberger Rebbe about a tzaddik who resolved to have a perfectly chametz-free Pesach. He cleaned and scoured for days and nights and made his matzos with great stringency, and at the Seder he rejoiced that his Pesach was kosher. Then he was served soup and saw a kernel of wheat floating in it. In a she'eilas chalom he asked why he deserved this an…

title.en: The Lechovitcher feels his rebbe's passing

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings, in the name of Reb Mottel of Slonim, that when Reb Shlomo of Karlin passed away the Lechovitcher was not told. He began to cry out and beat his head against the wall, saying that he no longer felt his rebbe and was cut off from him. When the chassidim told him that Reb Shlomo had passed away, he calmed down: if the rebbe is no longer in this world, that is why he no longer f…

title.en: The Rambam and the letter about techiyas hameisim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Toldos Yaakov Yosef, who heard from the Ba'al Shem Tov that a certain community wrote to the Rambam asking for the proof that techiyas hameisim is from the Torah, since the verses could be explained differently. The Rambam did not want to answer them, and told his student to write that they had been damaged by forbidden food. Had they not eaten forbidden food, they would…

title.en: Parting with a seudah

retelling.en: A couple without children for ten years came to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai to divorce. He told them that just as they married with a seudah, they should part with a seudah. The wife gave her husband good wine, and he told her to take the dearest thing from the house to her father's house; she carried him there. When he woke she told him he was the dearest thing, and Rabbi Shimon davened for them and…

title.en: A Sanzer grandson's family tradition

retelling.en: The Mashgiach met a friend, a grandson of Sanz living in Williamsburg, and asked whether he knew of this teshuvah. The friend said he did: his family has a tradition that an ancestor followed the advice of the Chiddushei HaRim and was helped.

title.en: The talmid whose house was full of visitors

retelling.en: A talmid of a great tzaddik complained to his Rebbe that the people of his town keep coming in to talk with him. He was told that this is the main thing: when Jews sit together, even without words of Torah, simply because they set themselves apart from the outside world, it is a great strength for emunah and for holding on in galus.

title.en: Leaving the table because of a joke

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who made a wedding for his child. At the meal the mechutan greeted him with some joke, and he stood up and left, because he could not sit at a table that had become a moshav leitzim. The Mashgiach contrasts leaving after hearing one joke with spending a whole day on leitzanus.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, through someone who was present as a bochur, that the Chofetz Chaim once gathered people to say a drasha calling for teshuvah because the Mississippi river had flooded in America. The Jews of Radin had never even heard a word as long as 'Mississippi', and it was thousands of miles away. The lesson the Mashgiach draws is that when Hashem brings upheaval on the world, He mean…

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech and the yud of yarbeh

retelling.en: Shlomo HaMelech took more wives than the Torah allows a king, reasoning that he knew himself and his heart would not be turned, and that he wished to bring them under the wings of the Shechinah. The yud of the word 'yarbeh' went up before the Kisei HaKavod to complain, and Shlomo HaMelech indeed stumbled.

title.en: The Kotzker and the Ushpizin

retelling.en: A great tzaddik from Galicia who disagreed with the Kotzker's path of avodah sent him a messenger asking how he dares to argue with him, since on Sukkos he sees the seven Ushpizin come into his sukkah. The Kotzker answered that on Sukkos he believes the Ushpizin come to him, and believing is greater than seeing.

title.en: Rabbi Yisrael of Vizhnitz and the chametz in the heart

retelling.en: Rabbi Yisrael of Vizhnitz was once searching for chametz with his candle, accompanied by one of his great chassidim, whose name the Mashgiach says he forgot. The Rebbe called out to the chassid to look into his heart and search it for chametz. The chassid answered with the Gemara that a place into which chametz is not brought does not need to be searched.

title.en: The simple Jew whose tefillah annulled a decree

retelling.en: When the Russians made a harsh decree, tzaddikim gathered and worked hard to annul it, and suddenly they began to smile. Asked why, one explained that they had been unable to annul the decree, but a simple Jew who did not even know Hebrew davened with kavanah, and his tefillah accomplished what they could not.

title.en: The Besht crosses the river on his gartel

retelling.en: The Degel Machaneh Ephraim writes what the Ba'al Shem Tov told him: he once had to cross a wide, dangerous river and had no boat or other way across. He spread his gartel on the water, stepped onto it, and it carried him across. The Besht told him not to think he did it with holy names or yichudim; he did it with emunah alone, believing that if a boat can carry a man across, so can a gartel.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's notes in Nissan

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar writes in his sefer, as an eyewitness, about the custom of his Rebbe, the Chozeh of Lublin. On the first day of Nissan the Rebbe wrote down everything that would happen in Nissan, on the second day everything for Iyar, on the third day for Sivan, and so on through the first twelve days. After the twelfth day he gave the writing to his talmidim, who were not allowed to look unt…

title.en: The home ready for Shabbos by midday

retelling.en: A shidduch was proposed for a great Rebbe with a woman from a simple, G-d-fearing family without yichus, and people asked why he agreed. He answered that he had been a guest in that home, and whenever he came on erev Shabbos at midday everything was already ready: the challos and the candles on the table, and the people sitting and waiting for Shabbos. Seeing such kedushas Shabbos, he had prayed…

title.en: Rabbi Aharon of Karlin on true pleasure

retelling.en: Rabbi Moshe Leib told Rabbi Aharon of Karlin about a wealthy porets who, in the middle of summer, had sugar spread out so he could go sled riding. Rabbi Aharon of Karlin answered: that is pleasure? The pleasure of the neshama, that is pleasure.

title.en: The Kotzker Chassidim on Pesach night and Yom Kippur night

retelling.en: Someone came into the Kotzk beis medrash on Pesach night and found two Kotzker Chassidim learning, and one said to the other, 'Let us go home to eat supper.' He was shocked that a Jew could call the seder 'supper'. Half a year later, on Yom Kippur night, he found the same two, and one said, 'Let us go daven Maariv.' When this was told to the Kotzker Rebbe, he said that by them every supper is a s…

title.en: The grandson who ran to see Eliyahu

retelling.en: Bringing it from Rabbi Mordechai of Slonim, the Mashgiach tells that Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver once said that Eliyahu HaNavi was in the street, and a grandson ran out to find him. He did not find Eliyahu, but at a fair he saw oxen tied to posts: some pulled to break free so they would be fed, while others stood quietly and waited. He wondered what the pulling ones gained, since they would all eat t…

title.en: In the last bench at the dedication

retelling.en: When the new building was dedicated, there were days of celebration at which the greatest rabbanim came and spoke, all of it organized by Reb Shraga Feivel. He himself sat in the last bench of the hall, as one of the audience. The talmidim knew that wherever he sat, that was the mizrach, and all eyes were turned to him.

title.en: The torn leaf in camp

retelling.en: Reb Shraga Feivel was the first to think of a summer camp for bnei Torah. Once, walking in camp with talmidim, one of them tore a leaf off a plant, and he stopped. He asked whether the talmid knew that all of creation sings shirah to Hashem, every blade of grass and every leaf, and said that by tearing the leaf he had interrupted its song in the middle.

title.en: The leaf that leads the song

retelling.en: In his last period, Reb Shraga Feivel sat in his home in Monsey on a still day when no leaf on the trees was moving. He pointed to the top of a tree, where a single leaf was shaking while all the others were still, and said that the top leaf is the chazan and the others answer after it.

title.en: Flowers in Monsey

retelling.en: When the yeshiva was being built in Monsey, then a place without Jews, one of the first things Reb Shraga Feivel did was plant flowers. He said the place must be beautiful so that there is something to say shirah on and to thank Hashem for, so that the bochurim see that Hashem made a beautiful world.

title.en: The kabbalos found after his passing

retelling.en: In his last years, when he was ill, Reb Shraga Feivel wrote down kabbalos for himself, and these were found later. His son passed two of them on to the Mashgiach. One was that every day he would come up with a new idea to improve the yeshiva, never letting a day pass without one; the other was to love every bochur and to deal warmly with each one.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: As a bochur, the Mashgiach heard a drasha from the elder Rav Kamenetsky, a talmid of the Chofetz Chaim. He related that the Chofetz Chaim once had the whole town called together, the townspeople and the yeshiva students, because he had an important drasha to say. He told them that in America a great river called the Mississippi had flooded and caused loss of life and property, and that this deman…

title.en: A tzaddik searches himself for chametz

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who went around searching for chametz with a candle, accompanied by his devoted gabbai, himself a great tzaddik. After searching with the candle, the tzaddik opened his shirt and spoke to the gabbai, and the gabbai answered him.

title.en: The father of the sick daughter on the stairs

retelling.en: The Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, counted every minute: once someone took two minutes of his time, and half a year later he told him those two minutes were still missing. Once, as he was going down the stairs, a man who had come up to his apartment wanted to speak with him, and the Rebbe said he had not a moment. The man answered that for twenty years he had been struggling with his sick daughter…

title.en: The blind chassid and the 'gifted years'

retelling.en: The second time, the Gerrer Rebbe visited an old chassid, R' Yankel, from the days of Kotzk, who had become blind. Asked how he was, he answered 'Baruch Hashem', but he could not look into a sefer and could not learn. The Rebbe told him these are gifted years. The chassid answered that he asks the Ribono shel Olam not to give him such gifted years.

title.en: Not peasant years

retelling.en: A chassid, a clever one, to whom the Ba'al HaTanya owed a favor, was offered a blessing for long life. He answered: 'Rebbe, but not peasant years', years with which one can accomplish something.

title.en: The Arizal and Rabbi Chaim Vital

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that the Arizal told Rabbi Chaim Vital he was as important as the Tannaim and Amoraim, and even the prophets. Rabbi Chaim Vital asked how he could compare to them. The Arizal answered that it was because he lived in a lowly generation; had he lived in an earlier one, he would have been among the greatest Tannaim and prophets.

title.en: 'There is a great yetzer hara'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what someone told him: a man went to visit an elder who had received many traditions from tzaddikim, a few days before the elder's passing, and asked him to say something from the tzaddikim. The elder said that a certain tzaddik had said there is a great yetzer hara, and then fell silent. When pressed to say more, he repeated the same words: there is a great yetzer hara.

title.en: Rav Chaim Ozer advises a move to Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who had a certain illness about which, in the laws of treifos, the Beis Yosef rules leniently and the Rema strictly. Rav Chaim Ozer advised him to move to Eretz Yisroel, where the halachah follows the Beis Yosef. The Mashgiach brings it to show that the halachah can differ from place to place.

title.en: Tears of joy after the Seder

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who, after the Seder, began to weep from joy, the tears running down his cheeks. He held his hands over his belly and said how fortunate it was, for it now held the holy names of the matzah, the maror, the afikoman, the karpas and the other mitzvos of the night. Realizing this gave him great happiness.

title.en: The author of Unesaneh Tokef asks for three days

retelling.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Yehuda with the author of Unesaneh Tokef. When the king pressed him with his demand, he asked for three days to think it over. Yehuda, the Mashgiach says, had no three days; he had to admit on the spot.

title.en: Lot's daughter who gave bread

retelling.en: In Sodom it was punishable to take in a guest or give charity. Citing a Midrash, the Mashgiach tells that Lot had a daughter who gave bread to a poor man. The people of Sodom seized her, smeared her with honey and exposed her to the bees, and she was killed because she had given bread. This, the Mashgiach says, shows that Lot's hospitality was real mesiras nefesh.

title.en: A spoonful every hour

retelling.en: A tzaddik in Yerushalayim, Reb Aryeh, had nothing to give the poor who came to him, so he would go with them door to door collecting tzedakah, and people knew to give him. Once he went around with one poor man, an hour later came another, and then a third, each time collecting again. One of the householders asked how much he could give, as this was the third time in three hours. Reb Aryeh answere…

title.en: The drunkard's reward

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a drunkard who resolved to stop drinking. One day passed without a drink, then a second, then a third. He then thought to himself that after such a hard battle of three days without wine or whiskey, he deserved a drink, took one, and was back where he had been.

title.en: A doubter at the Kaliver Rebbe

retelling.en: To show how faith was once visible, the Mashgiach mentions a man who had doubts in emunah and went in to the Kaliver Rebbe. He heard the Rebbe say words about emunah and immediately became a believer.

title.en: A gentile's words about the search

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that someone told him he had met a gentile after the search and the levayah. The gentile said to him, in English, that the Jews are a wonderful community. The Mashgiach contrasts this with a gentile child going missing, when the FBI and the police search but the people themselves do not.

title.en: The chaplain's call before leaving for Iraq

retelling.en: A former talmid of the yeshiva, Rabbi Horowitz, now an army chaplain based in North Carolina, called the Mashgiach before flying to Iraq to serve as chaplain. He told him that there were over a thousand Jewish soldiers in Iraq and that he was going to strengthen them, bringing matzos along. Soldiers fill out questionnaires to ask for a chaplain of their faith.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's notebook

retelling.en: The Bnei Yissaschar, a talmid of the Chozeh of Lublin, testifies that his Rebbe kept a notebook. On the first day of Nisan he wrote down everything that would happen in Nisan, on the second day what would happen in Iyar, on the third what would happen in Sivan, and so on through the twelve days, each matching its month.

title.en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and the scrubbing women

retelling.en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak was once walking in the street before Pesach when the women had brought their chametz utensils outside and were scrubbing and kashering them. He began saying words of praise over it, and when asked why, he answered with the women's own Yiddish words for kashering, rubbing and scraping.

title.en: The Malbim knows how to eat

retelling.en: The Malbim was a Rav in a German city with maskilim who had no yoke of Heaven, and he had many disputes with them. Once, after a group of them came to debate him and left, he said that they know. His students protested that he was much smarter and had beaten them, and he answered that they know, but he knows how to eat. He described waking up hungry and each time first doing what a Jew must do: n…

title.en: The Vizhnitzer Rebbe weeps on Rosh Hashanah night

retelling.en: A Jew came to Rabbi Yisroel of Vizhnitz for Rosh Hashanah. The Rebbe led the davening, and after Maariv, when 'L'Dovid Mizmor' was said, he wept greatly at the words 'lo nishba l'mirmah'. The man wondered who in the beis medrash had sworn falsely that the Rebbe should weep so. When he passed by for the Rebbe's brachah, the Rebbe asked him whether he knew the Gemara that a soul is made to swear to…

title.en: The wife whose husband became stricter

retelling.en: A wife brought her husband to a din Torah before a rav: when she married him he had certain standards in Yiddishkeit, and now he had become stricter and had taken on new practices, and she claimed she had not married such a man. The rav did not know what to answer and sent the question to the Chasam Sofer. The Chasam Sofer answered that a Jew must always become better, and when she married she sh…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the successful melamed

retelling.en: A very successful melamed asked the Chazon Ish whether he should study books on educational psychology to become a better melamed. The Chazon Ish answered him: why study psychology books, what is wrong with Chumash and Rashi? Learn Chumash and Rashi and you will know psychology.

title.en: The wolf and the sour grapes

retelling.en: In one of the well-known animal fables, a wolf came to a vineyard and saw beautiful, tempting grapes behind a high fence. For three days and three nights he struggled to climb over it. When he saw he could not, he turned around, said the grapes were sour, and walked away, because he did not want to admit he lacked the strength.

title.en: The physicist who refuted evolution

retelling.en: Some twenty years earlier, the Mashgiach recalls, the yeshiva invited one of the chief physicists of the Atomic Energy Commission in Washington, from the time the hydrogen bomb was made, to speak to the bochurim. He was an ehrlicher Jew who gave a shiur every night, and while waiting before his appointment he sat down to learn Gemara. In his lecture, not from the side of Torah but from science al…

title.en: A T-shirt in the street, years ago

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he was a boy, on a hot day, a man who went out into the street in only a T-shirt would not last five minutes. He would be arrested for disorderly conduct. He brings this to show how much the standards of the street have fallen since then.

title.en: The anatomy book in Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in an apartment he rented in Eretz Yisrael, the landlord had a son who studied medicine, and there he found a medical book on anatomy describing the shape of the body and its organs. The book had over three hundred pages, and on every page there were wonders, perhaps twenty to a page. One example: why is the spine curved and not straight? Because a straight spine would…

title.en: The club house in Telz and the buried blood

retelling.en: In Telz, a club of young maskilim and Zionists had a club house with rooms where they slept. One of them took his own life by cutting his wrists and bled to death. Afterwards plaster kept falling from the ceiling of the bar below, and no matter how often it was repaired it fell again, so they went to the Rosh Yeshiva. He said he did not know of hidden matters, but knew the halacha that the blood…

title.en: The Maharsham's heavenly judgment

retelling.en: As a young man devoted to learning, the Maharsham fell gravely ill, and when the illness reached its crisis his wife sent a messenger to Reb Ayzikl of Zidichov, who said he would have a complete recovery. At the crisis the Maharsham began to sweat, opened his eyes and told that he had been brought before the heavenly court, where good angels piled his Torah on the scale until it outweighed his si…

title.en: The Kotzker Rebbe and the ushpizin

retelling.en: The Kotzker Rebbe had a new path in serving Hashem that another great tzaddik disagreed with. That tzaddik sent a messenger asking why the Kotzker quarreled with him, since on Sukkos he sees with his own eyes the seven ushpizin coming into his sukkah. The Kotzker sent back that on Sukkos he believes with complete faith that the seven ushpizin come into his sukkah, for believing is greater than se…

title.en: Forty years of Rabbeinu Bachya

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of someone who used to learn Rabbeinu Bachya on the parsha every Shabbos. He said that he had been learning it for forty years, and every year he found things in it he had not seen before.

title.en: The elder's wedding Shabbos garment

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes an older Jew of the previous generation who had his Shabbos garment, a kapote. When he passed away he still had the original Shabbos garment he had bought for his wedding. It was worn and had lost the shine of a new garment, but it was clean, and that is what he was careful about.

title.en: The Satmar Rav in Meron during the nine days

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Satmar Rav visited Meron during the nine days. There he had Bar Yochai sung, because in Meron there is no mourning.

title.en: The Arizal's student who said Nachem in Meron

retelling.en: From the writings of the Arizal through Rav Chaim Vital, the Mashgiach tells of a student, Rav Avraham HaLevi, who the Arizal said had the soul of Yirmiyahu. He always lamented the churban and added Nachem in every bentching. When he came to Meron he said it there too, and the Arizal told him he had blemished the honor of Rabbi Shimon and would be in mourning; his son passed away. In Meron there…

title.en: The heretic who recanted on his deathbed

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a leading Zionist heretic in Eretz Yisroel who taught that there is no need to believe in the Torah and had many students who came to hear his ideology. When he fell ill and was dying, he told his students that he had lived his whole life in error and that the Torah is true. His students answered that he had taught them heresy all along, so how could they know he was not ly…

title.en: The expulsion from Spain on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The king and queen of Spain decreed that all Jews must either convert or leave, taking nothing but the clothes on their backs. The day set for leaving was postponed by three days and, without the king intending it, fell on Tisha B'Av. The Jews who left went out in a great procession with music, which the sages of the generation ordered so that they would leave with joy and not weaken in their fai…

title.en: The burning of the Gemara in Paris

retelling.en: Some time after the Rambam's works were burned in Paris, the French government decreed against learning Gemara and had all Gemaras gathered from the whole country. About thirty wagonloads of handwritten Gemaras were burned in the streets of Paris, leaving the country without Gemaras to learn from. A kinnah said on Tisha B'Av was composed as a lament over it. Rabbeinu Yonah, who had encouraged the…

title.en: The two periods of the Chazon Ish

retelling.en: In Vilna the Chazon Ish kept himself completely hidden, known to very few, and only learned, without involvement in communal needs. After the Chofetz Chaim passed away he felt he had no one left to stay for and moved to Eretz Yisrael, settling in Bnei Brak. There he became an entirely different Chazon Ish: he spent hours every day on communal needs, hundreds came daily for brachos and with their…

title.en: The Yam Suf claims seniority over Moshe

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that when Moshe Rabbeinu wanted to split the Yam Suf, the sea refused, saying it was older: it was created on the third day of creation and man only on the sixth. Then Hashem rebuked the sea and it dried up. The Mashgiach explains that by right the elder should have precedence, but Hashem intervened because the Jews were in trouble, and then there is no place for…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe on communism

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that in his younger years he davened in the Stoliner shul in Williamsburg, by the Stoliner Rebbe, a tzaddik who said wondrous things. Some thirty years earlier, when people spoke with him about communism, the Rebbe said it had come for a fixed number of years. The Mashgiach says that now one sees with one's own eyes that it is falling apart exactly on time.

title.en: The disguised guest at the Purim seudah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes sitting at the Purim seudah with the candles burning and challah on the table, when someone walks in dressed as a rasha in red pants and an orange blouse. He asks him which yeshivah he is collecting for, because he knows the guest is no rasha, only dressed up. This, he says, is what it is to be frum: to know that everything is a disguise.

title.en: The dibbuk in Radin

retelling.en: A girl in Radin suddenly became ill and swollen, and a man's voice spoke coarse words from her. Her father went to the Chofetz Chaim, who, being old, sent Reb Elchonon Wasserman as his messenger; the whole town and many yeshiva students came along. The dibbuk spoke about everyone present, exposing sins, but said Reb Yisroel Chaim Kaplan was a fine Jew, and that in Heaven the Chofetz Chaim is reck…

title.en: The secret of the forty-day fast

retelling.en: A young man with epilepsy could not find a shidduch and came to the Chofetz Chaim, who sent him to a rav in a nearby town for a brachah. Within a little over a month he was completely cured, and the Chofetz Chaim made him promise to tell no one. Many years later he told a sick relative, who went to that rav without success, and he himself fell ill again. The Chofetz Chaim then told him that the r…

title.en: Dancing in Meron on the fifth of Av

retelling.en: A great Rebbe, a strict halachic authority, visited Meron on the fifth day of Av. He told the people to sing Bar Yochai, and they danced. Asked how this was permitted, he answered that in Meron, where Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is, there is no mourning, only joy.

title.en: Saying Nachem at Rashbi's celebration

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital writes of a Jew who mourned Yerushalayim all his days and said Nachem every day in Shemoneh Esrei and in bentching. On Lag Ba'omer he was with the Arizal at the celebration of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and said Nachem there too. The Arizal told him that people would come to comfort him, and he lost a son. Rashbi was strict with him because he said Nachem on the day and in the plac…

title.en: The Gaon's hint in Ki Seitzei

retelling.en: The Vilna Gaon lived in the century that matched Ki Seitzei, and Rav Chaim Volozhiner asked him where he is hinted in that parsha. The Gaon answered with the words 'even shleimah', read as Eliyahu ben Shlomo, his own name. Rav Chaim asked further about the rest of the verse and the Gaon answered him, but Rav Chaim never revealed the answer to his students.

title.en: A boy hears of the coming war
