retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that on the eve of 5700, as a boy in yeshiva in Williamsburg, some well-off boys had a radio and brought news that Hitler would enter Poland and that England and France would defend it. The boys were sure the Royal Air Force and the Maginot Line would wipe out Hitler within days. On Rosh Hashanah, standing beside his father, who was the ba'al tefillah, he saw the congregatio…

title.en: The Malbim and the cookie

retelling.en: The Malbim, a master of all wisdoms, waged a constant war with the maskilim in Germany and always defeated them in debate. Once he surprised people by saying that the maskilim know better than he does. He explained: when he opens his eyes in the morning he is hungry and wants a cookie, but he cannot eat it; he must wash his hands, daven, and make the proper brachah. The maskilim can eat it as soo…

title.en: Rav Hillman's letter to Rav Scheinberg

retelling.en: Rabbi Yaakov Weisburg told the Mashgiach he has a photostat of a short letter from Rav Hillman to Rav Pinchas Scheinberg. Rav Scheinberg had complained that his father-in-law, who had gone to Eretz Yisroel, did not write to him. Rav Hillman answered that a mekubal had told him only twenty-eight years remain, that twenty-eight years are not enough for him to prepare for Moshiach, and asked whether…

title.en: Dovid HaMelech and Shimi ben Gera

retelling.en: When Dovid HaMelech fled Yerushalayim with his family, Shimi ben Gera cursed him, and his men wanted to kill Shimi for rebelling against the king. Dovid told them to leave him, because Hashem had told him to curse. Through this Dovid became the leg of the Divine chariot; Shimi was not killed then and had children, and only later did Shlomo HaMelech put him to death.

title.en: The souls who protested in Heaven

retelling.en: A great tzaddik among the disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov told his disciples, once at Kiddush Levanah, that he had seen millions of souls gather in Heaven and protest: they had been sent down to rectify, but in each gilgul they only added sins. The officer of the souls sent them higher, to the angels, the seraphim and the chayos hakodesh, until they reached Hashem. Hashem told them that instead o…

title.en: The Maharsham's illness and the heavenly court

retelling.en: As a young man the Maharsham fell gravely ill, and his family sent a messenger with a kvitel and pidyon to Rabbi Eizikl, who said he would recover; at that very hour the Maharsham began to sweat and recovered. He later told that in Heaven a black angel blew his Torah off the scale because it was not lishmah, until a new dayan, a young man with a black beard, cried out that in these times even Tor…

title.en: The Arizal's disciple who said Nachem on Lag Ba'omer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what Rav Chaim Vital writes about a disciple of the Arizal who lived constantly lamenting the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash and said Nachem in every Shemoneh Esrei. He said it also when he came to Meron on Lag Ba'omer. The Arizal told him that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was not at all satisfied with him, and the disciple was punished because he was not joyful at the hillula…

title.en: The Lechovitcher chassid and his friends

retelling.en: A chassid of the Lechovitcher Rebbe, travelling on the roads of Russia, faced a great temptation to sin. He thought that if he sinned the Rebbe would see it on his face, so he decided not to go to the Rebbe; then he realized his friends in the shtibel would drag him to the Rebbe, and even if he davened in another shul they would come and find him. Because of this reckoning he was saved from the s…

title.en: The boy who did not like fish

retelling.en: Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz told that when he began teaching in America, he once spoke to a class with great feeling about the Leviathan that is salted away for the tzaddikim, as mentioned in Akdamus. A child raised his hand and said, 'Rebbe, I don't like fish.' With that one sentence the whole talk went down the drain.

title.en: The bochurim who clung to Rav Shraga Feivel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a talmid in the yeshivah he saw that the good bochurim clung to Rav Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, following him and learning every word. Others called him 'the boss' and had no connection to him, and nothing came of them.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe, the beard and the Jew

retelling.en: A Slonimer chassid told the Mashgiach that when the Slonimer Rebbe, the Beis Avraham, came to Yerushalayim, he ate supper each night at a different chassid's home. One night he told Chaim Yankel, a simple, sincere Jew without a beard, that supper would be at his house. When the fish was served, the Rebbe asked Chaim Yankel to eat from his plate; Chaim Yankel looked at Zvulun, a learned chassid wi…

title.en: The gabbai and the knife that was not toiveled

retelling.en: A Jew named Singer told how the Rebbe's gabbai used to stay at his parents' home when he came collecting. His mother bought a new knife in the gabbai's honor and sent him, a small boy, to toivel it in the river. The river was frozen and a hole had to be broken in the ice; it was cold and he was lazy, so he did not do it and said that he had. On Friday night the gabbai did not use the knife, and t…

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the cake

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells from seforim that the Yeshuos Yaakov, the Lemberger Rav, stayed with a rav in a town, and the rebbetzin baked a fine cake in his honor. Asked to make the brachah, he cut into it and began a pilpul on a difficult Rambam for about ten minutes, then another for twenty, until the rebbetzin ran in: she had made a dairy cake with butter and found she had used a meat pan. Asked wheth…

title.en: Russian Jews who forgot Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what he heard from someone about a Rebbe who recently went to Russia for about ten days with three or four hundred people, and they spent Shabbosos and celebrations with the Russian Jews. The Russian Jews were deeply moved; they had forgotten nearly everything, since for decades no one dared to be a Jew or teach children. One man remembered Shabbos and now waits each Friday…

title.en: Blessing to be healthy, fresh and mad

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Rebbe who, when his chassidim took leave of him after Yom Tov, would bless them to be healthy, fresh and mad. He explains that in the heels of Moshiach one who turns from evil is considered mad, so a person who wants to be an upright Jew must be ready to be called mad.

title.en: His father's grief at the Chofetz Chaim's passing

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a young boy his father once came home very distressed, having just read in the newspaper that the Chofetz Chaim had passed away. The whole Jewish world knew then that the Chofetz Chaim led the Jewish people.

title.en: The wheat merchant in peace and in war

retelling.en: A man met his friend, a wheat merchant, looking gloomy, and the merchant explained that business was bad: in times of prosperity there is much wheat, so buyers inspect it, asking whether it is good, large, fresh, and compare with competitors. Some time later he met the merchant beaming, and the merchant said business was golden because of the war: wheat was scarce, people were hungry, and they no…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's father and the glass cup

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer's father was discussing the affairs of the kehillah with its president, and noticed that his young son, who later became the Chasam Sofer, was learning and not paying attention. He asked his son why he did not listen, since there was what to learn from what he said. He told him that even when he moves a little glass cup from one place to another, he does not do it without a halac…

title.en: A journey to learn freedom from kinah

retelling.en: A tzaddik living in Eretz Yisrael made a trip to Europe to Rav Yisrael of Vizhnitz, saying there was no Jew as sweet as he. He explained that all tzaddikim work on themselves and purify themselves, but one thing even tzaddikim are not fully free of is kinah, and Rav Yisrael of Vizhnitz is free of it. So he made a point of spending a few Shabbosos with him to learn how not to be jealous.

title.en: The Divrei Chaim on the fall of German Jewry

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Divrei Chaim asked why German Jewry, once so fine and full of great and holy sages, suddenly fell so low, giving rise to assimilation and the Reform movement. He answered that they were not careful about their shochtim, who were not God-fearing, so they ate non-kosher meat, and that is what brought it about.

title.en: The man who saw a figure while davening

retelling.en: A man came to a tzaddik, whom the Mashgiach calls Reb Mendel, saying he could not daven because whenever he stood to pray he imagined a gentile with a cross in his hand standing before him. The tzaddik told him to let the gentile stand there and do his business while he does his own and davens.

title.en: A friend's doubts and Reb Shraga Feivel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he was a bochur, one of his friends told their rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, that he had doubts in emunah. Hearing this bothered the Mashgiach greatly, since he thought such a Jew must be a heretic. Only later did he understand that it is not so, and that every person has such periods in his life.

title.en: Rav Moshe of Savran remembers every thought

retelling.en: Rav Moshe of Savran, a tzaddik from the students of the Ba'al Shem Tov's students, once said he remembered every thought he had had, exactly, over the past fifteen years. Someone asked him how this was possible. He asked the man whether he remembered his own wedding, who was the mesader kiddushin, the musicians, the witnesses and the sheva brachos; the man said yes, because it was his wedding. Fo…

title.en: The Malbim and the maskil

retelling.en: The Malbim, a great gaon who was also expert in all branches of wisdom, had to contend with the maskilim of his time, who could not catch him out. Once a leading maskil came to debate him, and the Malbim surprised everyone by saying that what he knew was waiting. He described rising in the morning hungry but unable to eat: first washing his hands, then preparing and going to daven, then washing f…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and the child's name

retelling.en: Someone asked the Chiddushei HaRim what name to give his new child. The Chiddushei HaRim answered that at the moment a parent names a child he is given a spirit of prophecy, and asked why he should deprive him of it: let him be a prophet and decide the name himself.

title.en: Reb Yechezkel Shinever goes to Belz for Shavuos

retelling.en: Reb Yechezkel of Shinev, son of the Sanzer Rav, Reb Chaim of Sanz, left his father for Shavuos and went to Reb Shalom of Belz. When he prepared to go again the next year, his father asked what was wrong with spending Shavuos at home. He answered that in Belz he saw the thunder and lightning of Matan Torah and the 22,000 angels who came down with Hashem on Sinai, which he did not see at home. His…

title.en: The Bluzhever Rebbe's heartbeat before Shavuos

retelling.en: When the king passed through Bluzhev, the country's leading doctor came with him, and the chassidim arranged for him to examine the Bluzhever Rebbe. The doctor, a Jew from a good family who had gone astray, told the Rebbe his heart did not beat regularly. The Rebbe asked him whether he knew what day it was: six days before Shavuos, when he was going to receive the Torah, and the doctor expected h…

title.en: The translation for King Talmai

retelling.en: In the time of Greek rule early in the second Beis Hamikdash, King Talmai gathered the elders and put each in a separate room, without knowing of one another, to translate the Torah into Greek. The Mashgiach notes that a fast was later fixed over this translation. With ruach hakodesh they all made the same changes, for example writing the opening of Bereishis so that it begins with 'Elokim'. The…

title.en: The Abarbanel refuses to stay in Spain

retelling.en: The Abarbanel, a great tzaddik and sage, was a minister of the king of Spain when the Jews were given the choice to convert or leave with nothing. The king told him that all the Jews must go but he should stay, because the king needed him. The Abarbanel refused, said he goes with his people, and left. After the Jews were gone, Spain, then the mightiest power, became a poor and insignificant count…

title.en: Napoleon and the mourners of Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: Napoleon, the ruler of France, passed a shul and heard crying inside. Curious, he went in and saw Jews sitting on the floor, and asked what day it was. They told him it was Tisha B'Av, when they weep because the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed and they were driven from Eretz Yisroel. He said that a people still longing for its land after seventeen hundred years will surely return to it.

title.en: The Mashgiach's first visit and the small fruits

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he first traveled to Eretz Yisroel some thirty years earlier, he had imagined it beautiful, but found it desolate, with stony ground. He also remembers that Jews coming from Eretz Yisroel to America would bring its fruits along, tiny apples and small walnuts. Today, he says, the land is covered with growth and its fruits are large.

title.en: R' Shlomke of Zvhil foresees the teshuvah awakening

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts what a R' Eliyahu, whom he says he knew well, told him. R' Shlomke of Zvhil once told R' Eliyahu that an awakening of teshuvah was now beginning. R' Eliyahu did not understand what the Rebbe meant, since at the time nobody imagined Jews returning; only later did the baal teshuvah movement appear.

title.en: A two-hour Ahavah Rabbah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a chassid who came on an errand from his Rebbe and was asked how Shavuos had been by his Rebbe. He answered that the Rebbe said Ahavah Rabbah and it took two hours.

title.en: The short-long road and the long-short road

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara's account of a sage who wanted to reach a town and asked a girl the way. She showed him a road that was short, but when he came near the town it was blocked by gardens and orchards and he could not enter. He had to go back and take the other road, which was long but actually brought him in.

title.en: Women who lifted a piano in a fire

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, as a known fact, of ordinary weak women who, when a fire broke out in a house, carried a piano on their shoulders. They suddenly had strength they did not know they had. He adds that doctors explain this through hormones such as adrenaline that enter the blood in an emergency.

title.en: The traveler and the warm inn

retelling.en: In the name of the Slonimer tzaddikim, the Mashgiach describes a traveler caught in cold snow mixed with rain, soaked, hungry, thirsty and tired. Halfway he reaches an inn where he is let in, dries his clothes, gets a hot meal and a warm bed, and revives himself. When he is ready, he must continue on his way.

title.en: Ibn Ezra's poem about his bad luck

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that things went badly for the Ibn Ezra all his days and he had to wander. He wrote a poem about his bad mazal, saying that had he dealt in shrouds or been an undertaker, nobody would have died. The Mashgiach brings it to show how mazal governs a person's physical lot.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembered being a sheep

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe said that he remembered being one of the sheep of Yaakov Avinu, since all Jewish souls were once sheep with Yaakov Avinu. He showed a mark on his back and said it came from Yaakov Avinu striking him with a stick when he was a sheep. He also remembered other earlier lives, and even sang the niggun Yaakov Avinu played on his flute, a niggun known among Chassidim.

title.en: The king's seven walls

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov told of a king who surrounded himself with seven walls, each guarded by beasts on top and each harder than the one before, with gifts for every soldier who broke through. Soldiers who broke through the first walls received gold, silver and diamonds and went no further. The prince kept going, answered those who asked why he risked himself that he wanted the king himself, broke t…

title.en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak and the poritz's comforts

retelling.en: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev stood holding the shamash, ready to light the Chanukah candles with his chassidim gathered, when a man named Chatzkel came in from working for the poritz. Instead of making the brachah, he asked how the poritz fares, and heard of golden vessels, fine dishes from cooks trained abroad, and a soft bed, while the Rebbe himself slept on straw. Then he asked whether th…

title.en: The poritz who sledded on sugar

retelling.en: People ran to Rabbi Aharon of Karlin to tell him that a poritz had gone mad from pleasures: in the middle of summer he wanted to ride a sled. Sugar was very expensive in Russia then, yet his workers spread hundreds of sacks of sugar over the field, and the poritz went sledding on it. Rabbi Aharon dismissed the poritz's pleasure, asking what connection it has to the pleasure he feels on Shabbos mo…

title.en: Reb Naftali of Ropshitz and the sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that tzaddikim said Reb Naftali of Ropshitz was rooted in the mitzvah of sukkah. Every day he either learned Maseches Sukkah, spoke about the sukkah, or banged a nail into his sukkah. He felt a great pull toward his mitzvah.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav's son sees Matan Torah

retelling.en: A son of Rav Chaim, himself a great tzaddik, went for Shavuos to Rav Shalom of Belz. When he wished to go again, his father asked why; he said that in Belz, at the reading of the Aseres Hadibros, he saw the thunder and lightning of Matan Torah. His father told him to stay, and at the reading he saw and heard the thunder and lightning and saw himself standing at Har Sinai. His father then told him…

title.en: The groom who would not buy a ring

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a groom told to pay for flowers, musicians, photographer and whiskey, who paid for all of them. When told to buy a ring, he refused, saying he had spent enough. Without the ring, the Mashgiach says, she does not become his wife; so too one who learns all night, goes to the mikveh and then sleeps through davening has done everything but brought the ring.

title.en: Charity first from pity, then for the mitzvah

retelling.en: A hungry poor man came to a Jew, who fed him, prepared him a bed, gave him good clothing and money to go home. After all this he took a large sum of money and gave it to him as well. Asked why, he answered that until now he had given out of pity, and now he was giving for the mitzvah of tzedakah.

title.en: The Maggid of Mezritch loses his world to come

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch sat and learned in the beis medrash while his family had nothing and the children cried from hunger. He gave a sigh, and was told from Heaven that with this sigh he had lost his world to come. He rejoiced that, having neither this world nor the world to come, he could now learn purely for Hashem, and learned with great joy. Afterwards he was told that through this he had re…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the boy singing Shir HaShirim

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once came into a shul and found Yankele sitting over the chumash, swaying and singing the words of Shir HaShirim with great fervor. When asked, Yankele answered that he was just saying the words. The Ba'al Shem Tov was very pleased: without knowing what the words meant, his neshamah felt that something very sublime was there.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rebbe and the court doctor

retelling.en: The king's court doctor once passed through Bluzhev, and the devoted chassidim paid him to examine their Rebbe. The doctor, raised in a Jewish home, had left it and studied medicine in Berlin. Listening with his stethoscope, he said the Rebbe's heart was not normal. The Rebbe asked whether he knew what the Torah is, and told him that in six days it would be Shavuos and he would have to receive th…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the Frankists

retelling.en: In the Ba'al Shem Tov's time the Frankists, followers of the false messiah, broke away from the Jewish people. The Ba'al Shem Tov felt great anguish over it. He was told from Heaven not to grieve, because they were cut off in their roots and did not belong to Klal Yisrael: they were the nails that grow past the finger.

title.en: The Rebbe Reb Elimelech and the mezuzah

retelling.en: After the Maggid passed away, students came to become disciples of the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. On the way he lay down and slept a whole night, about eight hours, and the students were puzzled that their rebbe slept so long. His brother Reb Zusha saw that it disturbed them, went over and put his hand on the mezuzah, and at that moment the Rebbe Reb Elimelech woke up. Reb Zusha explained that his brot…

title.en: The man who did not stand up

retelling.en: A Rav known in Warsaw as a great gaon, whom everyone respected, later became a Rebbe. Once, walking in the street with his students, where people usually stood up for him, a man passed by and did not stand. The students were upset, but the Rebbe's concern was for the man: if he is not moved by a talmid chacham, what will pull him out of Gehinnom?

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the poor man

retelling.en: A poor man passed by the Chofetz Chaim, who gave him tzedakah. Someone objected that the man could work for a living. The Chofetz Chaim answered that when the angel declared him poor, his legs were filled with lead: he lacks the courage and energy, and it is not his fault.

title.en: Reb Shimon Yaroslaver on his father

retelling.en: Reb Shimon Yaroslaver's father was a coarse, unlearned man, while Reb Shimon became a holy man. He said that had his father immersed in a mikveh even once before he was conceived, his avodah would have been far easier. He refined himself nonetheless.

title.en: Menashe in the heated pot

retelling.en: Menashe was a great rasha who spread idolatry and brought an idol into the Beis HaMikdash. The king of Ashur took him captive, put him in a huge pot and lit a fire under it. Seeing he would be roasted, Menashe did teshuvah and turned to Hashem, and he was brought back to Yerushalayim. The angels argued that he should not be accepted, so Hashem dug a tunnel under the Kisei HaKavod and accepted him…

title.en: Menashe teaches Rav Ashi about hamotzi

retelling.en: Rav Ashi was expounding Sefer Melachim and ended a shiur saying that tomorrow they would speak of 'our friend Menashe'. That night Menashe came to him in a dream and asked from which part of the loaf one cuts at hamotzi; when Rav Ashi did not know, Menashe asked how he could call himself his friend. Menashe told him to cut where the crust formed first, the best-baked part. Asked why, if he was so…

title.en: Yehoash, hidden in the Kodesh HaKodashim

retelling.en: Yehoash was hidden by Yehoyada the Kohen Gadol for seven years in the Kodesh HaKodashim and then came out to reign. As long as Yehoyada lived he was good, but after Yehoyada died he became a different person: he let himself be treated as a god and killed Zechariah the prophet, the son of Yehoyada who had saved him. Zechariah was killed on Yom Kippur, in the place of the Kodesh HaKodashim.

title.en: A long davening in the Stoliner shul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls a Jew, a great talmid chacham, who davened in the Stoliner shul in Williamsburg where the Mashgiach himself davened. He would sit down to daven with contemplation and with relish, until tears ran from both his eyes. Others would go home, eat, rest a little and learn, and come back to shul, while he was still davening. The Mashgiach brings him as an example of contemplation w…

title.en: Rabbi Elias's advice to a young mechanech

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when he began working in chinuch, he went to Rabbi Elias, a great mechanech, for pointers on how to succeed. Among his advice was not to be afraid of telling young boys something deep. One might think it is too deep for them, but young boys are precious neshamos and understand more than grown-ups.

title.en: Mordechai at a Purim seudah

retelling.en: On Purim, the whole crowd went to Reb Pinchas, where the seudah was lively with singing and dancing, while Reb Yoel sat almost alone. A Jew came in to Reb Yoel and began to dance and sing, so beautifully and so loudly that it could be heard far away. Afterwards it was said that this Jew had been Mordechai HaTzaddik, who showed himself there in this way.

title.en: Reb Yitzchak Chayes appears barefoot

retelling.en: Reb Yitzchak Chayes, one of the great ones, wrote a commentary on Mishnayos, and his son writes in his introduction that his father once came to him in a dream after his passing. He was dressed in extraordinary, beautiful garments, but he went barefoot. He told his son that all his mitzvos had become garments in Gan Eden, but he had never gone collecting money for the poor, so he had no shoes, an…

title.en: The Apter Rav and the Rambam's letter

people: Rabbi Avraham Yehoshua Heshel of Apta

retelling.en: The Ohev Yisroel, Rabbi Avraham Yehoshua Heshel, sat and learned until he became known as a wonder-worker, and people came to him for healing, children and other needs. Unable to learn, he went to his rebbe (the Mashgiach was unsure whether it was the Maggid or Rebbe Elimelech) to ask to close his door. Before he could speak, the rebbe showed him the Rambam's letter to Rabbi Shmuel ibn Tibbon: th…

title.en: The Beis Yosef at the Arizal's drasha

retelling.en: Rabbi Yosef Karo, the author of the Shulchan Aruch, was related by marriage to the Arizal. When he went to hear the Arizal's drasha, he fell asleep, and he was very pained by it. The Arizal told him that hearing the secrets of Torah was not his portion; his portion was in halacha and the plain meaning of Torah. The Mashgiach adds that the Beis Yosef became the teacher of halacha for all of Klal Y…

title.en: Rachel Imeinu comes to the bris

retelling.en: A woman in Eretz Yisrael, married to the brother of a maggid shiur, had no children for several years after her chasunah. She went to Kever Rachel, poured out her heart and begged for a child, and she was blessed. When she left the hospital with the baby she went straight to Kever Rachel to thank her and told Rachel the bris would be in eight days. At the bris an unknown woman of extraordinary be…

title.en: The Arugas Habosem learning fully dressed

retelling.en: The Arugas Habosem, a student of the Ksav Sofer in Pressburg who later became a chassid, was visited on a hot summer day by a former fellow student. He found him learning under a tree in his velvet hat and gartel. The visitor was annoyed and asked whether he had ever seen their Rebbe learn so dressed on a hot day. The Arugas Habosem answered that he had learned other things from the Rebbe.

title.en: The Ohev Yisroel and the pot of cholent

retelling.en: The Ohev Yisroel was known to eat a great deal. Once a large pot of cholent was prepared for Shabbos, but a heavy snow fell and the chassidim could not come. He stood by the big pot and ate until he finished all of it. The Mashgiach says there were many such hidden aspects in the conduct of tzaddikim.

title.en: R' Yitzchak Chayes without shoes

retelling.en: R' Yitzchak Chayes wrote a commentary on the Mishnah, and in its introduction his son writes that his father came to him after his passing dressed in unusually beautiful garments but without shoes. The father explained that he had done all the mitzvos and so received fine garments, but he had not gone around collecting money for poor people, and therefore he had no shoes.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya's last words

retelling.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya used to debate the minim and always defeat them. When he was about to pass away, his students asked who would now stand up to the minim. He answered with the passuk 'nis'ah v'neleichah v'eilchah l'negdecha', and the Gemara explains that as the wisdom of Israel diminishes, the minim's power diminishes too.

title.en: The Shinaver Rav sees Matan Torah

retelling.en: Rav Chatzkel of Shinava, son of the Divrei Chaim of Sanz, went to Rav Shalom of Belz for Shavuos. When the Torah reading began, everything went dark, there was thunder and lightning, and he heard Hashem say 'I am Hashem', as a rerun of Matan Torah. The next year he told his father he was going to Belz again; the Sanzer Rav told him to stay, and showed it to him at home. When the son asked why he…

title.en: Avraham fights the four kings on erev Pesach

retelling.en: On erev Pesach, while Avraham was baking matzos, Og came and told him that Lot had been captured by the kings. Avraham went to war against them and fought into the night, so that he spent the Seder at war. He threw dust at them and they were nullified.

title.en: Reb Chaim Ozer sends a sick man to Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: A man came to Reb Chaim Ozer with an illness of the lung, after the doctors told him to write a will. Reb Chaim Ozer advised him to go to Eretz Yisroel, and he went and stayed healthy. Reb Chaim Ozer explained that the Rema rules such a lung treif and the Mechaber kosher; where the Rema is followed he was judged treif, but in Eretz Yisroel, where the Beis Yosef is followed, he was judged kosher a…

title.en: The pilot who learned until kiddush levana

retelling.en: Among the ba'alei teshuvah in the Mashgiach's shul was a man who had been a top pilot in the Israeli army, an expert who taught other pilots aerial acrobatics, in whose training the government had invested over a million dollars. He became a ba'al teshuvah, left everything behind and now learns all day with mesiras nefesh. He told the Mashgiach that on Tisha B'Av night, after maariv, when everyon…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav's son and Shavuos in Belz

retelling.en: A son of the Sanzer Rav used to travel to Belz for Shavuos, and there, when the Torah was read, he experienced darkness, then light, and the heavens opening. The next year he came to take leave of his father, explaining that in Belz he sees the thunder and lightning of Matan Torah. His father told him to stay, and he would see it too; he stayed and saw the same in Sanz. When he asked why his fath…

title.en: The Yid HaKadosh of Peshischa

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great tzaddik in Peshischa who was called the Yid HaKadosh. He was called so because every day for him was as if until today he had been a gentile and today he had become a Jew.

title.en: A Rebbe sends tired chassidim to sleep

retelling.en: Chassidim came to a Rebbe for Shavuos, and in the early hours of the morning he came into the shul and saw them all gathered and tired. He told them that it is better to sleep so that they would be able to daven, and to prepare themselves to daven with attentiveness and excitement.

title.en: Feeling that a mikveh is kosher

retelling.en: When people claimed that a certain mikveh was not kosher, the son of a Rebbe asked to see it when no one was there. He put his hands into the water and declared it a kosher mikveh. The Mashgiach explains that he could feel the spirit of purity resting there.

title.en: The psychologist and the zipper

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that he once spoke with a great psychologist about this. The psychologist gave the example of a person whose doctor made an opening in his stomach with a zipper, so that each day a bit of meat and bread could be put in and he would live. Within a short time, he said, the man would have a nervous breakdown, because he gets no taste from eating.

title.en: Rebbe Nachum of Chernobyl

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rebbe Nachum of Chernobyl, the Me'or Einayim, was a stout, heavy man, yet he ate very little. The Mashgiach brings this to show that great tzaddikim have their pleasure from Torah and mitzvos, unlike a plain person.

title.en: A man who unknowingly ate forbidden food

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that someone once came to him with a question: he had been made to eat forbidden food without knowing it, and when he found out he was very distressed. The Mashgiach says he answered him at the time with the Tzemach Tzedek, who ties the Tanya's view to the Mechaber and the Rambam.

title.en: The cantonist children

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in the Mishnah Berurah's time and lands the Russian government seized thousands of Jewish children and took them away as cantonists for twenty-five years. There they had no choice and were forced to eat forbidden food, which would have brought them to a state from which they could not do teshuvah.

title.en: A tzaddik's last look at Hashem's world

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great tzaddik who came to Eretz Yisrael and who, when the German general threatened to enter the land, went with many people to the kever of the Ohr HaChaim HaKadosh on Har HaZeisim and said Hitler would not come in. The Mashgiach says the day before, Rommel had boasted he would drink coffee in Tel Aviv, and that was the turning point when Montgomery's army drove him back…

title.en: Davening while looking at the fields

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great man who came to a country place where the Jews did not know who he was. While davening he sat by the window looking out at the fields, and a Jew tapped him on the shoulder. Afterwards he explained that the other looks at the dead paper of the siddur, while he sees it before his eyes.

title.en: Rebbi's ten fingers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from the Gemara that when Rebbi was passing away, he raised his ten fingers and said to the Ribono shel Olam that he had not enjoyed this world even with his little finger. The Mashgiach stresses that this is a great chiddush, because Rebbi was very rich and had all foods even out of season, which in those days had to be brought from afar at great expense.

title.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya and the debates

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya used to debate the minim. When he was passing away, his students asked who would now conduct the debates for them, and he answered that when he is gone, they too will no longer be.

title.en: The nobleman's summer sled ride

retelling.en: A nobleman wanted to go sledding in the middle of summer, so his servants spread hundreds of sacks of sugar on the road until it was covered with sugar, and he rode his sled on the sugar. People told the Beis Aharon of the pleasure such a man could have. The Beis Aharon answered: what does he know of pleasure, compared to the pleasure he himself has when he stands on Shabbos and says Nishmas kol…

title.en: The Berditchever's Gemara Sukkah after Yom Kippur

retelling.en: On motza'ei Yom Kippur Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev cried out that he must hurry and catch up. When they brought him something to eat, he refused, and asked for a Gemara Sukkah, sat down and learned it through. Before Sukkos one should learn Maseches Sukkah, and on Yom Kippur there had been no time to learn; this was his pleasure.

title.en: The lion, the donkey and the fox

retelling.en: In the Midrash the Mashgiach tells, the lion went traveling with his entourage of animals and came to a bridge over a stream where a donkey collected the toll. The donkey demanded that the lion pay too; the lion said the toll's income goes to him, but the donkey insisted that everyone who crosses must pay. The angry lion tore the donkey apart and told the fox to prepare it as a meal for their ret…

title.en: The king who tested his son

retelling.en: From the Zohar the Mashgiach tells of a king who wanted to test whether his son was upright, and instructed a harlot to try to seduce him. The son, being a prince, did not let himself be seduced. The Zohar says the harlot is the yetzer hara, and her real joy is that the son not be enticed, for that fulfils the king's will.

title.en: The tzaddik and the kernel of chametz

retelling.en: A tzaddik resolved to have a perfectly kosher Pesach, cleaned day and night and prepared the best matzah and wine. At the Seder he rejoiced, until a kernel of wheat was found floating in his soup. He made the angel in charge of dreams tell him why and how it happened. The angel said he had done everything perfectly but forgot to daven to Hashem for a kosher Pesach; a bird had carried a kernel of…

title.en: The tzaddik and the competing store

retelling.en: A man came to a tzaddik in distress because someone had opened the same kind of business right next to his, and he watched customers go to his competitor instead of to him. The tzaddik told him that every time he saw a customer enter the other store he should thank Hashem for the other man's livelihood. If the thanks did not feel true in his heart, he should say it anyway, since the customer woul…

title.en: Avimi waits with water

retelling.en: Avimi's father asked him for water. When he returned, his father had fallen asleep, so Avimi stood bent over him the whole time, so that the moment his father opened his eyes he would have the water without delay. In that merit he was helped from Heaven to explain why the psalm of Asaf is called a song.

title.en: The same Satan

retelling.en: A great rav in Poland, as a small boy, once overslept, and his father pointed to the goyish boys already going to school and asked if he was not ashamed. The child answered that the same Satan that drives them to school keeps him in bed.

title.en: Dama ben Nesina's jewels

retelling.en: Dama ben Nesina of Ashkelon had precious stones needed for the Kohen Gadol's garments. The Sages came in haste to buy them, but the stones lay under his sleeping father's pillow and he would not wake his father, so he lost the sale. The next year a red cow was born in his herd and he received a great price for it.

title.en: Rav Chaim Vital at the grave of Benayahu ben Yehoyada

retelling.en: Rav Chaim Vital records in his Sefer HaGilgulim that he once came to his Rebbe, the Arizal, and the Arizal stood up for him. Without knowing it, Rav Chaim Vital had sat on the grave of Benayahu ben Yehoyada, one of the forgotten graves of tzaddikim the Arizal had revealed around Tzfas, and had concentrated on certain kavanos there. The Arizal told him that the soul of Benayahu ben Yehoyada was no…

title.en: The generation of the desert in their graves

retelling.en: Every year in the desert, about fifteen thousand of Bnei Yisrael died on Tisha B'Av. Each Tisha B'Av they dug graves and slept in them, and in the morning some did not get up. In the fortieth year everyone got up alive; thinking they had miscounted, they lay down again on the following nights, until on the fifteenth they saw the full moon and understood that the decree had ended.

title.en: The Lubavitcher chassid in the Stoliner shul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls an old Lubavitcher chassid, a sweet Jew learned in nistar, who used to come on Shabbos to the Stoliner shul in Williamsburg where the Mashgiach davened. He sat bent over his siddur, and on a winter Shabbos, when the Mashgiach came back for Minchah, he was still in the middle of Shacharis, having paused only to hear the Torah reading. He said each word separately, stopping be…

title.en: The Yismach Moshe asks to feel the yirah of the great

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe, a great dreamer of dreams, told the Yitav Lev that he asked in Heaven to feel the yiras shamayim of Avraham Avinu and was told it was too much for him. He asked for that of Dovid HaMelech, then the nevi'im and Tannaim down to Rabbi Akiva, and each time was refused, until he reached the Rambam and was allowed to taste it. Suddenly he began to tremble and shake so that the table…

title.en: Reb Zusha's fear

retelling.en: One who saw Reb Zusha's great yiras shamayim said that there is a vein that begins to beat when a person's soul departs, out of terror at seeing the angel with a thousand eyes. By Reb Zusha, that vein beat constantly.

title.en: Reb Shlomo of Karlin before the firing squad

retelling.en: The Ba'al HaTanya said of Reb Shlomo of Karlin that his yiras shamayim was like that of a man standing before a squad of soldiers who have already fired, who sees the fire leaving the barrel and the bullet flying toward him. This was his fear of Hashem constantly.

title.en: Reb Shmelke's dveikus

retelling.en: Reb Shmelke, brother of the Hafla'ah and like him a talmid of the Maggid, needed people to watch over him constantly. When he went into dveikus they would give him a push so that he would wake and know where he was, because his soul was in danger of leaving him through his dveikus to Hashem.

title.en: Reb Zusha and the fallen hay

retelling.en: Reb Zusha was traveling with a peasant who carried hay on his wagon, and a bundle fell off. The peasant called to him to help lift it, and Reb Zusha answered that he could not. The peasant replied that he could, he just did not want to. Reb Zusha took this to heart, saying the peasant had understood him: he could lift the hei but did not want to, since that is the avodah of Jews in exile.

title.en: Shlomo oversleeps on the day of the dedication

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that on the first morning the Beis HaMikdash was to begin its service, Shlomo, who had married Pharaoh's daughter the night before, overslept with the Temple keys under his pillow, and the first korban tamid was delayed. That same day, he says, it was decreed that the Beis HaMikdash would be destroyed.

title.en: Napoleon and the mourners

retelling.en: Napoleon once entered a synagogue on Tisha B'Av and saw Jews sitting on the ground weeping. He asked why, and was told it was over the Temple destroyed some 1,700 years earlier. He said that a people who still weep over a building destroyed so long ago will surely see it rebuilt.

title.en: Shlomo sends for a sword

retelling.en: When two women came before Shlomo disputing whose baby it was, he said 'bring me a sword'. The Mashgiach points out that in the court of the strongest king in the world, surrounded by soldiers and attendants, there was no sword in the room, and one had to be fetched.

title.en: R' Shimon of Yaroslav's two cows

retelling.en: R' Shimon of Yaroslav sat and learned all day in the beis medrash, relying on Hashem for his parnassah. A Jew who saw his holiness asked how he made a living, and he answered that he had two cows. The man asked the rebbetzin, who said they had no cows and often had nothing to eat, so he came back and asked why such an honest Jew had told a lie. R' Shimon answered that his two cows were not in a s…

title.en: R' Shalom of Kaminka and the port wine

retelling.en: After R' Shalom of Kaminka lost a child, he asked that port wine be brought to him. Port is a very expensive wine that tastes bitter to one who is not used to it, and only connoisseurs appreciate it. He drank it and remarked that port is a costly wine and it is bitter.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the glass on the table

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer once spoke with various people while his son, later the Ksav Sofer, was present, and the son went off to learn. His father told him that he should not think he had been speaking idle things. He said that even when he takes a glass on the table and puts it in another place, he does it only according to halachah, and he makes no movement without Torah and the will of Hashem.

title.en: The Lechovitcher and parshas Vayetze

retelling.en: Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch would not say Torah on parshas Vayetze. He said there is no need: the whole parsha tells how Yaakov goes to Lavan's house, raises a family, tends sheep and makes money, and that itself is the greatest Torah, since a Jew building a family and earning a living does it all for the sake of Heaven.

title.en: Tzaddikim who remembered being Yaakov's sheep

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe told his grandson, the Yitav Lev, that he remembered being a lamb with Yaakov Avinu. He showed a mark on his shoulder, a sign from when Yaakov once struck him with a stick while he was a lamb. The Apter Rav also said he remembered being a lamb with Yaakov, and remembered the tune Yaakov played on his flute to gather the sheep; chassidim know that niggun.

title.en: The Lechovitcher at the moment of his rebbe's passing

retelling.en: Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch was a talmid of Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin, of whom it was said that he had the soul of Moshiach ben Yosef and who was shot by a Russian Cossack. At the moment Rabbi Shlomo died in Karlin, the Lechovitcher, at home, began running about and crying out that he felt cut off from his rebbe, and his household did not know what to do. They already knew of the passing but had n…

title.en: The Rokeach's dream of the separated heh

retelling.en: The Magen Avraham brings the Rokeach, one of the mekubalim, who told of a tzaddik who dreamed on the first night of Sukkos that he wrote Hashem's Name and moved the last heh apart, making the Name invalid. He did not understand the dream until the morning, when he saw in shul a man holding the lulav in one hand and the esrog in the other without bringing them together. He then understood it and t…

title.en: The kohen and the sotah who was his mother

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash about a kohen who had to deal with a sotah brought to the Beis HaMikdash. When he uncovered her head, he saw to his dismay that she was his own mother, and he cried that he should be honoring her, not seeing her in such disgrace. The Midrash uses this to convey how Yirmiyahu felt when he saw Mother Tziyon in her disgrace.

title.en: A tzaddik raises an empty cup on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a Rebbe said that when Moshiach comes Tisha B'Av will be such a great festival that Kiddush will be made on it. One of the great tzaddikim once demonstrated this on Tisha B'Av: he took an empty cup, raised it, and showed what will be recited on Tisha B'Av when Moshiach comes. But for now, the Mashgiach says, it is still a day of mourning that must be transformed.

title.en: The Shpoler Zeide's thieves

retelling.en: The Shpoler Zeide, one of the great chassidic Rebbes, had among his chassidim thieves and all sorts of underworld people, and people wondered why he drew them close. Once the thieves planned to steal gold and diamond objects from a church, and they were caught. They were tortured to make them convert, and they refused; their hands were tied and set alight, and they were offered the best doctors i…

title.en: The chassid and the whipped soldier

retelling.en: A chassid of the Ba'al HaTanya had not come to his Rebbe for six years. He worked for the government near the soldiers, and once saw a soldier being whipped. He asked what the soldier had done, and was told that he had stood guard all night in the Russian frost and came in the morning with frozen ears; the service of the king should warm and boil the blood, and if his ears froze, his blood did no…

title.en: The old soldier in the frost

retelling.en: A king once went to visit his soldiers and saw a very old soldier standing guard in great frost. The king asked him whether his blood still warms him. The old soldier answered that the service warms, the serving of the king, but not the blood: his blood is already old and can no longer be warmed.

title.en: The exchanged children and the Gemara

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from old seforim, that a great gadol was faced with a Jewish child and a gentile child who had been exchanged, and no one knew which was which. The gadol said to put them both in cheder and teach them Torah until they learned Gemara. When they began Gemara, the Jewish child would sway over it and the gentile child would sit like a log, because Torah is fire.

title.en: Shlomo's wedding and the late korban tamid

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Chasam Sofer, citing the mekubalim, that the night before the day the Beis HaMikdash was to be inaugurated was Shlomo HaMelech's wedding with Pharaoh's daughter. Because of it the korban tamid was not brought on time, and on that day it was decreed that the Beis HaMikdash would be destroyed. Hundreds of years later Shlomo came down again into the world as Yirmiyahu,…

title.en: The Plancher Rebbe's Kiddush on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The Plancher Rebbe, a great tzaddik in Galicia, once on Tisha B'Av took an empty glass in his hand as if it were a becher. He said that when Moshiach comes we will make Kiddush on Tisha B'Av, and began to sing in the Yom Tov tune of Kiddush, with tears coming down from his eyes.

title.en: The tzaddik who drank the wine

retelling.en: As the Mashgiach brings it from Tosafos, a talmid chacham had a whole vat of wine, and a gentile, wishing to annoy the Jew, put his hand into the wine. The tzaddik drank from the wine right away in front of the gentile, to show him that he had accomplished nothing and that the wine was permitted. This same tzaddik later lived through a time of persecution and gave his life al kiddush Hashem.

title.en: The Ba'al haTanya and the king in prison

retelling.en: When the Ba'al haTanya was in prison, the king came to him in disguise; on his entering, the Ba'al haTanya made the blessing for a king, knowing it was the ruler. In a closed cell without windows, the king asked him what time it was, and he answered exactly. Asked how he knew, he said that Hashem created the world with the Name Havayah, whose permutations rule each hour, minute and second, and si…

title.en: The shoemaker who said tzaddikim's names

retelling.en: In Europe there was a simple Jew, a shoemaker, who knew very little and could not even say over Mishnayos while he worked. All day in his shop, with every blow of his hammer on the shoes, he said the name of a tzaddik: Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, and on. The Mashgiach explains that such simple Jews knew their neshamah would be purified by connecting to a tzaddik.

title.en: The castle that sheltered a tzaddik

retelling.en: A tzaddik was seen smiling, and when asked why, he said he had just seen something in a far-off country. A king had built a beautiful castle with twenty thousand workers over twenty years. A tzaddik passing by took shelter under it from the rain, and after he left an earthquake brought the castle down. The Mashgiach explains that the true reason for the whole building was those few minutes of she…

title.en: The Beis Halevi's chicken

retelling.en: The Beis Halevi stayed with Rav Yehoshua Leib Diskin, and when he had to travel on, the Rebbetzin prepared a piece of chicken for him to eat on the way. About two hours later she found something wrong with the chicken and that it was not kosher. Rav Yehoshua Leib said the Brisker would not eat it, and indeed it was found that he had not eaten it, saying it did not smell good.

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the pancake

retelling.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov visited a certain Rav, whose wife brought in a piping hot egg pancake, and he was honored to make the brachah. He stuck in the knife but delayed for a long while, until the Rebbetzin rushed in to say she had made it with butter in a fleishig pan. The Mashgiach said he had not known his guest had ruach hakodesh, and the Yeshuos Yaakov answered that the pancake had spurted in his…

title.en: The Vitebsker's fish and the voices of Tzfas

retelling.en: Rav Menachem Mendel of Vitebsk lived near a river, and every Friday his gabbai would announce there that the Vitebsker needed fish for Shabbos, and a big fish would swim into the net. In Eretz Yisrael he first lived in Tzfas, but the air was so clear that he heard the heavenly calls to teshuvah and could not sleep, so he moved to Teveria. There the gabbai announced at the Kinneres three times; th…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and the shaylah

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim had a practice never to eat anything on which there had been a shaylah. Once there was a shaylah in the kitchen, and the Rav of the city ruled that there was no shaylah at all, and that it could even be given to the Chiddushei HaRim. When it was served to him, he put it down and would not eat it: he sensed that it had been brought for a ruling.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe's supper

retelling.en: The Slonimer Rebbe, Rav Avraham, visited Yerushalayim and wished to draw close a poor, G-d-fearing Jew who did not wear a beard, so he announced he would eat supper at his home. Neighbors helped, and the Rebbe came with dozens of people, but when the fish was served he pushed the plate away and no one ate. The host admitted that a bearded neighbor had lent him the plates, and the neighbor, asked…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the hungry guest

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim brought a guest home from shul on Friday night and saw that he was very hungry. He made kiddush right away and they washed at once. His son asked why, since he usually said Shalom Aleichem and the other customs first. The Chofetz Chaim answered that one need not make a hungry Jew wait for Shalom Aleichem.

title.en: The Beis Aharon of Karlin and the poritz's summer sleigh ride

people: Reb Aharon of Karlin (the Beis Aharon)

retelling.en: A chassid came to Reb Aharon of Karlin, and when asked, told him that the poritz was doing well. The poritz had gone mad and wanted to ride a sleigh in the middle of summer, so his servants brought hundreds of sacks of sugar, spread it over a large field, and harnessed two horses to a sleigh. The Beis Aharon dismissed it: how could such a pleasure compare to the delight he has on Shabbos morning…

title.en: The king who sought a contented man's shirt

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard as a boy of a king who fell into melancholy, and none of the great sages and doctors could cure him. One sage prescribed that the king sleep one night in the shirt of a contented man. The king's messengers searched the whole land, but every man of wealth, power and fortune turned out, on examination, not to be content. At last they found a beggar in rags, laughing and beaming…

title.en: The wolves that spared the holy children

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from the Skulener Rebbe, who heard it from his grandmother, a descendant of Reb Eizikel. She once travelled by wagon through a forest with her children to visit their grandfather, when the horses reared up and a whole pack of wolves arrived. The leader of the pack jumped onto the wagon, went among all the people and sniffed each one, then leapt off and gave a signal, and all t…

title.en: Rav Shimon Sofer and the factory on Shabbos

retelling.en: When Rav Shimon Sofer, son of the Chasam Sofer, came to Krakow as Rav, some who had opposed him prepared questions to embarrass him at his first drasha. He stopped and told a story from his youth: in his father's city a factory owner kept his factory open on Shabbos, and the Chasam Sofer sent his son to warn him. The owner mocked him, then threatened to set his dogs on him; the third time his fat…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and naming a child

retelling.en: Someone asked the Chiddushei HaRim what name to give his newborn child. He answered that he did not want to deprive the father of the chance to receive ruach hakodesh, since a father merits ruach hakodesh when he names his child.

title.en: Chiel of Beis HaEli rebuilds Yericho

retelling.en: Yehoshua had declared that whoever rebuilt Yericho would lose his eldest son when he laid its foundation and his youngest when he set up its gates. Chiel of Beis HaEli, who had many children, wanted his name in the history books as the man who rebuilt Yericho. As he built, his children died one after another until he set up the gates. He did not see the curse being fulfilled: for each death he fo…

title.en: The Baal Shem Tov's circle

retelling.en: When the Baal Shem Tov would reveal great matters, he had those present stand in a circle and hold hands together, and he entered a state of deveikus. The Mashgiach uses this to show that the circle must be held together and not broken, like an electric current.

title.en: Talking during the dance

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that tzaddikim used to be very upset at people who talked while dancing. Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz would become very angry at someone who talked while dancing with the bochurim, since the dance is of a very high level.

title.en: Navos, Achav and Izevel

retelling.en: Navos had a vineyard next to Achav's property, and Achav coveted it and offered to buy it or exchange it for another vineyard. Navos refused, and Achav was dismayed. Izevel noticed, told him she would give him the vineyard, and hired false witnesses who testified that Navos had cursed G-d and the king, and he was killed. When Achav came into the vineyard, Eliyahu HaNavi confronted him and said th…

title.en: Navos the singer who stopped singing

retelling.en: According to the Midrash the Mashgiach brings, Navos had a wonderful voice. He used to come up to Yerushalayim, everyone gathered around while he sang, and the people enjoyed it greatly. Then he decided not to go up to Yerushalayim and stopped singing, and because he did not honor Hashem with his voice he was killed and his vineyard passed to Achav.

title.en: Izevel danced before chassan and kallah

retelling.en: When Yehu had Izevel killed, the dogs ate her, and all that remained was her skull, her hands and her feet. The Midrash the Tur brings explains that whenever she saw a chassan and kallah coming down the street she went out in front of them and rejoiced them with movements of her head, hands and feet, so those parts remained.

title.en: Yehoyachin's daily meals

retelling.en: Yehoyachin, king of Yehudah, was held captive by the king of Bavel, and when Evil Merodach took over the kingdom he freed him from prison and provided him with daily meals. The Mashgiach cites the Gemara in Sanhedrin that because David cursed Yoav with lack of bread, the curse came back on his descendant Yehoyachin, who had no food. Yehoyachin, a tzaddik, knew that his food came from Hashem and n…

title.en: The thief who would not convert

people: Adel, daughter of the Ba'al Shem Tov

retelling.en: The Toldos brings that a wise woman said that the Jews did not lose by attaching themselves to Hashem, and Hashem did not lose with the Jews, as was seen with Feivel, a sinner who died for kiddush Hashem. Chassidim say the woman was Adel, the Ba'al Shem Tov's daughter, whom they called a piece of fire. The man was a thief who stole from a church and was caught; he was told he would be burned unle…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya against Napoleon

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Napoleon stood for freedom and equality and gave the Jews freedom where he conquered, while the Russians made decrees against the Jews. The Ba'al HaTanya held that it was better to be under the Russians, since a Napoleon victory would be good for the Jews materially but bad spiritually, and he worked against Napoleon's power although other tzaddikim did not agree with him…

title.en: The chassid who drank the wine

retelling.en: Tosfos brings that a goy who wanted to cause a chassid a loss stuck his finger into his wine. The chassid drank the wine to show that it was not forbidden. Later the same Jew was forced to convert, refused, and gave his life for kiddush Hashem, and Tosfos brings this as a proof for the ruling.

title.en: Yishmael and Yitzchak argue over milah

retelling.en: Following Rashi, the Mashgiach tells that before the Akeidah Yishmael argued with Yitzchak. Yishmael said Yitzchak was circumcised at eight days, when as a baby he could not object, while he himself allowed himself to be circumcised at thirteen, so he was greater. Yitzchak answered that he was ready to give his whole self to Hashem, and the Akeidah followed to show it.

title.en: Rav Nachum of Tchernobyl and the maid

retelling.en: The talmidim of the Tchernobyler Maggid once saw him standing in a corner speaking to Hashem, and overheard him asking that the maid who helped his Rebbetzin, who was about to quit, should change her mind. They asked how one whose head and heart were always full of Torah and dveikus could spare a moment for so small a matter. He answered: to whom else should he turn? Asking Hashem for such a smal…

title.en: The poritz sledding on sugar

retelling.en: Karliner chassidim tell that a chassid who worked for the local poritz came to the Rebbe excited about his master's good fortune. On a hot August day, when sugar was very expensive, the poritz had hundreds of sacks of sugar spread over a meadow and went sledding over it on a sled drawn by four white horses. The Rebbe answered that this pleasure cannot compare to the pleasure he has on Shabbos mor…

title.en: Reb Moshe Leib of Sassov at the poritz's feast

retelling.en: Reb Moshe Leib of Sassov devoted his days and nights to redeeming captives. Once, on a fast day, he came to a poritz to secure the release of an imprisoned couple just as the poritz was holding a grand feast. When a very costly dish was carried past, its aroma brought on him a dangerous, overwhelming hunger, yet he did not want to eat the non-kosher food; he turned his thoughts inward and the hun…

title.en: The son of Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl who took 'nothing'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl had eight sons, and each took over a particular middah of his father: one Torah, one wisdom, one tefillah. The youngest said that he had taken his father's 'nothing', the way his father held himself as nothing, and that what remained for him was 'nothing with nothing'. The Mashgiach concludes that this is the way of tzaddikim.

title.en: Rebbe Reb Zusha's fear of Heaven

retelling.en: For the yahrzeit, the Mashgiach tells about the fear of Heaven of Rebbe Reb Zusha: when one merely mentioned a word of kabbalah to him, such as the word 'sefirah', he would be overcome with fear of Hashem. Someone else remarked that he himself speaks of lofty levels, of keser and Ein Sof, and is not overcome, whereas Rebbe Reb Zusha has true fear of Heaven.

title.en: The Breslover ger who roared at night

retelling.en: Among the Breslover chassidim there was a convert who became a great oved Hashem and would spend whole nights alone in the beis medrash. Old thoughts from his earlier life still stirred in him. People heard him through the window walking around and singing, and then letting out a lion's roar to cut the goy out of his head.

title.en: The Czar and the Jewish soldier

retelling.en: A Czar, thought to be Nikolai, liked to disguise himself as a simple man and sat in a tavern among soldiers, next to a Jewish soldier who made him drink and then, out of money, pawned his sword, the Czar's own, for more vodka. The next day the Czar ordered him to cut off the head of an innocent soldier beside him; the Jew, who had guessed who the stranger was and carved a wooden sword overnight,…

title.en: The Rayatz before the commissar

retelling.en: Under the Communists the Rayatz set up hidden chadarim and yeshivos, arranged davening and built mikva'os, and he was arrested. Asked who ran the yeshivos and chadarim, he refused to tell. The commissar pointed a revolver at him and said it had made many mute people talk; unmoved, he answered that such a weapon frightens people who have many gods and one world, but he has one G-d and two worlds.…

title.en: The Machnovker Rebbe on who came to him in Russia

retelling.en: The Machnovker Rebbe, of the Chernobyl dynasty, was so great that the Skverer Rebbe bowed before him when he came to Eretz Yisrael. He said that in Russia, when the Communists decreed against being a Jew, nobody came to him except the Breslover and Lubavitcher chassidim, and from then on he drew them close. The Mashgiach adds that hundreds of the Rayatz's chassidim were caught and never returned.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim foretells the future

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimshon Pincus told that he and his friend Hillel Zaks, a grandson of the Chofetz Chaim, visited Hillel's cousin, a granddaughter of the Chofetz Chaim. She told them that at about twenty she had thrown off Yiddishkeit and wanted to study at university, and told her grandfather that he sat in a corner and did not know about science, progress, the telephone, the radio and bombs that destroy…

title.en: The Rayatz senses the vessels of tzaddikim

retelling.en: After his wedding the Rayatz needed a livelihood, and a wealthy chassid, Reb Shmuel Gurary, hired him as a secretary for three hours a day so he could learn the rest. A dealer brought silver vessels and antiques said to belong to tzaddikim; the Rayatz lifted each one, called the others ordinary, and picked out a single vessel that held kedushah, the same one his father the Rebbe had picked when a…

title.en: The juggled coin that saved a life

retelling.en: Reb Peretz Chaim, later one of the great rabbanim in Russia, came as a young man to talk with the Rayatz, then the Rebbe's son. The Rayatz juggled a coin by the window, which Reb Peretz Chaim thought unbecoming, and when it fell he hesitated to pick it up because of his own honor, but bent down anyway. At that moment a bullet flew through the window from a Communist who took him for the Rebbe's s…

title.en: The tzaddik who would not kill a creature

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what he was told about a tzaddik who was very careful not to kill any living creature, even harmful ones. When his home had mice and people brought traps that kill, he had them removed and allowed only traps that catch the mice alive so they could be set free in the field. A mosquito, however, he said may be killed, as the Tanya explains.

title.en: The lions bowed to the Divrei Chaim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the well-known story that the Divrei Chaim of Sanz once went to look at the animals, perhaps with a holy intention, for the mitzvah to distinguish between pure and impure animals. When he came to the cage of the lions, they bowed their heads before him, because they saw in him the tzelem Elokim.

title.en: The wolves and the Komarna family

retelling.en: A descendant of Rabbi Yitzchak Eizik of Komarna traveled with her family by wagon through a forest to visit their grandfather. Suddenly the horses stopped and reared up, a sign that wolves were coming, and a whole pack arrived. The chief wolf jumped onto the wagon, went around the whole family sniffing them, climbed down and led all the wolves away. The Mashgiach explains: they saw that these peo…

title.en: The gadol and the leader who lost his tzelem Elokim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that a leader came to visit one of the great gedolim. At that moment the gadol looked out at the staircase, ran in to the rebbetzin and said that an ox was coming up the stairs. The Mashgiach explains that he saw that this man had lost his tzelem Elokim.

title.en: Avraham in the fire of Ur Kasdim

retelling.en: Avraham grew up in the house of his father, a maker of idols. Searching for the truth, he concluded that there is one Creator, not a god for each thing, and went around teaching it. Nimrod, who declared himself a god, warned him, and when Avraham did not stop he had him thrown into the furnace. The fire did not burn him, and only then did Hashem speak to him for the first time and reveal Himself…

title.en: Rav Eliyahu's white hand

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Rav named Eliyahu who had a white hand. He had once put his hand into fire, wanting to burn it as an atonement for something he had done as a small child. Afterward he was given a new, white hand, and he took suffering upon himself because through it he was bound to Hashem.

title.en: The chasan who slept at his wedding

retelling.en: As a mashal for one who stays up Shavuos night and then sleeps through the morning, the Mashgiach describes a chasan who prepared for his wedding, ordering whiskey, a photographer and every good thing. When it came time for the chuppah, he said he was very tired and went to sleep. The Mashgiach says this makes no sense.

title.en: The man in sackcloth

retelling.en: In Ropshitz there was a Jew who wore sackcloth as a self-affliction, and left his shirt a little open so that people would see he was wearing a sack. The Ropshitzer said of him that the Satan had caught him in the sack.

title.en: The Ropshitzer's last words

retelling.en: The Ropshitzer asked that no titles be written on his matzeivah. When he passed away he snapped his fingers and said that all his life the yetzer hara had thought he belonged to it.

title.en: The Steipler by the window

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that during the Gulf War, when the Scud missiles were falling, the Steipler had bitachon and stayed where he learned, near the window. Those who tried to hide somehow came to trouble, but he did not.

title.en: The soldier who said Shema Yisrael

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew in a world war who said Shema Yisrael whenever the bullets began to fly. He saw the bullets whiz past his fingers and make holes in his hat, yet he was unharmed. A soldier next to him asked to be taught to say Shema, and he too came out alive and untouched.

title.en: Russia collapses before the Gulf War

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that before the Gulf War the Jews worried that Iraq would attack and America could do nothing, since Russia threatened to help Iraq. Just before the war Russia suddenly fell apart, America was able to fight Iraq, and the Jews of Eretz Yisrael were saved.

title.en: Reb Shlomke and the gates of teshuvah

retelling.en: Reb Shlomke of Zvil said that now, before Moshiach, the gates of teshuvah are opening. When this was repeated, people wondered how teshuvah could come in such a world. The Mashgiach notes that afterwards a movement of teshuvah did begin, and today there are tens of thousands of baalei teshuvah, more and more.

title.en: The houses by the Kosel

retelling.en: Reb Shlomke came to Yerushalayim and for some years no one knew who he was; he sat at the Kosel among the poor. Standing at the Kosel, which was then narrow and hemmed in by Arab houses, he pointed out which houses would be torn down so that a wide place would open where Jews could daven. In the Six Day War, the Mashgiach relates, exactly those houses were demolished and a large plaza opened in f…

title.en: The Kuzmir chulent

retelling.en: One of the rabbanim spent Shabbos with Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir and tasted Gan Eden in the chulent. He asked the rebbetzin for the recipe, and his own wife made it, but it was not the same. The next time in Kuzmir he told the rebbetzin something must be missing, and she admitted that every erev Shabbos the Rebbe comes into the kitchen, takes a handful of beans, throws them into the pot and says 'l…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's face on yom tov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw the Satmar Rav many times, and on Shabbos he was not the same person. Each yom tov his face looked different, a Pesach face and a Sukkos face, so one could tell which yom tov it was. Above all on Simchas Torah his face shone, and opponents who came to look could not believe it.

title.en: The Lechovitcher rebbetzin's tears

retelling.en: Before Reb Mordechai of Lechovitch became a Rebbe he was poor, and his rebbetzin's rich sister once came for Shabbos. When the sister lit candles the rebbetzin wept, and the sister thought it was because she had silver candlesticks. The rebbetzin answered that she has no candlesticks at all, not even wooden ones: every erev Shabbos her husband carves holes in a potato for the candles, and when sh…

title.en: The ger tzedek and the Shabbos candle

retelling.en: Graf Potocki, one of the greatest nobles of Vilna and Lita, converted and became a ger tzedek. He was caught and sentenced to be burned. Before the execution he was asked why he would not return to a life of wealth and every pleasure. He answered that Jews have the mitzvah of Shabbos candles, and when a candle goes out it gives off a bad smell; yet that smell of the extinguished Shabbos candle is…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the man from Danzig

retelling.en: After davening the Ba'al Shem Tov greeted a man with shalom aleichem, as one welcomes someone back from Danzig, then a large trading city. The man said he had not been in Danzig for half a year. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that during davening his thoughts had been in Danzig. The Mashgiach concludes that a person is where his thoughts are.

title.en: The Ba'al haTanya looking at the ceiling

retelling.en: At the time of his passing, the Ba'al haTanya looked up at the ceiling and asked someone with him what was there. After the answer, the Ba'al haTanya said that he saw the truth there, not the covering that conceals it. The Mashgiach brings this to show what it means to see that the world is nothing before Hashem.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer during Napoleon's siege of Pressburg

retelling.en: When Napoleon pushed into Austria and besieged Pressburg for two or three months, cannon fire destroyed houses and killed many people. The Chasam Sofer had received signs from Heaven before the war, hearing noises from the graveyards, and wrote that he was recording only some of them. His yeshiva kept learning every day and said the long Tachanun daily. Hundreds of gentiles were killed but not on…

title.en: The one victim of the Scuds in the first Gulf War

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that in the first Iraqi war, about ten years earlier, 39 Scuds were fired at Israel and no one was killed except one man who had been cursed, since he had ridden his motorcycle into a shul on Rosh Hashanah to disturb the davening. Meanwhile a single Scud killed some thirty soldiers in an American barracks.

title.en: Chizkiyahu sleeps while Sancheirev's camp falls

retelling.en: Sancheirev, king of Ashur, had conquered the lands around and surrounded Yerushalayim on all four sides, planning to destroy it the next morning. It was Pesach night; the Jews were worried, but Chizkiyahu HaMelech, whom Yeshayahu the Navi had promised he need not fear, ate the korban Pesach and went to sleep calmly. That night Hashem sent a malach who killed Sancheirev's entire camp, and in the m…

title.en: Adam meets Kayin and learns the power of teshuvah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Adam met Kayin after Hashem had judged him for killing Hevel. Adam asked what had come of his judgment, and Kayin answered that he had done teshuvah. Although his teshuvah was not complete, his punishment was eased. Adam was astonished at how great the power of teshuvah is, and said the chapter Mizmor shir l'yom haShabbos.

title.en: The souls' protest against endless gilgulim

people: a disciple of the Ba'al Shem Tov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach repeats what one of the great disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov related about Heaven. The souls that keep coming down in gilgul came to the angel in charge of souls and complained that there is no end: they come down, sin, go up, and are sent down again to repair, sometimes coming out worse. The angel said he could do nothing and sent them higher, from angel to angel, until they reach…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the tailor's silk

retelling.en: After the destruction of the six million, someone asked the Chazon Ish why Hashem let six million Jews be killed. He answered with a parable: a tailor takes a beautiful piece of silk and cuts it up, and an onlooker cries out at the ruin of such fine silk. Wait, he is told, and you will see the beautiful garment the tailor sews from the pieces. Now one sees only the cutting, not the garment.

title.en: Reb Itzikl's anger heals a melamed

retelling.en: A melamed lost his voice, and great doctors told him he would never teach again. When Reb Itzikl of Pshevorsk came to America, the melamed went to him with a kvitel just after he had finished davening. Reb Itzikl grew angry, said he had no time, he had not yet eaten, and let the Aibershter help him; and Hashem did help him. The Mashgiach adds that tzaddikim bring a yeshuah through anger, as peopl…

title.en: Refusing Russian citizenship

retelling.en: During the war Reb Itzikl fled from Poland to Russia with many Jews, and the Soviet government offered the refugees citizenship, which most of them took. Asked whether to accept it, he said no, one must not identify with Russia. Soon after, the Russians took revenge and sent those who refused to Siberia, and people complained against him; he answered that they were exiled on 23 Sivan, the day Ham…

title.en: The lit windows at night

retelling.en: The Mashgiach lived near the Satmar Rebbe. Coming home from a late wedding at three in the morning, or out in the street at five in the morning, he would look into the Rebbe's lit windows, as he always did when passing, to see what the tzaddik was doing. He always saw him immersed in avodas Hashem. Except for Shabbos he never went to bed; he would doze on his table for a few minutes or half an ho…

title.en: Rav Reuven Grozovsky's visits

retelling.en: On the same block lived Rav Reuven Grozovsky, the renowned Rosh Yeshiva of Mesivta Torah Vodaath. He often went in to the Satmar Rebbe to discuss questions and matters of hashkafah, and on coming out he raised his hands and said that the whole Torah is open to him.

title.en: The seat given up on the plane from Morocco

retelling.en: A man from the Mashgiach's shul told of entering another shul a few months earlier and finding a large celebration. A Jewish businessman who did business in Morocco had been seated on a plane home when an Arab sheikh came and demanded his seat. The Arabs on the plane grew agitated and the crew told him he was playing with fire, a Jew on an Arab plane, and should get off before they harmed him; af…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's worry about his children

retelling.en: The Chasam Sofer once complained to his student Reb Daniel Prostitz that he had no time to look after his own children, being busy with his students, the town, the rabbanus, writing teshuvos and the yeshivah he led. Reb Daniel answered him with the passuk 'kol hayom chonen umalveh vezar'o livrachah': one who spends the whole day giving to others, Hashem puts the blessing into his own children. Th…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the worm

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once sat with his students under a tree on a very hot day, and suddenly a little breeze came up for a few moments. The Ba'al Shem Tov said that on top of the tree there was a small worm that was suffering from the heat of the sun and could not bear it. Hashem had mercy on the worm and sent a breeze that blew down several leaves, together with the leaf the worm was on, so that i…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the old soldier

retelling.en: Zealots from Yerushalayim complained to the Chazon Ish that he supported a cheder taught in Ivrit, though the Rav of Yerushalayim a century earlier had put a cherem on using Ivrit in chadarim. He answered with a parable of an old decorated soldier who, when a new war broke out against the same enemy, took his rusty rifle to the position he had held forty years earlier, and was told that the battl…

title.en: Rav Shlomke of Zvhil and the lost gold watch

retelling.en: A man came to Rav Shlomke of Zvhil in Yerushalayim complaining that he had lost a gold watch dear to him.
