Rav Shlomke asked whether he had recently acquired something that gave him much pleasure, and the man said he had bought a pair of beautiful curtains for his windows. Rav Shlomke told him that everyone has a ration of pleasure and satisfaction: having had the satisfaction of the curtains, he…

title.en: Rav Aharon of Karlin and the chassid's arrest

retelling.en: A chassid repeatedly complained to Rav Aharon of Karlin that his wife insulted and cursed him, and the Rebbe kept quiet. Once, after a particularly bad episode, the chassid ran to the Rebbe saying he could not take it anymore; the Rebbe told him to go home and she would be good. He came home to a sumptuous supper and kindness, but on his way out the police handcuffed him before everyone and held…

title.en: Rav Yisroel of Vizhnitz and the window string

retelling.en: Rav Yisroel of Vizhnitz davened on Rosh Hashanah at the eastern wall by a window with a shade and a hanging string. During Shemoneh Esrei he held the string between his fingers and turned it back and forth, and a man next to him wondered at it. After Shemoneh Esrei the Rebbe told him that he had in mind that the time should come when everything made should know Hashem made it, so that even the st…

title.en: The Baal HaTanya at his shtender

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch, who was particular about whom he took for his minyan, once needed a tenth man and sent a student to call the Baal HaTanya. The student found him at his shtender, knocking on it and singing 'veyeda kol pa'ul ki atah pe'alto', and could not speak with him. When he reported this, the Maggid said the Baal HaTanya was in the middle of a great avodah: he was praying that the tim…

title.en: The Chernobyler's youngest son took 'nothing'

retelling.en: Rav Mordechai of Chernobyl had eight sons, each distinguished in a different middah. The youngest, known for his humility, said that their father had many middos: Rav Aharon of Chernobyl took one, another son took another, and so on through all seven middos a person can have. What was left for him? Nothing, and so he took the nothing; he was nothing in his own eyes.

title.en: Rav Eizikel of Komarna saw only holy Names

retelling.en: Rav Eizikel of Komarna writes in his sefer that by the age of nine he had reached a level where, when he saw a woman, he did not see a woman before his eyes but only the holy Name that belongs to that thing. He had trained himself to see Hashem's presence in everything, until before his eyes he saw only Names.

title.en: R' Avraham Ziskind's long Shacharis

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when he lived in Williamsburg he davened in the Stoliner shul. A precious Chabad chassid named R' Avraham Ziskind davened there at great length, so that when people came for Mincha he was still in the middle of Shacharis with his siddur open. The Mashgiach brings this as an example of great Jews who could not tear themselves away from the words.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov at the door of a shul

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov came to a certain shul and stood at the door without entering. Asked why, he said he could not go in because it was full of Torah and tefilah. When they asked whether the Ba'al Shem Tov's own shul was not full of Torah and tefilah, he answered that there it flies up to heaven and the room is empty; here, without fear and love, it stays below.

title.en: R' Shimon of Yaroslav and the stone-throwers

retelling.en: R' Shimon of Yaroslav went to the mikveh every morning, passing a quarter where misnagdim lived, and they would throw stones at him. One morning he ran when they threw. His gabbai asked why the Rebbe ran now, when they throw every day and he is never hurt. He answered that there was one there who throws l'shem shamayim, and of him he was afraid.

title.en: A Rebbe in Siberia and 'gozer u'mekayem'

retelling.en: A Rebbe was exiled to Siberia for founding yeshivos and mikvaos in Russia when atheism was preached there, and suffered terribly in the cold and in the prisons. He said he could not understand how he survived so much suffering, and gave a new pshat in 'Baruch gozer u'mekayem': Hashem decreed the suffering, and Hashem also keeps him alive anyway.

title.en: R' Chaim Ozer sends a sick man to Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: A sick man with a lung illness, whom the doctors had given up on, came to R' Chaim Ozer Grodzinski for a brachah. R' Chaim Ozer advised him to move to Eretz Yisrael and settle there, and there he would live; he did, and lived. R' Chaim Ozer explained that the condition the doctor described is, as a treifus, a dispute between the Mechaber and the Rema, and in Eretz Yisrael, where the Mechaber is t…

title.en: The Avnei Nezer and a chiddush in Tosafos

retelling.en: A sick man with no hope of living came to the Avnei Nezer, the Sochatchover Rebbe. The Avnei Nezer delved into a Tosafos and said chiddushim in it, by which the matter came out kosher, and he told the man that he would have a refuah, and he was healed.

title.en: The Maggid and the Ba'al Shem Tov's meal

retelling.en: The Maggid of Mezritch said that he became the Ba'al Shem Tov's successor, despite the great companions around him, because he saw something they did not. When the Ba'al Shem Tov put a piece of food into his mouth, a fire came and carried the food up to heaven.

title.en: Rebbi, the calf and the mouse

retelling.en: A calf being led to slaughter ran to Rebbi and hid under his garment, and Rebbi told it to go, since it was created for this. The Mashgiach adds that the shochet was apparently not a fully upright Jew, for otherwise the animal would not have fled. Rebbi then suffered for thirteen years, until one day in his house the maid wanted to sweep away a little mouse and Rebbi told her to leave it, citing…

title.en: The poritz's sleigh ride over sugar

people: the Bais Aharon (Rabbi Aharon of Karlin)

retelling.en: A poritz lived near the Bais Aharon, and one of his chassidim worked for him. In the middle of summer the poritz wanted to go sleigh riding, so his servants spread thousands of sacks of sugar over a field until it was white as snow, and he rode across it, though sugar was very costly in Russia. When the chassid told this to the Bais Aharon, he asked what the poritz's pleasure is compared with the…

title.en: Rabbi Asher's Yechid Chai HaOlamim

people: the Bais Aharon (Rabbi Aharon of Karlin)

retelling.en: Rabbi Asher, the father of the Bais Aharon, davened with his minyan, and he cried out Yechid Chai HaOlamim in Baruch Sheamar so loudly that it was heard a mile away. The shepherds used it like a clock, knowing from it when to water their sheep. Later a son-in-law remarked that the words Yechid Chai HaOlamim remain the same, but such a Yechid Chai HaOlamim as his father-in-law said will not be hea…

title.en: Two friends in Rome and the king

retelling.en: In Rome the king's palace burned down, and a man suspected of setting it was taken to the gallows. His close friend ran up and said he had done it, so they untied the first and tied the second, whereupon the first claimed he was the guilty one. The officials brought the case to the king, who saw that each was ready to give his life for the other, and asked them to take him into their friendship s…

title.en: The coffin that floated

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Medrash that when a great tzaddik, an Amora of Eretz Yisrael, passed away, his coffin floated in mid-air with nobody carrying it, as if malachim were carrying it. The people who saw it recited the passuk that if a man gave all his wealth for this love he would be scorned, showing how Hashem's love for the tzaddik was revealed to all.

title.en: The pancake made in a fleishig pan

retelling.en: A gadol visited a city and was invited to lunch by its Rav, whose wife served a pancake. He began cutting it, then raised a strong kashya and went into a long pilpul, and did not eat even when the host urged him. The Rebbetzin then ran in, relieved it was untouched: she had baked it with butter in a pan that was fleishig. Asked whether he had ruach hakodesh, the guest said no: while he cut it, ho…

title.en: Yid, where is your beard? Beard, where is your Yid?

retelling.en: An elderly Yerushalmi in the Mashgiach's shul in Williamsburg told him of a beardless but sincere yerei shamayim in Yerushalayim whom a Rebbe loved, and at whose home the Rebbe came to eat with many chassidim. Fish was served, but the Rebbe did not eat and asked for one big plate; the host looked at a chassid with a beard and peyos from whom he had borrowed the dishes. The Rebbe asked the chassid…

title.en: The knife that was not toveled

retelling.en: Mr. Singer, a man in the shul where the Mashgiach davened as a boy, told him that a Rebbe's gabbai, himself a great tzaddik, came to his wealthy father for Shabbos, and the father bought a new knife and sent his young son to tovel it in the river. The river was frozen and the boy could not break the ice, so he came back and said he had toveled it. Friday night after kiddush the gabbai took the kn…

title.en: The serpent who changed his name

retelling.en: The yetzer hara, the original serpent, complained to Hashem that nobody listens to him because everyone knows who he is. He was told to change his name, and when his first new name too became known as evil, he took the name 'Yesh'. As 'Mr. Yesh' he went around the batei midrash and yeshivos, and the more Torah people learned, the more of a 'yesh' they became.

title.en: The poor young man's two cows

retelling.en: A poor young man sat learning in the beis medrash all day with nothing. A visitor who saw he was no simple person asked how he lived, and he said he had two cows. Seeing the children hungry, the visitor asked his wife, and then came back asking about the cows. He answered that his two cows were the verses 'ki vo yismach libeinu' and 'ki v'shem kodsho batachnu'.

title.en: The Ruzhiner and 'amar Rava'

retelling.en: Someone quoted a teaching of the Gemara, and the Ruzhiner said it was Rava's; the other insisted it was a different Amora. They brought a Gemara and the Ruzhiner was right. He explained that the other learned only the reasoning, so who said it did not matter to him, while for the Ruzhiner 'amar Rava' was also learned, part of the Gemara, because every word of it is holy.

title.en: The souls with a failing mark

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells what one of the great disciples of the Ba'al Shem Tov's disciples said was revealed to him from heaven. There was a great outcry in heaven by souls that kept coming down to this world, living seventy or eighty years, and each time going up with a failing mark and being sent back in another gilgul. They asked what the purpose would be, and went to the angel over the souls, wh…

title.en: The Toldos Yaakov Yosef and the guest at the bris

retelling.en: The Toldos Yaakov Yosef, a kohen with a certain strictness, came late to a bris and was upset that they had not waited for him. At the meal a guest came in, and to every question, what he wanted to eat, fish, herring, he answered only 'zol zain azoi', so be it, until the people laughed. That night it was revealed to the Toldos that the guest was Eliyahu Hanavi, come to teach him that whatever hap…

title.en: Reb Nachum of Chernobyl prays for the maid

retelling.en: The Rebbetzin of Reb Nachum of Chernobyl had an argument with the maid, who packed her things to leave. The chassidim heard Reb Nachum standing in a corner asking Hashem that the maid not leave. His students asked why a Rebbe who ascends to the high worlds prays for such a material matter, and he answered: to whom else should I pray, I have no one else.

title.en: The poritz who heard the Lechovitcher daven

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, in the name of the Slonimer Rebbe, that R' Mordechai of Lechovitch once stood davening when the local poritz and his wife passed by. They stopped to listen. The poritz turned to his wife and said that although he loves her very much, his love is nothing compared to how this Jew loves the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Young R' Shalom of Belz tells the megillah

retelling.en: When R' Shalom of Belz was young, he was once with the Lubliner and was asked to tell over the megillah. Afterwards it was said, the Mashgiach is not sure whether by R' Shalom or by the Lubliner, that the story had been heard many times but never told as beautifully as this young man told it. The Mashgiach adds that he put strength into it.

title.en: Hearing the Satmar Rav read the megillah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that he merited hearing the Satmar Rav read the megillah, which took him two hours. Everyone who heard him did not know what was happening to himself, and new explanations of the megillah were revealed through his reading. Once, at the words 'hakerovim v'harechokim', he gave a shout, and everyone understood that each year Mordechai sends his letter to the most distant Jews,…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the tailor's silk

retelling.en: After the destruction in Europe someone asked the Chazon Ish why Hashem brought such a churban. He answered with a mashal: a man who knows nothing of tailoring walks into a tailor's shop and sees him cutting a gorgeous piece of silk into pieces, and asks why he ruins it. The tailor answers that one does not show half-finished work to a fool; once it is sewn, a magnificent garment will come out.

title.en: Rebbi and the calf

retelling.en: As the Gemara tells, a calf being led to slaughter ran away and hid under Rebbi's garments. Rebbi told it to go, since for this it was created, and for thirteen years Rebbi suffered because of this. Later, when his maid wanted to sweep some creatures out of the house, he said 'His mercy is on all His creatures'.

title.en: The Arizal and the farmer's chickens

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital records that a man with no children came to the Arizal for a yeshuah. The Arizal told him the reason: he was a farmer with chickens, and the little chicks could not fly or climb up to the shelf where the chickens rest, and they suffered. He told him to make a ladder so the chicks could go up easily.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the worm in the heat

retelling.en: On a hot day the Ba'al Shem Tov sat under a tree with his talmidim when a light breeze suddenly passed. He said that on top of the tree there was a little worm suffering from the sun's heat, so Hashem made a breeze, and the leaf fell with the worm to the shade beneath the tree, and the worm was relieved.

title.en: The Malach and the two neighbors

people: the Malach (son of the Maggid of Mezritch)

retelling.en: Two neighbors came to the Malach, the son of the Maggid: one suffered greatly from a bad wife, and the other had a poor livelihood and an offer of a promising new one. The Rebbe told the second not to change his parnassah, but he did not listen, and he suddenly fell ill until the doctors gave up hope. He sent a messenger to the Malach, the neighbor with the bad wife, and the Malach explained to h…

title.en: The mezuzah affixed with kavanah

retelling.en: A young man lived after his wedding in an apartment his father-in-law gave him, and as children were born he asked the Sadigura Rebbe whether to move, and the Rebbe told him to stay. Eventually he moved to his own house and asked for a brachah for his chanukas habayis; the Rebbe sighed and told him to affix the mezuzah with great kavanah. As he affixed it, a fire broke out on the other side of th…

title.en: The Beis Aharon and the tormented husband

retelling.en: A man's wife tormented him, tearing at him and throwing dishes at his head, and he would come to the Beis Aharon to complain while the Rebbe stayed silent. Once he came and said he could no longer bear it, and the Rebbe told him to go home and it would be good. At home she greeted him with a smile and a fine supper, but when he went out to the street a policeman seized him, handcuffed him and too…

title.en: The queen who tried to make matches

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Midrash in which a queen, whom he names Cleopatra of Egypt, heard from a Tanna that the Ribono shel Olam occupies Himself with making matches and wondered why she could not do the same. She took a thousand slaves and a thousand maidservants and paired each one with the one opposite him. The next morning they were all bruised, with black eyes and bloody noses, and she saw t…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the shoemaker's daughter

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in Sanz shadchanus was given to anyone who suggested a shidduch even if it did not go through. A clever fellow who wanted some extra money came to the Sanzer Rav and suggested the shoemaker's daughter. The Sanzer Rav said it was not for him, and when the man asked for his shadchanus, the Sanzer Rav answered that the bas kol never announced such a mistake.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the wagon driver

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was once riding in a wagon with a gentile wagon driver when a priest came toward them in another wagon. The custom was that a gentile who saw his priest would cross himself, but this driver did not. The Ba'al Shem Tov jumped off the wagon and said he would not ride with a driver who does not cross himself before his priest. The Mashgiach explains that those without any belief a…

title.en: Reb Yissachar watches a sentencing

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that in earlier times tzaddikim learned fear of the King from the gentiles. Reb Yissachar used to go into the courtroom in Elul and watch a man being sentenced to death, and saw with his own eyes how the man trembled before the judgment. This gave him an awakening for Rosh Hashanah, the Day of Judgment.

title.en: The chassid who learned to daven from a soldier

retelling.en: A chassid who had not come for a long time asked the Ba'al HaTanya for something to use in his davening, and the Rebbe asked what he had used until now. He told that six years earlier, as a merchant among Russian soldiers, he saw a soldier flogged and asked why. He was told the soldier had stood guard in the forest on a frosty winter night and came back with frozen ears, which showed he had not s…

title.en: Czar Nikolai and the old soldier

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a Rebbe used to tell how Czar Nikolai, reviewing his troops, saw a very old soldier standing at attention with his rifle and asked him whether his blood was still warm. The soldier answered that the service warms it. The Rebbe would say that the service is what must warm the servants.

title.en: Reb Elchonon Wasserman and the musician

retelling.en: Reb Elchonon Wasserman, collecting money for his yeshiva, once stayed with a more modern Jew whose daughter was a musician who gave concerts. She asked him how we know there is a Ribono shel Olam, and he answered that we saw it at Yetzias Mitzrayim, at Matan Torah and at the splitting of the sea. She asked why Hashem does not show it to us, and he was silent. Some time later he asked her to play…

title.en: The Bach's sneeze

retelling.en: When the Bach passed away no sin could be found on him, so he could not enter Gehinom. Then an angel came with one: once, walking in the street deep in Torah thoughts, the Bach sneezed, and the sound startled an animal harnessed to a wagon, which moved the wagon a little. For that he had to go to Gehinom; it was cooled for forty days for him, and when he came out he took the wicked who were there…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the bird

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, in the cave, did not know whether to leave. He saw a hunter shooting at birds and heard a heavenly voice announce for each bird whether it would be hit or go free. He reasoned that if there is hashgacha on every bird, there is surely hashgacha on a person, and he left the cave.

title.en: The Tanna and the young lions

retelling.en: A Tanna or Amora, whose name the Mashgiach does not remember, met young lions in a forest that wanted to devour him. He lifted his eyes to Heaven and said the passuk of the young lions roaring for prey and asking their food from G-d, and a piece of meat fell from heaven, which the lions ate.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's thirsty disciple

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was traveling with a disciple who became dangerously thirsty. The Ba'al Shem Tov asked him whether he believed that since the six days of creation Hashem knew he would need water in this forest, and he said yes. Soon a man appeared carrying two barrels of water on a pole and gave them to drink; he explained that his poritz had gone mad and insisted on water only from a distant…

title.en: The hungry child and the coin

retelling.en: A great tzaddik, whose identity the Mashgiach is unsure of, was a poor man. His child said he was hungry and the father slapped him, thinking it was not true. Turning around, he saw a coin lying on the window, gave it to the child to buy bread and asked his forgiveness: since Heaven had sent a coin, he saw the child really was hungry.

title.en: The Strelisker's chassidim and parnassa

retelling.en: The Strelisker wanted his chassidim to be poor, holding that the lowliness of poverty is good for serving Hashem. His Rebbetzin asked why he did not bring them parnassa; he told her to watch at 'Vayevarech David' the next day. There he signaled that it was an eis ratzon and whoever wanted parnassa should come, but no disciple came, being absorbed in the praise of Hashem. After his passing, many o…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the water carrier

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov took a disciple out and they met a water carrier who drew barrels at the river and carried them up to people's homes. Asked how he was, he complained bitterly of his hard parnassa, and the Ba'al Shem Tov blessed him. The next day the same man thanked Hashem for hands, feet, shoulders, health, and bread for his wife and children. The Ba'al Shem Tov explained that on Rosh Hashana…

title.en: Moshe Rabbeinu and the heavenly treasures

retelling.en: When Moshe Rabbeinu went up to Heaven he was shown the treasures: one for those who learn Torah, one for those who do chesed, one for those who daven, and a treasure for every mitzvah. Then he saw a treasure greater than all the others. He was told that it is the treasure of free gifts, from which one who has no merits is given.

title.en: A Stoliner chassid who davened twice

retelling.en: The Mashgiach knew a fiery Stoliner chassid named Reb Nissen, who served Hashem with song and praise and would set the whole beis medrash aflame when he davened. After davening with a minyan, if another minyan began, he would say that he would daven again. He did not repeat the brachos, but he said Pesukei DeZimra again, so eager was he to praise Hashem.

title.en: Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach's letter and his own money

retelling.en: People in need, for example someone marrying off a child, would come to Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach for a letter of recommendation. Once he told such a person to come back an hour later. When the man returned, Rav Shlomo Zalman gave him the letter and also money. When one of his children asked why he had sent him away, he answered that he cannot write a letter telling others to give when he himsel…

title.en: Rav Yechezkel of Kuzmir asleep

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and Rav Yitzchak of Vorka were in Warsaw and wanted to visit Rav Yechezkel of Kuzmir, a student of the Lubliner. The Rebbetzin said he was sleeping, and they said they wanted to see how he sleeps. A fly bit him on the forehead, and in his sleep he pulled his sleeve over his fingers and rubbed the spot with the sleeve, so as not to touch his hair with his bare hand while aslee…

title.en: Rav Zusha dances from hunger

retelling.en: Rav Zusha was poor in his younger years, and once, after perhaps days without food, he was found dancing. Asked why, he said: Baruch Hashem, I have an appetite, I am hungry; if he were sick he would have no appetite. He praised Hashem for his hunger, since it showed that he was alive.

title.en: The Polish decree and Moses Montefiore

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and Rav Yitzchak of Vorka worked for the community when the Polish government decreed that a teacher must come into the chadarim to teach the language and similar subjects. To those tzaddikim this was a real decree, since young children should learn only Torah. Moses Montefiore, an important Jew from England who traveled the world and annulled many decrees, arrived just then,…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the man moving to Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: A man came to the Chofetz Chaim for a brachah before moving to Eretz Yisroel, at the time of the Tarpat pogroms, when many Jews in Chevron and Yerushalayim were killed by Arabs. The Chofetz Chaim told him that he must be in Eretz Yisroel and Hashem would take care of him, and that an Arab is a 'pere adam' whatever his occupation.

title.en: The Beis Yosef and the extra wine

retelling.en: In his sefer Maggid Meisharim, the Beis Yosef writes that an angel taught him and that he had a strong desire to die al kiddush Hashem. Once, at a meal, he drank a little extra wine and enjoyed it, and the angel told him that he had lost his chance to die al kiddush Hashem.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's talmid meets Avraham Avinu

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov sent one of his great talmidim on a mission to a far-off land by kefitzas haderech, warning him to be careful what he says. On the way a Jew asked him what was happening with their brothers in Poland, at a time of decrees and pogroms, and he answered that Hashem does not forsake them. On his return the Ba'al Shem Tov told him that the Jew was Avraham Avinu, who was arguing with…

title.en: The two worms

retelling.en: One worm lived in a strawberry and another in a radish. When they met at the surface, the strawberry worm invited the other in to taste his sweet strawberry, but the radish worm, not knowing what a strawberry is, thought the sweetest thing in the world is radish.

title.en: Reb Avraham of Ciechanow and the lottery

retelling.en: A boyhood friend who had learned together with Reb Avraham of Ciechanow asked him why he became a great rav and the friend did not, and the friend said his greatest simcha was winning ten thousand rubles in a lottery. Reb Avraham answered that every morning, when he stretches out his arm to put on tefillin, he has a greater simcha than the friend had with his ten thousand rubles.

title.en: The Kedushas Levi and the paritz's bedroom

retelling.en: The Kedushas Levi was standing on Chanukah with the shamash in his hand when a Jew who worked for a paritz came in and described how good the paritz has it: his bedroom with plush carpet, soft mattress, great pictures and furniture polished like a mirror. The Kedushas Levi asked whether the paritz lights Chanukah candles; the chassid laughed that he is a goy, and the Kedushas Levi said, so he has…

title.en: The paritz who went sledding on sugar

retelling.en: A Jew told a Rebbe that on an August afternoon the paritz wanted to go sledding, so he had his serfs spread sacks of sugar over the meadow until it was white, and rode his sled on it. The Mashgiach adds that sugar was then so costly that people held a tiny cube under the tongue while drinking tea. The Rebbe answered that this pleasure does not compare with his pleasure saying Nishmas Kol Chai on…

title.en: The lost gold watch and the new curtains

retelling.en: A Jew in Yerushalayim, in hard times, came to a tzaddik lamenting that he had lost his gold watch. The tzaddik asked whether he had recently had some special nachas, and the man said he had just bought new curtains for his home, a great nachas in Yerushalayim then. The tzaddik explained that a person's measure of nachas is set, and the extra nachas of the curtains was balanced by the loss of the…

title.en: A din Torah before Reb Yitzchak Hamburger

retelling.en: A lender died, and his heirs came to Reb Yitzchak Hamburger claiming a debt; the borrower said he had already paid. It became apparent that the deceased had come and cried out that he had indeed been repaid. Reb Yitzchak ruled that 'lo bashamayim hi' and the case had to be decided by the law, and the reckoning, the Mashgiach explains, was that in an earlier gilgul the borrower was the one who owe…

title.en: Nakdimon ben Gurion and the water

retelling.en: Nakdimon ben Gurion needed water for the olei regalim and borrowed it from a non-Jew, promising to return it by a certain day. The day was ending and there was still no water. Nakdimon went into the Beis HaMikdash and davened, and it began to rain until the cisterns filled; when the non-Jew claimed the day was already over, a miracle was made, the clouds dispersed and the sun shone.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the missing paroches

retelling.en: The Sanzer Rav said at his tish that every avodah of Jews builds the Beis Hamikdash, and when it is complete it will come down ready-made. Only one thing was still missing, the paroches. One of those at the tish said he was sure the Rebbe could complete it, and the Sanzer Rav answered that he had already done so.

title.en: The man who went to the land of diamonds

retelling.en: A poor man traveled by ship to a dark land where the sun does not shine and the streets are full of diamonds. Because it is dark there, candles are precious, and people work hard to earn them. He grew used to the place, forgot why he had come, and filled all his suitcases with tallow. Sailing back to the warm lands, his goods had rotted and were not let in, and when his wife asked for the diamond…

title.en: The Tzemach Tzedek's chassid who davened at length

retelling.en: A chassid of the Tzemach Tzedek used to daven at great length. He had been married for years without children, and his father-in-law, a misnaged, told him it was because he did not eat breakfast on time and davened all day, so he had no strength. The chassid went to tell this to the Tzemach Tzedek.

title.en: The yichud that could bring Moshiach

retelling.en: A tzaddik said that he knew a yichud that could bring Moshiach, but he would not do it, because some Jews had not yet reached their tikkun and would be pushed away. One of the rabbanim at his tish asked whether Moshiach should be held back for such Jews. The tzaddik answered that he himself might be one of the souls who would be pushed away if Moshiach came now.

title.en: The Steipler by the window

retelling.en: During the Gulf War, when Scud missiles were falling, the Steipler had bitachon and stayed where he learned, near the window. The Mashgiach says that those who tried to hide somehow came into trouble, while the Steipler was not harmed.

title.en: The soldier who said Shema

retelling.en: A Jewish soldier in the war would say Shema Yisrael whenever bullets started flying. The bullets whizzed past his fingers and made holes in his hat, but he was untouched. A soldier next to him asked to be taught to say Shema, and he too came out alive and unharmed.

title.en: Russia fell apart before the Gulf War

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls how Jews worried that Iraq would attack and America could do nothing, because Russia threatened to join Iraq if America went in. Just before the war Russia suddenly fell apart, and America was able to fight Iraq and save the Jews.

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim declines to name a child

retelling.en: A Jew once came to the Chiddushei HaRim after a baby was born and asked the Rebbe to tell him what name to give. The Rebbe answered that the father has one chance in the world to have ruach hakodesh, in naming his child, and asked why he should take that away from him.

title.en: Strawberries with cream

retelling.en: A German professor who fled Germany came to America and got a job at a college. In the college cafeteria he ordered strawberries and cream, and the order went wrong because of the difference between 'and' and 'with'. The Mashgiach uses it to show that 'and' and 'with' are quite different things, as in 'bachurim vegam besulos'.

title.en: The Lechovitcher's blessing

retelling.en: When the Lechovitcher took leave of his chassidim after Yom Tov, he would bless them that they be healthy and be called crazy. The Mashgiach explains that this is a sign of an honest Jew: the crowd says he is crazy.

title.en: The refugee carpenter in Detroit

retelling.en: A Jew who davens in the Mashgiach's shul came as a refugee from Poland with the concentration camp numbers on his arm, and went to his uncle in Detroit. Since he was a carpenter by trade, his uncle got him a job, and he went to work every day. When Shabbos came he stayed home, said Tehillim and went to shul. His uncle asked why he was not going to work, and when he answered that it was Shabbos, t…

title.en: The Or HaChaim's dream

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from the Or HaChaim on Parshas Vayechi, that the Or HaChaim had a dream in which the male and female forces of evil came to wage war with him. The male he threw down easily through all the levels and defeated. The female was much harder: he could only throw her down a few steps and could not vanquish her.

title.en: The Rebbe who wrote 'sometimes the opposite'

retelling.en: A chassid, on becoming a disciple of his Rebbe, drew up a schedule for the whole twenty-four-hour day: at this time he would learn this, and so on. He showed it to his Rebbe so the Rebbe would approve it. The Rebbe said it was a good seder, and beside every line he wrote: sometimes do the opposite.

title.en: A Rebbe at the Skverer Rebbe's wedding

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great man, a Rebbe who came to America after the war and lived in Williamsburg. When the Skverer Rebbe made a wedding, this Rebbe pushed his way to the chuppah, saying that he wanted to see the great ones. The Mashgiach connects this to the teaching that the souls of the ancestors come to a Jewish simcha.

title.en: Chizkiyahu sleeps during Sancheirev's siege

retelling.en: Sancheirev, the conqueror who had taken all the lands and exiled the ten tribes, besieged Yerushalayim. It was the night of Pesach; Chizkiyahu brought the korban Pesach, Hallel was sung, and he went to sleep without fear, though the walls were to be breached in the morning. He woke to find that Sancheirev's whole camp had died in the night.

title.en: The animals' trial over a plague

retelling.en: As a humorous reading of 'ta'isi k'seh oved', the Mashgiach tells that a plague broke out among the animals of the forest, and they set up a court to find who had sinned. One animal testified that the tiger had torn apart a man, and the judges ruled that a tiger was created to do so; another testified that the wolf had stolen a farmer's chicken, and they excused the wolf too. Then one told that a…

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the merchant who danced

retelling.en: A wealthy, clever chassid of the Ruzhiner from the Halpern family, who traded with the Russian government, fell into great trouble and came weeping to the Ruzhiner. The Ruzhiner told him of a merchant who forgot his box of money under a tree in a park and found it untouched two weeks later, and wept; afterwards his business went downhill until he wandered with beggars, and when his clothes were s…

title.en: The peddler who sold life

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Gemara's story of a peddler who went through the street calling out who wants to buy life. One of the Amoraim came over and asked what he was selling, and the peddler opened a Tehillim to the pasuk 'mi ha'ish hechafetz chaim'. The Amora said he had never known this until the peddler showed it to him. The Mashgiach asks how that could be, since the pasuk is said every Shabb…

title.en: 'Let's talk kugel' in Yerushalayim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts what a man named Reb Eliyahu, with whom he used to meet on Tuesday nights together with other young men when he lived in Williamsburg, told about a woman in Yerushalayim. Her husband had gone to America hoping to earn some money, and the children had nothing to eat. When they asked for food she told them that when father returns he will bring money and they will eat kugel a…

title.en: Rebuilding the Old City street by street

retelling.en: After the Six-Day War, the Mashgiach recounts, the Old City was primitive, with narrow alleys that twist like intestines. The man who rebuilt it, a German Jew with a sense for history, insisted on rebuilding it exactly as before, street by street with the same turns, to preserve the antiquity of Yerushalayim for tourists and professors. The Mashgiach says he himself did not know why he did it: Ha…

title.en: Yannai and Shimon ben Shetach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that a servant of King Yannai killed someone, and the case came before the Sanhedrin, headed by Shimon ben Shetach. Shimon ben Shetach told Yannai to stand up, since a litigant must stand before the court, but Yannai would not stand. From then on, the Mashgiach says, the rule was set that a king neither judges nor is judged.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov knocks once

retelling.en: In his young years, before he was revealed, the Ba'al Shem Tov needed parnassah and went to a wealthy man's house and knocked. The man was slow to open, and by the time he did the Ba'al Shem Tov was already far away. He ran after him and asked why he had knocked and why he had not waited. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that each person must do hishtadlus according to his level; he had done his by kn…

title.en: Reb Pinchas of Koretz and the coin

retelling.en: Reb Pinchas of Koretz was very hungry, having not eaten for perhaps a day or two, and was on his way to the beis medrash to learn. On the way he saw a coin on the ground and bent down for it, then caught himself: he must have bitachon in Hashem, so he threw it back and went on. A few minutes later a wealthy man came into the beis medrash, went over to Reb Pinchas and told him he had found the coi…

title.en: Rav Shraga Feivel and the living siddur

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that his rebbe, Rav Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, told how he was davening in the country and looked out the window. A man who did not know who he was came over and told him to look into the siddur instead of out the window. Rav Shraga Feivel answered that the man looks in a paper, man-made siddur, while he looks in the living siddur, seeing the whole creation sing to Hashem and…

title.en: Four of forty classmates

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he learned in the yeshiva on Wilson Street, in a class of about forty boys. Years later he received an invitation to a reunion of his class. He did not go, but he asked what took place there, and of the forty boys only four had remained Shabbos-observant.

title.en: The Williamsburg Jew who said 'Shabbos'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew in Williamsburg whom people mocked as odd; he davened loudly and with fervor. He told how he made a living: he would start work in a shop on Monday and not come on Shabbos. When he returned the next Monday and the boss asked where he had been, he answered 'Shabbos'.

title.en: Bread in the garbage can

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard in a mikveh from an old chassidishe Jew what another old Jew had told him: in America he went from shop to shop looking for a job, and every one demanded work on Shabbos. With a family to feed, he decided that in the next shop he would agree, since his family would otherwise starve. On the way he passed a garbage can with bread in it, something unheard of in Europe, and he sai…

title.en: The tzaddikim of the Spanish expulsion

retelling.en: At the time of the expulsion from Spain and the persecutions of those who stayed, there were great tzaddikim who knew they could overturn Spain. They asked in Heaven and were answered that it was a decree, because of accounts from earlier gilgulim. They accepted the decree and the suffering.

title.en: The Ten Martyrs accept the decree

retelling.en: The Roman ruler decreed the death of the ten great Tannaim. Rabbi Yishmael Kohen Gadol ascended to Heaven to ask, and was answered that the tzaddikim should accept it, for that is the decree. Though they could have destroyed Rome, they accepted it and let themselves be killed.

title.en: The Ruzhiner crosses the border

retelling.en: The Czar wanted to imprison the Ruzhiner, who fled and was chased until he crossed the border. Then he turned around and told a parable of a robber who once took in a man and fed him; later the man could have killed the robber but did not, because of the favor. The Ruzhiner had the power to act against the Czar and Russia, but Russia had once taken in Jews fleeing persecution in other lands, so h…

title.en: The Kotzker eases out a scoffer

retelling.en: Rebbe Reb Bunim's chevra was made of great minds, and a brilliant newcomer arrived. The Kotzker saw that he was not the same inside as outside: he had a streak of scoffing, lacked emunas tzaddikim and mocked the Ba'er Heitev's words on walking without washing the hands. The Kotzker drew close to him and talked with him until he decided on his own to leave. In the end he proved rotten, and the Kot…

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah and the porters

retelling.en: Rabbah bar bar Chanah hired workers to carry a barrel of wine, and they broke it and the wine spilled. The matter came before Rav, who ruled in the workers' favor and told him to go 'in the way of the good', and also that they should be paid for their day's work. When Rabbah bar bar Chanah asked whether that is the law, Rav answered yes: for a simple person it is not, but for someone of his level…

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the plate of grapes

retelling.en: A host in Boro Park told the Mashgiach that R' Aharon of Belz once stayed with him in winter, when grapes were hard to get in New York. The host went to great lengths to obtain grapes and set a large plate of them on the table, but the Belzer Rav did not eat. Asked why, he answered that the plate was not toiveled; the host then remembered that it was a crystal gift he had never toiveled, not expe…

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech and the night of the Beis HaMikdash's completion

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells from Chazal that on the night after Shlomo HaMelech finished the Beis HaMikdash, before the first offering was to be brought, he married Pharaoh's daughter, who brought him many kinds of music. He overslept with the keys of the Beis HaMikdash under his head, so the morning tamid was not offered on time, and the decree of the destruction was sealed. Then Gavriel stuck a reed…

title.en: Running after parnassah

retelling.en: A tzaddik, the Ba'al Mayim Chaim, saw a man running early in the morning and asked him why he was running. The man answered that he was running to his parnassah. The tzaddik asked him whether perhaps he was running away from it.

title.en: The Mashgiach's own experience with parnassah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he was never a big earner and in his younger years was a melamed. He remembers his first paycheck. With every child born to him his parnassah grew, he does not know how, and he marries off his children, though by his calculator it does not work.

title.en: Mercy on the floor

retelling.en: Great tzaddikim used to take exile upon themselves, wandering from town to town without saying who they were, staying with poor people. One such tzaddik came into the house of a Rav with muddy shoes, and the rebbetzin, from a wealthy family, asked why he had not wiped his shoes and dirtied her floor. He answered that he had thought Jews are merciful to people, and here they are merciful to the fl…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the man from Teveria

retelling.en: A man from Teveria came to the Chasam Sofer for a long stay collecting money. He remarked that Teveria is very hot, speaking about its climate. The Chasam Sofer did not speak with him for a whole year.

title.en: Two brothers and the mezuzah

retelling.en: There were two brothers in Yerushalayim, whose name the Mashgiach did not want to say; one was a leading figure of Agudas Yisrael and the other was among the kanaim. The first said that the difference between them was this: the law is that a town with even one mezuzah cannot be made an ir hanidachas, so if he knew the beis din would judge a town, he would sneak in at night and put up a mezuzah, w…

title.en: The fallen kugel in Belz

retelling.en: When Rav Sholom of Belz was distributing Shabbos kugel, a piece fell to the floor, and he said to pick it up and eat it. He explained that the wheat in the field had prayed to be harvested and not lost, so that it could reach a Jewish table and have a tikkun; when milled, it prayed that its flour not be blown away. It became challah for Shabbos, and the leftover challah was made into kugel. If th…

title.en: The Chazon Ish's Friday-night chiddush

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from Pe'er HaDor, the biography of the Chazon Ish, that one Friday night the Chazon Ish arrived at a new understanding of a certain halacha and repeated it to someone. He then remarked that such a chiddush can only be arrived at on Shabbos. The Mashgiach brings it to show the special light that Shabbos brings into learning.

title.en: The Sassover's daily new beginning

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rabbi Moshe Leib of Sassov, or perhaps Rebbe Reb Elimelech, would rise each morning and say that until now he had not been good, but today he would be an ehrliche Yid. Yesterday he had said the same, but today he meant it truly. So he would say every day.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe thought Moshiach had come

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe would instruct his gabbai every night that if Moshiach came he must not forget to wake him. He had a dear son, the tzaddik Rabbi Elazar Nisan, who was a rav in another town and was to come to him. While the Yismach Moshe was in the mikveh, the son arrived and the shamash called in to him that 'he has come'. The Yismach Moshe dressed quickly without drying himself and ran home, a…

title.en: R' Elya Roth foresees Russia's collapse

retelling.en: A Jew told the Mashgiach that many years earlier he was with R' Elya Roth, a great tzaddik in Yerushalayim whom the Mashgiach knew personally. At a time when Russia was so strong that America trembled before it, R' Elya Roth said it would not take long before Russia crumbled to pieces. It seemed a joke then. He also said, as a tradition from his rebbes, that Christianity could not last more than…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe: Russia will last seventy years

retelling.en: About thirty years earlier the Stoliner Rebbe, R' Yochanan, lived in Williamsburg; the Mashgiach describes him as a very great man with many wonders. Young men of the Stoliner shtibel asked him what would be with Russia, which was causing Jews such suffering. He answered that Russia would last seventy years. When Russia fell, the newspaper headlines noted that it had lasted seventy years.

title.en: The Malbim: the maskilim can do more

retelling.en: The Malbim was rav in a town with maskilim and defeated them in every debate. Once he said the maskilim can do more than he can, and his students were astonished. He explained that when he wakes up hungry he cannot eat: he must wash negel vasser, daven, wash his hands, make hamotzi and dip the bread three times. The maskilim open their eyes and call for breakfast in bed. In that sense they can do…

title.en: Rebbi and the ox that fled to him

retelling.en: The Gemara tells that an ox being led to slaughter ran and hid under Rebbi's garment, pleading to be saved. Rebbi told it to go, for it was created for this, and because he had no mercy he suffered for thirteen years. He was freed from his suffering when he had mercy on small creatures that someone wanted to sweep away.

title.en: The man who claimed to be the king's relative

retelling.en: A man was taken to prison and beaten, and he protested that he could not be beaten because he was a relative of the king. He was brought before the king, who did not know him, and admitted that he was not a relative but had shielded himself with that claim. The king ordered him released, since he had used the king's name.

title.en: The Blazhever Rav and the joke about Moshiach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Blazhever Rav, the grandfather of the last Blazhever Rav in Boro Park, a great tzaddik. Once someone made a joke and called out that Moshiach had come, and the Blazhever Rav turned pale as the wall. When asked why, he answered that he was not yet ready. The Mashgiach notes that this tzaddik constantly made yichudim and never turned his mind from Hashem, and still felt u…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's cry before a year of geulah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that in a year which seforim pointed to as a time of geulah, twenty years after the founding of the state, the Satmar Rav cried out in his Rosh Hashanah drashah that the year was mesugal for geulah, and that people must beg Ribono shel Olam and do teshuvah so as not to miss it. The year passed and nothing happened.

title.en: The Satmar Rav on Purim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw the Satmar Rav become drunk on Purim, to the point that he had to be carried out, and at that time he said lofty Torah and awesome revelations. Such a person, the Mashgiach says, may become drunk; one who becomes drunk and speaks foolishness should not.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rav never looked above the aron kodesh

retelling.en: The Shinover Rav, known for fearlessly rebuking anyone, came to the Bluzhever Rav's beis medrash. The wooden lattice of the women's balcony had several broken slats, leaving a hole too large. The Shinover asked how such a thing could be left unrepaired. The Bluzhever answered that he had never lifted his eyes above the small, low aron kodesh, so he did not know what went on in the women's section…

title.en: The Ruzhiner at Kiddush Levanah

retelling.en: The Ruzhiner once went out to Kiddush Levanah dressed like a king, in very expensive shining shoes. It was a frosty night, and he stood in one place for two hours in contemplation, while the chassidim who were with him could not bear the cold and took turns standing with him. Afterwards it was discovered that the shoes had no soles, and he had stood barefoot on the ground, suffering from the cold.

title.en: David and Shimi ben Gera

retelling.en: When David fled from his son Avshalom, Shimi ben Gera came out and cursed him with terrible curses. Yoav, David's general, wanted to kill Shimi, but David refused, saying Hashem had told him to curse. If not Shimi, another messenger would come, since it was a decree from Heaven. Later David instructed Shlomo to deal with Shimi when he became king.

title.en: Reb Mendel Vitebsker leaves the yetzer hara behind

retelling.en: Reb Mendel Vitebsker, one of the great disciples of the Maggid, set out for Eretz Yisroel. He told the yetzer hara that he had money for only one ticket, so one of them must stay, and the yetzer hara agreed to remain behind. When his ship reached the shores of Eretz Yisroel, he saw the yetzer hara already waiting for him, and asked whether it had not agreed to stay abroad. The yetzer hara answere…

title.en: The Bas Ayin and the earthquake in Tzfas

retelling.en: About a hundred and fifty years ago a great earthquake struck Tzfas and many Jews were killed. It came between Mincha and Maariv, while Jews were davening in the beis medrash of the Bas Ayin. When the floor began to shake, the Bas Ayin called his chassidim to come to him, and they crowded around him. Half of the beis medrash collapsed, but the place where he stood with his chassidim did not, and…

title.en: The diamonds of Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: A man was told as a child, by one of the holy meshulachim collecting abroad for Eretz Yisroel, that the ground there is covered with diamonds, and he took it literally. When he later came to Eretz Yisroel he found that gabbai and asked where the diamonds were. He was told that he did not see them because he had not yet merited it. He shut himself in his room, letting no one in and taking food thr…

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's note for the Kosel

retelling.en: A talmid of the Ohr HaChaim, in great poverty, came to him asking how long he would suffer without parnassah for his wife and children. The Ohr HaChaim wrote him a note, folded it, and told him to hold it tightly in his hand, go to the Kosel HaMaaravi and place it between its stones, and he would surely have a yeshuah. On the way a strong wind blew, but he held on, knowing he must not let go.

title.en: The penitent sent to the Rebbe Reb Elimelech

retelling.en: One of the great tzaddikim saw that a certain man who wished to do teshuvah needed a very great tikkun, and sent him to the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. The man wrote down his blemishes for the Rebbe to rectify. When he arrived, the Rebbe Reb Elimelech told him that he had already rectified almost everything through the journey.

title.en: Two weeks by donkey to Meron

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from old people how, before the war, Jews in Eretz Yisroel traveled to holy places, riding donkeys two weeks from Yerushalayim to Meron. They broke their bones rolling and dragging on hard benches, yet they went with great joy.

title.en: Great men who could not reach Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that great Jews wanted to go to Eretz Yisroel and Heaven did not let them. The Ba'al Shem Tov set out with mesirus nefesh and had to travel back; the same happened to the Vilna Gaon. The Chofetz Chaim had already packed his bags and the wagon was ready, and he had to unpack.

title.en: The letter from a fellow passenger

retelling.en: A Jew sat on an airplane returning from Yerushalayim. When he came home he found a letter that his gentile seatmate had written to him, saying that he was glad to have sat near him on the flight, that he was a keeper of the faith, and blessing him.

title.en: Former students thank the Mashgiach for the shiurim on emunah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that bochurim listened to his series on emunah, some more attentively and some less. Ten, twenty and thirty years later he met them, and they thanked him. When challenges to their emunah came up in life, they were equipped with the ideas of emunah and were able to face them and be victorious.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's journey that was stopped

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim had a great longing for Eretz Yisroel but stayed because Klal Yisroel needed him. Toward the end of his life, when he felt weak and that he could no longer do much for the Jews of Poland, he decided to travel there. The bags were packed and the wagon driver wanted to load them, but then the Rebbetzin fell ill. The Mashgiach says Heaven held him back.

title.en: Rav Chaim Shmuelevitz on arriving in the land

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says that in Poland, Russia and Lithuania people used to spit on the floor, and he remembers that the refugees who came to America after the war still did so. Rav Chaim Shmuelevitz writes that he had this habit, but when he arrived in Eretz Yisroel he could not spit on its ground for months, because he felt its holiness. With time the feeling went away.

title.en: The Vilna Gaon and the Chofetz Chaim held back

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Vilna Gaon set out on the way to Eretz Yisroel and wrote a letter on the road, but Heaven did not let him arrive. The Chofetz Chaim also wanted to go and was already fully packed, but a cause arose from Heaven and he could not go. The Mashgiach explains that had such Jews reached the land they would have stirred the world and brought the whole redemption.

title.en: A Rebbe who would not pass the Kosel unprepared

retelling.en: A Rebbe was traveling, and the driver offered to stop because they were passing the Kosel. The Rebbe refused, saying he does not go to the Kosel without preparation; one must prepare oneself.

title.en: The Shinever Rav and the dancing mountains

retelling.en: When the Shinever Rav came to Eretz Yisroel, Rabbi Elazar Mendel of Lelov took him to Chevron. As they reached the mountains, he said to him: Shinever Rav, see how the mountains dance, for the holy Avos walked here. The Mashgiach adds that we are not mountains, yet we do not dance; we should rejoice and dance at having merited to come to such a place.

title.en: The main post office

retelling.en: A Jew used to travel once a year to the holy places, to Yosef Hatzaddik in Shechem and to Tzfas. When he arrived in Yerushalayim, he ran to the Kosel and said that here is the main post office.

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the psychology books

retelling.en: A rabbi who was already a good rabbi wanted to improve, and asked the Chazon Ish whether he should study psychology books to become a better rabbi. The Chazon Ish answered that he could get it from Chumash and Rashi: one who learns Chumash and Rashi should know psychology.

title.en: The wolf and the sour grapes

retelling.en: A wolf came to a vineyard and saw beautiful grapes, but a high fence surrounded it. For three days and three nights he tried to climb over and could not. He turned around and said the grapes were sour anyway.

title.en: Chiel of Beis El rebuilds Yericho

retelling.en: Yehoshua cursed whoever would rebuild Yericho: his oldest son would die when he began and his youngest when he set up the gates. Chiel of Beis El, who had ten sons, rebuilt it, and his sons died one after another. The Mashgiach suggests that he wanted to be remembered in history, and for each death he found a natural cause rather than admit the curse.

title.en: The Gra turns back

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Gra set out for Eretz Yisroel and was already midway when he had to turn back. A letter he wrote to his family on the way is known, but from Heaven he was not allowed to arrive.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's packed bags

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim felt responsible to stay in Poland for his talmidim and as a leader of Polish Jewry. When he was very old and no longer felt that role, he decided to go to Eretz Yisroel and his bags were already packed, but his rebbetzin fell ill and he had to stay. The Mashgiach says that from Heaven he was not allowed to go.

title.en: R' Avraham Kalisker's letters on tefillah

retelling.en: R' Avraham Kalisker, a great talmid of the Maggid who helped found the first settlement of the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim with R' Mendel Vitebsker, wrote to his friends abroad that upon arriving he davened in Eretz Yisroel but had davened better abroad. Later he wrote that every tefillah there was sweet, yet none equaled a certain minchah they had davened under a tree. Later still he wrote that hi…

title.en: R' Sholom of Prohobisht's minchah

retelling.en: R' Sholom of Prohobisht, son of the holy Malach and father of the Ruzhiner, married a grandchild of R' Nachum of Chernobyl and stayed there for a time. On Erev Rosh Hashanah he davened the last minchah of the year and it would not go; he struggled with all his strength just to daven like a simple Jew with the meaning of the words. Afterwards R' Nachum came and told him that thousands of souls wai…

title.en: A serious moment at the Purim seudah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls the last Purim he sat with his rebbe, R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. It was a fine Purim with singing, dancing and rhymes, and at bentching R' Shraga Feivel called out that if there was no serious moment at the seudah, it was not Purim. That was his last Purim.

title.en: R' Zeira crosses the Yarden

retelling.en: The Gemara relates that R' Zeira crossed the Yarden on a rope bridge, at a time when one could otherwise cross on a proper bridge. A heretic asked why he crossed that way, and he answered that Moshe and Aharon did not merit to enter; how could he know that he would merit it? Perhaps now is a time of favor and later he would not merit it.

title.en: Shimon HaTzaddik and Alexander

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that the Greek king Alexander came to Yerushalayim to destroy it. Shimon HaTzaddik acted so that it would not be destroyed.

title.en: The Ramban's student Avner and the verse in Ha'azinu

retelling.en: A student of the Ramban named Avner left Yiddishkeit and became an army officer and then a general. On Yom Kippur he summoned the Ramban and argued against him in a matter of halacha, and when the Ramban gave him a sharp look he said he had gone off because he could not believe the Ramban's teaching that every Yid is alluded to in Ha'azinu, and challenged him to show where he was. After a short t…

title.en: The maiden who fled on an angel's wing

retelling.en: In the time of the Nefilim before the Flood there was great corruption. A maiden who was very afraid of it grabbed the wing of one of the Nefilim, the fallen angels, and flew up to the Kisei HaKavod. She asked Hashem to protect her from what was happening in the world. Hashem protected her and set her as a mazal in heaven, the mazal of the maiden, the sign of Elul.

title.en: The Imrei Emes at Kever Rachel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when the Imrei Emes came to Kever Rachel he did not daven with the long pesukim people usually say there. Instead he davened with the intentions Yaakov Avinu had when he set up Rachel's grave, that she should bring yeshuah to Klal Yisroel.

title.en: The Munkatcher Rav's fast over Montefiore's building

retelling.en: The Munkatcher Rav, whose tefilah was said earlier at the grave, held a great fast over Sir Moses Montefiore, who had put up a building over Kever Rachel. The reason was that, as is written, Rachel's grave must stay uncovered. The Mashgiach adds that this beautiful building, whose picture with an olive tree in front hung in every Jewish home, stood until some years ago, and has since been surroun…

title.en: Reb Nochum of Chernobyl and the maid

retelling.en: Mentioning that it is Reb Nochum of Chernobyl's yahrzeit that week, the Mashgiach tells that there was once a quarrel between his rebbetzin and the maid who helped in the house, and the maid said she was leaving. Reb Nochum stood up and davened to Hashem that the maid should not leave. Asked why he davened over such a simple matter, he answered: is there a different G-d for the matter of the maid?

title.en: The Satmar Rav davening with the bochurim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that the Satmar Rav used to daven with the bochurim in his minyan, slowly and in a loud voice. Nobody told them how to daven, but they felt that they were davening with the Rebbe.

title.en: The Africans who explained a watch

retelling.en: Over forty years earlier, when the Mashgiach taught ten-year-olds who had been taught evolution, he told them this story. Two illiterate but intelligent Africans, working in the principal's office of Rabbi Pinkus, saw a watch for the first time and wondered what made it go. One declared that inside were tubes with bugs, each with cheese before its nose and a string from its tail to a hand, the bi…

title.en: The Yemenite woman and the spaceship

retelling.en: When the first spaceship was sent around the world, the Mashgiach read in the New York Times an interview with a Jewish woman from Yemen about the Russians' feat. She said it could not be true, because she had heard from her father that the gates of heaven are in Yerushalayim, so a spaceship could not reach the heavens without passing through Yerushalayim. The Mashgiach says she knew the Chumash…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the torn bekeshe

retelling.en: A man wanted a new bekeshe cheaply and bought silk that had lain in a damp basement and rotted through, though it looked new. He came to Sanz for Yom Tov, and when people touched the fine new bekeshe it tore; jokers in the crowd kept touching it, tearing more holes, and he began to shout. The Sanzer Rav asked what the commotion was, and the man explained that his new bekeshe was rotten and tore a…

title.en: The bachur who belittled Rabbeinu Tam

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that he once heard someone learning Gemara who came to a Rabbeinu Tam he did not understand and spoke about him dismissively. The Mashgiach asks whether this is how one speaks about Rabbeinu Tam and whether this is respect for the Torah.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's table and Hashem's sky

retelling.en: A chassid of Kotzk traveled to a town where he saw the Ba'al Shem Tov's old table. When he returned, the Kotzker asked what he had seen, and he told him about the table. The Kotzker brought him to the window and told him to look at the sky, which is Hashem's sky and has been for thousands of years.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the glass on the table

retelling.en: While the Chasam Sofer was learning, a householder came about an important matter and he spoke with him. One of his sons moved away so as not to hear. The Chasam Sofer asked why he had not listened, and the son answered that it was only mundane talk. The Chasam Sofer replied that he had never spoken idle words, and that even when he picks up a glass from the table and puts it down, it is with a h…

title.en: Talmidim in Radin who did not go to the Chofetz Chaim

retelling.en: A rebbe of the Mashgiach's in yeshiva told that as a young talmid in Radin he and his brilliant friends did not go to hear the Chofetz Chaim's talks, thinking they were meant for simple tailors and shoemakers. Only later, when he went out into the world, did he understand who the Chofetz Chaim was; while learning there he had thought of him as just a pious elderly Jew.

title.en: The Imrei Emes learning with dveikus

retelling.en: A rebbe who attended the Knessia Gedolah of Agudas Yisrael saw the Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, sit in front of his house learning Gemara for hours with great dveikus. He was deeply moved, and said that he had seen many great tzaddikim with dveikus in tefillah, but dveikus in learning he had seen only in the Gerrer Rebbe.

title.en: The bochur and the baseball game

retelling.en: Someone complained to a bochur about why he davened so loudly. The bochur answered that the night before he had been at a baseball game, where the whole stadium screamed and got excited when a player hit the ball; if people get excited over that, he asked, why should one not get excited when speaking to the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Roped mountain climbers

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he once passed through the country and saw people climbing a straight wall as a sport. Since one could slip and fall, they were all tied to one another. When one slipped he did not fall, because he was bound to the others and caught hold again.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's long Shemoneh Esrei

retelling.en: In his youth the Chasam Sofer learned with friends and davened a long Shemoneh Esrei. A friend told him that in the time he davened, another bachur davened Shemoneh Esrei and also learned through a siman of Shulchan Aruch with the Magen Avraham. The Chasam Sofer answered that the Gemara says one who lengthens his tefillah has his days lengthened, so he would live long and have time to make it up.

title.en: Miriam bas Bilgah and the closed window

retelling.en: In the time of the Greeks, a daughter of the kohanic family of Bilgah married a Greek officer. When the Greeks entered the Beis HaMikdash she went with them, kicked the mizbe'ach and called out against it that it consumes the money of Yisrael and does not help them in their trouble. The Chachamim said she would not have acted so had her parents been in order, and as a penalty, when the Chashmona'…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and the late soul

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim used to bring tikkun to souls, and thousands of souls came to him. Once, sitting on erev Shabbos, he was heard telling a soul that it was too late, the Rebbetzin had already lit candles. It was the last Shabbos of his life, and he passed away that Shabbos toward evening, around the time of shalosh seudos, so the soul lost its chance for a tikkun, since it needed a tzaddik of…

title.en: The Maggid's dream and the garden

retelling.en: On Tisha B'Av the Maggid dozed and dreamt that he was hungry, took an apple and made a blessing, and only then remembered the fast. He awoke shaken and, with great teshuvah and tears, said the first book of Tehillim. Exhausted, he dozed and saw a garden full of fruit trees whose fruit fell as he said Tehillim; he understood it was planted for the sitra achra by his blessing in vain. With each fur…

title.en: The delayed messenger and the chief official

retelling.en: A good old poretz who treated the Jews well died, and his successor, a wicked antisemite, made harsh decrees. The townspeople asked the Maggid to daven, and he told them to send someone to Petersburg, to the official over all poritzim who can replace one. Their messenger, a talmid chacham and fine speaker, stopped at the Maggid for a brachah, but the Maggid told him twice not to go yet; on the th…

title.en: The Shinava Rav and the dybbuk at shalosh seudos

retelling.en: Rabbi Elazar Brizel's father was in Shinava for a Shabbos when a woman came with a daughter possessed by a dybbuk that spoke from her and made her suffer. She was told to bring her to the Shinava Rav's shalosh seudos, a time of great favor; Rabbi Brizel's father arrived late, found no seat in the dark, and sat on a window sill by the women's section. When the Shinava Rav began the zemiros, the dy…

title.en: Rabbi Moshe of Lelov tries to reach the Kosel

retelling.en: Rabbi Moshe of Lelov, son of Rabbi Dovid of Lelov, travelled to Eretz Yisrael to bring the geulah, believing that if he reached the Kosel he would bring it. He came to Tzfas but did not stay, and set out for Yerushalayim with great difficulty; on the way the kiddush cup from Lublin fell and broke, but he went on. In Yerushalayim he fell gravely ill and asked to be carried in his bed to the Kosel,…

title.en: The chassid, the robber and the Rebbe's glass

retelling.en: A chassid of Rabbi Moshe of Lelov needed a yeshuah in parnasah and wanted to travel to another country; the Rebbe gave him a glass as a segulah for parnasah and protection, and he wondered what a glass could help. In a forest a robber stopped him and he had to hand over the money he had borrowed for his business. He asked to take a drink of brandy to calm himself, and in the struggle that followe…

title.en: The letter to the editor after the Six-Day War

retelling.en: During the Six-Day War the newspapers were full of miracles, such as a firebomb that set a house ablaze and a second bomb that hit a water tank on the roof, whose water put out the fire. A woman in Tel Aviv wrote to a newspaper asking the editor to stop writing about the miracles. She explained that on Shabbos, her one day off, she drives to the beach, and the reports gave her a guilty conscience…

title.en: The falling ceiling and the boards with blood

retelling.en: Before the war, Jewish boys in Europe who had left home over Haskalah, communism and Zionism made clubs and dormitories. One boy, disappointed, cut his wrists and bled to death, and afterwards the plaster in the clubhouse below kept falling despite repeated replastering. A boy with a spark of emunah asked the Telzer Rosh Yeshiva, Rav Bloch, who said he was a man of halachah, not Kabbalah: the boa…

title.en: Saddam Hussein and the Jewish calendar

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says Saddam Hussein claims to be Nebuchadnezzar. He relates that someone told him of a magazine interview in America in which Saddam boasted of this. The Mashgiach notes that he entered Kuwait on Tisha b'Av, choosing that day, and compares it to Haman, who reckoned with the Jewish calendar.

title.en: The falling ceiling in the Telz club

retelling.en: R' Yosef Bloch writes in his sefer of something that happened with him in Telz, where boys who had left the yeshiva and thrown off Torah gathered in a club to eat, drink, smoke and mock the Torah. One of them, in distress, cut his wrists and bled to death in the room upstairs, and afterward pieces of the club's ceiling kept falling no matter how often a plasterer repaired it. When they came to th…

title.en: The tzaddikim on Har HaZeisim and Rommel

retelling.en: When Hitler's armies reached Alexandria in Egypt, near Eretz Yisroel, the Jews there trembled. Tzaddikim, among them R' Shlomke of Zvhil and R' Aharon Roth, went to Har HaZeisim, and on returning each told his people that Hitler would not be able to enter; one said he had seen Hashem's Name in fiery letters at the kever of the Ohr HaChaim, where they had gone to daven with a sefer Torah. General…

title.en: The Ramban shows Avner his name in Ha'azinu

retelling.en: Avner, a student of the Ramban, went off the derech, rose to become governor of the city, and on Yom Kippur summoned the Ramban, slaughtered, roasted and ate an animal, and asked him how many counts of liability he had incurred, arguing five against the Ramban's four. Frightened by the Ramban's sharp look, he explained that he became a heretic because the Ramban had taught that every Jew is found…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the brain surgery

retelling.en: A man from Eretz Yisrael who needed brain surgery was told by the Chazon Ish to go to America at once, to a certain doctor who alone could perform it. The man wanted to wait a week, but the Chazon Ish insisted; the doctor operated, and the next day the doctor died. The Mashgiach adds that neurosurgeons consulted the Chazon Ish, that he wrote out exact instructions for a surgeon on how to operate…

title.en: The worker who judged his employer favorably

retelling.en: A Jew worked for an employer for three years and, before going home for Yom Tov, asked for his wages. The employer said he had no money, no produce, no sheep and no land. The worker judged him favorably, and later it turned out that it was so: the employer had in fact had nothing available at the time.

title.en: Nasan's parable of the sheep

retelling.en: After Dovid took Bas Sheva from Uriah, Nasan the prophet came and told him of a man who had a sheep that was very dear to him, which another man took away. Dovid ruled that the taker was liable and must pay. Nasan told him that he himself was the one who had taken it; Dovid did not know that in judging the other he was judging himself.

title.en: The written-down stories of Reb Motel Slonimer

retelling.en: Reb Motel Slonimer, the Slonimer Rebbe in Yerushalayim, accepted stories only from people he knew to be trustworthy. One of his distinguished chassidim wrote down each day the stories he heard from him, so that no mistake would creep in. The Mashgiach received a typewritten copy some twenty or thirty years earlier, though Slonimer chassidim were unhappy that copies were made, and in recent years…

title.en: The Apter Rav on the war before Moshiach

retelling.en: Reb Motel Slonimer related that he heard from a chassid, who heard from Reb Yitzchak Meir of Zinkov, the son of the Apter Rav, that the Apter Rav said: before Moshiach comes, the nations will be dragged into a war they will not want to enter because they will see it is good for the Jews. They will meet and make agreements to avoid it, but they will be grabbed by the forelocks and pulled in, and a…

title.en: A rebbe's parting blessing

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a rebbe who, when taking leave of his chassidim after a Yom Tov, would bless them that they be considered mad. The reason was the Gemara that when Moshiach comes, the G-d-fearing will be considered mad.

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe: 'beard, where is your Jew?'

retelling.en: The Slonimer Rebbe sensed that something brought to him was not in order, and a learned man explained with lomdus that there was no need to be concerned. The Slonimer Rebbe turned to him and said that when a certain Jew comes to the next world they will ask him, 'Jew, where is your beard?', but when this man comes they will ask, 'Beard, where is your Jew?' The Mashgiach brings it as one of many s…

title.en: The Maggid trembles at the Ba'al Shem Tov's garment

retelling.en: The Ruzhiner told that his great-grandfather, the Maggid, was no small man, yet once on Shemini Atzeres, when the Ba'al Shem Tov davened tefilas geshem and sweated, the Maggid wanted to set his garment in order. As soon as he touched it he began to tremble so strongly that he could not control himself; he held on to a table, and the table shook with him.

title.en: Where the Ba'al Shem Tov answered worldly questions

retelling.en: People would come to the Ba'al Shem Tov with worldly questions, for example about a woman whose husband had gone away. He would answer only after coming out of the washroom, explaining that his mind was always in heaven and could not deal with worldly matters; only there, where one may not think words of Torah, could he look at the world and know how to answer.

title.en: Bachurim at a yeshiva lunch table

retelling.en: The Mashgiach was told that in a certain yeshiva bachurim sat at lunch and said that it does not pay to be an ehrlicher Yid, since all the troubles come from it: the ehrliche have no money and are not healthy. He says this is what one hears today even on the benches of the yeshiva, just as Malachi foretold.

title.en: Rabbeinu Yonah and the burning of the Gemaras

retelling.en: Because of the dispute over philosophy, Rabbeinu Yonah was instrumental in burning the Rambam's sefer in the streets of Paris. Some time later the authorities in Paris confiscated the Gemaras of France and burned thirty wagonloads of them, at a time when every Gemara was handwritten and precious. Rabbeinu Yonah concluded that this was the punishment for burning the Rambam's sefer, did teshuvah, a…

title.en: Simple Jews and philosophers at the expulsion from Spain

retelling.en: When King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella expelled the Jews from Spain, only those who converted could stay. Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz describes in his Or HaChaim that the ones who gave their lives were simple, unlearned Jews and women. The expulsion fell on Tisha B'Av, and the Rabbanim instituted that they march out with music to strengthen themselves; many were killed, sold as slaves or drowned at sea.…

title.en: The boy who laughed at the Livyasan

retelling.en: A teacher who had come to America taught children and wanted to plant emunah in them. He told them about Gan Eden, Gehinnom and the days of Moshiach, when the Shor Habar and the Livyasan will be eaten, the Livyasan being a fish so great that it encircles the whole world. One boy raised his hand and said he did not believe it, and the whole class burst out laughing. The Mashgiach uses this to show…

title.en: The animals' court and the sheep

retelling.en: A plague broke out among the animals of a forest, and they set up a court to find who had sinned and caused it. One animal testified that the bear had seized an ox and eaten it, and the court ruled that a bear may eat. Another testified that the wolf had entered a chicken coop and eaten a chicken, and this too was excused as its nature. Then one testified that a sheep had stuffed a hole in its sh…

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the untoveled plate

retelling.en: A grandfather of a man who davens in the Mashgiach's beis medrash helped the Belzer Rav during his escape in Europe, and the Belzer Rav stayed with him. At the Belzer Rav's tish a large crystal plate of grapes was served, a rare thing in Europe then, out of season. The Belzer Rav sensed that the plate had not been toveled. The host then recalled that he had received the large crystal plate as a g…
