title.en: The Thursday chaburah in Williamsburg

retelling.en: In Williamsburg several young men, the Mashgiach among them, used to gather on Thursdays for a chaburah to strengthen one another in Yiddishkeit. One of them, the father of a man who davens with the Mashgiach and a dear Slonimer chassid, would tell stories of tzaddikim. It was so enlivening that they left the chaburah as if washed clean and refreshed, wanting to learn and to daven; it lit a fire…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov crosses the river on his belt

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov had to cross a great river, and he spread out his belt on the water. He stood on the belt and crossed the river on it. He said that he had not done it with holy names or anything else, only with emunah.

title.en: The icicle that burned like a candle

retelling.en: As written in Shivchei HaBesht, the Ba'al Shem Tov once went to the mikveh at night, and the candle went out. His gabbai said they could not go in the dark. It was a frosty night with long icicles hanging from the roofs, and the Ba'al Shem Tov told him to take an icicle and light it. He who commanded the candle to burn could make the icicle burn, and it was done with emunah alone.

title.en: The Maggid saw a soul's root down to the earth

retelling.en: One of the great Gedolim asked the Ba'al HaTanya what made the Maggid so great. He answered that the Maggid could look at a kvitl and see the root of the soul, and the questioner was not impressed. Then he told him that the Maggid could see the root all the way down to the earth from which Adam was created, the very grain of earth from which that Jew came.

title.en: Rabbi Eliyahu Roth's two predictions

retelling.en: A Jew told the Mashgiach that about ten years earlier he had visited Rabbi Eliyahu Roth, a great tzaddik in Yerushalayim, who told him two things. First, that the bear is rotten and will collapse, meaning Russia, at a time when nobody knew it would. Second, that he had a tradition from kabbalah that the gentiles' count of years would not reach two thousand. The Mashgiach adds that nobody can trul…

title.en: The Slonimer Rebbe and the untoveled dishes

retelling.en: When the Slonimer Rebbe visited Yerushalayim, his chassidim ate supper with him each night at a different chassid's home. A poor chassid without a beard, whom the Mashgiach calls Yankel, was told the Rebbe would eat at his home; friends brought the food and a bearded scholarly neighbor lent dishes. The Rebbe talked and did not eat, and on learning the dishes came from the neighbor, asked whether…

title.en: The gabbai and the new knife

retelling.en: Mr. Singer told the Mashgiach that a Rebbe's gabbai, who collected money in small towns each year, stayed with his father for Shabbos. His mother wanted a presentable knife, so his father bought a new one and sent the boy, about ten or eleven, to tovel it in the river; the river was frozen and the boy, too lazy to break the ice, came home and said he had done it. On Friday night the gabbai would…

title.en: Rabbi Binyamin Diskin and the chicken for the road

retelling.en: The Rav of Brisk visited Rabbi Binyamin Diskin, father of Rabbi Yehoshua Leib Diskin, and was given a piece of chicken to take on his journey. After he left on the train, the rebbetzin rushed in: a question had arisen about the chicken. Rabbi Binyamin told her not to worry, he would not eat it. When the guest returned a few days later he said he had had a bellyache and could not eat it, then smel…

title.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov and the pancake

retelling.en: The Yeshuos Yaakov, the Lemberger Rav, stopped at the home of a certain Rav while traveling, and the rebbetzin served him a hot pancake of eggs fried in butter. He cut it but kept discussing a difficult Rambam instead of eating, though the host urged him to make a brachah before it got cold. The rebbetzin then realized she had made it in a meat pan; when the host asked whether this was a wonder,…

title.en: The Apta Rav and the Kotzker Rebbe on the ushpizin

retelling.en: There was a machlokes between the Kotzker Rebbe and the Apta Rav. The Apta Rav sent a messenger asking how the Kotzker could disagree with him, when every Sukkos he sees the seven ushpizin enter his sukkah. The Kotzker Rebbe answered that every Sukkos he believes the seven ushpizin come into his sukkah, and believing is a higher level than seeing.

title.en: The pearl from the depths of the sea

retelling.en: A king who ruled over the whole world wanted a crown showing his rule over every land, and asked that each land bring a precious stone. A servant who loved the king wanted to show that his kingship reaches even the dark depths of the sea, so he lowered himself at great risk into depths where the sun's light has no hold, and brought back a pearl. The king ordered it set at the head of the crown. W…

title.en: The Satmar Rav and his chair

retelling.en: A great rav once asked the Satmar Rav whether he could teach him how not to sleep, since the Satmar Rav did not lie down in a bed the whole week, only dozing for a few minutes at a time, and was still fresh and alert. The Satmar Rav answered that it was too late: his mother had already trained him not to sleep when he was six. Once a small boy sat on the Satmar Rav's fine chair in the beis medras…

title.en: One o'clock in the Gur yeshiva

retelling.en: The Lev Simcha of Gur made a takanah that every bachur must go to sleep at one o'clock; he may sleep as long as he wants, but must be in bed at one, and he said it was a segulah. If he knew a bachur was not going to sleep at one, he would not speak with him. The Mashgiach recalls that on a visit to Yerushalayim he needed to speak with the mashgiach of the Gur yeshiva, and when he asked for him he…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the moth-eaten bekeshe

retelling.en: A man in Sanz bought a new silk bekeshe cheaply from old stock that had lain in storage so long the moths had eaten through it, and it tore at any touch. He kept shouting at people not to touch it, which only led jokers to touch it more. When he complained to the Sanzer Rav, the Sanzer Rav said he indeed has an excuse, but that with such excuses one comes to the next world: whoever wants an excus…

title.en: Rav Aharon Kotler on the seventh hour

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a bochur during the war, when a large gathering of yeshiva bochurim was called, he heard Rav Aharon Kotler speak about learning seven hours in a row. Rav Aharon said the seventh hour cannot be compared to the other six; it is far higher.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the torn paroches

retelling.en: The Sanzer Rav said at his tish that the Beis HaMikdash, built from what Jews do, was already almost finished except for the paroches. One of the rabbanim present said that the Rebbe is the tzaddik of the generation and could sew the paroches together, so why does he not? The Sanzer Rav answered that he had already sewn it, but this or that rasha came and tore it.

title.en: The bachur who davened long

retelling.en: A young bachur in the beis medrash used to daven very long. A friend told him that in the time he davened, the friend had also davened and learned a siman of Shulchan Aruch. The bachur answered that the Gemara says one who prolongs his tefillah has his days lengthened, so he has enough time for what matters.

title.en: A Galitzianer chassid in Kotzk

retelling.en: A Galitzianer chassid came to Kotzk on Yom Kippur night and saw two chassidim learning, until one told the other that they must go daven maariv. He was surprised that they called Kol Nidrei just maariv. Half a year later he came again on Pesach night, saw them learning, and heard one say they must go eat. When he asked, they told him that in Kotzk they learned that every tefillah is a new creatio…

title.en: The Ramban and his student Avner

retelling.en: The Ramban had a student named Avner who went off the derech and became a general in the king's army. One Yom Kippur he summoned the Ramban, ate a pig in front of him, and argued with him. Avner said he had left because of the Ramban's teaching that Haazinu contains every Jew's history, and asked where he was in it. After praying by the wall, the Ramban showed him the passuk 'amarti af'eihem ashb…

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the brain surgeons

retelling.en: In the Mashgiach's own adult years the Chazon Ish was known in America to know everything. When doctors were unsure how to perform a brain operation, they sent the patient to the Chazon Ish, who drew a diagram showing how to do it. The professors followed it and succeeded. Asked how he knew medicine, he answered that it is in the Torah: from Hilchos Treifos and the Gemara one knows the anatomy of…

title.en: The stranger at Reb Aharon of Karlin's minyan

retelling.en: A stranger came to Reb Aharon of Karlin's minyan when they began Baruch She'amar. He waited for the chazzan to finish the brachah, but the chazzan did not. Thinking the chazzan was not heard, he davened on alone up to Shemoneh Esrei and was still waiting, until it suddenly grew quiet and the chazzan concluded the brachah, so long had Baruch She'amar taken.

title.en: The Karliner shtiebel on Orchard Street

retelling.en: An older Jew the Mashgiach davened with used to tell about a Karliner shtiebel on Orchard Street on the East Side, fifty to seventy years earlier, where immigrants gathered to daven and the Rebbe would send them letters of chizuk. There they davened weekday Shacharis for about two hours, and after davening Ephraim Tenenbaum asked why they had rushed so today, since two hours was not enough when e…

title.en: Davening or learning: which is more important?

retelling.en: Someone once asked a tzaddik what is more important, davening or learning. The tzaddik answered that if one asks a small child whom he loves more, his father or his mother, the child says he loves each one more. Both are needed: they are the heart and the mind.

title.en: The scoffer in Peshischa

retelling.en: At the court of Rebbe Reb Bunim in Peshischa there was a young man, a great scholar, who mocked the avodah of the chassidim. The Kotzker took him aside and told him that Rebbe Reb Bunim was not as great a tzaddik as he seemed. The young man took it seriously and left Peshischa, and the Kotzker used to say that he had saved the group, because that young man was killing their yiras shamayim.

title.en: The previous Skverer Rebbe and the sweetness of Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls an audience with the previous Skverer Rebbe in which the Rebbe spoke of how sweet Shabbos is. He was so absorbed in Shabbos that he could not grasp that there is a Jew who does not feel its sweetness.

title.en: The chassid, the frozen soldier and the Ba'al HaTanya

retelling.en: A chassid came to the Ba'al HaTanya after six years away and explained that he was a businessman supplying the government's army. He once saw a soldier stretched out and whipped, and was told the soldier's ears had frozen while he stood guard on a frosty winter night; one who serves the Czar must have boiling blood. The chassid took from this a path that in davening the blood must boil, and it se…

title.en: The Czar and the old soldier

retelling.en: The Czar was reviewing his soldiers and saw a very old soldier of about eighty standing with his rifle. He asked whether his blood was still warm enough for army service. The soldier answered that the service warms him: his own blood is cold, but serving the king keeps him warm.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rebbe's kneidlach on the last day of Pesach

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that by the Bluzhever Rebbe it was the custom on the last day of Pesach for everyone in town to bring meat kneidlach, which were mixed together in a large pot. The Rebbe ate from it and gave out shirayim, even from people whose food he would surely not eat all year. The Mashgiach explains that on that day there is a special protection, so people mix and are joined with one a…

title.en: R' Asher of Stolin and the hundred and twenty tzaddikim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that R' Asher of Stolin traveled to a great many tzaddikim, about a hundred and twenty. He said that he went to tzaddikim who could have been his Rebbe, to tzaddikim who could have been his friends, and to tzaddikim who could have been his talmidim, to learn something from each. The Mashgiach adds that hiskashrus to one's own Rebbe is good, but mocking another is not.

title.en: The farmer and the buried statue of the king

retelling.en: As a parable heard in his youth, the Mashgiach tells of a farmer who dug up the figure of a man holding a stick on land inherited from his grandfather, and used it as a scarecrow; he also used a heavy bowl for the pigs' slop and a heavy rod for spreading manure. A descendant of a king recognized the statue as his ancestor's, hidden in a war, made of gold with diamond eyes and a ruby in the sword…

title.en: The kvitel against the troublemaker

retelling.en: Jews came to the Rebbe of Lublin and told him that in their town there was a man who caused Jews great troubles. They gave him a kvitel with the man's name, asking that he no longer be able to harm Jews. The Rebbe looked at the kvitel and said that the Jew whose name was written there shines in all worlds, which astonished them. The Mashgiach connects what the Rebbe saw in this man, his hidden li…

title.en: Rebbi, Divrei Hayamim and the Megillah

retelling.en: When Rebbi learned Divrei Hayamim and Nebuchadnezzar was mentioned, he said nothing, but when he learned the Megillah with his students he cursed him. The students asked why he cursed him in the Megillah, where he is mentioned once, but not in Divrei Hayamim, where he is mentioned many times. Rebbi answered that when one learns Divrei Hayamim one is in the time when Nebuchadnezzar was alive and k…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's lament

retelling.en: In his hesped on his rebbe, Rabbi Nosson Adler, which he wrote down and which appears in Derashos Chasam Sofer, the Chasam Sofer lamented that he had not been present at his rebbe's passing. Had he merited it, he writes, he would have received a double portion, twice as great as his own.

title.en: The chassid and the misnaged: the world founded on teshuvah

retelling.en: A man who had been a misnaged met a chassid and asked him to say something from his Rebbe. The chassid said his Rebbe taught that 'He founded it upon the seas' means the world was established on teshuvah, the 'sea' meaning teshuvah.

title.en: Rebbe Elimelech's letter to the forest

retelling.en: In the days of Rebbe Elimelech a woman's husband suddenly disappeared, and she was advised to go to Rebbe Elimelech, who gave her a letter and told her to go to a house in the forest and hand it over. Her husband had been seized by the forces of impurity; when they read the letter there was an uproar, and their head said one cannot quarrel with Rebbe Elimelech, so they let him go. He came home ov…

title.en: The Arizal stands for Rabbi Chaim Vital

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital wrote that he once came in to his teacher the Arizal, and the Arizal stood up for him. He asked why, and the Arizal asked whether he had done anything special that day; he had been involved in redeeming captives. The Arizal told him that this was the mitzvah of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, who came in with him, and he had stood up for Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, not for him.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the wagon driver

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was once riding in a wagon driven by a non-Jewish wagon driver. The custom was that when a priest passed, a gentile would make the sign of the cross to pay him homage. When the priest came and the driver did not do so, the Ba'al Shem Tov jumped off the wagon, saying he did not want to ride with someone who has no emunah. The Mashgiach explains that the gentile's faith is false,…

title.en: The tzaddik who saw letters in the ceiling

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a tzaddik said before his passing that when he looks at a ceiling he does not see the ceiling. He sees only the letters, the holy names and the inner part, the words through which Hashem created the world.

title.en: The Beis Yosef and the Arizal

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Beis Yosef wanted to learn kabbalah from the Arizal, but at the Arizal's lectures he would fall asleep. The Arizal told him that this is not his portion in the Torah; his place is to be great in halacha.

title.en: The Lechovitcher's student

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Lechovitcher had a student who was a great gaon and served as rav of a town. The Lechovitcher told him not to learn kabbalah, because his portion in Torah is its plain meaning; this is no lack, and he is greater than others, it is simply his portion. The student listened to him.

title.en: Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman and the dibbuk in Radin

retelling.en: In Radin a girl suddenly fell ill with a swelling that moved through her body and sometimes choked her. Her father asked the Chafetz Chaim for help; he was old and sent his talmid Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman as his messenger. The dibbuk said it had done many sins, spoke about the townspeople who gathered, called one a tzaddik and said of the Chafetz Chaim that he was a Tanna. It explained that it ha…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the machine-made tzitzis

retelling.en: In the time of the Divrei Chaim a factory began producing tzitzis by machine. Asked whether they were kosher, he answered that they were unfit, since tzitzis must be made lishmah and a machine has no intent. When he was told the machine kept producing tzitzis that spread across the country, he wrote in a second teshuvah that he was certain he would soon see the downfall of that machine. His son,…

title.en: A chassid at the Ruzhiner Rebbe's

retelling.en: A Jew came to the Ruzhiner Rebbe and did not follow what the Rebbe was saying. One chassid remarked on it, and another chassid answered that with the Rebbe, who is altogether different from everyone, understanding him is not the measure. The Mashgiach applies this all the more to Rashbi, with whom even the lowest find a place.

title.en: Rashbi drives off an official with a decree

retelling.en: A man came with a decree against the Jews and wanted to carry it out, and Rabbi Shimon drove him away. He went to his superior and said he had been sent to carry out a decree but Rabbi Shimon would not allow it. He was told that if Rabbi Shimon does not allow it, it cannot be done. The Mashgiach calls this Rashbi's power to annul harsh decrees.

title.en: The valley filled with golden dinars

retelling.en: One of Rashbi's students went abroad, traded and came back wealthy, and the other students wished they had done the same. Rabbi Shimon took them to a valley and said, 'Valley, valley, fill with golden dinars,' and the whole valley filled. When the students wanted to grab, he told them that whoever takes now will not have later, and nobody took. The Mashgiach adds that the valley was the valley of…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta's gift taken back

retelling.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta suffered from poverty, prayed, and was sent a great treasure from heaven. His wife told him that in the next world, when he sits with his friends, their table will have four legs and his only three, since this was already taken in this world. He prayed that it be taken back, and it was; the Midrash says the second miracle was greater than the first.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's niggun from Meron

retelling.en: The Satmar Rav spent some time in Eretz Yisrael before coming to America and learned this niggun in Meron. He taught it to his chassidim, and it was the only time the Mashgiach heard the Satmar Rav sing a niggun while everyone else was silent so they could hear him.

title.en: The Gra and Reb Chaim of Volozhin

retelling.en: Reb Chaim of Volozhin asked his rebbe, the Gra, where he himself is found if the sixth century is the sedra of Ki Seitzei. The Gra answered that it says 'even shleimah', which stands for Eliyahu ben Shlomo, himself. Reb Chaim then asked where he was, and the Gra answered, but when Reb Chaim told the story to his talmidim he did not reveal it; the Mashgiach supposes he held back because of an ayin…

title.en: Rosh Hashanah at the start of the war

retelling.en: As a boy in Torah Vodaath on Wilson Street in Williamsburg, as war approached, the Mashgiach and his classmates stayed in at recess to hear a boy who owned a radio report the news. He told them that if Germany invaded Poland, England with its Royal Air Force and France with its Maginot Line would crush Germany in a few days. On Rosh Hashanah the Mashgiach stood by his father, who led Shacharis, a…

title.en: The Maggid chooses a baal korei

retelling.en: In the beis medrash of the Maggid of Mezritch there was a vacancy for a baal korei, and someone told the Maggid that Reb Shneur Zalman, later the Ba'al HaTanya, knew how to learn. The Maggid called him in and asked whether he knew the connection of the sedra to the events of the week, whether he could find each day's events in its aliyah, and whether he understood why a particular person is calle…

title.en: The stolen bread in the camp

retelling.en: At the end of the war, when the Nazis knew the Americans were near, they announced that every prisoner could get fresh bread. One very hungry Jew got back in line twice and ended up with three pieces. Russian prisoners of war in his quarters saw it, beat him and stole his bread. In the morning the Nazis had fled, and the Russians who had eaten his bread lay dead: the bread had been poisoned.

title.en: A tzaddik who thanked for everything

retelling.en: The Mashgiach reads from the will of a tzaddik, whose avodah the Rebbe of Lublin said was precious in Heaven, telling his children to learn from him that he had thanked Hashem for everything. He thanked Hashem many times a day, for decades, for having a private room to serve Him, and for his Shabbos clothes. When his snuff box fell without opening, and when his glasses fell without breaking, he t…

title.en: Four thousand shluchim photographed at 770

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that two weeks earlier there was a picture in the newspapers of four thousand shluchim standing in front of 770 to be photographed. The last Rebbe had sent them to the darkest, most remote places in the world to spread Yiddishkeit, Torah and mitzvos and Chassidus with mesiras nefesh. Twenty years after the Rebbe, the work keeps growing, and the whole world marvels at the Rebbe…

title.en: Reb Avraham Zuskin's Shabbos davening

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that as a young man he knew a Lubavitcher chossid in Williamsburg, Reb Avraham Zuskin, an oved Hashem. On Shabbos he davened in the Stoliner shul on Rodney Street, coming at about nine o'clock to start davening. When people came back at four on a short Shabbos for Mincha, he was still sitting and davening, with tears flowing from his eyes. The Mashgiach says he was in heave…

title.en: Reb Shraga Feivel chooses the Tanya

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that his first meeting with the teaching of Chabad was in Mesivta Torah Vodaath, through his rebbe Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. He describes him as a Hungarian gadol baTorah with a deep mind, who swam in all the seas of Torah wisdom. Out of all the seforim he had learned, he chose specifically the Tanya to learn with the talmidim. He told the bochurim that they learn Gemara…

title.en: The sparks of the Ba'al Shem Tov's pipe

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what one of the Polish tzaddikim said: the Ba'al Shem Tov lit his pipe, and sparks began to fly. Each talmid caught one of the sparks, sparks of every color. That is why each talmid has a different nusach: all are sparks of the Besht's pipe.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin and the informer

retelling.en: As the Imrei Emes brings from the Chiddushei HaRim, in one town there was an informer who made terrible trouble for the Jews and denounced them to the gentiles. They sent a messenger to the Chozeh of Lublin with a kvittel bearing the informer's name and his mother's name, asking that he have a great downfall. The Chozeh looked at it and said, 'What do you want of this Jew? He shines in all worlds…

title.en: Avraham in Ur Kasdim

retelling.en: Avraham as a boy searched for the truth and could not accept that the world made itself. He first thought the sun made it and worshipped the sun, but at night the sun set and the moon came out; then the moon disappeared in the morning. He concluded that one Master runs this harmonious world and began to serve Him without knowing who He was. Nimrod told him to stop; Avraham refused and was thrown…

title.en: The am ha'aretz and Rabbi Hoshaya

retelling.en: An am ha'aretz asked Rabbi Hoshaya whether, if he told him a word of Torah, he would say it in public in his name. Rabbi Hoshaya agreed if it was a good word. The am ha'aretz said that Yaakov sent Eisav a gift of animals, and when Moshiach comes Eisav will have to give it back, because the passuk says 'mincha yashivu'. Rabbi Hoshaya liked it and said it in the beis medrash in his name, and it is…

title.en: The Apter Rav's niggun

retelling.en: It is handed down among the Russian chassidim that the Apter Rav, the Ohev Yisrael, used to sing a niggun and told his chassidim that he had heard it from Yaakov Avinu when he was one of Yaakov's sheep. The niggun is known and is sung on Motza'ei Shabbos.

title.en: The Rebbe and the lokshen

retelling.en: At a seudah a Rebbe was served a plate of soup with lokshen, and he moved his spoon back and forth. A simple man there thought the Rebbe was looking for the lokshen, and called out that he should lower the spoon deeper, and there he would find them. The Rebbe told him that he had truly revived him. The Mashgiach applies it: we are deep down in the plate, and that is where the lokshen are.

title.en: The release at 'Padah beshalom'

retelling.en: When the Alter Rebbe was in prison and the news came that he would be freed, he was in the middle of saying Tehillim, at the words 'Padah beshalom nafshi'. He wrote this in his famous letter, and took it to mean that his redemption should bring peace among Jews.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim on the 'pere adam'

retelling.en: A Jew once took leave of the Chofetz Chaim before going to Eretz Yisroel and spoke of the Arabs there. The Chofetz Chaim told him that the Torah calls Yishmael a 'pere adam': if he becomes a doctor, he is a 'pere adam' doctor; a judge, a 'pere adam' judge; a professor, a 'pere adam' professor. This he cannot change.

title.en: The woman who carried out her piano

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions a well-known story of a woman whose house caught fire. She had a piano that was very dear to her, and she carried it out of the house, although carrying a piano is a great ordeal. He uses it to show that a person in distress discovers strengths he did not know he had.

title.en: The donor who had no time for the pushke

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes a wealthy man being honored that night at a dinner for a bikur cholim organization that helps sick Jews on a large scale, with ambulances and hospitals. On his way down the steps to his new car, a Jew with a pushke sits there asking for a donation, and the wealthy man gives him nothing. He gives charity, the Mashgiach explains, but wholesale, not retail.

title.en: A hose for the sukkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that about sixty years earlier he needed a hose for his sukkah and went into a plastics store to buy one. They answered that they do not sell retail, only wholesale.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya senses a listener

retelling.en: The Ba'al HaTanya set times to speak to the 'young chassidim', simple Jews who could not learn. Once a chassid came in and hid so he could listen, and heard the Ba'al HaTanya speak to the simple Jews about the kelipah that tells a person to look where one may not look. The Ba'al HaTanya sensed a disturbance in the room, stopped, and said it came from that chassid, because he had woken from sleep…

title.en: The Rebbe Maharash's journey to Paris

retelling.en: The Rebbe Maharash made a long journey to Paris to save one Jew from drinking yayin nesech. He came in and told him that yayin nesech harms the mind and the heart. Fine generations descended from that Jew.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe stands for a young man

retelling.en: In his young years the Mashgiach davened in a Stoliner shul in Williamsburg, where old Stoliner chassidim told him this story. The young Lubavitcher Rebbe, then a young man who was not yet Rebbe, came to Rabbi Yisrael of Stolin, known as the Frankfurter, and the Stoliner Rebbe stood up for him. Asked why he stood for a young man, he said that he was unique in his generation in mesirus nefesh. The…

title.en: The Alter Rebbe answers Shklov with a niggun

retelling.en: Shklov was a city of great scholars and misnagdim, who protested the Alter Rebbe's reading of a Mishnah about singing as speaking of angels. When he came to Shklov they gathered and each one asked his questions. He asked to hear all the questions first, then stood and sang a niggun. As they listened they were drawn in, their minds and hearts opened, and all their questions were answered.

title.en: The Stoliner's pat on the Blozhover's shoulder

retelling.en: The young Stoliner Rebbe, Rav Yisrael of Stolin, once spent a Shabbos together with the Blozhover Rebbe. The Blozhover read the Torah, and afterwards he asked the Stoliner Rebbe to daven Musaf. The Stoliner patted him on the shoulder and said that he himself should daven Musaf. Later the Stoliner Rebbe explained that he had not needed the Blozhover to daven Musaf; he had wanted to pat such a holy…

title.en: The tzaddik who learned on Nittel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Bnei Yissaschar a story of a tzaddik who learned on Nittel. A dog came in to him, because on that night the dogs hold sway.

title.en: The Rebbe's second dollar

retelling.en: Each summer, when the yeshiva went to camp, the Mashgiach spent the summer in Yerushalayim, and before leaving he would take leave of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, who blessed him with 'one who changes his place changes his mazal for the good'. Once, going with a friend who was present at the gathering, he told the friend that this time he would only sit and learn and accept no invitations to speak. The…

title.en: A blessing for the Rebbe

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he once came to the Rebbe and gave him a blessing that he should merit to lead the Jews toward Moshiach. The Rebbe answered: with all Jews together. The Mashgiach says he learned from this that this is how one should give a blessing.

title.en: The Maggid's ba'al korei

retelling.en: The Mezritcher Maggid once lacked a ba'al korei, and he was told that the young Shneur Zalman could do it. He called him in and asked whether he knew the bond of each parsha to its week, of each aliyah to the days of the week, and of each person called up to his aliyah from the root of his soul. Each time the young man answered yes, and the Maggid said that then he could be his ba'al korei.

title.en: Money hidden in the thief's bag

retelling.en: As the tzaddikim tell it, a rich merchant came to an inn with money and had to hide it over Shabbos. He realized that a thief was staying at the inn, and it occurred to him to hide the money in the thief's own bag, where the thief would never look. Right after Shabbos he took his money back out of the thief's bag; his own bag had been turned over and searched, and nothing was found there.

title.en: The Alter Rebbe's interrogation

retelling.en: When the Alter Rebbe stood for interrogation in his trial in Russia, he was asked whether he was a talmid of the Ba'al Shem Tov. It was understood that if he answered no, he would be set free. He could have said he was a talmid of the Maggid, but, as he himself said, he would not cut himself off from the Ba'al Shem Tov even for a moment. One of the charges was that he sent money to Eretz Yisrael,…

title.en: The Tzemach Tzedek and the blank letter

retelling.en: In the stories of R' Mottel Slonimer it is told that three of the greatest rabbanim of Russia and Lita were called to Moscow to be questioned; one was the Tzemach Tzedek. They were handed a blank letter to sign, which the government would fill in later, and were promised it would bring good things. The other two signed and the Tzemach Tzedek refused, though refusing put his life in danger. The le…

title.en: The Rebbe Rayatz's arrest

retelling.en: The Rebbe Rayatz spread Torah and Yiddishkeit under the Communists, with Torah study, yeshivos and mikvaos, and was arrested for it. The Americans took up his cause, and the Russians did not want trouble with the American government. He not only had mesiras nefesh himself but demanded it of his Chassidim, many of whom were arrested and sent to Siberia.

title.en: The neshamos' protest against endless gilgulim

retelling.en: A tzaddik, after Kiddush Levanah, told his talmidim what he had seen. Neshamos that keep being sent back to this world as gilgulim, failing their mission each time, decided to protest. They came to the malach in charge of neshamos, who sent them to his superior, and so on higher and higher until the highest malach sent them to Hashem. Hashem told them to go down again; if they slip in a mitzvah H…

title.en: Rabbi Naftali of Ropshitz asks for a strong glass of milk

retelling.en: Rabbi Naftali of Ropshitz went into the kitchen and asked why he was not given a glass of milk for all his toil in serving Hashem. When they brought one, he came back and complained that it was thin, watery milk with no strength in it, and asked for strong milk. The Chassidim wondered at such strange words. Soon a woman came who had just had a baby and had no milk; he told her she would have milk…

title.en: The package of matzos for Stuttgart

retelling.en: A Jew traveling to Germany on business came to the Lubavitcher Rebbe for a dollar; the Rebbe gave him another dollar and a package of matzos, telling him to give it to the first Jew he met in Stuttgart. He wondered, since he was not going to Stuttgart. On the way an announcement said there was engine trouble and they would stop in Stuttgart, and he understood he was a messenger. He asked around f…

title.en: A gematria at a Lubavitch farbrengen

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a bochur he went on Chol HaMoed to a farbrengen where the Lubavitcher Rebbe, who was not yet Rebbe, spoke to bochurim. He said that in Lubavitch they do not say gematrios, but allowed himself to say one: that 19 Kislev is the gematria of 'on that day a great shofar will be sounded'.

title.en: The Rebbe's call before the Yom Kippur War

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that some weeks before the Yom Kippur War broke out, the Lubavitcher Rebbe began speaking about 'from the mouths of babes... to silence the enemy'. He called for children to say Tehillim, daven and learn extra, and repeated it again and again, and nobody understood what he meant. The war came suddenly on Yom Kippur, when the Jews were unprepared and men ran from the batei me…

title.en: The Satmar Rav's question to the Chazon Ish

retelling.en: When the Satmar Rav visited Eretz Yisrael, he visited the Chazon Ish and asked him: the Rambam says to move to another place, but today bad influence is everywhere, so what should one do? The Chazon Ish answered that one should run away to the yeshiva, for the yeshiva is good. The Mashgiach adds that he is not certain the Chazon Ish would answer the same today, since every yeshiva has its influen…

title.en: The chassid who feared facing his friends

retelling.en: A chassid who used to travel to his Rebbe several times a year once saved a woman from drowning in a river in the woods, and a strong temptation came upon him. Fear of Gehinnom did not stop him, nor did the thought that the Rebbe would see the sin on his face, since the yetzer hara answered each one. What held him back was that he could not face his friends in the shtibel where he davened every S…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the wagon driver

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was once riding on a wagon when a priest came toward them, and the non-Jewish wagon driver did not cross himself. The Ba'al Shem Tov jumped off the wagon, saying he did not want to ride with someone who does not cross himself when the priest passes. The Mashgiach explains: they believe in the wrong thing, but at least they believe.

title.en: The Rebbe of Lublin and the informer's kvitel

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim relates that Jews came to the Rebbe of Lublin to complain about an informer in their town who caused Jews great troubles, and gave him a kvitel with the man's name so that he would fall. The Rebbe looked at the kvitel and said that the Jew written there lights up all the worlds. Puzzled, they asked the Rebbe's close talmidim, who advised them to give the kvitel again in the m…

title.en: The Skverer Rebbe and the orange juice

retelling.en: The Skverer Rebbe, the father of the present Skverer Rebbe, visited the Tzelemer Rav, who offered him a glass of orange juice. The Skverer Rebbe refused, and when told it had been squeezed from oranges in their own kitchen, he answered that his father did not drink orange juice and he eats nothing his father did not eat. Before Pesach he would go to the fields at harvest time, cut a whole year's…

title.en: The kernel of wheat in the Pesach soup

retelling.en: A tzaddik who wanted a truly chametz-free Pesach worked for a month cleaning the house, the pots, the cellar and the garden, and was very stringent about the food he brought in. At the Seder, at Shulchan Orech, he found a kernel of wheat floating in his soup and was dismayed. He asked a sheilas chalom: why did he deserve this, and how could it have happened? He was answered that he had worked har…

title.en: The Ohev Yisrael remembers Yaakov's niggun

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that it is well known that the Ohev Yisrael remembered the time when he was one of Yaakov Avinu's sheep. He even remembered the niggun Yaakov Avinu played on his flute for the sheep. That niggun is still known among Chassidim, who sing it especially on parshas Vayeitzei.

title.en: The am ha'aretz and Rabbi Hoshaya

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates the Midrash in which an am ha'aretz asked Rabbi Hoshaya whether, if he said a dvar Torah, Rabbi Hoshaya would repeat it in his name. Rabbi Hoshaya answered that if it was a proper dvar Torah he would. The am ha'aretz then pointed out that the passuk says 'minchah yashivu', they will return a gift, and not that they will bring one: the nations will return to Moshiach the anim…

title.en: The man who forgave everyone

retelling.en: Rabbi Abba, sitting at the gate of Lod, saw a man sit down on a ledge jutting out of a mountain and fall asleep. A snake came toward him, and a creature came and killed the snake. The man woke, saw the dead snake, got up and walked on, and right after, the ledge fell into the valley. Rabbi Abba asked him what deeds had earned him two miracles, and the man said that he had always forgiven anyone w…

title.en: The prisoner's question to Rabbi Shlomo Kluger

retelling.en: Someone held in prison was to be let out for a short time and asked Rabbi Shlomo Kluger whether to go in at night and light Chanukah candles, or to go in the morning, daven and say Hallel with a minyan. Rabbi Shlomo Kluger answered that he should not use it for lighting but go in the morning to shul and say Hallel with the tzibbur. The Mashgiach brings it to show the great worth of Hallel.

title.en: The dreidel and what is won on Chanukah

retelling.en: In a story connected with Ruzhin, someone came in and saw several young men playing with the dreidel, and one of them had lost a few coins. He said that what one wins on Chanukah can no longer be lost.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's dream of two dogs

retelling.en: The Ohr HaChaim relates a dream in which the forces of tumah came to fight him in the form of two dogs, a male and a female. He overpowered the male at once, but with the female he had a hard battle and prevailed only partly. The Mashgiach explains that in tumah the female is stronger than the male.

title.en: Rabbi Nachman and the man who could not daven

retelling.en: A man came to Rabbi Nachman of Breslov and said he could not daven, because whenever he began he saw in his imagination a man carrying a cross. Rabbi Nachman answered: what do you care, let him carry it; ignore it. The Mashgiach says this is how to treat thoughts of doubt.

title.en: The chassid of Reb Mendel of Vitebsk and the mazikim

retelling.en: The Tzemach Tzedek told his chassidim that a mazik invited a chassid of Reb Mendel of Vitebsk to perform a bris; there a captive Jewish woman warned him not to eat or he could never leave, so he pleaded a bellyache. Reb Mendel told him these were mazikim and that next time he should tell them they are nothing. When they turned into fierce animals and charged, he kept saying they were nothing and…

title.en: The oved who thanked for his snuff

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of an oved Hashem who thanked Hashem for every small thing. When he took out his snuff, he thanked Hashem that it had not fallen to the ground. And when it did fall, he found something to thank for as well.

title.en: The Imrei Emes's letter about Chofetz Chaim

retelling.en: When the Chofetz Chaim published his sefer on lashon hara, the Gerer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, wrote a letter to be hung in all his chassidim's shtiblach asking them to learn it. He wrote that he himself had learned the sefer and felt a benefit for his soul. Through this he broke the divide between chassidim and Litvaks.

title.en: Friday nights as a young man

retelling.en: The Mashgiach remembers that as a young man he used to go to a beis medrash on Friday night, and it was the high point of his week. Ten or fifteen Jews sat together, among them Jews from Eretz Yisroel, telling stories of tzaddikim and singing the Shabbos zemiros.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe runs from the mikvah

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe was expecting his son, who later succeeded him, to visit for Yom Tov, and went to the mikvah. As he came out, the gabbai told him that 'he came'. He grabbed his clothes and ran out without putting on his socks, asking where he was; when they pointed out his son, he burst out crying, for he had thought Moshiach had come.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva and Ben Koziva

retelling.en: Ben Koziva was a powerful king and a tzaddik who ruled from the city of Beitar, had an army and went to war against the Romans. Rabbi Akiva, the greatest of the Tanna'im, was his right-hand man and announced that he was Moshiach. The Romans captured and destroyed Beitar and Ben Koziva was killed, and then it became known that he was not Moshiach. He had performed no miracles.

title.en: In six days it will be Shabbos again

retelling.en: Chassidim once sat at a melave malka on a summer motzaei Shabbos until it was already day. On their way to daven they met a distinguished Jew of Williamsburg, whose name the Mashgiach says he has forgotten. One of them went up to him and told him he had good news: in six days it will be Shabbos again.

title.en: Give me Shabbos in the challah

retelling.en: An old chassid would ask Hashem, when he ate his piece of challah, that since He gave challah for Shabbos, He should give him Shabbos in the challah. He asked the same over the fish: give me Shabbos in the fish.

title.en: R' Dovid Biderman and the spoiled cholent

retelling.en: R' Dovid Biderman was once in Meron with his companions for Shabbos, and a cholent was prepared for the seudah. It was a hot day, the fire went out, and when it came time to eat, the cholent had spoiled and gave off a bad smell, so nobody wanted to eat it. The Mashgiach relates that R' Dovid took some and ate it, and draws the lesson that one may not disgrace a Shabbos food.

title.en: R' Shlomo of Karlin's foot did not feel Shabbos

retelling.en: R' Mordechai of Slonim used to tell that R' Shlomo of Karlin went to the mikveh with his gabbai, who brought his Shabbos clothes. One Shabbos sock fell into the water, so the gabbai gave him his weekday sock. When Friday night came, the Rebbe began to cry out that his left foot did not feel Shabbos, and the gabbai told him it was not the Rebbe but the sock. R' Shlomo then said he had heard procla…

title.en: The tzaddik who could not go to the mikveh

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that one of the early tzaddikim, who could not immerse, came into the crowd, bent down among them and said 'Mikveh Yisrael Hashem': Jews are a mikveh.

title.en: The patience of Reb Shlomo of Zvhil's gabbai

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw this yielding by great people. In particular he mentions Reb Eliyahu, the gabbai of Reb Shlomo of Zvhil, whose wife was unwell, and describes how greatly he had to bear with her.

title.en: Farmers who kept shemitah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that in the past shemitah year about four thousand farmers in Eretz Yisroel kept shemitah. The papers reported that their farms flourished and they lost no money, while other farms did not grow as well.

title.en: The Steipler's wealth

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Steipler was asked why he was not rich, given what is written in the Shulchan Aruch about a tzaddik becoming wealthy. The Steipler answered that he was rich. Wealth takes many forms, material and spiritual, and learning Torah is the greatest wealth there is.

title.en: Shimi ben Gera curses Dovid HaMelech

retelling.en: As Dovid HaMelech was driven out of Yerushalayim, Shimi ben Gera, of the house of Shaul, came toward him and cursed him with a terrible curse. Yoav, who was with Dovid, wanted to kill Shimi on the spot for disrespecting the king. Dovid said no, let him be: Hashem told him to curse, and if not he, another would curse.

title.en: A letter to the Yismach Moshe about doubts

retelling.en: A Jew wrote to the Yismach Moshe that he was tormented by doubts in emunah and asked for advice against the yetzer hara that confused his head. The Yismach Moshe answered that he would not speak to him through philosophy but through the way of the holy Torah: a tradition handed down from a multitude who saw cannot be false, since no one could tell his child that six hundred thousand people saw Ha…

title.en: Ten years of learning for the cats

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story he heard from Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. In earlier times a man took a bochur who was a talmid chacham as a son-in-law and gave him ten years of support, giving the couple a room on the upper floor of his house. At night the young man heard noise and movement above his ceiling and decided his father-in-law wanted to hear him learning at night, so he learned and hard…

title.en: The Karliner chassid in Chortkov

retelling.en: In Ruzhin and Chortkov the davening was quiet. A Karliner chassid, used to the loud davening of Karlin, came to Reb Yisroel of Chortkov and asked permission to shout while davening, and the Rebbe refused. When he came to daven he forgot himself and shouted, and afterwards he went to ask forgiveness. The Rebbe told him it had been very good: he dislikes shouting on order, but shouting that comes f…

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech and the yud of 'yarbeh'

retelling.en: The Torah limits how many wives a king may take, so that they not turn his heart away from the Torah. Shlomo HaMelech, as the passuk relates, took a thousand wives, confident that he was master over his yetzer hara and that they would not sway him. The yud of the word 'yarbeh' came up before the Kisei HaKavod and complained that Shlomo was uprooting it. Hashem answered that Shlomo and a thousand…

title.en: The soldier who washed laundry on the front

retelling.en: The speaker learned with a ba'al teshuvah who had just returned from the Gulf War and would not say what he did there, calling it a military secret. Weeks later he admitted that he had been on a ship of over two thousand soldiers that was entirely the laundry department, and his work on 'the front' was moving washing into the dryer. The speaker uses it to show that an army sends only its stronges…

title.en: R' Mendel of Rimanov's sigh before his passing

retelling.en: According to what R' Shimon of Zhelichov wrote, a few weeks before R' Mendel of Rimanov passed away he sat on his bed on a Friday afternoon after the mikveh and groaned, saying he had done all he could for Napoleon to win, and asking what more to do. Asked about the Ba'al HaTanya's letter, he answered that Moshiach cannot come without the last and hardest battle; if it did not happen then, it wou…

title.en: The classmate's mother's talk-only phone

retelling.en: A respected yungerman in Monsey sent his son, about twelve, to a chassidish cheder, where the boy became distracted and withdrawn. A counselor found that the boy had seen terrible things, shown to him by a classmate on the classmate's mother's simple flip phone. The classmate's father insisted he had bought only a talk-only phone, but a friend on the street had taught his son how to open it to th…

title.en: The menahel's 'kosher' phone

retelling.en: At a gathering of menahalim in Boro Park, a technician asked a respected menahel whether his phone was kosher. The menahel said he had bought it kosher; within two minutes the technician showed him it was fully open to the internet, and the menahel turned pale.

title.en: The yungerman who would not take an internet job

retelling.en: A yungerman whose company closed decided he would take no job connected to the internet. Months passed with eight or nine children and growing debts to the grocers. When offered a good job that required internet, he asked a rav, who told him he must take it and guard himself, and then a great Rebbe in Monsey, who blessed him with success in the new job and told him to be careful. Both told him he…

title.en: The father who would not check the weather

retelling.en: A Boro Park yungerman whose business requires a smartphone keeps it in his car and carries only a flip phone; when there is a problem he goes out to the car, even at night. Before Chol Hamoed his son asked him to check the weather on his phone, and he answered that he does not touch it except when he is required to.

title.en: The mother with the pink smartphone

retelling.en: A couple came to the speaker for an hour about which yeshiva to send their difficult seventeen-year-old son. As they rose, the mother took out a smartphone. She offered to show that it was disconnected and held only pictures and clips, and the speaker asked only whether her children saw her sitting and enjoying it, since they would learn to enjoy it too. He says that ten minutes after they left,…

title.en: The Abarbanel refuses to stay in Spain

retelling.en: King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella decreed that the Jews must either accept Christianity or leave Spain, taking nothing but the clothes they wore. Thousands chose to leave; many were killed by bandits or drowned, and the survivors settled in the eastern lands, which is why they are called Sefardim. The king asked one Jew to stay: Don Yitzchak Abarbanel, his finance minister, who ran the finances o…

title.en: The generation of the mann discovers bread from the ground

retelling.en: For forty years in the desert bread came down from heaven, and the children born there knew nothing else. When they crossed the Yarden and the mann stopped, they saw bread rising from the ground and were amazed at the wonder, and made the bracha on it for the first time in their lives.

title.en: R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld after R' Yehoshua Leib Diskin

retelling.en: R' Langer relates that R' Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld was a great zealot while his rebbe, R' Yehoshua Leib Diskin, was alive, and quieted down after he passed away. Asked what had happened, he answered that zealotry is a double-edged sword and the rebbe is its handle; without the handle one can cut oneself.

title.en: The filter expert's son

retelling.en: A boy came into class crying and finally told R' Langer that his father, a professional who installs filters, had given him a filtered device as a gift. The boy found a trick around the filter and reached terrible places. The father cried that he, the expert, had been fooled by his own child.

title.en: How monkeys are caught

retelling.en: R' Langer describes how natives catch monkeys: they cut a small hole in a coconut, fill it with cooked rice and tie it high on a tree. A monkey pushes its hand in and grabs the rice, and with its fist closed it cannot pull it out. It only needs to let go of the rice, but it holds on, struggles until its hand bleeds, and is caught in the net.

title.en: The policeman and the phone

retelling.en: R' Langer tells that on his way to his yeshiva early one morning a policeman pulled him over for not stopping fully at a stop sign and went to write a ticket. He then decided before the Ribono shel Olam that he would buy a new kosher phone and rather spend the money on that than on tickets and lawyers. Within seconds the policeman returned his license and let him go without a ticket.

title.en: Reb Zusha and the Biur

retelling.en: Reb Zusha was once invited into a house but stopped at the door and could not enter, because he sensed tumah there. The host was confused and asked why the Rebbe would not come in. Reb Zusha asked them to search the bookcase, and they found the Biur, the commentary on the Chumash written by Moshe Mendelssohn, an apikores. Once it was thrown out, Reb Zusha was able to enter, and the tumah had left…

title.en: The bachurim's davening and the Chevra Emunas Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach introduced that bachurim should daven with geshmak, saying the words aloud and together, and the people around delighted in their davening. After a summer season they asked why they should have it only in the summer and not in town, in Boro Park. So the Chevra Emunas Yisroel was founded, with about forty fine bachurim with yiras Shamayim, beginning as a minyan in a store front, with…

title.en: Davening mincha gedolah

retelling.en: Someone used to daven mincha gedolah, at about half past twelve, with a private minyan. He was asked why, since many hold that mincha ketanah is preferable. He answered that once the time of mincha comes and he can already speak to the Creator, he cannot hold himself back; his heart pulls him to it.

title.en: Ephraim, the brandy and 'Tzam'ah nafshi'

retelling.en: As the Beis Avraham told it, a simple Jew named Ephraim sold brandy without a permit to avoid heavy taxes, a serious crime in Russia. An informer threatened to report him. He went to shul, opened the aron kodesh and began saying Tehillim; Reb Yehuda Leib, passing by, heard him cry out 'Tzam'ah nafshi l'Elokim' again and again with great feeling. Asked about it, Ephraim said he had come to pray to…

title.en: The fire in Skver

retelling.en: A fire broke out in the Skverer Rebbe's beis medrash in Skver and it burned down. One thing remained: the small room where the Rebbe davened stayed whole. It was said that this was because in that room no one talked during davening.

title.en: The soul that came late

retelling.en: On an Erev Shabbos souls would come to a tzaddik for a tikkun. One soul merited to come, but arrived late, and was told that nothing more could be done for it because Shabbos had already begun. It came late because in its lifetime it used to come late to davening and learning, middah k'neged middah.

title.en: The Mashgiach's first visit to Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls how excited he was before his first visit to Eretz Yisroel, dreaming of seeing the beautiful land. Riding to Yerushalayim, he looked out on both sides and was disappointed: empty fields, long deserts, mountains of sand and rocks. Every year since then it became better, and now vegetables, trees and grapes grow along the roadsides.

title.en: The river of Jewish tears

retelling.en: After the passing of the Ruzhiner Rebbe, the Sadigura Rebbe once saw the Ruzhiner standing by a great river, bent over it. He said that this is the river of Jewish tears, where all the tears of the Jews gather together and come to that place.

title.en: The young man who cried to the Satmar Rav

retelling.en: A young man came to the Satmar Rav crying that he could not free himself from bad thoughts. The Rebbe paced back and forth for a while before answering him. The Mashgiach brings the story to show that Torah alone is not enough and tefillah is needed.

title.en: The maskil and the snuff

retelling.en: In the time of the Haskalah, a maskil wanted to show a great talmid of the Vilna Gaon, the founder of the Volozhin yeshiva, that he knew more, and asked him the names of Rashi's daughters. The answer came back with a question: what brand of snuff did Rashi take? You know that better than I; what Rashi said, that I know. The Mashgiach uses it to say that the history of Chassidus matters less than…

title.en: Carrying the Maggid's head

retelling.en: When the Maggid passed away, his disciples drew lots for which part of the body each would carry, and the Baal HaTanya won the head. They carried him to the mikveh, and the Baal HaTanya said to let the Rebbe immerse himself, and he did; the Mashgiach says this is the tradition as it was handed down.

title.en: Water from Eretz Yisroel

retelling.en: A man preparing to travel to Eretz Yisroel went around taking leave of the tzaddikim of the generation. One of them, who was sick at the time, told him that he needed a refuah, and that his refuah was to drink water of Eretz Yisroel. He asked the man to take a little water in his mouth and pour it back into the glass, and he would drink it, because one who is already preparing to go to Eretz Yisr…

title.en: The Ruzhiner's question

retelling.en: A man came to the Ruzhiner already packed to travel to Eretz Yisroel, not to ask whether to go but only for a brachah. The Ruzhiner asked him what Rosh Hashanah was like for him, and told him that Eretz Yisroel is Rosh Hashanah: could he take upon himself to live every day there with the seriousness of Rosh Hashanah? The man said no, and did not go.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim's journey that did not happen

retelling.en: The Chofetz Chaim said he could not go to Eretz Yisroel because he was needed in Poland. Later he decided he could go, packed and was ready to travel, but he suddenly became sick and had to cancel his plans. The Mashgiach brings this, together with the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Vilna Gaon who set out and had to turn back, to show that from Heaven they were not allowed to go.

title.en: Shlomo sleeps late after completing the Beis HaMikdash

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Shlomo built the Beis HaMikdash, but on the next morning, when it had to be opened to bring the morning korban tamid, he got up late. The night before had been his wedding. He adds that because of this it was decreed that the Beis HaMikdash would be destroyed.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembers his gilgulim

retelling.en: The Yitav Lev wrote that he heard from his grandfather, the Yismach Moshe, that he remembered all his gilgulim. He remembered being one of the sheep of Yaakov Avinu, could show a mark on his shoulder from Yaakov's staff, and remembered the niggun Yaakov played to gather the sheep, which chassidim still sing. He also remembered being in the desert at the dispute between Korach and Moshe Rabbeinu;…

title.en: The Apter Rav remembers the Beis HaMikdash

retelling.en: When the Apter Rav davened the Avodah of Yom Kippur and reached the description of what the Kohen Gadol did, he said out loud that he remembered it, from when he served in the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Tzaddikim at the Ohr HaChaim's grave as Rommel advanced

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that over fifty years earlier the Germans came close to Eretz Yisrael. Tzaddikim with open ruach hakodesh went up to the Ohr HaChaim's grave on Har HaZeisim, saw there the Name of Hashem in fire, and said that nothing would come of it. The German general Rommel had said he would drink coffee in Tel Aviv the next morning, but he did not live to see it.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav at a wedding in Oberland

retelling.en: The Sanzer Rav, the Divrei Chaim, came with great honor to Oberland, a part of Hungary with an Ashkenazi, non-Chassidic population. There he spoke with the father of the chasan and asked whether he remembered when the boy was born. The father recalled that he had found the child in a river, taken pity on him and adopted him. The Sanzer Rav revealed that the chasan was in fact the kallah's brother…

title.en: The childless couple and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells the Midrash of a couple who lived together in peace and love for ten years without children and decided to divorce. They made a feast, and the husband told his wife she could take whatever she wished from his house. She had him carried to her parents' home, and when he awoke she told him he was the thing she wanted most. They went to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who blessed them,…

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim's advice to the Sanzer Rav

retelling.en: The Mashgiach found a teshuvah of the Chiddushei HaRim answering a question from the Divrei Chaim about a talmid chacham, married many years without children, who wanted to give a get against his wife's will. The Chiddushei HaRim argued that a get could not be given that way and advised the Sanzer Rav to do as in the Midrash and bless the couple with children. The Mashgiach adds that a grandson h…

title.en: Rav Nachum of Chernobyl waiting for the esrog

retelling.en: Someone described seeing Rav Nachum of Chernobyl before dawn on Sukkos, standing with the esrog in his hand and waiting for daybreak so he could do the mitzvah. The expression on his face showed he was thirsting to fulfill it.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin and the informer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, as the Imrei Emes and the Shem MiShmuel bring from the Chiddushei HaRim, of an informer who brought much trouble on the Jews of his town. The townspeople, chassidim of the Chozeh of Lublin, gave the Chozeh a kvittel with the man's name so that he would curse him, but the Chozeh refused, saying the man's soul was shining in all the worlds. When they asked again later, the Choz…

title.en: Frankfurt before and after the Haskalah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Haflaah, Rabbi Pinchas Horowitz, wrote in his introduction that he thanked Hashem for becoming Rav in Frankfurt, a city full of talmidei chachamim and a yeshivah. Some thirty years after the Haskalah began to rage, Rabbi Samson Raphael Hirsch came to Frankfurt and found only thirteen families keeping Shabbos. He brought German Jewry back to emunah.

title.en: Rabbi Hirsch answers a maskil

retelling.en: The maskilim wrote their heretical books in Hebrew, and one of them criticized Rabbi Hirsch for writing his works in German rather than in the eternal language. Rabbi Hirsch answered that his writings in German would remain forever, while the other's writings in the eternal language would be lost. The Mashgiach adds that so it indeed was.

title.en: The bitter apple juice

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the previous week he had an upset stomach, and was given a glass of apple juice. It tasted bitter to him and he thought it was spoiled, but he was told it was good apple juice. Once his stomach recovered, the same apple juice tasted wonderful. So too, one with a spiritually upset stomach does not know what Shabbos is.

title.en: The man who counted 310 immersions with a finger

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts seeing someone, a great man among the ba'alei mussar, who wanted to immerse 310 times but did not want to spend the time. He stayed in the mikvah and pushed a finger out and back in again and again, counting each time as an immersion. The Mashgiach says that this is not the point of the mikvah, since the whole person must be in the water and its essence is bitul.

title.en: The Alter Rebbe and the disguised Czar

retelling.en: The Czarist government imprisoned the Ba'al HaTanya, suspecting him of building a kingdom within the kingdom. Hearing reports of him, the Czar disguised himself and came in like a prison official, but the Alter Rebbe stood up before him, and when asked why, said that he was the Czar, for he sensed his malchus. The Czar then tested him by asking the time, and though he sat in a windowless cell wit…

title.en: The woman who wanted to go to the beach

retelling.en: During a great war in Eretz Yisroel, when the surrounding Arab countries fought against a small number of Jews and the Jews won with Hashem's help, even irreligious newspapers wrote about the miracles. A woman wrote a letter to one paper asking them to stop writing about the miracles. Every Shabbos she went to spend her time at the beach, and reading about the miracles she saw that there is a Rib…

title.en: Rav Bloch and the falling plaster

retelling.en: In Telz a group of young men who had left their parents' ways opened a club with a dormitory, where they ate forbidden food and smoked on Shabbos. One of them, broken over a desire he could not fulfill, cut his wrists in his room and bled until he died. Afterwards the plaster of the ceiling below that room kept falling, no matter how often a craftsman repaired it. One young man who still had some…

title.en: Adam's Shabbos in Gan Eden

retelling.en: After the sin Adam was to be sent out of Gan Eden, but it was already erev Shabbos, and he was allowed to remain there until after Shabbos. Since this was already after the sin, he needed garments, and he took special garments for Shabbos from the trees.

title.en: Moshe asks Pharaoh for a day of rest

retelling.en: Moshe grew up in Pharaoh's house, adopted by Pharaoh's daughter. He went out to the field and saw how hard the Jews worked, and told Pharaoh that they were so exhausted they could hardly work; if they were given one day a week of rest they would work much better all week. Pharaoh agreed to a set day, and Moshe chose Shabbos.

title.en: Give me Shabbos for the challah

retelling.en: One of the great chassidim worked all week in poverty so that he would have enough to buy a little challah and fish for Shabbos. At last he had it; he made kiddush, washed, ate a piece of challah, and said: Ribono shel Olam, You gave me challah for Shabbos; I ask You, give me Shabbos for the challah.

title.en: The cholent of Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir

retelling.en: A rav who spent Shabbos with Reb Yechezkel of Kuzmir ate from the Rebbe's cholent and had never tasted such a cholent. After Shabbos he asked the Rebbetzin for the recipe, and she wrote down everything that goes into it, but when his wife cooked it exactly so, it was an ordinary cholent. The next time he came he asked again, and the Rebbetzin told him that every erev Shabbos her holy husband come…

title.en: Nishmas in the fish at Karlin

retelling.en: At Reb Aharon of Karlin the chassidim used to prepare the Shabbos food. A chassid in the kitchen salting and preparing the fish remembered that on Shabbos morning one says Nishmas, and he began to say Nishmas while preparing the fish. Friday night, when the fish was served to Reb Aharon, he remarked that there is a piece of Nishmas in the fish.

title.en: Rav Yisrael of Vizhnitz at bedikas chametz

retelling.en: Rav Yisrael of Vizhnitz was once searching for chametz together with his gabbai. Finding nothing, he asked the gabbai how it could be that they searched and found no chametz. The gabbai, a chassidishe Jew, answered with the Mishnah that a place where no chametz is brought in needs no search.

title.en: The Karliner chassid's wine and fish

retelling.en: One of the great Karliner chassidim, a poor man, prepared himself for Shabbos constantly. When he made kiddush on Shabbos, he said to Hashem that since He had given him wine for Shabbos, he asked Him to give Shabbos to the wine. When the fish was served, he asked the same: give Shabbos to the fish.

title.en: The Satmar Rav eating fish on Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw the Satmar Rav eat fish on Shabbos. Every Shabbos, as he ate the fish, his face became red and aflame, and he ate with holiness.

title.en: The storekeeper's fiery kiddush

retelling.en: One of the great tzaddikim, when young and still unknown, kept a store where women came to buy flour, sugar and candles for Shabbos. His rich neighbor, who sat and learned all week, was annoyed that the storekeeper dealt with women all week, yet every Friday night he heard the storekeeper's kiddush blaze while his own was ordinary. He asked him why, and the storekeeper answered that when he sold…

title.en: Reb Nissan Pilchik after melaveh malkah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he knew a Jew who davened in the Stoliner beis medrash, Reb Nissan Pilchik, who went from house to house every day selling goods to women, yet on Shabbos he blazed. One short summer Shabbos he sat with a group at melaveh malkah until the sky was already light. On his way home he met another Jew who had just woken to go learn, and he called out to him to rejoice, because in six…

title.en: The Chida and the Rebbe Reb Elimelech in heaven

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: The Chida's many sefarim were accepted in heaven and are learned to this day, yet when the Rebbe Reb Elimelech's name was mentioned there was a far greater stir in heaven. When they met in heaven, the Chida asked him why. The Rebbe Reb Elimelech answered that his kitchen was busy all week cooking for the chassidim who came to him, and the women there sometimes quarreled; but on erev Shabbos they…

title.en: The taste of a Friday night gathering seventy years later

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a young man there was a Friday night gathering in a shul, with stories of tzaddikim and singing of zemiros, and he looked forward to it greatly. Seventy years later, he says, the taste of that gathering still stays with him.

title.en: Shammai's week of eating for Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Shammai haZaken went out on Sunday morning and bought a good, fat animal for Shabbos. On Monday he found a better one, ate the first with friends, and set the better one aside for Shabbos, and so on through the week. The Mashgiach concludes that Shammai lived the entire week in honor of Shabbos.

title.en: Rav Aharon Kotler and the second steering wheel

retelling.en: Rav Aharon Kotler was given a ride and sat in the front seat, where he noticed a second steering wheel in front of him and asked the driver about it. The driver explained that his little boy loves to drive, so a mechanic installed a wheel at the boy's seat; the boy turns it and, seeing the car turn, thinks he is driving. Rav Aharon said that so it is with people who turn the wheel and think they…

title.en: The Stoliner and the Blazhever Rav's laining

retelling.en: The Blazhever Rav and the Stoliner, Reb Yisroel, were together for a Shabbos in the Blazhever's shul. The Blazhever lained from the Sefer Torah, and the Stoliner could hear in it all the thoughts and kabbalistic intentions he had in mind. Afterwards the Blazhever asked the Stoliner to daven Musaf, but the Stoliner gave him a pat on the shoulder and said the Blazhever Rav should daven. He later ex…

title.en: Reb Dovid'l Biderman and the spoiled cholent

retelling.en: Reb Dovid'l Biderman of Yerushalayim used to spend Shabbos in Meron with his chassidim. One summer Shabbos the fire under the cholent went out, and in the heat the cholent spoiled and gave off a bad smell when the lid was lifted, so no one could eat it. Reb Dovid'l asked for the pot and ate as much of it as he could, saying that one may not disgrace food of Shabbos, because Shabbos food is holy.…

title.en: Rebbe Elimelech's melave malka

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that Rebbe Elimelech did not eat a full meal at melave malka but used to drink tea. Once the King came to his melave malka and the Rebbe addressed him as 'Adoni HaMelech'. Rebbe Elimelech instructed his children to be careful about melave malka.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mother

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the mother of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was speaking on Shabbos, and he told her, 'Mother, today is Shabbos.' The Mashgiach brings it to show that idle talk does not fit Shabbos.

title.en: The Rebbe of Rimanov's one push

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that Rabbi Tzvi of Rimanov said he had never bothered a Jew except once. He once saw a Jew chatting during shalosh seudos and gave him a push, and he said he did not regret it, because shalosh seudos is not a time for chatting or foolish talk but a holy time.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's kiddush

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he lived on the same block as the Satmar Rav and went every Friday night to hear his kiddush. When the Satmar Rav said Vayechulu, it was as if the whole beis medrash, the lights, the door and the handle, testified that Hashem created the world in six days. He also went to hear him read Bereishis and the Aseres HaDibros from the Torah, and it seemed the walls believed; t…

title.en: Tzaddikim in Williamsburg after the war

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that after the war many great tzaddikim who survived gathered in Williamsburg: the Satmar Rav, the Klausenburger Rav, the Skverer Rebbe, Rabbi Yonasan Steif, the Vizhnitzer Rebbe Chaim Meir and others. He says there had never been so many tzaddikim in one place, and then one could hear a real kiddush.

title.en: Come to me before kiddush

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik to whom Jews came in a time of great trouble needing a yeshuah. He told them to come to him before kiddush, because according to the Gemara one who says Vayechulu becomes a partner with Hashem in creation, and as a partner he could act and be heeded in heaven.

title.en: Reb Dovid'l of Tolna takes leave of the train

retelling.en: As a boy, Reb Dovid'l of Tolna was a lively child like all boys, and he used to ride on a train, the way one rides a horse. When he became bar mitzvah, he went over to the train and took leave of it. The Mashgiach explains that he no longer had any connection to it: with his bar mitzvah he entered a new period.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's son at thirteen

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, from the Zohar, that on the night the son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai turned thirteen, his father married him to the daughter of another sage. He did so so that, having become a chassan, the boy would be a chassan on all sides: to his bride and to the other kallah, the Torah.

title.en: The father of Elisha ben Avuya at his son's bris

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts from Chazal that at the bris of Elisha ben Avuya, his father decided to have him learn Torah. He did so not for its own sake but because he saw the honor given to the Tannaim and wanted his son to have such honor too.

title.en: A tzaddik too busy in Nissan to answer

retelling.en: Someone wrote to a tzaddik and asked him a question. The tzaddik answered that it was hard for him to take time off to answer, because it was Nissan, and one hour in Nissan is worth as much as a whole day at any other time of the year.

title.en: Dina's daughter becomes Osnas

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, citing Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, Targum Yonasan and Da'as Zekeinim, that Dina gave birth to a daughter from Shechem. The brothers were unhappy with the child and wanted to kill her, so Yaakov carried her away, placed her in a small thornbush and hung a necklace on her neck saying that its bearer was a child of Yaakov. Angels carried her to Mitzrayim, where she was adopted by…

title.en: The sage who appeared without shoes

retelling.en: A great sage of a few hundred years ago, Reb Yitzchak Chayes, who wrote a commentary on the Mishnah, appeared to his son in a dream, as the son writes in his introduction. He wore a wonderful garment and a crown, but was barefoot. He explained that above they found he had done all the mitzvos, which made his garment, except that he had never gone around town collecting tzedakah for the poor, so h…

title.en: The Vilna Gaon reads it backwards

retelling.en: Someone always spoke of the greatness of his rebbe, the Gaon. Asked why his rebbe was greater than he, he answered that his rebbe could read it backwards: everyone can say Ashrei, but not everyone knows it backwards, while to the Gaon it was as clear as reading from a siddur in front of him.

title.en: The Beis Yosef at the Arizal's shiurim

retelling.en: The Beis Yosef, author of the Shulchan Aruch, was related by marriage to the Arizal and wanted to hear from him the profound secrets of the Torah. Whenever he came to the Arizal's shiurim he fell asleep, and the Arizal told him it was of no use and he should not come. The Mashgiach explains that the Beis Yosef was very great, and even received sod from a malach as recorded in Maggid Meisharim, bu…

title.en: The lion, the donkey and the fox

retelling.en: In the Midrash, a lion walked with his ministers and came to a log bridge where a donkey collected the toll. The donkey insisted the king pay too, so the lion tore him apart and told the fox to prepare a meal from him. The fox ate the heart, and when the lion asked where it was, the fox answered that a donkey who spoke such chutzpah to the king could not have had a heart. The Midrash ends with 'k…

title.en: The two mixed-up children

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he saw in a sefer, though he cannot promise it is true, that a Jewish child and a non-Jewish child were once mixed up. A sage was asked what to do, and he said to send both to cheder and see, when they begin learning Gemara, which child shakes. The one who shakes is the Jew.

title.en: The professor of philosophy who came to discuss Tanya

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he once had a very brilliant student who became a professor of philosophy at a university. He came with a colleague to discuss the Tanya, which they found to be a work of philosophical depth, but, the Mashgiach says, they had no taste for its flavor.

title.en: The visitor at the symphony

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who had just come from Africa and was taken to Carnegie Hall to hear a wonderful symphony. Asked which part he enjoyed most, he picked the noises the musicians made while tuning their violins before the symphony began.

title.en: The Satmar Rav at his Shabbos tish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says that about fifty years earlier he used to go to the Satmar Rav's tish on Friday night and saw how he enjoyed every fiber of Shabbos. When he made Kiddush his face became red and flaming. When the fish was served he ate it with great delight, yet he was above physicality and did not care for its taste; he felt the Shabbos in the fish.

title.en: Give me Shabbos for the challos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a Jew who struggled the whole week without a livelihood and fasted Monday and Thursday, partly because he had nothing to eat. He scraped together a little money and bought challos and fish for Shabbos. Eating the challos he said: Ribono shel Olam, You gave me challos for Shabbos, please give me Shabbos for the challos; and he said the same over the fish.
