title.en: The Yismach Moshe and three generations saying Torah

retelling.en: The Yitav Lev relates that he once sat together with his grandfather, the Yismach Moshe, and his father. The Yismach Moshe asked that all of them say Torah: the grandfather, the son and the grandchildren. The Mashgiach connects this to the verse promising that Torah will not depart from the mouths of a man, his children and his grandchildren.

title.en: The Rebbe and the milk

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a well-known story of a Rebbe who was given milk while visiting a town. When he found out it was chalav akum, he put his fingers down his throat and brought it all up.

title.en: Adel and Fayvish the thief

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's daughter Adel said that Hashem was clever to choose the Jewish people. There was a man named Fayvish, a thief who committed many aveiros. He was caught and sentenced to death, and told he would be spared if he converted, but he refused and gave his life. Adel said that if even a Fayvish the thief is ready to give his life for Hashem, Hashem chose wisely.

title.en: Rebbe Chaim Meir of Vizhnitz blesses a Chanukah child

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he was told that Rebbe Chaim Meir of Vizhnitz once spoke to a child born on Chanukah. He said to him 'Elokim yechonecha beni', and wished him that he be a Chanukah child.

title.en: The Or HaChaim's dream of two dogs

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Or HaChaim HaKadosh, at the beginning of Parshas Vayechi, tells of a dream, which the Mashgiach says was a kind of prophecy, in which he encountered the sitra achra in the form of two dogs, a male and a female. He overpowered the male at once without extra effort, but had a very hard fight with the female and could not fully overcome her. The Mashgiach explains that…

title.en: The psychologist and the zipper

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he once spoke to a psychologist. The psychologist told him that if a person had a slit made in his stomach with a zipper, and every day food was put in that way, giving him all the nutrients he needs, after a while he would have a nervous breakdown. The Mashgiach explains that just as a person needs food and air, he needs a certain gratification for his health.

title.en: The professor and the word 'kordiakos'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a professor at a seminary who came to give an hour-long lecture in Talmud. They were learning a Gemara with the word for a certain malady of the heart, and he spent the whole hour explaining the word's Latin and Greek roots. When the hour was up he looked at his watch and said they had already learned for an hour.

title.en: Onkelos and his uncle

retelling.en: The Mashgiach cites Chazal about Onkelos, who wanted to learn Torah. In the exchange with his uncle, the Roman emperor, the point is made that one cannot learn Torah without circumcision. Torah does not enter an uncircumcised person; only after the bris can one merit Torah.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim's dream of two dogs

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Ohr HaChaim, in Parshas Vayechi, tells of a dream in which he confronted the Sitra Achra in the form of two dogs, a male and a female. He overcame the male very quickly. With the female he had a great struggle; he threw her down but could not nullify her completely, because in the Sitra Achra the female is stronger than the male.

title.en: The tzaddik and the apple on motzaei Shabbos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he saw in a sefer the day before about a great tzaddik who, every motzaei Shabbos, took an apple, cut it across its width and looked at it. Cut that way, an apple shows a star with ten points, which corresponds to the ten utterances of creation. Leaving the spiritual world of Shabbos for the physical weekday, he saw the ten utterances in a physical thing, and that gave hi…

title.en: The old man and the wine the goy touched

retelling.en: Tosafos brings a story of an old man, a wine merchant, who had a large barrel of wine he needed for his livelihood. A goy stuck his hand into the wine in order to make it forbidden and cause the Jew a loss. The old man took some of the wine and drank it, relying on the ruling that touching done only to cause damage does not make it yayin nesech. Tosafos adds that this old man was later killed.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya and the man with doubts

retelling.en: A man came to the Ba'al HaTanya and complained that he could not free himself from doubts in emunah, which gave him no rest. The Ba'al HaTanya told him that he had surely drunk chalav akum, which causes doubts in emunah because it goes to the root of the shedim.

title.en: Rav Moshe Feinstein and the cup of milk

retelling.en: Rav Moshe Feinstein once visited a talmid, who offered him a cup of milk. After tasting it he found out that the milk had no hechsher and asked why he was given it; the talmid answered that Rav Moshe himself had permitted it in the Igros Moshe. Rav Moshe answered that he had said one may be lenient, but he himself does not do so, and he went and made himself vomit up the milk. The Mashgiach notes…

title.en: The tzaddik who made a siyum every day

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of tzaddikim who were careful that all their eating be in holiness. One never ate a meal unless it was a seudas mitzvah, so he managed to complete a masechta every day and ate his meal as the meal of the siyum.

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the brain surgeons

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that there are people today who still remember that great professors, neurologists and neurosurgeons, used to consult the Chazon Ish on how to perform brain surgery. He mapped out for them exactly where to cut, and they listened to him. Asked how he knew all this, he said that he had learned it from the Torah.

title.en: The lion, the donkey and the fox

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash: the lion, king of the jungle, walked with his ministers and came to a log across a stream where the donkey collected the toll. The donkey insisted that even the king pay, and the furious lion tore him apart and told the fox to prepare a meal from him. The fox ate the heart himself, and when the king asked for it the fox answered that if the donkey had had a heart h…

title.en: The Maggid's snuffbox

retelling.en: A great tzaddik came to visit the Maggid with his child. While the Maggid stepped out, the child picked up the silver snuffbox on the table, looked at it and put it back. When the Maggid returned he asked who had touched it, and explained that when he puts something down he puts it where it is supposed to be, and it had been moved from its place.

title.en: The Maggid's hand behind his back

retelling.en: Once the Maggid kept his hand behind his back for a number of hours without moving it, though it was evidently painful. Asked why he did not relax it, he explained that he does not move a limb without a holy purpose, and he had not found a reason to move his hand forward.

title.en: The king who tested his son

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Zohar's parable of a king who wanted to test the purity of his son the prince, and hired a harlot to try to seduce him, to see whether he was strong enough to overcome his yetzer hara. The harlot was really in the king's service, and so too the yetzer hara is in the service of Hashem.

title.en: Eliyahu's zeal in the episode of Zimri

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls the episode of Zimri as the Gemara tells it: the tribe of Shimon wanted to kill the zealot, and even angels sought to harm him. He was nevertheless moser nefesh, ready to have his own blood spilled, for the holiness of the bris among Bnei Yisroel, and through it atoned for them. In the merit of this he became the angel of the bris.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe remembers Korach's dispute

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe said he remembered Matan Torah and near whom he stood there. His grandson asked whether he remembered the dispute of Korach and assumed he had sided with Moshe Rabbeinu; he answered that he was neutral. When the grandson wondered at this, he said that had the grandson been there, he would have sided with Korach, because Korach was a very great man, not a mischievous quarreler.

title.en: Why Czar Nicholas died a natural death

retelling.en: A great tzaddik, perhaps of Tchortkov or Sadigura (the Mashgiach is unsure), was brought the news that Czar Nicholas had died. He was asked why this tyrant, who decreed that Jewish children be seized for decades of army service, did not receive a visible punishment from Heaven. The tzaddik answered that some resha'im merit to sanctify Hashem's name through their downfall, but he was so wicked tha…

title.en: The Apter Rav and the matzah of the Seder

retelling.en: The Apter Rav used to eat a great deal. Once, at a feast with great tzaddikim, after everyone was full from the first course, a roasted goose was brought and he ate it all by himself. At the end of his life, when he was very sick and allowed only liquids, he took a piece of matzah on the Seder night as every year; his children warned that it was dangerous, and he answered that all year everything…

title.en: The drunkard who rewarded his sobriety

retelling.en: In the Slonimer Rebbe's mashal, a habitual drunkard firmly resolved to stop drinking. He went a whole day without a drink, then a second and a third. Proud of his heroism, he decided he deserved to treat himself to a glass of brandy, and that was the end of his heroism; he was a drunkard again.

title.en: The am ha'aretz and Rabbi Hoshaya

retelling.en: As the Midrash tells, an am ha'aretz asked Rabbi Hoshaya whether, if he told him a piece of Torah, he would say it in his name in the beis medrash. Rabbi Hoshaya agreed if it was suitable. The am ha'aretz said that the kings will return the gift to Moshiach: all the animals Yaakov sent to Esav will be returned. Rabbi Hoshaya called it a good piece of Torah and said it in his name, and it is still…

title.en: Reb Shmelke asks to be reminded of his dveikus

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Rebbe Reb Shmelke, a brother of the Hafla'ah, told his students that if they saw him lose his dveikus with Hashem while delving into a sugya, they should tap him on the shoulder to remind him. Once they tapped him, and he answered that he had not lost his dveikus.

title.en: The Lechovitcher Rebbe and the competing store

retelling.en: A Chassid complained to the Lechovitcher Rebbe that someone had opened a store across the street selling the same merchandise. The Rebbe asked him where his emunah and his love of Jews were, and told him to work on himself until the resentment left his heart. The Chassid returned and said that it no longer bothered him when customers went to the competitor. The Rebbe answered that this was not en…

title.en: The Arizal stands up for Rabbi Chaim Vital

retelling.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital writes that he once came in to his rebbe, the Arizal, who stood up for him. He asked why the rebbe was standing up for him. The Arizal answered that the soul of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was now with him, because he had come from the mitzvah of redeeming captives, a mitzvah Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair was involved in.

title.en: A Nittel night in a sefer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that an author recounted in his sefer that on a Nittel night someone sat down to learn and was not careful about the custom. A dog then came into the house, and the author saw from this that one must keep Jewish customs.

title.en: The Ruzhiner and the chassid who came to see him

retelling.en: A chassid felt a strong urge simply to see the Ruzhiner and traveled several days to reach him. As he entered the courtyard, the Rebbe called him over and asked whether he was fond of him, and the chassid answered that this was why he came. The Ruzhiner told him that his fondness bears no comparison to the Rebbe's love for his chassidim, and that this in turn bears no comparison to Hashem's love…

title.en: Rosh Hashanah of the war's outbreak

retelling.en: As a bochur the Mashgiach went with his father, who davened Shacharis for the amud on Rosh Hashanah, and helped him. The congregation wept, and after davening he asked his father why this year was different; his father answered that Hitler had invaded Poland, where they had many relatives. His friends at yeshivah whose wealthy parents owned a radio reported that England and France had declared wa…

title.en: The Vilna Gaon and Rav Chaim of Volozhin on Ki Seitzei

retelling.en: When the Gra lived, at the beginning of the century corresponding to Ki Seitzei, his talmid Rav Chaim of Volozhin asked him where the Gra himself is hinted in that sedra. The Gra answered with the words 'even shleimah', whose letters spell Eliyahu ben Shlomah, his own name. Rav Chaim then asked where he himself is hinted, and the Gra answered him, but Rav Chaim never wanted to reveal that answer…

title.en: The Jewish thief who refused to kiss the cross

people: Adel, daughter of the Ba'al Shem Tov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings, from the sefer of Rabbi Yaakov Yosef, a woman's saying that Klal Yisrael did not err in choosing Hashem, and Hashem knew what He was doing in choosing them; by tradition the woman was Adel, the daughter of the Ba'al Shem Tov. A Jewish thief stole from a church and was caught, and they told him they would burn him unless he converted. He had done every aveira one can think of…

title.en: The king's son and the ground-up stone

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, unsure of who said it, of a king's son who transgressed a law for which the punishment was to have a large stone dropped on him from a roof. The king, unable to change the law, had the stone ground into sand and thrown on him, so each grain did him no harm. The Mashgiach uses it to show that what comes little by little can be borne, but Hashem counts the sum total.

title.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin and the shtender

retelling.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin once said, while davening on Rosh Hashana, that everything is judged, even the shtender on which he was davening: whether it would stay whole or break. The Mashgiach returns to this later, explaining that if something breaks after Rosh Hashana, it is a sign that it was not found worthy in the judgment.

title.en: The guest from Miami at the tisch

retelling.en: On Shabbos Bereishis, a distinguished Jew from Miami, with whom the Mashgiach stays when he goes there, was present at the tisch. He was amazed to see the bachurim standing with awe, singing, and not talking to one another. The Mashgiach says he was so struck that he felt he was on another planet.

title.en: Rabbi Eliezer's last lesson

retelling.en: When Rabbi Eliezer the Great fell ill and was leaving the world, his students, Rabbi Akiva among them, came to visit and asked him to teach them the ways of life by which they would merit the World to Come. He told them to be careful with the honor of their friends. The Mashgiach notes that he did not tell them to learn with diligence, daven with fire or give tzedakah, though all are good, but ch…

title.en: Rachel pleads for her children

retelling.en: When the Jews served idols in the time of the Beis Hamikdash, the attribute of judgment was strong. Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov each pleaded for their children, and it did not help. Then Rachel came and told Hashem that Yaakov had worked seven years for her, and that when her father planned to give Leah in her place she gave Leah the signs Yaakov had given her, so that her sister would not be sh…

title.en: Shaul searching for the donkeys

retelling.en: When the donkeys of Kish, Shaul's father, were lost, Shaul went with his father's servant to look for them. After searching long he said they should turn back lest his father worry for 'us'. When he came to Shmuel the Navi to ask where the donkeys were, Shmuel anointed him king instead. The Mashgiach explains he merited this because he included the servant with himself.

title.en: Tamar and Yehudah

retelling.en: Tamar was brought to beis din and was to be thrown into the fire. She held the pledge Yehudah had given her, yet she did not say to him that she was pregnant from him. She only sent word that the owner of these items was the father, so that if Yehudah admitted it she would be saved, and if not she would be burned, but she would not shame him before others.

title.en: Shabbos for the challah

retelling.en: A great tzaddik was poor in his youth and scraped together a few pennies to buy challah and fish for Shabbos. When he sat down Friday night to eat his challah, he asked Hashem: You gave me challah for Shabbos, please give me Shabbos for the challah, and he said the same over the fish. The Mashgiach adds that he himself watched a wondrous tzaddik eat fish on Friday night with obvious enjoyment, ye…

title.en: The poritz's sugar and Nishmas on Shabbos

retelling.en: A chassid worked for a wealthy poritz at a time when sugar was very expensive in Russia. He came running excitedly to his Rebbe and told how the poritz had his workers carry thousands of sacks of sugar to cover a meadow and went sled riding on it in the middle of August. Then the chassid said: how does this compare with the pleasure I have on Shabbos when I say Nishmas kol chai, which the poritz…

title.en: Children born on the mountaintop

retelling.en: Someone who worked very hard to reach the level of a young prodigy from a distinguished family, whose father was Rav Avraham HaMalach, asked him how he reached it without struggle. The young man answered with a mashal: a man spent days climbing a very difficult mountain, and at the top he found small children playing. When he asked how they got there, they answered that they were born there.

title.en: Standing up for the soul of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair

retelling.en: A tzaddik stood up for a talmid and told him he was not standing for him but for the soul that had just come to him temporarily, and asked what he had done to merit it. It emerged that the talmid had done the mitzvah of pidyon shvuyim, redeeming captives. Since that was the mitzvah in which Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair excelled, his soul came as an ibbur to help him in that mitzvah.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's mashal of the dancing prisoner

retelling.en: A minister sinned against the king and was put in prison, and was told he would be judged on the king's coronation day, when the king makes a feast. On that day he began singing and dancing in his cell. The prison officer thought he had gone mad and asked why he was dancing when he might be hanged; he answered that today is the king's joy and he rejoices with his king. The officer told the king,…

title.en: Boaz did not invite Manoach

retelling.en: Boaz had sixty children and married them all off, but never invited his neighbor Manoach, who was childless at the time. The Mashgiach explains that Boaz meant it for the sake of Heaven, so that Manoach would feel it and daven harder. Still, Manoach was shamed, and Boaz lost all his children. Later Boaz had a son from Rus, from whom came the house of David, and Manoach was answered with a son, Sh…

title.en: The chol bird in the teivah

retelling.en: Noach was busy day and night feeding every creature in the teivah on its own schedule. Making his rounds, he found a bird called chol hidden in a corner and asked whether it had eaten. The bird answered that it saw how busy Noach was and did not want to trouble him. Noach blessed it that it should live forever.

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim and the Berditchever's grandsons

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from talmidim that two grandsons of the Berditchever Rav wanted to learn in the Chofetz Chaim's yeshivah in Radin, but the menahel turned them away for lack of room. They went in to the Chofetz Chaim, who heard who they were and had the menahel admit them. Asked why, he answered that Rosh Hashanah was coming and a meilitz yosher was needed, and since the Berditchever was a mei…

title.en: Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin refuses to sign the cherem

retelling.en: When the Vilna Gaon called for a cherem against the chassidim, it was passed among all his talmidim to sign, and only Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin refused. Asked how he could refuse when his Rebbe had ordered it, he answered from the akeidah: Hashem Himself told Avraham to bring Yitzchak, but sent an angel to tell him to stop. His Rebbe is holy and like an angel, he said, but to harm a Jew an angel is…

title.en: The search for a lost child this week

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that this week a child was lost and thousands of Jews, the masses of Boro Park and people who came from other places, went searching through the whole night until morning. Among the nations, he says, the FBI and the police search, but the people do not. The levayah was a great kiddush Hashem, and someone told the Mashgiach that a non-Jew said to him that the Jews are a wonderf…

title.en: The chassid's gesture on his deathbed

retelling.en: A chassid who all his life was careful not to do wrong lay on his deathbed. At his last moment he made the European gesture of a thumb between two fingers, as if to tell the yetzer hara that he had won. When the Chiddushei HaRim was told of it, he said that at that very last moment he lost the battle, since the struggle lasts until the last breath.

title.en: The young masmid of Koretz

retelling.en: A young married man in Koretz sat and learned all day. While his father-in-law was away, his mother-in-law and wife pressed him to earn a living; he answered that he had never caused anyone pain and would rather give a get than stop learning, and they went to the town rav for the divorce. As he rode back to the yeshiva immersed in learning, his returning father-in-law met him, brought him home an…

title.en: The camp minyan that became the shul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that he was rosh hamasmidim in Camp Torah Vodaath and organized young bachurim to daven in the morning a good, unhurried davening, and taught them how to daven slowly. They enjoyed it so much that when the camp season ended they asked him for such a minyan in the city, in Boro Park. A minyan was founded, it began with bachurim, and from those bachurim who wanted to daven well…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer and the long shemoneh esrei

retelling.en: A story is told that when the Chasam Sofer was a young bachur he used to daven long. A friend told him that in the time he davened shemoneh esrei, the friend davened shemoneh esrei and also learned a whole siman of Shulchan Aruch. The Chasam Sofer answered that the Gemara says one who lengthens his prayer is granted long days, so Hashem would give him long years in which to make up the siman the…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the business competitor

retelling.en: In Sanz a Jew had a business, and another Jew opened the very same business across the street. The first went to the Sanzer Rav, the Divrei Chaim, who called the competitor to a din Torah. The competitor claimed the first man was not a proper Jew and that it was a mitzvah to ruin him. The Sanzer Rav answered that when the Jews in Egypt lacked mitzvos Hashem gave them the blood of the Pesach and o…

title.en: The boy outside the Belzer Rav's window

retelling.en: A boy in Belz had strayed from the Jewish path and wanted neither to learn nor to daven. His father once took him to Belz for Rosh Hashana, and while everyone davened inside he stood outside with a few rough friends, chatting and laughing. Passing the window, he heard the Belzer Rav read the Rosh Hashana Torah reading with a cry, at Hagar's words that she did not want to see the child die. The cr…

title.en: Eretz Yisrael then and now

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when he first came to Eretz Yisrael everything was dust and sand. Since Jews began coming, the land has been cultivated, and every year he goes he sees it more developed than the year before.

title.en: What he heard from Rav Weissmandl

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says the study of equally spaced letters in the Torah was begun by Rav Michoel Ber Weissmandl before the computer was invented, and that he heard it from him directly. Rav Weissmandl showed how letters at fixed intervals from the start of a sefer spell out words, and said many marvelous things without any computer.

title.en: The tzaddik and his pocket watch

retelling.en: A great tzaddik, whose name the Mashgiach does not recall, took out his pocket watch in the middle of Shemoneh Esrei and played with it. Some onlookers frowned, but tzaddikim who saw it understood. He had reached such dveikus that without some contact with the physical his soul would have flown out of him, so he had to do something physical to keep it down.

title.en: Avraham, Sarah and the Akeidah

retelling.en: According to a sefer the Mashgiach cites, Avraham at the Akeidah reached such dveikus that his soul should have left him, but because he had said 'we will return' he was not 'zocheh' to have it surge out to Hashem. When Sarah heard that her son had been ready to give his life for Hashem, she was so charged with love of Hashem that her soul left her.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov at the shul door

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once came to a shul, stood by the door and said he could not go in. Asked why, he explained that the shul was packed with Torah and mitzvos done without love and fear, out of mere habit; such mitzvos do not fly up but stay below, filling the shul.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav visits the Ruzhiner

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells, as R' Shlomo Eliezer heard it through his family, that the Sanzer Rav went to visit the holy Ruzhiner, before whom even the older Sanzer Rav made himself small. Seated together, the Ruzhiner spoke of oxcarts going out from a town in Hungary, and the Sanzer Rav answered about the red uniforms of the Hungarian soldiers. Coming out, the Sanzer Rav said he had great siyata dishma…

title.en: Answering an objector with a baseball game

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that a man complained to him about loud davening, asking why one cannot daven quietly. The Mashgiach answered him that at a professional baseball game, when the batter hits a home run, the whole crowd screams. When we come before Ribono shel Olam in davening, he said, that is our home run, and so we shout.

title.en: R' Aharon of Karlin before the beis din

retelling.en: R' Aharon of Karlin, a talmid of the Maggid, lived in Karlin and had a minyan that davened loudly, which angered people. A beis din summoned him; its head was a great talmid chacham and a misnaged. R' Aharon came in and greeted him familiarly as 'Avrahaml', which angered him.

title.en: Reb Aharon Roth visits the Vizhnitzer Rebbe

retelling.en: Reb Aharon Roth traveled from Yerushalayim to Vizhnitz, to Reb Yisroel of Vizhnitz. He said afterwards that the Rebbe was an awesome tzaddik with a virtue no other tzaddik had: he had worked the trait of jealousy out of himself and was not jealous at all. The Mashgiach calls it a wondrous thing for a person not to be jealous.

title.en: The silver spoon

retelling.en: A poor man came to the Chernobyler for tzedakah and received a generous gift, and on his way out he took a silver spoon from the table. The household noticed, ran after him, found the spoon, and were about to beat him, when he claimed the Rebbe had given it to him. They brought him to the Rebbe, who said he had indeed given him the spoon, so as not to shame him. The poor man then demanded payment…

title.en: The Berditchever and the matzah bakers

retelling.en: When the Kedushas Levi became Rav of Berditchev, the communal leaders asked for takanos in the matzah bakery because the women worked slowly. He gathered the bakers and told them that the goyim say Jews put blood in matzos, and he asked them not to put blood in the matzos: the blood of the widows who work hard all day and are rushed. A Jew should not eat matzos for which the widows' blood was spi…

title.en: Reb Mordechai Banet's six months in Lichtenstadt

retelling.en: Reb Mordechai Banet, the Rav of Nikolsburg, died while away in Karlsbad and was buried in nearby Lichtenstadt. The people of Nikolsburg demanded that he be brought to their city, and the question went to the Chasam Sofer, who wrote that he should be moved but ended that the matter was not yet clear to him. Six months later he sent word to move him. The secret was that Reb Mordechai Banet came to…

title.en: The young ilui and the visiting rav

retelling.en: Reb Shlomo Bloch, a talmid of the Chofetz Chaim, told of a seventeen-year-old ilui in the yeshiva who later became one of the gedolei hador, whose name is not told. When a distinguished rav came to town and gave a pilpul in public, the ilui asked a strong question that toppled it, refused the rav's answer, and a heated debate followed. When the rav would not concede, the ilui told him he could le…

title.en: Reb Hershele Rimanover and the mezuzah

retelling.en: Reb Hershele, a tailor's son who learned Torah with great strength, came to Reb Mendel of Rimanov and became his shamash; once he made the Rebbe's bed in place of the gabbai, and the Rebbe felt such kedushah that he told him to make it every night, and Reb Hershele later became his successor. When he came to the city of the Yeshuos Yaakov, who did not want to honor him, the Yeshuos Yaakov had all…

title.en: A Rebbe who no longer knew the taste of food

retelling.en: To show that tzaddikim reached a level where nothing else had place in their heart, the Mashgiach says he knew such people in his own generation. One Rebbe once said that for twenty years he had not known the taste of food; he was in a different world.

title.en: Two Rebbes recall the wartime transports

retelling.en: Two Rebbes sat together, with chassidim standing around, recalling what they went through in the camps during the war. One told how they were transported in a wagon packed like herring in great heat, many near death from thirst, and at a certain station they were allowed down to drink at a fountain. He drank three glasses of water and spoke about the intention of each drink.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe and the dishwater

retelling.en: Once the wife of the Yismach Moshe had to go to a simcha and asked him to take supper himself; she left a pot of meat and a pot of soup on the stove. When she returned, the soup was untouched though he said he had taken it. She found that on the same stove stood a pot of dirty dishwater with suds, and he had eaten that, not knowing the difference.

title.en: The Lechovitcher no longer feels his Rebbe

retelling.en: Reb Mordechai of Lechovitch was a talmid of Reb Shlomo of Karlin. When Reb Shlomo passed away, people were afraid to tell the Lechovitcher. He began crying out that he did not feel the Rebbe, until they had to tell him the Rebbe had died. Then he calmed down, saying he now understood why he no longer felt him.

title.en: The fox and the grapes

retelling.en: In Ben Sira's fables, which the gentiles later took over as Aesop's fables, a fox came to a vineyard and saw beautiful grapes, but there was a high fence. For three days and three nights he struggled to climb over it. In the end he said the grapes were sour.

title.en: The melamed who wanted psychology books

retelling.en: A successful melamed came asking to learn books of psychology so he would understand a child's way of thinking and become a better melamed. He was answered: why not learn Chumash and Rashi? Everything can be learned from the Torah.

title.en: The atheist and the banana peel

retelling.en: A man climbing a staircase slipped on a banana peel at the top and tumbled down the stairs, crying out 'Oh G-d!'. He was asked why he was calling out to G-d.

title.en: The Six Day War and the woman's letter

retelling.en: Before the Six Day War the Jews in Eretz Yisroel faced terrible danger: a small army surrounded by huge Arab forces that vowed to push them into the sea, and newspapers wrote it was the end of Israel. In six days the Jews won wondrously, and for months even secular papers reported miracles, such as a bomb setting a house on fire and a second bomb bursting the water tank on the roof, which put out…

title.en: Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz's long davening

retelling.en: In a letter to a student, Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz wrote that he was still in the middle of davening when the tzibbur had already said kedushah and finished. Young people made jokes about him and laughed. He wrote that this was his portion from all his toil, the time he stands before Hashem in tefillah.

title.en: The Bnei Dan left outside the clouds

retelling.en: When the pillar of cloud moved, most of the Jews packed quickly and hurried after Moshe Rabbeinu. The Bnei Dan took their time packing their bags and tents, and the clouds did not wait for them. They remained outside the clouds of glory, and Amalek attacked those stragglers.

title.en: The Chiddushei HaRim and the late soul

retelling.en: Souls used to come to the Chiddushei HaRim on erev Shabbos for a tikkun, and people heard him speaking without seeing anyone there. Once he was heard saying to a soul that he could do nothing for it, because the Rebbetzin had already lit candles. The Mashgiach explains that rectifying a soul is a kind of separating bad from good, which is not done on Shabbos.

title.en: The bachur who exposed a borrowed chiddush

retelling.en: In Slabodka a brilliant bachur disappeared from the yeshiva for a whole day, and the mashgiach pressed him until he told why. A fellow bachur he envied had said a chiddush at a chaburah, and he knew it came from a sefer that the yeshiva did not have. He traveled to Vilna, bought ten or fifteen copies, brought them to the yeshiva and laid one, open to the chiddush, on the other bachur's shtender,…

title.en: The soul that came to Reb Moshe of Savran

retelling.en: Reb Moshe of Savran, a great tzaddik and a friend of the Ruzhiner, told that a soul came to him for a tikkun because it was not let into Gan Eden. The man had been a talmid chacham who confessed his sins and did teshuvah before he died, but he forgot one thing: a chassan once sat next to him in shul, brought by his father-in-law, and he corrected a word the chassan said wrongly, shaming him befor…

title.en: Reb Shraga Feivel and the old man in shul

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, told that he once sat in shul on Friday night next to an older man who said a word in the bracha of Hashkiveinu wrongly. After davening he quietly showed him how it is written in the siddur. The man became angry, saying he had been saying it that way for sixty years.

title.en: Reb Akiva Eiger and the Rav of Lissa

retelling.en: Reb Yaakov of Lissa, author of the Nesivos HaMishpat, came to Posen, where Reb Akiva Eiger was Rav. The Rav of the town was called up for shlishi and the Rav of Lissa received a different aliyah. After davening Reb Akiva Eiger went over and asked him not to hold it against him: although he could learn much more from the Rav of Lissa, the honor went to him only because Posen is a bigger city. The…

title.en: Reb Akiva Eiger as a young chassan

retelling.en: As a young illui, Reb Akiva Eiger was taken as a chassan by a wealthy man who gave a large dowry and expected a great pilpul. All Shabbos he said only simple words on the sedra, and afterwards the father-in-law wanted to break the shidduch. Reb Akiva Eiger asked to stay seven more days, and the next Shabbos he said a wondrous pilpul that amazed the lomdim. He explained that another wealthy man in…

title.en: The wine spilled at the Seder

retelling.en: At Reb Akiva Eiger's Seder a poor guest accidentally spilled wine on the beautiful white tablecloth and was surely embarrassed. Reb Akiva Eiger pretended not to notice, and a few minutes later he lifted his own cup and spilled it, saying the table was shaking. He did it on purpose so the guest would not feel bad.

title.en: The kashya of Reb Mordechai Benet

retelling.en: Reb Akiva Eiger spent a Shabbos in Nikolsburg, where Reb Mordechai Benet, a great illui, was Rav, and gave a derashah. In the middle Reb Mordechai Benet asked a strong kashya on the pilpul, and Reb Akiva Eiger said it was a kashya. The next day, escorting him on his way home, Reb Akiva Eiger told him the answer, explaining that saying it in public would have made the Rav of Nikolsburg look small…

title.en: Reb Yisrael Salanter leaves a yeshiva

retelling.en: Reb Yisrael Salanter was given a position in a yeshiva together with another great talmid chacham, each saying the shiur on alternate days. When he noticed that the bachurim liked his shiur more than the other one, he left the yeshiva so that the other would not be pained.

title.en: The shoemaker's wedding in Vilna

retelling.en: In Vilna there was a lavish wedding hall where only the very rich made weddings. A poor shoemaker who had become wealthy made his daughter's wedding there, and the established rich men were displeased. As he walked his child to the chuppah, one of them came over, took off his shoe and asked him how much it would cost to put on a new heel, shaming him. When Reb Yisrael Salanter heard the story, he…

title.en: The five-hour seudah and the tired maid

retelling.en: A wealthy talmid chacham asked Reb Yisrael Salanter to eat the Shabbos meal at his home, and described it: glatt kosher meat from the best shochet, a G-d-fearing maid supervised by his wife, and a meal of courses, zemiros and divrei Torah lasting late into the night. Reb Yisrael Salanter agreed on condition that the whole meal last no more than two hours. After bentching he called in the maid and…

title.en: The Bach and the fire of Gehinnom

retelling.en: When the Bach passed away, his deeds were examined and no sin was found, so he was to go straight to Gan Eden. A malach then complained: while walking, steeped in his learning, the Bach sneezed, and two animals of kilayim, an ox and a horse harnessed together, startled and gave the wagon a slight push. For this he had to pass momentarily through Gehinnom, so that even this tiny blemish would not…

title.en: A night in the Vienna jail

retelling.en: A Rebbe was held one night in a jail in Vienna. A Jew was brought in who had married a non-Jewish woman about twenty-five years earlier; he spent the whole night beating against the wall and crying out, and the Rebbe went over to strengthen him. The Rebbe was freed the next morning and did not understand why he had to spend that night in jail. Years later in America the Jew came to him with his s…

title.en: The Lechovitcher feels his Rebbe's passing

retelling.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin had great disciples, among them Rabbi Mordechai of Lechovitch, Rabbi Asher of Stolin and the Rebbe of Strelisk. When Rabbi Shlomo was killed by a goy, people were afraid and did not tell the Lechovitcher. He began crying out that he no longer felt his Rebbe and that he must have been cut off from him. Only when they had to tell him that the Rebbe had passed away did he calm…

title.en: The fox and the sour grapes

retelling.en: A fox came to a vineyard and saw beautiful grapes that he wanted to eat, but a high fence stood in the way. For three days and three nights he struggled to climb over it and could not. At the end he turned away and said that the grapes were sour. The Mashgiach brings it as one of Ben Sira's fables, later known among the nations as Aesop's fables.

title.en: The melamed and the Chazon Ish

retelling.en: A successful melamed came to the Chazon Ish and asked whether to study books of psychology, so that he would understand a child's way of thinking and be a better melamed. The Chazon Ish told him it was not needed: one who learns Chumash and Rashi properly can learn everything from the Torah.

title.en: The bomb and the water tank

retelling.en: During the Six Day War a fire bomb fell on a Jewish house, the house caught fire and the people could not get out. Seconds later a second bomb fell and burst the large water tank on the roof, and the water put out the fire. The Mashgiach says many such miracles happened, and every Jew had his own miracles to tell.

title.en: The letter about the beach on Shabbos

retelling.en: After the war the newspapers wrote about the miracles for months. A woman wrote a letter to a newspaper asking it to stop, because on Shabbos she drives to the beach to swim, and while the papers write about miracles she cannot do it. The Mashgiach says she did not want to hear of the miracles because of her desire to go to the beach.

title.en: The slap that cost a place in the minyan

retelling.en: The Chiddushei HaRim usually davened alone, and on his yahrzeit he asked the gabbai to arrange a small minyan of about ten. A chassid who was not invited insisted on coming in, slapped the man in his way, and entered. When the Rebbe asked where the minyan was, the gabbai said there were ten; the Rebbe answered that Choshen Mishpat says one who slaps another Jew is in cherem and is not counted for…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim and the tallis and shtreimel

retelling.en: A poor man asked the Divrei Chaim for money for a tallis and shtreimel for his daughter's chassan, and received it. The Divrei Chaim's son-in-law said he had seen the man buy a tallis and shtreimel the day before, and the man stood there ashamed. The Divrei Chaim told his son-in-law to ask forgiveness, saying the man may still need money for his wife's clothing for the chuppah, and told the man n…

title.en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan keeps a secret

retelling.en: Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan went with an askan to the wealthy men of the city to raise several hundred rubles each for a once-rich man who had lost everything and needed to restart his business. One wealthy man offered twenty-five, then fifty, then a hundred rubles if only he were told who it was; Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan refused, so the man would not be shamed. As they left, the wealthy man called hi…

title.en: The Dukla Rav and the kerosene cholent

retelling.en: Rabbi Avigdor Halberstam, the Dukla Rav and the Divrei Chaim's brother, spent a Shabbos at a wealthy man's home, where the custom was for the head of the house to serve the cholent. To honor him, the host set the pot before the Dukla Rav, who tasted it and ate the entire pot, leaving none for anyone. When his gabbai asked why, he said it smelled of kerosene: the maid had mistakenly poured kerosen…

title.en: The yarmulke on the windowsill in Kelm

retelling.en: Rabbi Yaakov Kamenetsky, a talmid in Kelm, told that a yarmulke someone forgot was found on a windowsill. He left the yeshiva for a rabbinical post, and when he came back a few months later to visit the rosh yeshiva, the yarmulke still lay there: no one had touched what belonged to another.

title.en: Rabbi Shmuel Salant and the cat

retelling.en: While Rabbi Shmuel Salant was giving a shiur, a simple woman came in: a cat had eaten meat she had left to salt, and she asked what the din was with the cat. The students wanted to laugh, but he silenced them with a stern look, took a sefer from the bookcase, looked into it, and ruled that the cat is treif, warning her not to leave meat where a cat can reach it. Afterwards he told his talmidim th…

title.en: The baal tokea who thought he was better

retelling.en: In Rabbi Shmuel Salant's beis medrash an old baal tokea grew weak, but rather than tell him to stop, they prepared a young substitute. The old man made the brachah and could not blow, so the young man took over and blew well, until he too got stuck in the middle; with great difficulty they finished the tekios. After davening Rabbi Shmuel told him that while blowing he had thought that he could bl…

title.en: Rabbi Yisrael Salanter and the wagon driver

retelling.en: Rabbi Yosef Yoizel, a talmid chacham who had become a wealthy merchant, visited Rabbi Yisrael Salanter and was moved by his mussar. On a second visit, in the middle of a warm conversation, Rabbi Yisrael asked him to stay a few days; when he said a wagon driver was already waiting for him, Rabbi Yisrael told him to run, lest the driver look for him, be distressed, and lose another customer. Seeing…

title.en: Rabbi Elya Lopian and Eliyahu HaNavi

retelling.en: When Rabbi Elya Lopian was a young man his wife fell gravely ill and the doctor said there was no hope. Broken, he went outside, where a Jew asked what was wrong, came in, said it was nothing, and showed him a plant whose leaves should be cooked and given to her to drink. When he gave her the drink the Jew vanished, and she opened her eyes, asked for water and recovered fully; he understood it wa…

title.en: The Chofetz Chaim, the thief and the chutzpadik bachur

retelling.en: Rabbi Elya Lopian heard from Rabbi Hirsch Levinson, the Chofetz Chaim's son-in-law and the administrator of the Radin yeshiva, that a bachur was caught stealing. Asked whether to expel him, the Chofetz Chaim said to let him stay, as he would yet become a rav, and he later became a rav in America. A few weeks later a woman complained that a bachur had spoken to her with chutzpah, and the Chofetz C…

title.en: The chassid and the soldier with frozen ears

retelling.en: A chassid came to the Ba'al HaTanya after not having been there for some years and asked for something to stir his fear and love of Hashem in davening. The Rebbe asked what had kept him going until then. He said that he did business with the Russian government and once, visiting the barracks, saw a soldier being flogged for coming back from night guard duty in the cold Russian winter with frozen…

title.en: Praying at Shimon HaTzaddik in wartime

retelling.en: Rav Yehoshua Leib Diskin used to send people to Shimon HaTzaddik's resting place to pray. During a war, when the situation was very tense and the Arabs had risen up, a Rebbe instructed that people go and pray at Shimon HaTzaddik. When asked whether perhaps the Kosel would do, he agreed the Kosel too, but he specifically sent them to Shimon HaTzaddik.

title.en: The Satmar Rav detains a businessman

retelling.en: A wealthy Jew named Reb Avraham, a brother of Reb Dovid, had a shop on Jaffa Street. He came to greet the Satmar Rav, who kept him talking for two hours, from ten until twelve, while he sat on pins and needles because he needed to open his shop. When he finally ran to the shop, he was told that men had been waiting there from ten to twelve, and when he did not come they left. He said he now under…

title.en: The Satan's threat to the Ba'al Shem Tov

retelling.en: When the Ba'al Shem Tov wanted to send his talmidim to Germany, the Satan said he would not let Chassidus enter Germany and would wage war against him. The Ba'al Shem Tov answered that he was not afraid of that war. The Satan then said that if so, he would make chassidim of his own; this frightened the Ba'al Shem Tov, and he did not send his talmidim to Germany.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and 'my rebbe is the greatest'

retelling.en: The Sanzer Rav once heard someone say that his rebbe was the greatest and the others were worthless. He reacted that one may not speak that way. A Jew may say that his own rebbe is good for him, but not that the others are worth nothing.

title.en: The Yesod HaAvodah and the grass of the moon

retelling.en: The Yesod HaAvodah met in the street a chassid who had stopped coming to him, and asked him why, telling him to say the truth and not politics. The chassid answered that he goes to Reb Aharon of Karlin, a greater rebbe. The Yesod HaAvodah agreed that the Beis Aharon was greater, but explained with the angel that strikes every blade of grass and the crops of sun and moon: grass that grows by the m…

title.en: The frum head of the Atomic Energy Commission

retelling.en: About forty years earlier, after America developed the atomic bomb that ended the war in Japan, the government set up a Federal Atomic Energy Commission staffed by many scientists. Its head was a frum Jew, and the Mashgiach's yeshiva invited him to speak. He came from Washington, arrived early and sat learning in the beis medrash until it was time for his talk. In his derashah he took apart the c…

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin and the informer

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings, via the Imrei Emes from the Chiddushei HaRim, that an informer was causing great suffering to the Jews of a town by reporting them to the Czar's government. They brought a kvittel with his name to the Chozeh of Lublin, asking him to curse the man. The Chozeh looked at it and said this man's soul was now shining in all the worlds, and he could not curse him. The next day they…

title.en: Two babies mixed up at birth

retelling.en: The Mashgiach says he heard that two children, one Jewish and one not, were once mixed up at birth and no one could tell which was which. They asked a Rav, who said to teach both of them Torah until they began learning Gemara. The child who swayed while learning would be the Jew, and the one who sat rigidly would be the non-Jew.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim and the two dogs

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings that the Ohr HaChaim, on a passuk in Parshas Vayishlach, tells how he was confronted, somewhat like Yaakov Avinu, by the sitra achra in the form of two dogs, a male and a female. He overpowered the male quickly and threw him down, but with the female he had a terrible struggle and subdued her only partially. The Mashgiach explains this is because in the sitra achra the female…

title.en: The son who said 'me'

retelling.en: A great tzaddik sent his son to learn avodas Hashem by a greater tzaddik. After a year or two the son returned and knocked on the door. His father asked who it was, and the son answered 'me'. The father said that if he can still say 'me', he has learned nothing there, since by a real tzaddik the 'me' does not exist.

title.en: The Satmar Rav on the Kasztner train

retelling.en: Money from America let the Zionist leader Kasztner arrange, through a Nazi official, a train to take leading Zionists out of Hungary. Satmar chassidim offered him much money to save the Satmar Rav, but he refused. His late mother came to him in a dream and warned that if he saved the Satmar Rav the whole train would succeed, and if not the Germans would catch it. The Satmar Rav at first refused t…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe and the eviction case

retelling.en: A Stoliner chassid, a singer, rented an apartment near the Stoliner shul in Williamsburg on condition that he put out the garbage cans. Once he left the garbage over Pesach, and the landlady, who could charge a new tenant more under rent control, sued to evict him. The Stoliner Rebbe told him the trial would be postponed, and it was, again and again, until the last possible date, set as the first…

title.en: The Atzei Chaim and the young man's thoughts

retelling.en: A young man came to the Atzei Chaim, whom the Mashgiach calls the brother of the Satmar Rebbe, and complained that he could not drive away his stray thoughts. The Rebbe paced back and forth for some time. Then he said he had thought the matter through, and there was no other way than to put one's head entirely into it; that is how one rises.

title.en: The tzaddik who lit candles late

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a great tzaddik, whom he thinks was Rabbi Shmelke though he is not sure. Something happened and the tzaddik lit the Shabbos candles somewhat late, and he asked his students whether it had been on time. Each wanted to please him and said it was still light, but one, a man of truth, told him it had been a little after the time.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the old bekishe

retelling.en: A man wanted a new bekishe for Yom Tov but did not want to spend much, so he bought cheap old cloth that had been lying in the store and had a tailor sew it. When he came to the Sanzer Rav for Yom Tov, people tugged at the fine new bekishe and it tore into holes, and he began to shout. The Sanzer Rav asked what happened, and the man said he had bought old merchandise; the Sanzer Rav remarked that…

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the hasty chazzan

retelling.en: Someone went up to the amud and began Hodu. The Sanzer Rav came over to him and led him away from the amud. He said that a chazzan has to lift the tzibbur, and this is not how one lifts the tzibbur.

title.en: The heretic named Eliezer

retelling.en: A Jew became a heretic, but in the end he did teshuvah. It was said that what helped him merit teshuvah was his name, Eliezer, which means that Hashem is the helper, as in the verse of the G-d of my father being my help. His name caused his return.

title.en: Rav Yosef Chaim and the Kosel question

retelling.en: On Yom Tov, Jews from the New City would come to the Old City and visit Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld. Once the Lubliner Rav, a great man, was sitting with him, and Rav Yosef Chaim asked every visitor whether he had already been at the Kosel. Asked later why, he explained that the guest might feel hurt that everyone came to greet Rav Yosef Chaim, so he wanted to show that people come for the Kosel a…

title.en: Back to the Old City

retelling.en: The Old City was crowded and airless, so Rav Yosef Chaim's doctors had him move to the New City, which was still mostly empty fields. A few weeks before his passing, weak, he insisted on moving back. He explained that he knew his end was near, and since burial is on Har HaZeisim beside the Old City, from the New City everyone would have to walk a long way.

title.en: The son of the baal musaf

retelling.en: The baal musaf for the Yamim Noraim died a few days before Rosh Hashanah, and the gabbaim asked Rav Yosef Chaim who should replace him; he said there was still time. At musaf he called the son of the deceased, who had a good voice, to the amud. Asked how a mourner could lead the davening, he said the widow, whose husband had led musaf for decades, would sit in the ezras nashim and suffer seeing a…

title.en: The only esrog in Radin

retelling.en: During the First World War no esrogim could reach Radin, but one man brought a single esrog for the Chofetz Chaim. On Sukkos morning everyone in town made the brachah on it. At Hallel the Chofetz Chaim did no na'anuim, and when asked why, he explained that everyone could fulfil the mitzvah of taking it, but in the middle of Hallel the others could not shake it, and he would not cause them pain.

title.en: The eruv in Teveria

retelling.en: Teveria had a Sefardi and an Ashkenazi kehillah; the Sefardi chacham oversaw the eruv, and the Ashkenazim had Rav Moshe Kliers. When the eruv broke, Rav Moshe Kliers was asked on Shabbos and said it was kosher. After Shabbos he learned the Gemara with the chacham, it became clear the eruv had been pasul, and the chacham was deeply distressed. Asked privately why he had said it was kosher, he answ…

title.en: Rav Chaim Ozer's summer apartment

retelling.en: Rav Chaim Ozer Grodzensky went away in the summer for his health, and the rebbetzin asked to take a spacious, airy apartment. He hesitated and first asked the servant, provided by the community, whether she was satisfied; she said the kitchen was far from the dining room but the apartment was worth it. Only then did he agree, since his concern had been not to trouble her.

title.en: Keeping the guest company in the sukkah

retelling.en: Rav Chaim Ozer was ill on Sukkos and lived several floors up, so he did not eat in the sukkah, being a mitztaer. A poor Jew came with nothing to eat, the rebbetzin invited him, and Rav Chaim Ozer told him to eat in the sukkah downstairs. In the middle of the meal Rav Chaim Ozer came down and sat with him. When the man protested, he said he was exempt from sukkah but not from hachnasas orchim, lik…

title.en: The woman whose parents were alive

retelling.en: A simple woman came to the Chofetz Chaim with a trouble and received a brachah. She then lamented that usually one who needs a yeshuah goes to the graves of his parents, but her parents were still alive and she could not. The talmidim laughed, and the Chofetz Chaim rebuked them sharply: a woman with a heavy heart comes with her troubles, and they laugh?

title.en: Rav Elchonon's single smile

retelling.en: Rav Elchonon Wasserman was never seen laughing or smiling, in line with Chazal's words about laughter in this world. Once, at a gathering of rabbonim, a foolish man came in and made a joke; no one laughed, but Rav Elchonon smiled, and that was the only time a smile was seen on his face.

title.en: Graf Potocki and the house of blocks

retelling.en: Graf Potocki, one of the greatest lords in Poland, became a Jew at a time when this was punishable by death. He was found and was to be thrown into the fire. The man charged with throwing him in sensed he stood before a holy man and asked him, by then called Avraham, whether he would take revenge on him in the world to come. He answered: of course not; when one child destroys another's house of b…

title.en: Reb Shmuel Munkes and the Alter Rebbe's arrest

retelling.en: When the Tsar's soldiers came to take the Alter Rebbe to prison, in the episode that ended with his release and Yud-Tes Kislev, he wanted to hide. The great chassid Reb Shmuel Munkes told him there was no use hiding, they would find him. The danger was real, the Mashgiach explains, because the opposing forces had concentrated against the Alter Rebbe, whose teaching was spreading too much for the…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim after the seder

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that the Divrei Chaim of Sanz, after the seder, with tears of joy, patted his stomach and called on it to rejoice. All the holy Names of the matzah, the maror, the charoses, korech and the four cups, he said, were now inside him.

title.en: The Satmar Rav: learn Tanya

retelling.en: The Mashgiach heard from the son of the Toldos Aharon Rebbe a teaching passed down in his family, based on the Noam Elimelech's Tzetel Katan, that whoever wants to serve Hashem can do so; he only needs to want it. The Satmar Rav was asked how one comes to want it, and he answered that one should learn Tanya.

title.en: The Czar's visit and the pennies

retelling.en: The Czar feared the Ba'al HaTanya was becoming like a king among the Jews and had him arrested. Having heard of his wisdom, he disguised himself as a simple soldier and visited him, and the Ba'al HaTanya made the blessing said on a king. The Czar asked how many pennies would be needed to make a pile from the table to the ceiling; he looked and gave a number. The Czar then had a penny put under ea…

title.en: The hidden pit

retelling.en: On the way to the judge, they dug a deep hole in the aisle and covered it with a fine carpet, so that the Ba'al HaTanya would fall in, be broken, and confess to rebellion. When he reached the spot he walked around it. The judge asked why he did not walk straight, and he said there was a hole there; the Mashgiach does not remember exactly how he answered how he knew, but he had understood it from…

title.en: Kiddush levanah on the boat

retelling.en: The prison stood in the middle of a river, and at night, while being taken across by boat, the Ba'al HaTanya asked the boatmen to stop so he could say kiddush levanah, which is said standing. They refused, and after he said something the boat stopped. He then told them that since they saw he could stop it, they should stop it themselves until he finished, and they did. The chassidim explained tha…

title.en: The judge's last question

retelling.en: The judge prepared twenty-four questions about the accusations, and the Ba'al HaTanya answered each with great wisdom. The last asked why he wrote in his sefer that a gentile's body comes from an impure source, unlike a Jew's, and instead of answering he smiled; the judge understood and moved on. The Ba'al HaTanya later explained that the judge, having heard twenty-three wise answers, should have…

title.en: Rosh hamasmidim in the summer camp

retelling.en: A summer camp had a regular division with sports and swimming and only an hour of learning morning and afternoon, and a masmidim division where good bachurim learned all day in a separate building. The Mashgiach was asked to become head of the masmidim and did not want to, but the Skverer Rebbe told him to accept, and he did. Looking for a place where one could daven properly, he went from beis m…

title.en: The minyan that became a beis medrash

retelling.en: Afterwards the bachurim asked the Mashgiach to daven this way all year. He feared the mockery of scoffers, but the Skverer Rebbe encouraged him to make a minyan, and it began in a store near the tracks, every Shabbos. People mocked them and called them names, but the bachurim paid no attention. As it grew they moved to ever larger places; a woman living in the building objected to enlarging the r…

title.en: How can one want to want?

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that someone asked the Satmar Rebbe how a person can come to want to want to be good. The Satmar Rebbe answered that for wanting one should learn the sefer Tanya, and by learning it one will want to be an ehrlicher Yid.

title.en: Avraham makes Eliezer swear

retelling.en: Avraham sent Eliezer to make the shidduch with Rivkah. Eliezer had hoped to become related to Avraham through the match, and Avraham had refused him. Since the yetzer hara might creep in and Eliezer might not carry out the mission properly, Avraham made him swear, and the oath gave him the strength his yetzer tov alone might have lacked.

title.en: The yiras Shamayim of Rav Shimon of Amshinov

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that he was often with Rav Shimon of Amshinov, a Jew of yiras Shamayim. He was afraid of every small thing, and took on all the Brisker stringencies.

title.en: Shabbos pleads for Adam HaRishon

retelling.en: Adam HaRishon was sentenced to be sent out of Gan Eden on Erev Shabbos in the afternoon. Shabbos came before Hashem and pleaded that Adam be allowed to stay over Shabbos, and he stayed. Later, after Kayin killed Hevel and did teshuvah, Adam learned of the power of teshuvah, and the Mashgiach says this is the power of Shabbos. Adam then sang Mizmor Shir L'yom HaShabbos, David HaMelech's song, with…

title.en: The poritz's mistake

retelling.en: A Jew in Europe could not pay his rent to the poritz, and the debt grew from year to year until the poritz threatened to drive him out. He went to a tzaddik, who told him the poritz would make a mistake. The poritz made a calculation, it came out the opposite way, and he ended up owing the Jew money and paying him. The Jew ran to the Rebbe, worried that the poritz might later discover the mistake…

title.en: Rabbi Dovid of Tolna and the roll

retelling.en: On Rosh Hashanah the chassidim waited for Rabbi Dovid of Tolna to come in for the shofar blowing, but he did not come. Listening at the door, they heard him pacing back and forth, saying that Hashem is great and awesome and he is asking Him for a roll. They understood he was ashamed to ask so great a King for livelihood, like asking a president for a cracker. Suddenly he grasped: from whom else s…

title.en: The Chernobyler tzaddik and the household helper

retelling.en: A Chernobyler tzaddik once stood in a corner whispering to Hashem, and those who listened heard him ask that the helper who worked in the Rebbetzin's kitchen, who had quarreled with the Rebbetzin and wanted to leave, should not leave. When the chassidim later asked why he needed to ask Hashem for such a thing, he answered that one must ask Hashem for every big thing and every small thing.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe and the Rambam's yiras shamayim

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe asked in Heaven to be granted the yiras shamayim of the Tannaim and was told it was too much for him; the same answer came when he asked for that of the Amoraim. He then asked for the Rambam's yiras shamayim, and this was granted. He was suddenly seized by such awe that he began to tremble and fall, and he begged that it be taken from him, and it was. The Ba'al Shem Tov later sa…

title.en: Reb Elchonon Wasserman and the wealthy man

retelling.en: Reb Elchonon Wasserman came to America to collect money for his yeshiva. There was a very wealthy man who did not give to yeshivos but gave to colleges, and Reb Elchonon asked him for money. The man offered chai, eighteen dollars, which the Mashgiach notes was a large sum in those days. Reb Elchonon answered him by contrasting the chai offered to the yeshiva with what the man gave to the college.

title.en: Reb Avraham of Ciechanow and his tefillin

retelling.en: Reb Avraham of Ciechanow told a friend that every morning, when he stretched out his hand to put on tefillin, he felt greater joy than someone who had won a lottery of ten thousand rubles.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's parable of the parrot

retelling.en: The great ministers and wise men of a kingdom stand before the king and offer him wisdom and counsel. Someone brings the king a gift, a parrot, a bird that talks without knowing what it says. The king stands by its cage and delights when it says 'good-bye', more than at all the words of his wise men, because wisdom from a wise man is no wonder, but a parrot speaking is a wonder.

title.en: Rabbi Yishmael asks Heaven about the decree

retelling.en: When the Roman emperor decreed death on ten Tannaim, Rabbi Yishmael Kohen Gadol, one of the ten, said he would ask Heaven. He wanted to know whether they must accept the decree, since otherwise he could save himself. The Mashgiach adds that these Tannaim, Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, Rabbi Chanina ben Tradyon and the others, could have destroyed Rome with one curse, but a tzaddik does what…

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai smuggled out of Yerushalayim

retelling.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai wanted to make peace with the Romans so that the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim would be spared, but the rebels, the biryonim, refused to surrender. He was carried out of Yerushalayim while people were told he had passed away, and then he could speak to the Romans and ask for favors: to save the Sanhedrin and to give Yavneh for their yeshiva so Torah would continue. He…

title.en: The tailor cutting silk

retelling.en: Right after the Holocaust someone asked why Hashem had done this. The answer given was a parable: one who enters a tailor's shop and sees him cut pieces from a precious roll of silk might ask why he is ruining it. But the tailor is making a garment that is not ready yet, and when the garment is seen, one will understand why he cut.

title.en: Speaking of Reb Shlomke of Zvhil during the war

retelling.en: According to a sefer from the Belzer Rav's gabbai, during a war the Belzer Rav sent word to the people in the beis medrash to speak about Reb Shlomke of Zvhil, who had already passed away. Speaking about him would arouse his merit to save the Jews from their enemies. About fifteen minutes later the gabbai came out and asked whether they were indeed speaking about Reb Shlomke.

title.en: Standing by the candles on Friday night

retelling.en: On a Friday night during that war, the Belzer Rav stood by the candles from Maariv on and did not move away for hours. He kept repeating the words 'hapores sukkas shalom aleinu'. The Jews then saw miracles beyond nature: the Arabs, who could have taken over all of Eretz Yisrael from an unprepared population, fled, and that became the turning point.

title.en: The Gerrer Rebbe abolishes pushing

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that by the previous Gerrer Rebbe the bochurim used to push at the tish, and he saw it himself many years ago. The Rebbe abolished it, saying everyone must sit in his place. In earlier times, he explained, people pushed toward the Rebbe out of love; today one pushes the other person away.

title.en: The kugel at the Stoliner Rebbe's tish

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes how at the Stoliner Rebbe's tish, when the kugel is served, there is no pushing. The Rebbe tastes from the kugel, the plate goes around, and each person takes a little and passes it on.

title.en: The Satmar Rav's mikveh

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when the Satmar Rav built his mikveh on Bedford Avenue, he wanted it built on spring water. They dug and dug until they found a spring, but the water was salty, and those who immersed there tasted salt water in their mouths.

title.en: The Ropshitzer's wedding rhymes

retelling.en: As a young man, R' Naftali of Ropshitz used to act as a wedding jester and say rhymes. His father-in-law was very upset that he busied himself with jokes and complained to the Linsker Rav, his father. The Linsker Rav suggested they go together and hear what he says; they stood by the window and listened. The Linsker Rav said that until now every word his son had said was according to Kabbalah, bu…

title.en: R' Aharon of Belz and his father's talk of politics

retelling.en: Someone wanted to speak with R' Aharon of Belz, but he was always busy learning and davening. Once, when his father, the Belzer Rebbe R' Yissachar Dov, was talking with people about the politics of the day and R' Aharon stood listening, the man thought he could now approach him, but R' Aharon hushed him. Later he told him that these were holy words of his father; he understood what his father was…

title.en: Singing 'we will outlive you' in the camps

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions an account from one who survived the Holocaust. When Jews in the concentration camps knew they were about to be taken into the gas chamber, they all began to sing, facing the Nazis, that they would outlive them.

title.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's donkey

retelling.en: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair came to a place, and the innkeeper gave his donkey barley, but the donkey would not eat. When the innkeeper asked why, Rabbi Pinchas suggested that perhaps the grain was demai, produce bought from an unlearned person from which the tithe had not been separated. The Mashgiach explains that a person with free choice knows what he may eat, but here the soul of Rabbi Pinchas be…

title.en: Rabbah bar bar Chana's wine barrels

retelling.en: Rabbah bar bar Chana hired workers to carry his barrels of wine, and on the way they dropped them and the wine spilled out. He called them to a din Torah before Rav, who ruled that since they were poor they need not pay. When the workers then said they had not been paid for their day's work, Rav ruled that he must pay them. Each time Rabbah bar bar Chana asked whether this was the law, Rav answer…

title.en: Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin refuses to sign

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that shortly before the Ba'al Shem Tov there was the false messiah Shabbsai Tzvi, who told people the mitzvos no longer had to be kept, and many Jews were drawn after him. The Vilna Gaon feared the Ba'al Shem Tov might be another such case and, for the sake of Heaven, made a cherem against the chassidim and told his students to sign it. Only Rabbi Chaim of Volozhin refused.…

title.en: Rabbi Chaim Vital and the spring of Gichon

retelling.en: King Chizkiyahu stopped up the waters of the Gichon, a river by the Beis HaMikdash, so that the invading king of Ashur would have no water; the Gemara says the Chachamim did not agree with him. In Rabbi Chaim Vital's time the Arab ruler of Jerusalem heard of this and called Rabbi Chaim Vital, telling him that as a holy man he could reopen the Gichon. Rabbi Chaim Vital was afraid to open what Chiz…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the breeze

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov was once sitting with his talmidim under a tree on a very hot day, when a breeze swept across the meadow. He asked them whether they appreciated the breeze and told them why it came. A small worm on top of a tree was suffering from the beating sun, Hashem had mercy on it and sent the breeze, which blew it down into the shade, and it was relieved. The Mashgiach adds that a breez…

title.en: The Sekulener Rebbe pleads with the commissar

retelling.en: In Russia the Sekulener Rebbe freed hundreds of Jews through his connections with the Communists. Once a commissar told him that he had always listened to him because he was a true 'communist', giving everything for others, but warned that if he came again to plead for Jews he would shoot him. When a Jew was then arrested and faced trial, the Rebbe asked the Potiker Rebbe to daven for him; told h…

title.en: The Berditchever Rav and the blood in the matzos

retelling.en: When the Berditchever Rav became rav in Berditchev, he gave a derashah before Pesach warning people not to put blood into the matzos, at a time when gentiles spread blood libels against Jews. Asked which Jew would ever do such a thing, he explained that the widows and poor women hired to roll matzos work all day and are exhausted, and fine Jews, eager for the mitzvah of speed, keep shouting at th…

title.en: Rabbi Akiva Eiger hides his learning

retelling.en: When Rabbi Akiva Eiger became a chasan, he came to the bride's town for the wedding and the seven days of sheva brachos, and the whole town expected a great lamdan. At the seudos he said only simple divrei Torah that a young bachur could say, and people wondered. After the seven days he began saying wonderful Torah, and when asked why he had held back, he said that another chasan had come along w…

title.en: A boy in Bnei Brak teased for his name

retelling.en: The Mashgiach mentions that Rav Aharon of Chernobyl had a gabbai with an old Yiddish name, once a respectable name. In Bnei Brak there was a boy given that name, and other boys ran after him mocking him with it. The Mashgiach says the child will be ashamed of his name, and that those who mocked him also had no right to shame him.

title.en: R' Yehoshua of Belz and the dybbuk

retelling.en: A girl was seized by a dybbuk and suffered greatly; a coarse man's voice spoke from her with obscenity and kefirah. She was brought to R' Yehoshua of Belz, who ordered the dybbuk to leave, and it answered that it had trembled before R' Sholom of Belz but not before him. R' Yehoshua had the girl brought to the women's section on Shabbos at Mussaf, and when he said Kesser, the dybbuk cried out that…

title.en: The dybbuk in Radin and the Chofetz Chaim

retelling.en: In Radin a girl suddenly fell ill and a voice spoke from her with ugly words, shaming the people around. Her father ran to the Chofetz Chaim, who made R' Elchonon Wasserman his shliach to order the dybbuk out in his name. Asked what they say in heaven about the Chofetz Chaim, the dybbuk said he is called a Tanna; asked why it entered the girl, it said malachei chabalah chased it with fiery whips…

title.en: The machine tzitzis factory

retelling.en: A large factory began making machine tzitzis and spread them through the country, taking away the livelihood of the honest tzitzis makers who made them by hand. The Divrei Chaim ruled them pasul and ended his teshuvah with a wish to see the machine's downfall. A footnote by the one who published the teshuvos records that some time later the whole factory burned down.

title.en: Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld and the daily mikvah

retelling.en: A great man saw Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, the Rav of Yerushalayim, going to the mikvah on a weekday, and learned that he went every day. Rav Yosef Chaim told him that a gentile who wants to become a Jew does so through milah and then immersion in a mikvah. If a mikvah can make a Jew out of a gentile, it can make a better Jew out of a Jew. From then on that man also went to the mikvah every day;…

title.en: Bochurim who waited for Shabbos to end

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that bochurim poured out their hearts to him that Shabbos was the worst day of the week for them. They would stand by the window waiting for three stars so they could return to their pursuits. He calls it a pity and explains that they had not prepared for Shabbos and so were, in effect, not admitted into it.

title.en: Avraham in Nimrod's fire

retelling.en: Avraham thought about who created the world until he concluded that there is one Creator, and he served Him with his understanding though Hashem had never spoken to him. He went about telling people that they should serve the Creator rather than the sun and moon. Nimrod, who held himself a god, told him to stop; when he did not, he was thrown into the fire, and a miracle happened and he came out…

title.en: The Rebbe and the interrogator's gun

retelling.en: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak of Lubavitch kept Torah alive in Russia when the Communists forbade it, and taught his chassidim that one must have mesiras nefesh; many of them were killed for running hidden yeshivos. He was arrested, and his interrogators wanted the names of the chassidim who ran the yeshivos. When he refused, they pointed a gun at him and said it had made many people talk. He answered tha…

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe stands up for a young man

retelling.en: When Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak was still a young man, while his father was Rebbe, he came to Stolin to Rabbi Yisrael of Stolin, who stood up for him. The chassidim asked why the Rebbe should stand up for a young man who was not yet a Rebbe. The Stoliner answered that this young man is the one in the generation with mesiras nefesh. Later, when he became Rebbe, people saw his great mesiras nefesh.

title.en: A Rav fleeing the Nazis

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates from biographies of a certain Rav that he experienced many miracles while escaping from the Nazis. Whenever the Nazis confronted him, searched his car and looked for him, he kept one thing in mind: there is nothing besides Hashem, and this wicked man has no power of his own; whatever power he has is Hashem's.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe eats the dish rag

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe's Rebbetzin had to go to a wedding and asked him to take supper himself, telling him the meat and soup were on the stove. She had also prepared water with kosher soap and a rag for washing the dishes. Not knowing the difference, he poured himself a plate of the soapy water with the rag and ate it. When she came home and asked, he said it was fine, only the meat was a little cold…

title.en: The young tzaddik who sold brandy

retelling.en: One of the great tzaddikim, before he became a famous Rebbe, sold brandy by the glass in a store when he was young. A man came in, took a glass of brandy and drank it without even making a brachah. The tzaddik asked him when his father's yahrzeit was, and told him it was that very day, which the man had forgotten. He told him that a brachah would have brought an aliyah, and instead there was a gr…

title.en: Adam and the grapes of the Tree of Knowledge

retelling.en: According to the view that the Tree of Knowledge was a vine, Adam, created on Friday, should have waited, squeezed the grapes into wine and made kiddush with it on Shabbos night, and he would have been elevated. He did not wait and ate it on Friday, when it was not yet permitted, just as the fruit of a tree in its first three years, orlah, may not be eaten and afterwards may.

title.en: The souls who demanded their purpose

retelling.en: A disciple of the Ba'al Shem Tov, who would reveal great things at kiddush levanah, once told his chassidim what he had been shown. Souls came to the angel in charge of souls and complained that they live seventy or eighty years, come up to Heaven, are told they did not fulfil their task, and are sent down again, over and over. The angel did not know what to answer and sent them higher, from ange…

title.en: David and Shimi ben Gera
