retelling.en: When Avshalom waged war against his father and David had to flee Jerusalem, Shimi ben Gera of the family of Shaul, angry that David had taken the kingship, cursed him harshly. Avishai, David's general, wanted to kill him, but David refused: Hashem had told Shimi to curse, and if not he then someone else would. At that moment it was decided in Heaven that David would become the fourth leg of the D…

title.en: The woman who carried out her piano

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls a case that was much talked about: a woman who played the piano saw a fire in her home, and fearing that her very costly piano would burn, she carried it outside by herself. Ordinarily only special movers can move a piano, since it is extremely heavy, yet in the emergency she found strength she never knew she had.

title.en: The lion that bowed to the Divrei Chaim

retelling.en: The Divrei Chaim, the Sanzer Rav, went with his gabbaim to a zoo, which surprised people. When he came to the lion, the lion bent down before him, and the gentile zookeepers were amazed that a lion should bow to a man. The Mashgiach explains that the lion saw the kingship of Torah and fear of Heaven in him.

title.en: The ox on the stairs

retelling.en: One of the great Rabbonim, whose name the Mashgiach does not recall, lived upstairs and stepped out into the hall for a minute. He came back in and told his household that an ox was climbing the stairs. They went to look and saw that it was the head of the community coming up; the tzaddik had seen an ox because that man did not have a tzelem Elokim.

title.en: The wolves that left the wagon

retelling.en: The Skulener Rebbe told what his grandmother told him: her family once traveled by wagon through the forests to visit a Rebbe. Suddenly the horse reared up on its hind legs, a sign of danger, and a pack of some ten or fifteen wolves surrounded the wagon. Their leader jumped up, went among all the people in the wagon and sniffed them, then gave a signal and all the wolves went away. The Mashgiach…

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the valley of gold

retelling.en: A student of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai went abroad and returned wealthy, and other students wanted to do the same. Fearing they would leave their learning, Rabbi Shimon took them out to a valley and said, 'Valley, valley, fill with gold dinarim,' and it filled with gold coins. When the students went to grab them, he told them that the reward is kept for the World to Come, and whoever takes it now w…

title.en: A misnaged davens in Karlin

retelling.en: A misnaged came to Karlin, needed a minyan, and went to daven in the minyan of Reb Aharon Karliner. When they began Baruch She'amar the congregation burned with fervor and did not move on. Thinking the chazzan simply does not stop after each part, as in Litvish minyanim, he davened on by himself and finished the entire davening. All that time the congregation was still saying Baruch She'amar.

title.en: The Yismach Moshe's single plate

retelling.en: The Yismach Moshe asked why he needed so many courses; one portion, a little larger, was enough to have strength to serve Hashem. His gabbai knew the Rebbe ate with closed eyes, swaying as in Pesukei d'Zimra, without knowing what he ate, and wanted him to get the nutrients of different foods. So on the same plate he gave him soup, then meat with vegetables, then dessert. Afterwards the Yismach Mo…

title.en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe and 'lev nishbar'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he used to spend time each year in Eretz Yisrael, staying in the Old City of Yerushalayim, and every night went down to the ruined beis medrash there to say Krias Shema before sleep, which in the chassidish version includes Tehillim 51. When a member of his family became ill, he repeated the passuk 'lev nishbar' perhaps twenty times each night with tears, all summer. On…

title.en: The Chabad chassid who davened until the afternoon

retelling.en: The Mashgiach remembers from his boyhood a Chabad chassid in Williamsburg, a disciple of the Rebbe Rashab, who knew Shas thoroughly. When he was not in Lubavitch he davened in the shul where the Mashgiach davened. On Shabbos he came at nine in the morning and began davening very slowly, paused to hear the Torah reading, and went back to davening. On a winter Shabbos, when the others returned at f…

title.en: The upstairs room of the Tzemach Tzedek shul

retelling.en: In the Old City of Yerushalayim, where the Mashgiach spent many summers, the Tzemach Tzedek shul had two floors. Downstairs there was a regular minyan, and upstairs a large domed room called the Chassidaniya, for those special chassidim who could not keep up with the minyan and davened the entire day.

title.en: The serpent and the king's daughter

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a parable of a dangerous serpent that endangered people, and a king who promised his daughter to whoever would kill it. One man killed the serpent and received the king's daughter. The king's daughter, he explains, is tefillah; one who wins her becomes the king's son-in-law, with access to the king and his requests fulfilled.

title.en: Not Rabbi, but Mister Mendlowitz

retelling.en: Reb Shraga Feivel could not tolerate pretense. When people called him Rabbi Mendlowitz, he was displeased, and they had to call him Mister Mendlowitz.

title.en: The Rebbe who put the tisch before Tehillim

retelling.en: Someone told a Rebbe that he said the whole Tehillim before davening on Shabbos morning with sweetness. The Rebbe asked whether he had been at the Shabbos tisch the night before, and he answered no, since he had to get up early. The Rebbe waved his hand: coming to the tisch and singing zemiros with joy and dveikus binds a Jew to his Rebbe, and that is more important than getting up early to say a…

title.en: The protest against the rushing chazzan

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who always protested that the chazzan said Emes V'yatziv so quickly. He explained that when the chazzan rushes, he too must hurry to begin Shemoneh Esrei together with the congregation. He compared it to a hungry man eating a juicy piece of meat, when someone pulls it out of his mouth.

title.en: Mordechai and the three children

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Midrash that when Haman wanted to harm Mordechai, Mordechai met a child and asked him to say his passuk. The child answered 'Al tira mipachad pisom'. A second child said 'Utzu eitzah v'sufar, dabru davar v'lo yakum, ki imanu Kel', and a third child said a third passuk.

title.en: Not spitting on the holy ground

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that when Jews from Poland and Lithuania began coming from Europe after the war, they had a habit of spitting on the ground, which he says he saw himself. A certain Reb Chaim who arrived in Eretz Yisrael suffered greatly over it, since he was used to spitting. The Mashgiach exclaims that one cannot spit on Eretz Yisrael; its ground is to be kissed. He adds that one of the Am…

title.en: Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's daily mikvah

retelling.en: Reb Isser Zalman Meltzer, walking in the morning, saw Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld coming out of the mikvah at a time when going to the mikvah was not commonly emphasized and Torah study reigned supreme. He asked whether it was not a loss of learning time. Reb Yosef Chaim answered that a ger becomes a Yid through tevilah, drawing a Jewish neshamah upon himself; if a mikvah can make a Yid from a ger…

title.en: The Chafetz Chaim and the Mississippi flood

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls hearing as a bochur a derashah of Rabbi Avraham Kalmanowitz, who was close to the Chafetz Chaim. Once the Chafetz Chaim called a gathering and told everyone that in America a river called the Mississippi had flooded, people were killed and there was great damage. He cried out that Hashem was warning the Jews, citing the passuk about destroying nations so that Israel take mus…

title.en: The boy's kvitel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that by the Rebbe many people would hand in kvitlach, and he was once curious what people write in them. Among them he found a kvitel from a young boy asking for something childish, apparently a bicycle and a dog. The Mashgiach notes that the boy did not come to him but turned to Hashem, knowing Hashem could give it to him, and this is pure emunah.

title.en: The Lubliner's notebook

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings from the Bnei Yissaschar, a talmid of the Lubliner, that on Rosh Chodesh Nissan the Lubliner took a new notebook. On each of the first twelve days of Nissan he wrote on a separate page what would happen in the month that day corresponds to, and showed it to no one. At the end of the year, in Adar, he showed it to his talmidim, and they saw that everything he had written had c…

title.en: Waiting for Tav Shin

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that as a boy he waited eagerly for the year Tav Shin, when the Toldos Yaakov Yosef wrote that Moshiach would come. When Tav Shin came it was a catastrophe: a few days before Rosh Hashanah of that year Hitler invaded Poland.

title.en: The boy's kvitel at the Kosel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach describes the many kvitlach people put into the cracks of the Kosel, which workers sweep out every few days, and jokes that he once thought of publishing a book of them. He once picked one up: a boy had written in Hebrew asking Hashem for two things, a bicycle and a dog. The Mashgiach says he gives the boy credit, because the very fact that he turned to Hashem shows emunah.

title.en: The man freed from the chitzonim by the Rebbe Reb Elimelech

people: the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk

retelling.en: A man disappeared and his wife was left not knowing where he was, so she went to the Rebbe Reb Elimelech. The Rebbe said he had been captured by the chitzonim, wrote a letter of circles that nobody could read, and sent her to find a house in a certain forest and hand it in. She did so and, waiting outside, heard them say that the Rebbe Reb Elimelech of Lizhensk orders his release and must be obey…

title.en: Polish Jews and the habit of spitting

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates something he was told: the Jews in Poland had a habit of spitting, even the learned ones. Whoever came from there to Eretz Yisrael had great difficulty, being used to spitting, because one cannot spit on the earth of Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: How the beis medrash began in camp

retelling.en: About fifty years earlier, the bochurim were in camp, where the Mashgiach was in charge of the masmidim. He introduced loud, warm davening, and it was felt so strongly that when they returned to yeshiva they still had Torah but missed the tefillah. They asked that a separate beis medrash be made for them.

title.en: Why Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld went to the mikvah

retelling.en: Someone walking in the morning saw Rabbi Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld coming out of the mikvah, in a Litvish setting where the mikvah was not much stressed and Torah learning reigned. He asked whether the time was not bittul Torah, since he could have been learning. Rabbi Yosef Chaim answered that a goy becomes a Yid by immersing in a mikvah, drawing a Jewish neshamah upon himself; if a mikvah can make…

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov and the driver who did not cross himself

retelling.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov once rode in a wagon driven by a gentile, and a priest came toward them with a cross. Usually a gentile who saw a priest would bow to the cross, but this driver ignored it. The Ba'al Shem Tov jumped down from the wagon, saying he was afraid to ride with someone who believes in nothing.

title.en: The Williamsburg school with two doors

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that Williamsburg was once a gentile neighborhood with large public schools. When the Jews moved in and the schools emptied, the government sold a whole block for a dollar, and Jewish mosdos now stand there. Over the two entrances of the old school are still carved the words 'Boys' and 'Girls', because once boys and girls did not enter by one door; today, he says, it is not…

title.en: The bachur who learned Mishnah Berurah in English class

retelling.en: A diligent bachur sat at the back of his English class learning a Mishnah Berurah hidden under his desk. When his rosh yeshivah, Reb Yaakov Kamenetsky, found out, he called him in and rebuked him sharply. He told him that the teacher wants him to know arithmetic or English, and by ignoring him he is in effect telling him to talk to the wall; this is bad middos, and what he thinks is a great mitzv…

title.en: 'Rebbi, I don't like fish'

retelling.en: Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, who taught children when he came to America, once gave a talk about reward and punishment, saying the tzaddikim will eat the Shor Habor and the Livyasan. The children absorbed it with joy at being Jews. Then one boy raised his hand and said, 'Rebbi, I don't like fish', and the class laughed. With that one remark the whole seriousness of the talk was lost.

title.en: The Shinover Rav in Belz

retelling.en: The Shinover Rav, son of the Divrei Chaim of Sanz, used to travel to Reb Sholom of Belz for Shavuos. When his father asked why he goes there, he answered that in Belz, when the Rebbe reads the Ten Commandments, one sees the thunder and lightning of Sinai and hears Hashem Himself say Anochi. His father told him to stay there. Later, at the Torah reading in Sanz, the Shinover Rav saw the same thing…

title.en: The Kotzker: believing is greater than seeing

retelling.en: The Kotzker Rebbe had a new path in Chassidus, and the Galician Rebbes were not pleased. One of the great Rebbes sent him a message asking why he fights him, when every Sukkos he actually sees the seven ushpizin, Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Moshe, Yosef and Dovid, enter his sukkah. The Kotzker answered that every Sukkos he believes with complete faith that the ushpizin come into his sukkah, and hi…

title.en: The Blazhever Rav's heartbeat

retelling.en: When the Blazhever Rav felt weak, the king's chief physician, who as a boy had learned in cheder before leaving the path, was brought to examine him. The doctor told him that his heart was not beating normally. The Blazhever Rav asked him what day it was; it was Rosh Chodesh Sivan. He answered that Shavuos is coming and he must receive the Torah, so how could the doctor expect his heart to beat n…

title.en: The Imrei Emes's takanah for Shavuos

retelling.en: The Imrei Emes of Ger made a new takanah that his chassidim should rise early and daven early, even on Shabbos, and then learn after a quick kiddush. On Shavuos he announced at the tish that since they would daven early in the morning, they should sleep at night, so that they could daven with fervor and listen to the Torah reading.

title.en: Reb Yisroel of Vizhnitz and the bachurim

retelling.en: Bachurim from a yeshiva came to Reb Yisroel of Vizhnitz for Shavuos. After the night, the Rebbe went into the beis medrash and saw them hurrying to daven so they could go to sleep sooner. He told them that sleeping in order to be able to daven and learn is right, but davening in order to be able to sleep is not. They listened, went to sleep, and davened three hours later.

title.en: Rommel at the gates of Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: When the Nazis occupied Europe, the German general Rommel went from conquest to conquest until he reached Alexandria in Egypt and declared that the next morning he would drink coffee in Tel Aviv. The Jews were in great danger, and tzaddikim went up to daven with a Sefer Torah. One of them told the Jews with him that Hitler would not come into Eretz Yisrael, saying he had seen Hashem's Name in fie…

title.en: The Six Day War

retelling.en: Before the Six Day War hundreds of millions of Arabs surrounded Eretz Yisrael on three sides and swore to push the Jews into the sea. The Jews had little to fight with, and newspapers such as the New York Times wrote beforehand that this was the end of the Jewish nation, while nobody thought of helping. Hashem helped with great miracles, and the Jews won and were delivered.

title.en: A cup in hand on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a tzaddik who took a cup in his hand on Tisha B'Av. He showed the chassidim how kiddush will be made on Tisha B'Av when Moshiach comes, holding the cup and saying words over it, and tears flowed.

title.en: The Vilna Gaon and the man who saw a cross

retelling.en: There was a Jew who, whenever he davened, saw in his imagination a gentile with a cross standing before him, and he could not daven. He came to the Vilna Gaon, who told him: let it stand there. The Mashgiach says the same applies to doubts: pay them no attention.

title.en: Bachurim complain to a Rav about politics

retelling.en: Some bachurim came to a Rav to complain about another political party and argue why one must vote for theirs. That Rav answered that when he was a bachur, bachurim did not involve themselves in politics, and that because today's bachurim do, gedolei Yisroel no longer grow from them.

title.en: Watching the sunset with Barchi Nafshi

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recounts that when his children were young and the family was in the country, he would take them up a hill toward evening to watch the sunset. They looked at the colors in the clouds, red, green, blue and orange, and took a Tehillim and said the chapter of Barchi Nafshi.

title.en: Reb Shraga Feivel davening at the window

retelling.en: Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, the Mashgiach's rebbe, was once in the country and stood davening by the window, looking out. People there did not know who he was, and one of them gave him a push and told him to look into the siddur instead of out. He answered that he was looking out, and in that way looking in, to the pesukim of the siddur that speak of the creatures, trees and birds.

title.en: Dovid Hamelech and the frog

retelling.en: As brought in Perek Shirah, after Dovid Hamelech completed his sefer of songs of praise to Hashem, he felt it was a great thing. A frog came down by the water and said that its song is greater, for it too sings to the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Parvah's tunnel to the Kodesh HaKodashim

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that there was a chamber in the Beis HaMikdash called after Parvah, a sorcerer. Parvah wanted to see the Kohen Gadol enter the Kodesh HaKodashim, so he dug a tunnel underground toward it. He was caught and killed, yet the chamber was named after him.

title.en: The rasha who asked for warm plums

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells a story over which the Ba'al Shem Tov once laughed. A certain wicked man, who had committed every sin, was being held, and he asked to be served warm plums. Asked why exactly warm plums, he answered that he knew his punishment would be endless beating, and he wanted to know where he stood. His beating began over the warm plums, and from there it went back over everything else.

title.en: The lion's feast and the fox's song

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash: the lion made a feast and spread out a canopy of hides. The animals asked who would sing for them, and the fox took it upon himself, saying the others would sing along. The fox began to sing.

title.en: Tzedakah as advice for peace

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates, as brought in seforim, that a man who needed advice for shalom bayis was told to give tzedakah. The reason, he explains, is that a poor man has a quarrel with Hashem, and the one who gives him tzedakah makes peace between them, so Hashem in turn grants him peace.

title.en: The Mogielnicer Rebbe's Nishmas

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Mogielnicer Rebbe, a great tzaddik in Poland. At a Purim gathering together with the Grodzisker, the Mogielnicer began saying Nishmas, starting from 'min ha'olam ve'ad ha'olam'. The Grodzisker hinted to the crowd that they should say it together with him.

title.en: The bar mitzvah suit

retelling.en: A bar mitzvah boy did not get a new suit and had to wear a hand-me-down. Later he complained to his mother that he had not even gotten a new suit. The Mashgiach asks where his thankfulness was: his parents could not afford it, but they spent sleepless nights raising him, worried over him when he was sick, and gave him whatever they could.

title.en: The tzaddik who thanked for everything

retelling.en: In a will to his children, a tzaddik wrote that he thanked Hashem for whatever happened to him, good or bad. He thanked Hashem for a private room to learn in, for having money to buy even a box of toothpicks, for the file with which he sharpened his knife after Shabbos, and when he remembered something he had forgotten. When a bottle or his eyeglasses fell without breaking, or when he found his m…

title.en: Haman's breastplate and Mordechai's reminder

retelling.en: According to the Chasam Sofer as the Mashgiach brings it, Haman wore a breastplate on which all his possessions were written. Whenever he boasted of his wealth, Mordechai would remind him that he was a slave, and that what a slave acquires belongs to his master. This is why Haman said 'all this is worth nothing to me'.

title.en: A tzaddik's matanos la'evyonim to children

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that a great tzaddik, in whose beis medrash he davened, would give out sweets to children on Purim. He said that children are the true evyonim, and with this he fulfilled the mitzvah.

title.en: The Tannaim in Bnei Brak

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Jews of Bnei Brak, descendants of Haman, could keep every mitzvah but could not complete krias shema of the morning. The holy Tannaim came to Bnei Brak and sat there all that night. They repaired the place and cleansed the souls of Haman's descendants of every remaining spark of him, and then the time of krias shema of shacharis arrived.

title.en: Haman's tree from the Kodesh Hakodashim

retelling.en: Following the Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer, the Mashgiach relates that Haman brought a tree fifty amos tall from the Kodesh Hakodashim of the destroyed Beis Hamikdash, and from it he made the gallows. He planned, by his own reckoning, to hang Mordechai on it in the morning.

title.en: The young man who read the Megillah on Pesach night

retelling.en: A young man finished the Haggadah on the second night of Pesach, and his heart was still burning, so he took a Megillah and began to read it. A soul appeared to him and told him that on Purim there is a great eis ratzon in heaven, when souls that can find no tikkun on Shabbos or Pesach rush to receive one; when the gates closed it had been left outside and had to wait a year. When the young man r…

title.en: The cow that would not work on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a non-Jew, and the cow would not work on Shabbos. The non-Jew asked whether it was witchcraft; the Jew whispered to the cow that it now belonged to a non-Jew and may work on Shabbos, and it worked. Seeing this, the non-Jew converted and became the great R' Yochanan ben Torsa, named after the animal. The Mashgiach brings from the Gilgulei Neshamos that this cow was a gilgul o…

title.en: The Lubliner chassidim and Shabbos clothes

retelling.en: Chassidim in Lublin felt a great light on Shabbos and wondered whether it truly came from Shabbos or only from the good food, the wine and the singing. They tried making a Shabbos-like meal with wine, challah and fish on a weekday. When they came to their Rebbe, he asked whether they had worn their Shabbos clothes, and they said they had. He told them that this was in order, because one who wears…

title.en: Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld on building a mikveh

retelling.en: Someone came to Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld with a complaint about why he invested so much in building a mikveh. Rav Yosef Chaim answered that a mikveh can make a gentile into a Jew, and it can also make a Jew into a better Jew.

title.en: The Lechovitcher chassid in the river of Petersburg

retelling.en: Jews were not allowed to live in Petersburg, except a great merchant who received permission. A Lechovitcher chassid who was such a merchant came there, and there was no minyan and no mikvah. A river ran through the middle of the city, with benches on both sides where men and women sat looking at the water. The chassid went and immersed in the river in front of them all. When he returned, his Reb…

title.en: Belshazzar's last night

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls that writing appeared on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. Daniel came and read it, and Belshazzar had him dressed in royal garments. That same night Belshazzar was killed.

title.en: The Klausenberger Rebbe chooses Kriyas HaTorah

retelling.en: When the Klausenberger Rebbe was old and weak, even Kriyas HaTorah was difficult for him. His chassidim suggested that he not lein the Torah on Rosh Hashanah as usual but only blow the shofar. He refused, saying he would rather do the Kriyas HaTorah than the shofar, because in the reading Sarah says that the son of the maidservant must be driven out and not inherit with Yitzchak, and he wanted to…

title.en: The Chasam Sofer's parable of the imprisoned minister

retelling.en: A minister of the king was put into a dungeon to await judgment, and the king passed judgment on his servants on his coronation day. On that day the prison warden heard singing, dancing and clapping from the prisoner's cell and asked whether he did not know that today was his trial. The prisoner answered that it was, and no one knew the verdict, but it was also the king's coronation, and he was s…

title.en: Haman leads Mordechai

retelling.en: When Haman had to honor Mordechai, he had to help him up onto the horse. Mordechai stepped up on him and, as he mounted, gave him a kick. Haman protested, and Mordechai answered that the rule he cited applies to Jews, but about him it says 've-atah al bamoseimo tidroch'.

title.en: The one who sang all night

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of a man who could spend an entire night alone in the beis medrash. From far away people heard him singing, and he sang 'shiru lo zamru lo sichu bechol nifle'osav'.

title.en: The cow that kept Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a non-Jew, and on Shabbos the cow refused to work. The Jew spoke into its ear that it now belonged to a non-Jew and must work. The non-Jew, seeing this, converted and became Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa, 'son of the cow', one of the great Sages.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva and Ben Koziva

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva thought that Ben Koziva, then called Bar Kochba, was Moshiach. When it became clear he was false, he was called Ben Koziva. Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa told Rabbi Akiva that grass would grow on his cheeks and Moshiach would still not have come.

title.en: The merchant who kept his bitachon

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a story told by Rebbe Nachman of Breslov. A merchant put his whole fortune into scrolls, knowing he could sell them for much money overseas, and set out by ship with no money for the fare, showing the captain the scrolls he would sell. During the voyage his goods were thrown into the sea, yet he acted as if nothing had happened and held on to his bitachon. When they arrived,…

title.en: The plague in Rav's neighborhood

retelling.en: There was a plague, but in the neighborhood of Rav there was none. People thought it was in Rav's merit. It was revealed that Rav's merit was too great for this, and that it was rather in the merit of a man who used to lend out his tools for burials.

title.en: Achashverosh's feast for the seventy years

retelling.en: Achashverosh calculated when the seventy years of the exile would end. When he saw that, by his count, the seventy years had passed and no redemption had come, he made a great feast to celebrate. Mordechai went about at that feast declaring that he belonged to Jerusalem.

title.en: The Chazon Ish and the surgeons

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that in his generation neurologists and neurosurgeons came to the Chazon Ish for instructions on how to perform surgery. He gave them small notes saying how it should be done, and people in Eretz Yisrael still remember it. When asked how he knew, he answered that he knew it from the Torah.

title.en: Fish prepared with Nishmas

retelling.en: A chassid prepared the fish on Erev Shabbos, and while preparing it he sang Nishmas. When the fish was served at the Shabbos tish, the Lechovitcher was moved and said the fish tasted of Nishmas. The Mashgiach brings this to show that what is prepared with holiness carries it.

title.en: The soul and the gate of Gan Eden

retelling.en: A soul came and said that in Heaven there is a gate of Gan Eden. When a soul has finished with its judgment, it waits at that gate until Purim, when the Megillah is read; then the gates open and the souls enter Gan Eden.

title.en: The gedolim and the czar's blank paper

retelling.en: Czar Nicholas summoned three gedolim of Russia. The Mashgiach names the place of one of them and says he will not name the other two. The czar demanded that they sign their names on a blank sheet of paper, on which he would write above whatever he wished, while saying he would not write anything bad. The danger was that above the signatures would be written that they accept the Christian faith. O…

title.en: Mordechai mounts the horse

retelling.en: When Haman came to lead Mordechai on the horse, Mordechai said he was weak and could not climb up, and Haman should bend down so he could climb onto him. Haman bent down, Mordechai went up on him and gave him a kick with his foot. When Haman protested that it is written not to rejoice at an enemy's fall, Mordechai answered that this applies among Jews, but regarding the wicked it says 'and you sh…

title.en: A tzaddik in Amsterdam on Purim

retelling.en: In Amsterdam there was a great danger of flooding, and the tzaddik was regularly asked to daven when trouble came. Once, on Purim, at a time of great danger, he was found sitting with his people, drinking and rejoicing. Asked why he was not davening, he answered that today is Purim, and on Purim one achieves with simcha what all year one achieves with tefillos and fasts.

title.en: How Osnas came to Egypt

retelling.en: Citing the Targum Yonasan, the Mashgiach tells that Osnas was the daughter Dina bore after Shechem abducted her. The Midrash adds that the Shevatim were unhappy with her and wanted to harm her, so Yaakov took the infant to the desert and placed her on a thornbush. Angels carried her to Egypt, where the wife of Potiphera adopted her as a daughter, and she became the wife of Yosef, carrying the spa…

title.en: Yosef reveals himself to his brothers

retelling.en: When the brothers came to Egypt they knew only Tzafnas Pane'ach, the ruler, who seemed to them a tyrant: he caused them great anguish, took away Shimon and then wanted to take Binyamin. At one moment he said 'I am Yosef', and they understood who the 'tyrant' was and that he had meant only their good.

title.en: Chananya, Mishael and Azarya in the furnace

retelling.en: Nevuchadnetzar made a golden image and commanded that when the music played, everyone bow to it. All bowed except Chananya, Mishael and Azarya, who were thrown into the fire. Hashem made a miracle: they came out whole, not even their clothes were touched, while the gentiles standing near the furnace were burned by its heat.

title.en: The Ramban's student and Ha'azinu

retelling.en: The Ramban had a student who went off the path. The Ramban said that everything is hinted in Parshas Ha'azinu, and the student asked how that could be and where he himself was hinted there. The Ramban showed him a pasuk in which his name was hinted. The student then went off to sea in a small boat, and no one knew what became of him.

title.en: The Sefer Torah written by a heretic

retelling.en: A beautiful Sefer Torah was found, and no one knew who had written it. A chacham looked at its last words, 'le'einei kol Yisrael', and said a heretic had written it, which later proved true. Asked how he knew, he explained that Jews call people to write the last letters of a Sefer Torah, so they are usually less neat; these were perfect, showing that the scribe paid no heed to a minhag Yisrael. W…

title.en: The Tzemach Tzedek: make Eretz Yisrael here

retelling.en: A Jew who wanted to move to Eretz Yisrael came to ask the Tzemach Tzedek. The Tzemach Tzedek told him to make Eretz Yisrael where he was, and to make Yerushalayim there.

title.en: Rabbi Eliezer and the reader of Yechezkel

retelling.en: As the Gemara in Megillah tells, a man read before Rabbi Eliezer the verse 'Son of man, make known to Yerushalayim her abominations'. Rabbi Eliezer told him to go and examine his own mother's lineage instead of Yerushalayim's, and when it was checked a blemish was found.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya reads 'heh-elef'

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates a tradition guarded in Chabad: the Ba'al HaTanya once read the Torah in Parshas Pekudei, and at the pasuk of the extra silver used for the vavim he read 'ha'elef' as heh-elef. He was corrected but refused to be corrected and repeated it, saying the geulah is hinted in this pasuk in 5775. Though he was very exacting in reading the Torah, this is how he read it. The Mashgiach…

title.en: Bnei Dan outside the clouds

retelling.en: In the midbar the 600,000 Yidden traveled under the Ananei HaKavod, but some unfortunate Yidden, Bnei Dan, were expelled from the camp. Since they were outside the protection of the clouds, Amalek came and waged war with them. The Mashgiach adds that Hashem's anger at Amalek for daring to attack these Yidden is still in full flame.

title.en: The Amora who said Mordechai nursed Esther

retelling.en: An Amora taught in the beis medrash that Mordechai could not find a nurse for Esther when she was a small child, and a miracle happened so that he nursed her himself. The listeners laughed. He asked them why they laughed, since a Mishnah states explicitly that the milk of a male is tahor.

title.en: Zeiri's donkey from Alexandria

retelling.en: Zeiri bought a donkey in Alexandria of Egypt, a city full of sorcery. It was really a plank of wood that sorcery had made look like a donkey. When it was brought to water to drink, the sorcery was annulled and it became a plank again.

title.en: R' Chanina and the sorceress

retelling.en: A sorceress wanted to work sorcery on R' Chanina. He told her that she could do nothing to him, because a Jew who holds to ein od milvado, that there is none besides Hashem, is beyond the reach of sorcery.

title.en: The child who fell into the mud

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a mashal from the Divrei Shlomo: a father warned his child not to go where there was mud and soil his new clothes. The child did not listen, fell in and soiled everything, then came crying, and the father forgave him. A wise child kept crying: you are my father, why did you let me go there, why did you not watch over me? Until the father, feeling responsible, brought him gift…

title.en: Simchas Torah at the Rebbe R' Elimelech

retelling.en: The Apter Rav related that once on Simchas Torah the Rebbe R' Elimelech told him of a harsh decree on Jews that Rosh Hashanah, which crying, Torah and good deeds had not removed. On Simchas Torah, when the joy of Jews showed the difference between a Jew and a gentile, the decree was annulled. The Apter Rav was asked in Heaven what he wished for; he asked to see the Beis HaMikdash above, the Kodes…

title.en: Esther and the Shabbos maiden

retelling.en: Esther had seven maidens, one for each day, so that she could count the days and keep Shabbos without revealing who she was. The Shabbos maiden was named for rest, so Esther could call out 'Shabbos' aloud to her, and the maiden thought she called loudly only because she was far away. The Mashgiach adds that Esther would even dance with the maiden, singing 'Shabbos', and so she honored Shabbos.

title.en: Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam dancing on Purim

retelling.en: Whenever the queen of the Netherlands needed a salvation, she would send to Rabbi Elazar of Amsterdam to pray, and his prayers were always answered. Once the walls of the dams broke and the water could not be controlled, and she sent to him. Her messenger found him sitting with his students on Purim, dancing and drinking. Asked what this was, he answered that today, with dancing and drinking, one…

title.en: The Roman king's palace of shoes

retelling.en: As brought in the piyut of the Ten Martyrs, the king of Rome gathered the holy Tannaim into his great hall, whose walls he had covered with shoes. He asked them why their forefathers had sold Yosef and bought shoes with the money. The Mashgiach asks why the king needed to cover the walls with shoes rather than simply say it, and explains that he was making a sign to arouse the sin of the sale of…

title.en: Hillel and the Pesach knives

retelling.en: Erev Pesach once fell on Shabbos, and they did not know how the knives for the korban would be brought without carrying. Hillel said to wait and see what the Jews would do. The next day they saw that the Jews had stuck the knives into the wool of the sheep, and the sheep carried them in. The Mashgiach brings this to show that Klal Yisrael has prophecy.

title.en: Graf Potocki and the Vilna Gaon on sensing Shabbos

retelling.en: It is accepted among Jews that the Ger Tzedek of Vilna, Graf Potocki, asked the Vilna Gaon about the Gemara's case of one walking in the desert who does not know when Shabbos is. How could that be, he asked, when every grain of sand, every star and every stone testifies that it is Shabbos? The Gaon answered that he was right: an elevated Jew can look at the world and see that it is Shabbos, but n…

title.en: Esther's maiden named Shabbos

retelling.en: Esther longed to say 'Shabbos' aloud, but she could not reveal that she was Jewish. So she gave the seventh maiden the name Shabbos. When Shabbos came and Esther wanted to cry out 'Shabbos', she would call the maiden, who came thinking she was being called; everyone thought she meant the maid, but only Hashem and Esther knew the secret of what she meant.

title.en: The Ponevezher Rav greets Eretz Yisrael

retelling.en: On the first night of Rosh Hashanah in Bnei Brak, decades ago, a Shemitah year was beginning. After Maariv the Ponevezher Rav walked out, bent down to the ground and said 'Gut Shabbos, dear Eretz Yisrael'. Rosh Hashanah fell on Wednesday night, but it was Shemitah.

title.en: Mordechai steps on Haman

retelling.en: When Haman led Mordechai on the horse, Mordechai stepped on Haman in order to mount it. Haman protested that this was not allowed, citing a verse. Mordechai answered that it is written of Haman's people 'and you shall tread on their high places'.

title.en: Esther points at Achashverosh

retelling.en: When Esther said 'a foe and an enemy', she pointed at Achashverosh, and a malach struck her hand so that she would point at Haman. The Mashgiach explains that she was speaking to Hashem the whole time, and meant that Achashverosh was the real enemy.

title.en: The Megillah read on the Seder night

retelling.en: The Spinka Rebbe told of a Jew, whom everyone knew to be himself, who finished the Haggadah on the second Seder night and wished to continue praising Hashem. He took out the Megillah and read it. A soul then revealed that it had been waiting for a tikkun that comes only through reading the Megillah, and that in Heaven there was a debate whether a reading on Pesach counts. The ruling was that the…

title.en: The Divrei Chaim without fear

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that water was once poured on the head of a general, who came up with a sword against the Divrei Chaim. The general went away, and the Divrei Chaim said that his miracle was that he had no fear of him, for where there is no fear nothing can happen.

title.en: The cow that would not work on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a gentile, but on Shabbos the cow would not work however much it was beaten. The gentile ran to the Jew, who whispered into the cow's ear, and the cow began to work. When the gentile accused him of witchcraft, the Jew explained that the cow was used to resting on Shabbos and he had told it that it now belonged to a gentile who may work on Shabbos. Seeing the greatness of the…

title.en: The Sefer Torah with perfect final letters

retelling.en: Someone brought a beautiful Sefer Torah to one of the gedolei hador of several generations ago; he looked it over and said it was kosher. Afterwards it emerged that its sofer was a maskil and a heretic, and the gadol was asked how he knew. He explained that the Jewish custom is to leave the last letters hollow so that people can fill them in at the siyum, and such letters never look perfect; this…

title.en: Mordechai mounts the horse

retelling.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara: when Haman came to lead Mordechai on the king's horse, Mordechai had no strength to climb up, so Haman bent down and Mordechai stepped on him to mount, giving him a kick. Haman protested that the Torah says 'when your enemy falls, do not rejoice', and Mordechai answered that this applies to Jews, but of the nations it says 'and you will tread on their high places…

title.en: The Sfas Emes accepts the Rebbe of Alexander

retelling.en: When the Chiddushei HaRim passed away, Rabbi Chanoch Henoch of Alexander became Rebbe. The Sfas Emes, still a young man but already great, came to Alexander to decide whether to accept him. While the Alexander Rebbe spoke with ruach hakodesh to each person present, the Sfas Emes stood unimpressed, twirling his peyos, until the Rebbe turned to him and spoke of 'yayin hameshumar'. The Sfas Emes the…

title.en: Yoav and his teacher

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates the Gemara that Yoav, sent by David HaMelech to fight Edom, killed only the males. When David asked why, Yoav said his teacher had taught him 'zachar' instead of 'zecher'. Yoav went to his teacher, who confirmed it, and the Gemara gives two opinions whether Yoav killed him or only meant to. Because the females were spared, a remnant of Amalek survived.

title.en: The cow that kept Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a gentile. On Shabbos the cow would not work, and the gentile complained to the Jew. The Jew whispered in the cow's ear that it now belonged to a gentile who may work, and it began to work. The gentile said the Jews were sorcerers, but the Jew explained that his cow had never worked on Shabbos. Seeing the greatness of the G-d of Israel, the gentile converted, and he was call…

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta and Bar Koziba

retelling.en: Bar Koziba called himself Moshiach, was a great warrior who defeated the Romans, and Rabbi Akiva supported him. Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta told Rabbi Akiva that grass would grow on his cheeks and Moshiach would still not have come. Bar Koziba was later killed, and it was seen that he was not Moshiach.

title.en: The Ropshitzer Rav's two days of drunkenness

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Ropshitzer Rav said he became drunk twice a year: on Shemini Atzeres at the kedushah of 'Keser', and on Purim when reading the Megillah. He did not need wine; the words of the Megillah made him drunk.

title.en: The mashpia on the way to his daughter's levayah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells of Reb Mendel, one of the great Lubavitcher mashpi'im, whom many people alive today still remember. He lost a daughter, and on the way to the levayah he was in pain over the loss. Suddenly he shook himself and said to himself, 'Mendel, Lehaskil HaBinah!', the first words of this letter, and became a new person.

title.en: A boy's answer about the brachos

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that when he was a melamed teaching Chumash with Rashi, they learned the parsha of Ki Savo, where the curses are written out but the blessings are not. He asked the boys why the Torah did not rather write the blessings. A boy, a descendant of the Bnei Yissaschar, answered that the Torah wanted to leave the honor of the blessings to Torah shebe'al peh. The Mashgiach says the…

title.en: A favor through machlokes

retelling.en: The Mashgiach tells that a Rebbe of the Sanz family once met a great descendant of Ruzhin in Yerushalayim and apologized for the machlokes of Sanz against the Ruzhin family. The Ruzhin descendant answered that the Divrei Chaim did them a great favor with his machlokes: before it, the Ruzhin family were not long-lived, as the Maggid, the Malach, Rabbi Shalom of Prohobisht and the Ruzhiner himself…

title.en: A Chernobyl grandson at the Divrei Chaim's table

retelling.en: A tzaddik of the Chernobyl family passed through Sanz and visited the Divrei Chaim, who was happy to see him and asked him to eat with him. He refused, saying the Divrei Chaim attacks his holy uncles, the Ruzhin family; the Divrei Chaim protested that he would never do such a thing. During the meal a foolish chassid came in and spoke against the Ruzhin family, and the Divrei Chaim began to shout;…

title.en: Water blessed by the Baba Sali

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that decades earlier he visited the Baba Sali, who used to bless water. He brought water from the Shiloach spring below the Beis HaMikdash, and the Baba Sali blessed it. He says he puts a few drops of this water into his Shabbos kiddush, and that this year it was mixed into the wine of the seudah.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov's spring

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates what the Netzer Chesed writes: near Mezhibuzh the Ba'al Shem Tov once went to daven Mincha with his chevra, and there was no water to wash their hands. He struck the ground with his stick and a spring came forth, and they washed. The spring, the Netzer Chesed writes, exists to this day and is known for healing; the Mashgiach received water from it and mixed it into the wine…

title.en: Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin and the crowbar

retelling.en: A man who had sinned greatly came to Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin and asked for a tikkun. Rabbi Shlomo told him that he had sinned so much that he had no key to open his house. The ba'al teshuvah answered that if he had no key, he should open it with a crowbar: every lock has its own key, but a crowbar opens any lock.

title.en: The soul let in on Pesach night

retelling.en: The Imrei Yosef told of a Jew who, on the second night of Pesach after the seder, did not want to go to sleep and read the Megillah. A soul came to him waiting for a tikkun: on Purim souls stand in line and are let in, but when its turn came the gate was closed, since it had come late. When a Jew read the Megillah, it came to the gate, and when the question arose whether it was Purim or Pesach, t…

title.en: The cow that would not work on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a goy. On Shabbos the cow would not work, and the goy complained to the Jew. The Jew went to the cow and told it that it had been sold to a goy and must now work on Shabbos, and the cow began to work. The goy saw this, converted, learned Torah, and became Rabbi Yehudah ben Torta, 'son of the cow'.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon's seudah for Elazar's bar mitzvah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach reads from the Zohar that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai invited the Tanna'im to a great seudah, adorned his house and rejoiced greatly. When the Chachamim asked about the special joy, he said that on this day a holy neshamah comes down upon his son Elazar, who is bar mitzvah; this is his wedding and a great simcha. A heavenly fire came down and rested on the boy's head. Rabbi Yossi ben La…

title.en: Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld and the mikvah

retelling.en: Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld was met coming out of the mikvah and was asked why he spent time on it when he should sit and learn. He answered that a goy who wants to convert must immerse in a mikvah; if a mikvah can make a goy into a Jew, it can surely make a Jew into a better Jew. The Mashgiach brings it from his biography and applies it to Purim.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin and Reb Dovid of Lelov's seder hayom

retelling.en: When Reb Dovid of Lelov became a talmid of the Chozeh of Lublin, he drew up a seder for all twenty-four hours of his day: learning, avodah, tefillah. He showed it to the Chozeh to see whether he agreed. The Chozeh looked it over and, beside every line, wrote 'or the opposite': it need not always go this way; sometimes one must serve Hashem with v'nahafoch.

title.en: Mordechai steps on Haman

retelling.en: As the Gemara relates, when Mordechai had to mount the horse he had no strength, so Haman bent down to serve as a step. Climbing on him, Mordechai gave Haman a kick. Haman protested with 'binfol oyivcha al tismach', and Mordechai answered that this is said about Jews, not about him.

title.en: Reb Shraga Feivel's serious moment

retelling.en: The Mashgiach recalls a Purim seudah with Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz. After the seudah Reb Shraga Feivel complained that there had not been a truly serious moment. Every Purim he created such a moment, and that year he had not managed to.

title.en: The fiddler in Teveria

retelling.en: As an example of Mordechai coming in every generation, the Mashgiach tells that someone in Teveria was alone when a Jew came and began to play a fiddle, and suddenly everyone gathered around him. It was Mordechai HaTzaddik.

title.en: The Arizal and R' Chaim Vital

retelling.en: R' Chaim Vital said that he is nothing compared to the Tanna'im. The Arizal told him that each generation is measured by its own standard, and in his generation he is like a Tanna.

title.en: The heavenly judgment and the Maharsham

retelling.en: A man who was very ill was brought up for judgment, and his mitzvos, aveiros and packs of Torah were weighed. A black angel blew on the Torah and it fell off the scale, as it was not lishmah. Suddenly a new judge stood up and cried out that in this generation one cannot look at Torah that way, and the Torah was put back; the man recovered. When he later visited the Maharsham, he recognized him as…

title.en: The Chozeh's talmidim and the Wednesday seudah

retelling.en: The talmidim of the Chozeh of Lublin, who felt great kedusha on Shabbos, wondered whether it came only from the fine Shabbos food. They made a seudah like Shabbos on a Wednesday and felt the kedusha of Shabbos, and came broken to the Chozeh. He asked them whether they had also put on Shabbos clothes.

title.en: The cow that would not work on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a gentile, and on Shabbos the cow would not work. The gentile complained, and the Jew went and spoke into the cow's ear that now that it belonged to a gentile it may work on Shabbos, and it began to work. Seeing the honor of Shabbos, the gentile did teshuvah, converted, learned Torah and became the Tanna R' Yochanan ben Torasa.

title.en: The farmer and the horses

retelling.en: A farmer's horse ran away, and his neighbors came to console him, but he said he did not know whether it was good or bad. The horse came back with twenty wild horses it had befriended in the forest; when the neighbors congratulated him, he again said he did not know. His son rode one of the new horses, was thrown and broke his leg, and the farmer again said he did not know. Then war broke out and…

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's mezuzos

retelling.en: The Ba'al HaTanya sent a chassid to bring him mezuzos from a certain sofer. The sofer said these mezuzos were made only for the Ba'al HaTanya, who wanted specifically mezuzos written on the fifteenth of the month, when the moon is full. The chassid took one mezuzah for himself, and the Ba'al HaTanya noticed that one of the mezuzos was not of those.

title.en: The line of petitioners in Lubavitch

retelling.en: In Lubavitch on Purim a whole line of people formed between the niggunim, each wanting a moment with the Rebbe to ask for his needs. The Rebbe was not pleased and cancelled it: on Purim one must not come to him to ask for one's needs.

title.en: A kvittel at the Kosel

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he was once at the Kosel and one of the hundreds of kvitlach in the wall had fallen to the floor. He picked it up and, wondering whether it was proper, read it. It was written by a boy asking Hashem for something; the Mashgiach uses it to teach that requests for spiritual things are always answered.

title.en: The homeless guests at the Shabbos table

retelling.en: The Mashgiach's chavrusa, the bar mitzvah boy's great-grandfather Chaim Meir, told him that his father never sat down to the Shabbos table without guests, and the guests were the homeless Jews of the East Side who had no food or shelter. As a young boy Chaim Meir told his father he could not sit near them because of their unpleasant odor. His father answered that beneath their wretched bodies is…

title.en: The fox's song at the lion's feast

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash: the lion, king of the forest, made a feast for all the animals, with a canopy made of the skins of lions and tigers. When they asked who would sing, they looked to the fox, the clever one among the animals. The fox sang that the One who had shown them the skins of the others would show them the skin of the one sitting above, and all had to join in. So too, the One…

title.en: Rabbi Meir of Premishlan's question to the Butchatcher Rav

retelling.en: Rabbi Meir of Premishlan took the cup for havdalah three times and set it down each time. He asked who could ride a horse, and sent the man to the Butchatcher Rav, telling him to strike the horse three times outside the town; within moments he was in Butchatch, found the Rav at shalosh seudos and asked his question. The Butchatcher Rav answered 'Bnei Yishmael', and when the answer was brought bac…

title.en: Sweets for the children on Purim

retelling.en: A young man who davened by a great tzaddik and mekubal saw that on Purim the tzaddik would give sweets to all the small children. This was understood as the answer to how the Megillah's gifts will be given when there are no poor: they will be given to the children.

title.en: The donkey without a heart

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash: the lion, king of the forest, went with his companions and came to a bridge where a donkey collected the toll. The donkey insisted that even the king must pay, so the lion struck and killed him and told the fox to prepare a feast from him. The fox ate the heart, and when the lion asked where it was, the fox answered that the donkey had no heart, for if he had a hea…

title.en: The cow that rested on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a gentile, and the cow would not work on Shabbos. The gentile complained of a mistaken sale, so the Jew whispered in the cow's ear that she now belonged to a gentile and could work, and she worked. The gentile was so moved that a Jewish cow would not work on Shabbos that he converted and became the great Tanna Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa, 'son of the cow'. The Mashgiach brings…

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa and Bar Koziva

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva held that Bar Koziva was Moshiach, but Beitar fell and he was killed, and it became clear he was not Moshiach. Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa had told Rabbi Akiva at the time that he was not Moshiach, so when this became clear, the Jews were spared a crisis of faith, seeing that Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa had been right.

title.en: The Spinka Rebbe and the soul that came late

retelling.en: On the second night of Pesach, after the piyutim, the Spinka Rebbe, the Imrei Yosef, began saying the Megillah, since the second day of Pesach was the day of Haman's downfall. A soul came to him: it had missed Purim, when souls that reach the king's gate receive their repair, and the angels told it to go to the Jew reading the Megillah and have him rule that it is Purim. The Rebbe ruled so, and t…

title.en: The Satmar Rav in Meron

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Satmar Rav came to Meron during the Nine Days and told them to sing at Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's place. When the chassidim asked about it, he answered that here 'strength and joy are in His place'.

title.en: The late soul and the Megillah on Pesach

retelling.en: The Spinka Rebbe, the Imrei Yosef, told that souls that cannot otherwise have a tikkun crowd into the gate of Purim in Heaven. One soul came late, and just as it reached the door, the door closed. On the second night of Pesach a young man finished the Seder and read the Megillah; the soul ran to him and asked him to rule, and he ruled that when the Megillah is read it is Purim, and the soul recei…

title.en: Rebbe's mother and the queen

retelling.en: The Roman king decreed that no child be circumcised, on pain of death for mother and child. Rebbe's mother circumcised him; an informer told the king, who summoned her to bring the child. The queen, who loved her, gave her own child to Rebbe's mother and nursed Rebbe meanwhile, so the king saw an uncircumcised child. The queen's son, Antoninus, nursed from Rebbe's mother and later converted.

title.en: The Satmar Rav: worth a lifetime

retelling.en: Once in America, at the Purim seudah, the Satmar Rav said that after everything he had gone through in Europe, in the camps, it was worth all he had endured in his life to be able to read the Megillah once.

title.en: The Ruzhiner explains Shaul's words

retelling.en: A young man who traveled among tzaddikim and sages came to visit the Ruzhiner. The Ruzhiner told him the meaning of Shaul's words 'I have fulfilled the word of Hashem': because Shaul left Agag alive, Agag fathered a child that night, Haman came from him, and so the Jews have Purim in the world. That, he said, is how Shaul fulfilled the word of Hashem.

title.en: The emperor's nephew who wanted a bris

retelling.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara about the nephew of the Roman emperor who wanted to convert. He told his uncle he wanted to learn Torah, and the uncle answered that he may learn Torah, but why must he circumcise himself? The nephew answered that without milah one cannot learn Torah: wisdom one can learn, but not Torah.

title.en: The Spinker Rebbe and the soul who always came late

retelling.en: On the second night of Pesach, after the seder and the songs, the Spinker Rebbe, author of the Imrei Yosef, sat learning the Megillah and saw a soul that asked him for a tikkun. The soul said there is a palace in heaven called Purim, and whoever enters it is helped; all souls rush to enter on Purim, but every time its turn came the gate was closed, for it was already after Purim. Now it heard the…

title.en: The Rebbe back from Siberia who sat facing the people

retelling.en: A Rebbe who had been in Siberia, unlike the custom of Chassidishe Rebbes to daven facing the wall, sat facing the people when he davened in the yeshiva after his release. Asked why, he said that in Siberia he had been cut off with no contact with Jews; now that Hashem had freed him he wanted to look at Jews and be together with them.

title.en: The Lubavitcher Rebbe and R' Yosef Weinberger's mission

retelling.en: A Jew had helped the Lubavitcher Rebbe greatly when he was in prison, and that man's grandson had drifted away. The Rebbe sent R' Yosef Weinberger to strengthen him; the grandson took out his checkbook, but R' Yosef said he had come to strengthen him in Yiddishkeit, telling him that every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah and a Jew who strays erases part of his letter. When R' Yosef reported bac…

title.en: R' Nachman's merchant and the ship's captain

retelling.en: A merchant acquired a very precious item that no one in his town could afford to buy, so he arranged with a ship's captain to take him to England and pay him after selling it. At every meal he would take it out and look at it, until one day he fell asleep and the cleaner shook the tablecloth into the sea with it. He kept his composure, told the captain nothing and kept talking with him cheerfully…

title.en: The Kotzker's shout and Reb Yitzchak of Vorka's call

retelling.en: Chassidim were sitting at a seudah in the beis medrash, drinking l'chaim and telling stories of earlier chassidim. The door opened, the Kotzker came out and began shouting at them, and they all ran. Reb Yitzchak of Vorka, known for his great love of Jews, stood up on a bench and called, 'Yidelach, come to me!' They all came to him, and he comforted them.

title.en: The plague that spared Rav's neighborhood

retelling.en: There was a plague where Jews lived, but not in the place where Rav lived. People thought they were saved in Rav's merit, but it was revealed in a dream that Rav was too great for that. It was in the merit of a man who lent out tools for digging graves.

title.en: The Belzer Rav in the mikveh and without his beard

retelling.en: The Belzer Rav went into the mikveh and asked what news there was in the world, because the minhag of Jews is to talk news in the mikveh, and he wanted to be part of them. He arrived in Eretz Yisrael without his beard; he did not need to shave it, since he knew he would be saved, but all the Jews had their beards cut, and he wanted to be part of them.

title.en: The cow that would not work on Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold his cow to a gentile, but it would not work for him. The gentile complained, and the Jew explained that it did not work on Shabbos because by him it had not worked on Shabbos. He whispered in its ear that it now belonged to the gentile and could work on Shabbos, and it began to work at once. Seeing this wonder, the gentile converted and became Rabbi Yochanan ben Torasa.

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torasa and Bar Kochva

retelling.en: Rabbi Akiva held that Bar Kochva was Moshiach. Rabbi Yochanan ben Torasa told him that grass would grow on his cheeks and Moshiach would still not have come. Later Bar Kochva was killed, and because Rabbi Yochanan ben Torasa had said he was not Moshiach, the Jews were spared a crisis in their faith.

title.en: The Plantcher Rebbe's Kiddush on Tisha B'Av

retelling.en: The Plantcher Rebbe, a great tzaddik and the father-in-law of the Satmar Rav, once took a cup on Tisha B'Av. He held it as if it were full of wine and acted out the Kiddush that will be made on Tisha B'Av when Moshiach comes. As he spoke, two streams of tears ran from his eyes.

title.en: The Satmar Rav at his Purim seudah

retelling.en: The Mashgiach relates that he heard the Satmar Rav read the Megillah many times, and it was like hearing a different Megillah. Once at his Purim seudah the Satmar Rav said that when he read the Megillah that day he saw neither Mordechai nor Haman, only the Ribono shel Olam alone.

title.en: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani and the famine

retelling.en: In the days of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani there was both a famine and a plague. Since a fast is declared for one trouble only, the people wanted to pray about the plague. He told them to pray about the famine instead, for when Hashem grants sustenance He grants it to the living, and both would be resolved.

title.en: Shlomo HaMelech oversleeps the dedication

retelling.en: Through the seven years of building the Beis Hamikdash Shlomo drank no wine. On the night of its dedication he drank wine and slept late, the Tamid could not be offered in time, and a decree of destruction followed.

title.en: The cow that kept Shabbos

retelling.en: A Jew sold a cow to a gentile, and on Shabbos the cow refused to work. The Jew whispered to it that it now belonged to a gentile and could work, and it began working. When the gentile heard this he was moved and converted, and became Yochanan ben Torsa.
